# TIMELINE — The Flat Chronological Index

> **Every notable event in the corpus, sorted on the cosmic clock.** Auto-generated cross-index: each entry links to the file where it is detailed. Hindu chronology is cyclic and often unordered within an age, so sequence inside each period is approximate. Back to the [master index](README.md) · see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) for how to use this.

**7918 distinct events** across 9 periods. Current address: 7th (Vaivasvata) Manvantara → 28th Mahāyuga → **Kali Yuga**.

---


## Before Time — Cosmogony & the First Creation  ·  473 events

*The creation accounts (Vedic, Upaniṣadic, Vaiṣṇava, Śaiva, Śākta) and the first emanations — catalogued as parallel variants, not a single sequence.*

- **"With sacrifice the gods sacrificed to sacrifice"** — The primal rite closes as the first ordinances (dharmas), by which the mighty reach the heaven of the ancient Sādhyas _(actors: the devas, the Sādhyas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/purusha-sukta.md) — (Ṛgveda, 10.90.16)
- **Acchodā generated as mind-born daughter of the Pitṛs** — The Agniṣvātta ancestors produce the maiden Acchodā, at once celestial girl, Himalayan river, and the clear-water lake Acchoda _(actors: Agniṣvātta Pitṛs, Acchodā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/acchoda-satyavati-rebirth.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa, 14)
- **Acchodā's lapse and fall** — After a thousand years of tapas Acchodā desires the descending Pitṛ Amāvasu, who refuses; the misplaced longing strips her celestial standing and she falls from the sky _(actors: Acchodā, Amāvasu, Adrikā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/acchoda-satyavati-rebirth.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa, 14)
- **Aghamarṣaṇa cosmogony (creation from tapas)** — From kindled tapas (cosmic heat/austerity) are born ṛta (cosmic order) and satya (truth), then night, the cosmic ocean, the year, and the Dhātṛ-ordained sun and moon, heaven and earth, mid-air and light — a terse austerity-driven creation sequence _(actors: Tapas, Ṛta, Satya, Dhātṛ; ṛṣi Aghamarṣaṇa Mādhucchandasa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedic-deities-and-suktas.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.190)
- **Aṅgiras born as mind-born Prajāpati of Brahmā** — Aṅgiras is emitted as one of Brahmā's mānasaputra Prajāpatis and primordial ṛṣis at the dawn of creation _(actors: Brahmā, Aṅgiras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/angiras.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7; Manusmṛti 1.35; Bhāgavata 3.12)
- **Atharvaveda elevated as Brahmaveda** — The Pūrvabhāga opens by proclaiming the Atharvaveda the Brahmaveda, source and crown of the other three Vedas _(actors: Atharvan/Śaunaka school; Brahman (the absolute))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/gopatha-brahmana.md) — (Gopatha Brāhmaṇa Pūrvabhāga 1.1)
- **Atri emitted as mind-born Prajāpati** — Brahmā emits Atri as one of his mānasaputra Prajāpatis and primordial Saptarṣi at the dawn of creation _(actors: Brahmā, Atri)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/atri-anasuya.md) — (Bhāgavata 3.12; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Being wills to become many (Chāndogya cosmogony)** — In the beginning Being alone (Sat) exists; it wills 'May I be many' and emits heat, water and food, from which all forms recombine _(actors: Sat (Being))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/chandogya-upanishad.md) — (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.2)
- **Bhṛgu emitted as mind-born Prajāpati** — Brahmā emits Bhṛgu as a mānasaputra and Prajāpati, apical patriarch of the Bhārgavas _(actors: Brahmā, Bhṛgu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhrigu.md) — (Manu Smṛti 1.35; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1)
- **Bhṛgu's vision of the eaters and the eaten in the other world** — Varuṇa sends his proud son Bhṛgu to the next world, where he sees men devoured by the men, animals, and plants they had consumed in this life, then teaches him the Agnihotra as release _(actors: Bhṛgu, Varuṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/jaiminiya-brahmana.md) — (Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa I.42–44; cf. Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 11.6.1)
- **Bila-svarga named as the heaven of caverns** — Sukadeva designates the seven subterranean realms collectively as bila-svarga and declares their sense-enjoyment superior to the upper heavens _(actors: Sukadeva Gosvami (narrator), Daityas, Danavas, Yakshas, Nagas)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/bila-svarga-and-the-patalas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.24.7-10)
- **Birth of Agastya from the Pot** — Mitra and Varuna, aroused at the sight of the apsara Urvashi, spill their seed into a clay pot, from which Agastya (and in some tellings Vasishtha) is born _(actors: Agastya, Mitra, Varuna, Urvashi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/agastya.md) — (Rigveda 7.33; Mahabharata; Puranas)
- **Birth of Aruṇa from the Broken Egg** — Impatient Vinatā cracks one egg early, releasing the half-formed Aruṇa, who curses her to 500 years of slavery and flies up to become Sūrya's charioteer and the red dawn _(actors: Aruṇa, Vinatā, Sūrya)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/garuda.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Birth of Brahmā from the navel-lotus** — Brahmā emerges seated on the lotus growing from Viṣṇu's navel as Viṣṇu reclines on Śeṣa in the cosmic ocean at the start of each Kalpa _(actors: Brahmā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/trimurti-and-tridevi.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Gaṇeśa and the elephant head** — Pārvatī forms a guardian boy from her body-paste; Śiva beheads him for barring the door, then revives him with an elephant's head as Gajānana with first-worship precedence _(actors: Pārvatī, Gaṇeśa, Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganesha-and-kartikeya.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā, Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Kāma from Brahmā's mind** — as Brahmā emanates his mind-born sons, the love-god Kāma springs from his mind alongside Sandhyā, the first woman, and is given his flower-bow and the office of driving procreation _(actors: Brahmā, Kāma, Sandhyā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sandhya-arundhati.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Rudra-saṃhitā, Sati-khaṇḍa 2)
- **Birth of Kaśyapa from Marīci** — Kaśyapa is born to the mind-born seer Marīci (and Kalā), making him a second-generation Prajāpati and grandson of Brahmā _(actors: Brahmā, Marīci, Kalā, Kaśyapa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kashyapa.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.10; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.6)
- **Birth of Madhu and Kaiṭabha** — Two asuras embodying tamas arise from the sleeping Viṣṇu's body (ear-wax) and threaten the newborn Brahmā on the lotus _(actors: Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Madhu, Kaiṭabha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/hayagriva.md) — (Mahābhārata; Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Devī Māhātmya 1)
- **Birth of Narmadā from Śiva's Sweat** — While Shiva performs tapas on Mount Riksha/Mekala, a drop of his perspiration falls to earth and becomes the maiden Narmada, whom he commands to flow as a sin-destroying river _(actors: Shiva, Narmada)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/narmada-parikrama.md) — (Matsya Purana; Skanda Purana (Reva-khanda))
- **Birth of the Āptya trio from Agni-in-the-waters** — the fourth Agni hides in the waters in fear, and from his spittle spring the water-born deities Trita, Dvita, and Ekata, the "watery ones" _(actors: Agni, Trita, Dvita, Ekata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/trita-aptya.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.2.3.1)
- **Birth of the Rākṣasas from Brahmā** — As Brahmā recited the Vedas at the dawn of creation he grew hungry, and beings born of his hunger cried 'rakṣāma!' becoming rākṣasas (and those of thirst, yakṣas) _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rakshasas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.5)
- **Birth of Yama and Yami** — Yama and his twin sister Yami are born to Vivasvat/Surya and Saranyu/Sanjna as the primordial mortal pair _(actors: Yama, Yami, Surya, Saranyu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yama.md) — (Rig Veda 10.17; Puranas)
- **Brahma emits the mind-born sons (Manasaputras)** — At the dawn of the kalpa Brahma produces his first conscious offspring from mind without union, the Prajapatis and first Saptarshis _(actors: Brahma, Marichi, Atri, Angiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Vasishtha)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Manusmriti 1.34-35; Vishnu Purana 1.7; Bhagavata Purana 3.12)
- **Brahmā's curse on Kāma (the first curse)** — enraged at the incestuous flush, Brahmā curses that Śiva will one day burn Kāma to ash, softening it with the promise of rebirth when Śiva marries _(actors: Brahmā, Kāma, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sandhya-arundhati.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Sati-khaṇḍa 3)
- **Brahmā's seed-pot floated on the pralaya** — at the close of the last kalpa Brahmā seals the bīja of all future beings with amṛta in a kumbha and floats it on the deluge, whence it drifts south and grounds at Kuḍandhai _(actors: Śiva, Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kumbakonam-adi-kumbheshwara-mahamaham.md) — (Ādi Kumbheśvara sthala-purāṇa, Skanda tradition)
- **Brahma–Vishnu Supremacy Quarrel and Lingodbhava** — Brahma and Vishnu dispute who is supreme, and Shiva manifests as a boundless flaming pillar of light (jyotirlinga) piercing the three worlds to settle the contest _(actors: Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/12-jyotirlingas.md) — (Shiva Purana (Vidyeshvara Samhita); Linga Purana)
- **Brahmā Creates Mānasarovara from His Mind** — Brahmā forms the lake Mānasa-sarovara out of his consciousness as the abode of his haṃsa mount, manifesting it on earth for the gods' austerities at Kailāsa's foot _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/manasarovar-kailash-yatra.md) — (Skanda Purana, Manasakhanda; Matsya Purana)
- **Brahmā creates the worlds (Brahma Purāṇa sarga)** — Brahmā emerges from the cosmic egg / Viṣṇu's navel-lotus and brings forth the Prajāpatis, the Manus, and the worlds _(actors: Brahmā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahma-purana.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa (Pūrva-bhāga))
- **Brahmā emits the mind-born seers** — At the dawn of the present kalpa Brahmā emits Marīci, Pulastya, Pulaha and Kratu (with the other mānasaputras) from his mind without union, making them the first sāttvic beings, Prajāpatis and original Saptarṣi _(actors: Brahmā; Marīci; Pulastya; Pulaha; Kratu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-mind-born-seers.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12)
- **Brahmā First Sacrifices in Ānandavana (Founding of Kāśī)** — In its origin-myth Kashi is the first light-pillar of creation, the ground where Brahmā first performed sacrifice and the liṅga of light manifested in the grove of bliss _(actors: Brahmā, Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kashi-varanasi.md) — (Skanda Purana, Kashi-khanda)
- **Brahmā reveals Āyurveda at creation** — Brahmā recalls/recites the beginningless science of life (as an upāṅga of the Atharvaveda) in 100,000 verses at the dawn of creation _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/ayurveda-and-the-science-of-life.md) — (Suśruta Saṃhitā Sū. 1; Caraka Saṃhitā Sū. 1)
- **Brahmā Slays the Demon Vajranābha with the Lotus** — Brahma strikes down the asura Vajranabha with the lotus he holds; petals fall to earth at three places and well up as the three Pushkar lakes _(actors: Brahma, Vajranabha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pushkar-brahma-tirtha.md) — (Padma Purana (Pushkar-mahatmya))
- **Brahmā's lotus-creation** — The Purāṇas narrate the primary creation (sarga), including Brahmā's emergence and the lotus-creation unfolding the universe at the start of his day _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Padma Purāṇa; Matsya/Vāyu/Viṣṇu Purāṇas)
- **Brahmā's Prakṛṣṭa Yajña at Prayāga** — At the start of creation Brahma performs the supreme prakrsta yajna at the confluence, giving Prayaga its name and making it the cosmic sacrificial altar _(actors: Brahma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/prayagraj-triveni-sangam.md) — (Matsya Purana (Prayaga-mahatmya); Padma Purana)
- **Cosmos emitted from Death/Hunger (Bṛhadāraṇyaka cosmogony)** — In the horse-sacrifice opening, Death (Mṛtyu / Prajāpati / Hunger) appears as the primal reality from which the worlds are emitted _(actors: Mṛtyu/Prajāpati)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/brihadaranyaka-upanishad.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.1–1.2)
- **Creation by Vishnu/Vasudeva (sarga)** — Vishnu as material and efficient cause unfolds prakriti and the tattvas, the cosmic egg, and Brahma's emergence in the model Puranic cosmogony _(actors: Vishnu/Vasudeva, Brahma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 1))
- **Creation of Svayambhuva Manu & Shatarupa** — Brahma divides his body into male and female halves, producing the first human couple and progenitors of mankind _(actors: Brahma, Svayambhuva Manu, Shatarupa)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Manusmriti 1; Vishnu Purana 1; Bhagavata Purana 3-4)
- **Creation, the cosmic egg, and Brahma's day (Vamana)** — The Vamana Purana supplies a sarga account of the cosmic egg (anda) and the unfolding of the elements and the gods at the start of the kalpa _(actors: Brahma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vamana-purana.md) — (Vamana Purana)
- **Dakṣiṇā wed to Yajña-puruṣa** — the barren personified Sacrifice receives the fee-goddess Dakṣiṇā in marriage and their son Phala is born, so no rite bears fruit without the priestly fee _(actors: Yajña-puruṣa/Viṣṇu, Dakṣiṇā, Phala)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/prakriti-khanda-goddess-origins.md) — (Brahmavaivarta, Prakṛti-khaṇḍa)
- **Definition of the Āraṇyaka stratum (the 'forest book')** — The Āraṇyaka is the third śruti layer, a forest-studied bridge from ritual karma-kāṇḍa toward the gnosis of jñāna-kāṇḍa _(actors: Vedic ṛṣis; forest-dwelling students (vānaprastha); Vyāsa as divider)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/aranyakas.md) — (Āraṇyaka tradition; Vedānta classification)
- **Diggajas Created by Brahmā** — The eight directional world-elephants, headed by Airāvata, are born at creation and ordained by Brahmā to uphold the earth at the quarters and serve as the Dikpālas' mounts _(actors: Brahmā, Aṣṭa-diggaja)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/dikpalas-and-lokapalas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8; Mātaṅga-līlā)
- **Emanation of the four Kumāras** — Brahmā emits Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana and Sanatkumāra from his mind as his first, seniormost mind-born sons at the dawn of the kalpa _(actors: Brahmā; the four Kumāras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-four-kumaras.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12.4; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **Emūṣa the boar raises the Earth (Brāhmaṇa antecedent)** — The boar Emūṣa, identified with Prajāpati, lifts the hand-span Earth out of the primeval waters in the Vedic cosmogony _(actors: Emūṣa / Prajāpati, the Earth, the cosmic waters)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/varaha-hiranyaksha.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 14.1.2.11; Taittirīya Saṃhitā 7.1.5; Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 10.1.8)
- **Etymology of the name Rāma (rā + ma)** — The Pūrva-tāpanī analyses the name Rāma as the resting-place of yogins and as a Brahman-disclosing mantra split into liberating seed-syllables _(actors: Rāma, yogins)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/ramatapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Rāma-tāpanī Up., Pūrva)
- **Gaṇeśa identified as Brahman (tvam eva pratyakṣaṃ tat tvam asi)** — The Atharvaśīrṣa addresses Gaṇeśa directly as the perceptible Brahman, maker-sustainer-destroyer, and eternal Self, folding 'tat tvam asi' into worship of Gaṇapati _(actors: Gaṇapati/Gaṇeśa, the reciter)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/ganapati-atharvashirsha-upanishad.md) — (Gaṇapaty-atharvaśīrṣa Upaniṣad 1)
- **Gavam-ayana year-long sattra** — The year-long soma session modelled on the solar year, with its Vishuvant turning-point and Mahavrata crowning day, identified with Prajapati's body reassembled in time _(actors: Udgatr priests, Prajapati, the year (samvatsara))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/panchavimsha-brahmana.md) — (Panchavimsha (Tandya Maha-) Brahmana)
- **Hayagrīva recovers the stolen Vedas** — Viṣṇu in his horse-headed Hayagrīva form recovers the Vedas stolen from Brahmā by the demons Madhu and Kaiṭabha (or slays the asura Hayagrīva who stole them) _(actors: Hayagrīva (Viṣṇu), Madhu, Kaiṭabha, Brahmā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vishnu-forms-and-vyuhas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Hayagrīva Upaniṣad; Devī Bhāgavata)
- **Indra Shears the Wings of the Mountains** — In primeval ages winged mountains flew about crushing settlements until Indra cut off their wings with his vajra to fix them in place _(actors: Indra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/meru-kailash-and-cosmic-mountains.md) — (Brahmanda Purana; Kathasaritsagara)
- **Kāma's first arrows** — testing his power, Kāma looses the five effect-arrows (Harṣaṇa, Rocana, Mohana, Śoṣaṇa, Māraṇa) on Brahmā and the prajāpatis, striking them with lust for Sandhyā _(actors: Kāma, Brahmā, the mind-sons, Sandhyā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sandhya-arundhati.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Sati-khaṇḍa 3)
- **Mahāviṣṇu gives the Guruvāyūr icon to Brahmā** — at the beginning of creation Viṣṇu hands his own worship-image to Brahmā, first custodian in the icon's lineage _(actors: Mahāviṣṇu, Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/guruvayur-krishna-kshetra.md) — (Guruvāyupura-māhātmya) [late text]
- **Manu's cosmogony (Manusmṛti ch. 1)** — the Self-existent deposits his seed as a golden cosmic egg from which Brahmā and the ordered world arise, prefacing the law-code with a Sāṃkhya-tinged creation account _(actors: Svayambhū, Brahmā, Manu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/manusmriti-map.md) — (Mānava-Dharmaśāstra 1.5–57)
- **Mūla-Prakṛti's aṁśa-catalogue** — Prakṛti manifests as five full goddesses and then a train of part- and digit-portions, issuing Sanskritic pedigrees to Ṣaṣṭhī, Maṅgalā Caṇḍī, Svadhā and Dakṣiṇā _(actors: Mūla-Prakṛti, Brahmā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/prakriti-khanda-goddess-origins.md) — (Brahmavaivarta, Prakṛti-khaṇḍa 41–44; Devī-Bhāgavata IX.44–47)
- **Nikumbha's piśācas make Kashmir a half-year land** — Under the piśāca king Nikumbha, whose hordes occupy the valley each winter, humans may dwell in Kashmir only in summer, evacuating before the snows _(actors: Nikumbha, the piśācas, the first settlers)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/nilamata-purana.md) — (Nīlamata Purāṇa)
- **Nīla-nāga declares his ordinances to Candradeva** — The serpent-king Nīla teaches the wintering brahmin Candradeva the festivals and rites whose observance ends the piśāca terror and lets humans dwell in Kashmir year-round — the nīla-mata that names the text _(actors: Nīla-nāga, Candradeva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/nilamata-purana.md) — (Nīlamata Purāṇa, ordinance section)
- **Padma-sṛṣṭi, the lotus creation** — from Viṣṇu on the causal waters rises the lotus bearing Brahmā, who creates the worlds — the padma that names the Purāṇa _(actors: Viṣṇu, Brahmā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/padma-purana-khanda-map.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa)
- **Prajāpati desires his daughter** — the Creator conceives a passion for his own daughter, the Dawn (Uṣas) or the Sky (Dyaus), and pursues her as a stag while she flees as a red doe _(actors: Prajāpati, Uṣas/Dyaus)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prajapati-ushas-rudra-piercing.md) — (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 3.33; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.7.4.1)
- **Puruṣa and Virāj beget each other** — From the Puruṣa is born Virāj, and from Virāj the Puruṣa again — the circular double birth at the head of creation _(actors: Puruṣa, Virāj)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/purusha-sukta.md) — (Ṛgveda, 10.90.5)
- **Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa's pañcarātra sattra** — Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa performs the five-day sacrificial session and thereby becomes all this, welding the hymn's Puruṣa to Nārāyaṇa _(actors: Puruṣa Nārāyaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/purusha-sukta.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, 13.6.1)
- **Rādhā emanates in Goloka** — before creation, Rādhā emerges from the left half of Kṛṣṇa's body in the eternal cow-realm Goloka as his co-eternal śakti and presides as Rāseśvarī over the rāsa-maṇḍala _(actors: Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/radha.md) — (Brahma-vaivarta Purāṇa, Prakṛti- & Kṛṣṇa-janma-khaṇḍas) [late text]
- **Rati created and wed to Kāma** — from Dakṣa's perspiration arises Rati, and Brahmā gives her to the newly-cursed Kāma as his consort _(actors: Dakṣa, Rati, Kāma, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sandhya-arundhati.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Sati-khaṇḍa 3)
- **Ṛbhu born a son of Brahmā, innately realized** — The sage Ṛbhu comes into being as a son of the supreme Brahmā, endowed from birth with knowledge of truth and needing no instruction _(actors: Ṛbhu, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ribhu-nidagha-vishnu-purana.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa, II.15)
- **Rebirth as Arundhatī and marriage to Vasiṣṭha** — reborn fire-bright from Medhātithi's sacrifice and named Arundhatī, Sandhyā is wed by the Trimūrti to Vasiṣṭha, becoming the chastity-exemplar and mother of his hundred sons _(actors: Sandhyā/Arundhatī, Medhātithi, Vasiṣṭha, the Trimūrti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sandhya-arundhati.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Sati-khaṇḍa 7)
- **Rudra's boon of Paśupati** — before shooting, the avenger bargains for the over-lordship of animals, the charter of the name Paśupati, as his fee for punishing the Creator _(actors: Rudra, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prajapati-ushas-rudra-piercing.md) — (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 3.33)
- **Sandhyā's vow against lust-at-birth** — shamed that desire arose in her father, brothers and herself, Sandhyā vows to legislate that no creature feel lust at the moment of its birth and departs for penance at Mount Candrabhāga _(actors: Sandhyā, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sandhya-arundhati.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Sati-khaṇḍa 5)
- **Ṣaṣṭhī emanates as the sixth portion of Prakṛti** — in the Prakṛti-catalogue, Mūla-Prakṛti's aṁśa-rūpā goddesses include Ṣaṣṭhī-Devasenā, whence her name "the Sixth" _(actors: Mūla-Prakṛti, Ṣaṣṭhī/Devasenā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/gramadevata-shashthi-cross-links.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata, IX.44–47)
- **Śiva assumes the Śarabha form to subdue Narasiṃha** — Śiva takes the eight-legged lion-bird Śarabha form to pacify or overpower Viṣṇu's raging man-lion Narasiṃha after the slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu _(actors: Śiva (as Śarabha), Narasiṃha (Viṣṇu), Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/mythic-beasts-and-composites.md) — (Śarabha Upaniṣad; Liṅga Purāṇa 2.48; Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Kṛṣṇa divides into male and female (Brahmavaivarta cosmogony)** — The universe issues from Kṛṣṇa as Para-Brahman, who first divides into male (Kṛṣṇa) and female (Rādhā/Prakṛti); Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva are produced as functionaries _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Rādhā, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmavaivarta-purana.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa (Brahma-khaṇḍa))
- **Kaśyapa's progeny seed the beings of the cosmos** — Kaśyapa's unions produce the opposed classes of beings: Ādityas (devas) by Aditi, Daityas by Diti, Dānavas by Danu, Nāgas by Kadrū, and Garuḍa and Aruṇa by Vinatā _(actors: Kaśyapa, Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadrū, Vinatā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/README.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.6)
- **Liṅgodbhava** — An infinite pillar of fire erupts in the Brahmā-Viṣṇu supremacy quarrel; neither finds its end, establishing Śiva as the unbounded Absolute and origin of the liṅga _(actors: Śiva, Brahmā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Liṅga Purāṇa, Kūrma Purāṇa, Vāyu Purāṇa)
- **Liṅgodbhava — the pillar of fire** — When Brahmā and Viṣṇu quarrel over supremacy, an infinite fiery liṅga erupts; both fail to find its end, Viṣṇu concedes and Brahmā lies and is cursed, establishing Śiva as the unbounded Absolute _(actors: Śiva, Brahmā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa Vidyeśvara-saṃhitā; Liṅga Purāṇa; Kūrma Purāṇa; Vāyu Purāṇa)
- **Lingodbhava** — Brahma and Vishnu quarrel over supremacy; Shiva manifests as an infinite pillar of fire (jyotirlinga) and challenges them to find its ends, establishing the origin of linga-worship _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/shiva-purana.md) — (Shiva Purana (Vidyeshvara-samhita); cf. Linga, Kurma, Vamana, Skanda, Brahmanda, Vayu Puranas)
- **Lingodbhava — rising of the cosmic pillar of light** — Brahma and Vishnu quarrel over supremacy; Shiva manifests as an infinite blazing jyotirlinga and neither finds its end — Vishnu (as Varaha) admits failure while Brahma lies and is cursed to receive no worship, establishing the linga as supreme _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu (Varaha), the ketaki flower)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/linga-purana.md) — (Linga Purana (Purva-bhaga))
- **Lotus cosmogony (padma-srishti)** — From Vishnu's navel on the cosmic ocean rises a lotus bearing Brahma, who creates the worlds — the myth giving the Padma Purana its name _(actors: Vishnu, Brahma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/padma-purana.md) — (Padma Purana (Srishti Khanda))
- **Manu catches the fish (Śatapatha layer)** — Manu finds a tiny fish in his cupped hands that begs protection in exchange for warning him of a coming flood _(actors: Manu, the fish (unnamed / Prajāpati))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/matsya-pralaya.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1)
- **Muktikā enumeration of the 108 Upaniṣads** — The Muktikā Upaniṣad lists 108 Upaniṣads, from which editors group a sectarian block by deity _(actors: Muktikā Upaniṣad; Rāma teaching Hanumān (frame))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/vaishnava-shaiva-shakta-upanishads-overview.md) — (Muktikā Upaniṣad)
- **Music derived from the Sāmaveda / divine origin** — Classical song (gīta) is traced to Sāmavedic chant and to divine musicians — Sarasvatī's vīṇā, Nārada, the Gandharvas — and classed under the Gāndharvaveda _(actors: Sarasvatī, Nārada, the Gandharvas/Kinnaras)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sangita-classical-music-svara-raga-tala.md) — (Sāmaveda tradition; Nāṭya Śāstra 28; Purāṇic tradition)
- **Nadīstuti — the praise of the rivers** — The ṛṣi Sindhukṣit sings RV 10.75, exalting the Sindhu as the mightiest, roaring bull-flood among streams and rolling off the river-catalogue of the Sapta-Sindhu _(actors: Sindhukṣit Praiyamedha (ṛṣi); Sindhu (Indus); the river-deities)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sapta-sindhu-and-the-indus-rivers.md) — (Ṛg Veda 10.75 (Nadīstuti Sūkta), esp. 10.75.1–6)
- **Namakam: pacification of the wrathful Rudra** — The Namakam (TS 4.5) salutes and pacifies the fierce-and-gracious Rudra, begging him to lay down his bow and arrow and turn his benign (śiva) face to the worshipper _(actors: Rudra–Śiva; the Vedic reciter)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/sri-rudram-namakam-chamakam.md) — (Kṛṣṇa-Yajurveda, Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.5 (Namakam / Rudra-praśna))
- **Nasadiya Sukta — Hymn of Creation** — Before existence/non-existence, 'That One' (Tad Ekam) breathes windless and arises through tapas, with kama as the first seed of mind — the agnostic origin hymn _(actors: Tad Ekam (That One))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Rigveda 10.129)
- **Nasadiya Sukta — the first impulse from That One** — Before existence or non-existence, 'That One' breathes windless by its own impulse; through tapas it arises and kama (desire) becomes the first seed of mind, the agnostic Vedic origin account _(actors: Tad Ekam (That One))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Rigveda 10.129)
- **Nārada born as Brahmā's mind-born son** — Nārada springs from Brahmā's mind as a mānasa-putra prajāpati and refuses the command to procreate, choosing celibacy and ceaseless wandering _(actors: Brahmā, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12; Manu-smṛti 1.35; Mahābhārata)
- **Nārada mind-born from Brahmā** — Nārada is emitted as a manasaputra/Prajāpati from Brahmā's mind among the foundational sages _(actors: Brahmā, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada.md) — (Manu Smṛti 1.35; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12)
- **Nārada teaches Prācīnabarhi via parable** — Nārada arrives to redirect the sacrifice-obsessed King Prācīnabarhi from karma-kāṇḍa to self-knowledge by telling the veiled story of Purañjana _(actors: Nārada, King Prācīnabarhi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/puranjana-allegory.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.25.1–8)
- **Parvati's Penance and the Sand-Linga at Kanchipuram** — Parvati, having covered Shiva's eyes and plunged the cosmos into darkness, does penance at Kanchi and moulds a sand-linga under a mango tree to worship as Ekambareswarar _(actors: Parvati, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-bhuta-sthalams.md) — (Ekambareswarar mahatmya)
- **Pitṛs Beget the Devas, Asuras and Humans** — As primordial demiurges the sevenfold Pitṛ orders precede and beget the three great classes — devas via Agniṣvātta, asuras via Barhiṣad, and humankind/varṇas via the four corporeal orders _(actors: Pitṛs, Devas, Asuras, Humans)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/pitrs-and-ancestors.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa; Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa)
- **Prajāpati emits and is dismembered in creation** — Prajāpati emits the cosmos out of himself and falls apart, exhausted and scattered, requiring ritual reintegration _(actors: Prajāpati)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/shatapatha-brahmana.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (Agnicayana kāṇḍas))
- **Prajāpati emits creation from the waters** — Prajāpati, the Lord of Creatures, arises from the primal flood and through tapas emits the gods, worlds, the year, and the metres _(actors: Prajāpati, the gods, the metres (chandas))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/taittiriya-brahmana.md) — (Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 2.2–2.3)
- **Prior birth — Sudāmā cursed to become Śaṅkhacūḍa** — Kṛṣṇa's gopa-attendant Sudāmā is cursed by Rādhā in Goloka and reborn as the daitya Śaṅkhacūḍa, son of Dambha _(actors: Sudāmā/Śaṅkhacūḍa, Rādhā, Kṛṣṇa, Dambha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shankhachuda-tulasi.md) — (Brahma-Vaivarta Purāṇa, Prakṛti-khaṇḍa)
- **Priyavrata Furrows the Earth-Disc into Oceans** — Priyavrata, grandson of Manu Svayambhuva, furrows the lotus-disc Bhu-mandala with his chariot-wheels to make the seven ring-oceans, his seven sons ruling the seven dvipas _(actors: Priyavrata, sons of Priyavrata)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/bharatavarsha-and-puranic-geography.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.1; Vishnu Purana 2.1)
- **Puruṣa Sacrifice (Puruṣa Sūkta)** — The cosmic person (Puruṣa) is sacrificed, and from his dismembered body the worlds and the four varṇas originate _(actors: Puruṣa, the gods)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shruti-vedas-and-upanishads.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.90 (Puruṣa Sūkta))
- **Śiva brings down the Vitastā** — At Kaśyapa's entreaty Śiva causes Pārvatī to flow forth as the river Vitastā through a trident-dug channel one vitasti deep, purifying the piśāca-defiled valley _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī/Vitastā, Kaśyapa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/nilamata-purana.md) — (Nīlamata Purāṇa)
- **Śiva shames Brahmā, the Pitṛs sweat-born** — Śiva rebukes Brahmā for desiring his own daughter; the ashamed creator perspires, and from his sweat the Pitṛ classes (Agniṣvāttas, Barhiṣads) are born _(actors: Śiva, Brahmā, the Pitṛs)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sandhya-arundhati.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Sati-khaṇḍa 3)
- **Śiva the kirāta breaks the kumbha** — to begin the new creation Śiva takes the form of a hunter and shatters the grounded pot with an arrow, its amṛta pooling as the Mahāmaham tank _(actors: Śiva-kirāta, Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kumbakonam-adi-kumbheshwara-mahamaham.md) — (Ādi Kumbheśvara sthala-purāṇa)
- **Śiva's three boons to Sandhyā** — after four yugas of penance Śiva grants that creatures feel no lust at birth, that Sandhyā attain matchless chastity, and that any lustful gazer be struck impotent _(actors: Śiva, Sandhyā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sandhya-arundhati.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Sati-khaṇḍa 6)
- **Śrī Sūkta as a Ṛgveda khila** — The Śrī Sūkta is composed/transmitted as a khila (appendix) hymn attached to Ṛgveda maṇḍala 5, outside the received saṃhitā _(actors: Vedic ṛṣis; Ṛgveda khilāni tradition)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/sri-suktam.md) — (Ṛgveda khilāni (Śrī Sūkta))
- **Saptarishi emitted as mind-born sons of Brahma** — The original Saptarishi are emitted as manasaputras (mind-born sons) from Brahma to begin procreation, simultaneously titled Prajapatis and seeders of all beings _(actors: Brahma, the Saptarishi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Manu Smriti 1.34-35; Vishnu Purana 1.7; Bhagavata Purana 3.12)
- **Sarasvati as Vac utters creation** — Sarasvati, who is Vac, the primordial sound/speech, is the means through which Brahma utters creation; she is co-emergent with the spoken cosmos _(actors: Brahma, Sarasvati (Vac))_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saraswati.md) — (Vedic/Puranic theology; Shatapatha Brahmana)
- **Sati's birth as Daksha's daughter** — The Great Goddess incarnates as Sati, daughter of the Prajāpati Daksha, specifically to win Shiva as her husband _(actors: Sati (Adi Shakti), Daksha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita Sati Khanda, Devi-Bhagavata Purana VII)
- **Sri emerges from Prajapati** — In an early distribution-of-fortune myth, Sri emerges radiant from Prajapati and the gods seize her many powers (food, sovereignty, beauty) _(actors: Sri, Prajapati, the gods)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lakshmi.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana)
- **Svadhā given to the Pitṛs** — Brahmā manifests the personified ancestral oblation-call Svadhā and weds her to the Fathers, making every śrāddha offering efficacious _(actors: Brahmā, Svadhā, the Pitṛs)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/prakriti-khanda-goddess-origins.md) — (Brahmavaivarta, Prakṛti-khaṇḍa)
- **Svayambhū Raṅga-vimāna worshipped by Brahmā** — The self-manifest reclining Raṅganātha vimāna arises in the Ocean of Milk and is first worshipped by Brahmā _(actors: Brahmā, Raṅganātha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srirangam-ranganatha.md) — (Śrīraṅga-māhātmya)
- **Tapas ignites creation** — before gods or being, "That One" arises through the power of tapas-heat, and ṛta and satya are born of blazing tapas _(actors: Tad Ekam, Prajāpati)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/tapas-boons-and-curses.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.129.3, 10.190.1)
- **The Ādi Kumbheśvara liṅga hand-made by Śiva** — Śiva gathers the nectar-soaked sand of the broken pot and forms the liṅga with his own hands, giving Kumbakonam its name-charter deity _(actors: Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kumbakonam-adi-kumbheshwara-mahamaham.md) — (Ādi Kumbheśvara sthala-purāṇa) [regional]
- **The contest of the faculties (prana-vidya)** — In the recurring Upanishadic parable the senses each leave the body to prove their primacy and the body survives, but it collapses when Prana prepares to depart, proving breath the chief and support of all faculties _(actors: Prana, the senses)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/prana-and-the-vital-airs.md) — (Chandogya Upanishad 5.1; Brihadaranyaka 6.1; Prashna Upanishad 2)
- **The cosmogonic world-bearing tortoise** — The pan-Indic image of a great tortoise supporting the earth/cosmos on its back, the 'Atlas' substrate Kurma inherits _(actors: Kurma (cosmic tortoise))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kurma-avatara.md) — (Puranic cosmography; Kurma Purana)
- **The curse of Śrīdāman** — Rādhā curses Kṛṣṇa's attendant Śrīdāman to fall as the demon Śaṅkhacūḍa, and he counter-curses her to a human birth in Vraja with a hundred years' separation from Kṛṣṇa _(actors: Rādhā, Śrīdāman/Sudāman, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/radha.md) — (Brahma-vaivarta Purāṇa, Prakṛti-khaṇḍa) [late text]
- **The four varṇas from the Primeval body** — Brāhmaṇa is brought forth from the mouth, Kṣatriya from the arms, Vaiśya from the thighs and Śūdra from the feet of the Self-existent, echoing the Puruṣa-sūkta _(actors: Svayambhū, the four varṇas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/manusmriti-map.md) — (Mānava-Dharmaśāstra 1.31, 1.87–91)
- **The four varṇas issue from the Puruṣa's body** — Brāhmaṇa from the mouth, Rājanya from the arms, Vaiśya from the thighs, Śūdra from the feet — the sole Ṛgvedic four-varṇa passage [late text] [disputed] _(actors: Puruṣa, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/purusha-sukta.md) — (Ṛgveda, 10.90.12)
- **The gods compound Bhūtavat/Rudra** — finding no punisher among themselves, the gods pool their most dreadful forms into one avenging god, Bhūtavat (Rudra), named for being made of the terrors _(actors: the devas, Rudra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prajapati-ushas-rudra-piercing.md) — (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 3.33)
- **The Gods Question the Goddess** — All the gods approach the Great Goddess and ask 'Who are you and whence have you arisen?' _(actors: the gods (devas), Mahādevī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/devi-upanishad.md) — (Devī Upaniṣad v.1)
- **The heavens figured as the Śiśumāra (cosmic dolphin)** — The Bhāgavata directs contemplation of the entire stellar sphere (jyotiś-cakra) as the coiled body of a porpoise/dolphin, head bent down, identified as the body of Viṣṇu/Vāsudeva-Kāla _(actors: Viṣṇu (as Kāla/Vāsudeva), Śuka narrating to Parīkṣit)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/shishumara-chakra.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.23.4-9; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.9)
- **The Kumāras' question on mind and sense-objects** — Brahmā's four mind-born sons (Sanaka, Sananda, Sanātana, Sanat-kumāra) ask how the mind can be separated from its sense-objects, which seem inextricably bound _(actors: The Four Kumāras (Sanakādi), Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/hamsa-avatar.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.13.18-19)
- **The naming of amāvāsyā** — Because the steadfast Pitṛ of the episode is Amāvasu, the new-moon day is called amāvāsyā after him and śrāddha offered then is declared inexhaustible _(actors: Amāvasu, the Pitṛs)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/acchoda-satyavati-rebirth.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa, 14; Harivaṃśa, Pitṛ-kalpa)
- **The piercing of the Creator** — Rudra takes aim and pierces Prajāpati mid-act; the wounded Creator flies upward into the sky _(actors: Rudra, Prajāpati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prajapati-ushas-rudra-piercing.md) — (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 3.33; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.7.4.3)
- **The Pitṛs decree Acchodā's rebirth as Satyavatī** — Consoling the fallen maiden, the ancestors script her mortal sentence: birth in the 28th Dvāpara from King Vasu's seed via the fish Adrikā, life as Kālī/Satyavatī, motherhood of Vyāsa, queenship under Śāntanu, then restoration to heaven _(actors: the Pitṛs, Acchodā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/acchoda-satyavati-rebirth.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa, 14; Harivaṃśa, Pitṛ-kalpa ~18)
- **The Prātiśākhyas as a text-class** — Veda-specific phonetic-grammatical manuals fix the precise oral text of each śākhā, deriving the saṃhitā recitation from the padapāṭha _(actors: Vedic ṛṣis and śākhā schools; phoneticians of the Śikṣā vedānga)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/pratishakhyas.md) — (Prātiśākhya tradition; Śikṣā vedānga)
- **Ātman creates the worlds (Aitareya cosmogony)** — In the Aitareya Upaniṣad's opening, Ātman alone exists and brings forth the worlds, the cosmic guardians, and the human person _(actors: Ātman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/principal-upanishads-detail.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad 1)
- **The primal sacrifice of the Puruṣa** — The gods, Sādhyas, and ṛṣis offer the thousand-headed Cosmic Man as the first sacrifice, with spring as ghee, summer as fuel, autumn as oblation _(actors: Puruṣa, the devas, the Sādhyas, the ṛṣis)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/purusha-sukta.md) — (Ṛgveda, 10.90.6–7)
- **The seed becomes a lake** — Prajāpati's spilled seed runs on the ground; the gods make it a lake ringed with Agni so it is not lost, and creatures arise from it _(actors: Prajāpati, the devas, Agni)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prajapati-ushas-rudra-piercing.md) — (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 3.34; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.7.4.4)
- **The Vārāha war (third saṅgrāma)** — Viṣṇu as the Boar raises the sunken Earth on his tusks and slays Hiraṇyākṣa in the underwater duel _(actors: Viṣṇu as Varāha, Hiraṇyākṣa, Bhūdevī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/twelve-devasura-battles.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa 47; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.13–19)
- **The Vedas, animals, and worlds arise from the sacrifice** — From the dismembered offering come the ṛcs, sāmans, metres and yajus, the beasts of air and village, and the worlds — moon from mind, sun from eye, sky from head, earth from feet _(actors: Puruṣa, the devas, Indra, Agni, Vāyu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/purusha-sukta.md) — (Ṛgveda, 10.90.8–14)
- **Varaha lifts the Earth and instructs Bhu-devi** — The Boar avatara Vishnu raises the submerged Earth-goddess Bhu-devi from the cosmic ocean and instructs her, the kalpa-opening frame of the whole Varaha Purana _(actors: Varaha/Vishnu, Bhu-devi/Prithivi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/varaha-purana.md) — (Varaha Purana; cf. Vishnu P., Bhagavata 3, Linga P.)
- **Varaha lifts the submerged Earth** — At the dawn of the Shveta-Varaha Kalpa the Varaha (boar) avatara lifts the submerged Earth, opening the Svayambhuva manvantara and naming the whole Kalpa _(actors: Varaha (Vishnu), Earth)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Vasiṣṭha instructs Sandhyā** — Brahmā sends Vasiṣṭha, disguised as a brahmin boy, to teach the untrained Sandhyā the mantra Oṃ Namaḥ Śaṃkarāya Oṃ and the method of tapas by Lake Bṛhallohita _(actors: Brahmā, Vasiṣṭha, Sandhyā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sandhya-arundhati.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Sati-khaṇḍa 5)
- **Vishnu Reclines on the Ocean of Milk (Tiruparkadal)** — In the celestial Vyuha state, Vishnu reclines as Kshirabdhinatha on Adishesha upon the Ocean of Milk attended by Lakshmi, the cosmic source from which the Dashavatara descents issue _(actors: Vishnu, Lakshmi, Adishesha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (Naalayira Divya Prabandham)
- **Viśvakarmā's twin-bow contest (Pināka and Śārṅga)** — Viśvakarmā forges two bows — Pināka for Śiva and Śārṅga for Viṣṇu — to settle the dispute over which deity is supreme; Viṣṇu prevails and Śiva's Pināka passes to the kings of Mithilā while Śārṅga remains Viṣṇu's own _(actors: Viśvakarmā, Śiva, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (mysutradhar (All About Divine Bows); Rāmāyaṇa (variant tradition))
- **Adyar sectarian groupings established** — Adyar Library editions with Upaniṣad-brahmayogin's commentary fix the Vaiṣṇava, Śaiva, and Śākta groups and their membership _(actors: Upaniṣad-brahmayogin; Adyar Library editors)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/vaishnava-shaiva-shakta-upanishads-overview.md) — (Adyar Vaiṣṇava/Śaiva/Śākta Upaniṣad editions)
- **Aṅgiras marries Smṛti / daughters of Dakṣa** — Aṅgiras weds Smṛti (or Dakṣa's daughters Śraddhā/Svadhā), founding his ṛṣi-progeny line _(actors: Aṅgiras, Smṛti, daughters of Dakṣa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/angiras.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7; Bhāgavata 4.1)
- **Ardhanārīśvara manifestation** — Śiva fuses with Pārvatī into a single half-male, half-female body, expressing the inseparability of consciousness and energy and enabling sexual generation _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī, Brahmā, Bhṛṅgi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Liṅga Purāṇa, Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Ardhanārīśvara — the half-male/half-female form** — Śiva fuses with Pārvatī into one body split down the centre, expressing the inseparability of Śiva (consciousness) and Śakti (energy); in one variant it enables sexual generation when Brahmā's mind-born creation cannot multiply _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Garuḍa** — After five hundred years the second egg bursts and Garuḍa emerges fully formed and blazing like cosmic fire, mistaken for Agni until he diminishes his heat _(actors: Garuḍa, Vinatā, Devas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/garuda.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Brahman knows itself as 'I am Brahman'** — In the beginning Brahman knows only itself, declaring 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi,' and thereby becomes the All _(actors: Brahman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/brihadaranyaka-upanishad.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.4.10)
- **Brahma's lie and curse over the lingam** — Brahma falsely claims to have found the pillar's top, producing the ketaki flower as false witness; Shiva curses Brahma to receive no worship and rewards the honest Vishnu _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu, ketaki flower, Kamadhenu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/shiva-purana.md) — (Shiva Purana (Vidyeshvara-samhita))
- **Brahma's mind-born daughter and the growth of his heads** — Brahma brings forth Sarasvati from his own mind as a being of dazzling beauty; captivated, he sprouts a face on each side and one upward to never lose sight of her, the origin of his four or five heads _(actors: Brahma, Sarasvati)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saraswati.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Brahmā meditates and the Lord appears as the swan** — Unable to resolve the doubt, Brahmā meditates on the supreme Lord, who manifests before the Kumāras as a haṃsa (swan); they ask 'Who are you?' _(actors: Brahmā, Viṣṇu as Haṃsa, the Four Kumāras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/hamsa-avatar.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.13.20-22)
- **Brahmā's Yajña and Marriage to Gāyatrī at Pushkar** — To complete his Pushkar fire-sacrifice on time without the delayed Savitri, Brahma marries the local girl Gayatri to sit beside him as ritual wife _(actors: Brahma, Gayatri, Savitri)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pushkar-brahma-tirtha.md) — (Padma Purana (Pushkar-mahatmya))
- **Cosmogony grounding Atharvan primacy** — Brahman and the cosmic waters generate the worlds and the Vedas, weaving the Atharvan corpus into the origin of knowledge _(actors: Brahman; cosmic waters)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/gopatha-brahmana.md) — (Gopatha Brāhmaṇa Pūrvabhāga 1)
- **Creation from Vāc, the waters, and tapas** — Subsidiary ŚB cosmogonies derive creation from Speech (Vāc), from cosmic waters bearing a golden egg, and from Prajāpati's heat/austerity _(actors: Prajāpati, Vāc, cosmic waters)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/shatapatha-brahmana.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa)
- **Creation of the Prajāpatis and Manus** — Brahmā emanates his mind-born sons (the Kumāras, Saptarṣi, Marīci, Atri, etc.) and the Manus who govern each Manvantara _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/trimurti-and-tridevi.md) — (Manusmṛti; Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
- **Descent of the Sarayu from Vishnu's Foot** — The Sarayu river issues divinely, created from Vishnu's left foot-thumb as the Ganga issued from his right, making it a pada-tirtha of Vishnu _(actors: Vishnu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ayodhya.md) — (Skanda Purana, Ayodhya-mahatmya)
- **Dhruva fixed at the tail-tip as the cosmic pivot** — Dhruva the pole star sits at the tip of the dolphin's upraised tail as the immovable point about which the whole heaven revolves, untouched even by pralaya _(actors: Dhruva, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/shishumara-chakra.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.23.1-4; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.9)
- **Earth sunk in the cosmic ocean at the kalpa's dawn** — At the start of the Śveta-Varāha-Kalpa the Earth lies submerged in the lower waters, blocking Brahmā's recreation _(actors: Brahmā, the Earth (Bhūmi/Pṛthvī), the cosmic ocean)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/varaha-hiranyaksha.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.4; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.13)
- **Gangā's Descent on Brahmapurī** — The celestial Gangā falls onto Brahmā's city atop Meru and divides into four cosmic rivers flowing to the four quarters off Meru's flanks _(actors: Gangā, Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/meru-kailash-and-cosmic-mountains.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.17)
- **God Bears and Watches the Seer Kapila at the Beginning** — The Lord brings forth and observes the seer Kapila, born at the beginning, an early scriptural reference tying the founding of Samkhya to the cosmic dawn _(actors: Ishvara, Kapila)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/svetashvatara-upanishad.md) — (Shvetashvatara Upanishad 5.2)
- **Hamsa Avatara Instructs the Four Kumaras** — Vishnu's swan-avatara Hamsa reveals the doctrine to the four Kumaras, the origin myth of the Kumara/Sanakadi Sampradaya transmitted through Narada to Nimbarka _(actors: Hamsa Bhagavan, the four Kumaras, Narada, Nimbarka)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/four-vaishnava-sampradayas.md) — (vedanta.redzambala; Wikipedia)
- **Heti and Praheti, the first rākṣasas** — The two first-born rākṣasa brothers spring at creation; Praheti turns ascetic while Heti founds the dynasty by marrying _(actors: Heti, Praheti)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rakshasas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Hiranyagarbha arises as sole lord** — A golden germ arises in the beginning as the sole lord of all, floating on the primordial waters and becoming the cosmic egg / source of the world _(actors: Hiranyagarbha, Prajapati)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Rigveda 10.121)
- **Hiranyagarbha — the Golden Womb arises** — A golden germ (Hiranyagarbha) arises in the beginning as sole lord, floating on the primeval waters and becoming the cosmic egg / source of the world _(actors: Hiranyagarbha, Prajapati)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Rigveda 10.121)
- **Internalization of the sacrifice** — The outward yajña is reinterpreted as inner meditation, with breath (prāṇa) as the inner fire and body/cosmos mapped onto the altar _(actors: Vedic seers; the meditating sacrificer)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/aranyakas.md) — (Aitareya Āraṇyaka; Taittirīya Āraṇyaka)
- **Invocation of golden, lotus-borne Śrī** — The hymn invokes Agni/Jātavedas to bring Śrī, described as golden-hued (hiraṇya-varṇā), lotus-seated, and elephant-attended _(actors: Śrī–Lakṣmī; Agni/Jātavedas; the worshipper)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/sri-suktam.md) — (Śrī Sūkta 1–5)
- **Śiva Vows Never to Leave Kāśī (Avimukta)** — Śiva installs the liberation-giving liṅga at Kashi and binds himself never to abandon the city, making it Avimukta, the never-forsaken zone outside ordinary time and karma _(actors: Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kashi-varanasi.md) — (Skanda Purana, Kashi-khanda)
- **Kala draws forth the worlds (Kala-sukta)** — In the oldest hymn personifying Time, Kala as a seven-reined horse draws forth the worlds, the waters and even Prajapati, creating heaven and the earths _(actors: Kala (Time))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/kalachakra-wheel-of-time.md) — (Atharvaveda 19.53-54)
- **Kaśyapa among the Saptarṣi** — Kaśyapa is counted among the Seven Sages presiding over the current Vaivasvata Manvantara _(actors: Kaśyapa, the Saptarṣi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kashyapa.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.1)
- **Ṛk-Prātiśākhya composed** — Śaunaka's verse Prātiśākhya for the Śākala branch of the Ṛgveda, stating rules deriving the saṃhitā from Śākalya's padapāṭha _(actors: Śaunaka (ascribed); Śākala/Śaiśirīya school)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/pratishakhyas.md) — (Ṛk-Prātiśākhya (Śaunaka))
- **Madhu and Kaiṭabha slain through the Goddess** — At the dawn of creation the demons Madhu and Kaiṭabha menace Brahmā on the lotus; Brahmā hymns the Goddess as Yoganidrā, who withdraws from Viṣṇu and wakes him, enabling the demons' slaying _(actors: Madhu, Kaiṭabha, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the Goddess)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/devi-bhagavata-upapurana.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata, skandha I)
- **Madhu and Kaitabha arise from Vishnu's ear** — While Vishnu lies in Yoganidra on Shesha at the end of a cosmic cycle, the asuras Madhu and Kaitabha arise from his ears and move to kill Brahma on the navel-lotus _(actors: Madhu, Kaitabha, Vishnu, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-mahatmya-and-the-great-goddess.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 1)
- **Marīci begets Kaśyapa** — Marīci by Kalā (daughter of Kardama) fathers Kaśyapa, becoming the genealogical apex and grandfather of devas, asuras and nearly all beings _(actors: Marīci; Kalā; Kaśyapa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-mind-born-seers.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.10; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1)
- **Marriages to Khyāti and Pulomā** — Bhṛgu weds Khyāti (mother of Śrī and Dhātṛ/Vidhātṛ) and Pulomā (mother of Cyavana) _(actors: Bhṛgu, Khyāti, Pulomā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhrigu.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.10; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 5–6)
- **Mind-Born Daughters of the Pitṛs** — Each Pitṛ-class generates a mind-born daughter — Menā (mother of Pārvatī and Gaṅgā), Acchodā, Narmadā — seeding the river- and mountain-genealogies of the cosmos _(actors: Vairājas, Menā, Acchodā, Narmadā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/pitrs-and-ancestors.md) — (Vāyu, Brahmāṇḍa, Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Narada praises Patala over Svarga** — Returning from the nether regions, the sage Narada tells the gods that Patala is far more delightful than Indra's heaven, the canonical statement of the inversion doctrine _(actors: Narada, the devas)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/bila-svarga-and-the-patalas.md) — (Vishnu Purana 2.5 (Wilson))
- **Nāsadīya creation-mystery hymn** — The Ṛgvedic creation hymn contemplates the primordial state before being and non-being, framing the cosmos's emergence from neither existence nor non-existence → [details](90-literature-corpus/shruti-vedas-and-upanishads.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.129 (Nāsadīya Sūkta))
- **Origin of Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya within the Namakam** — The Namakam line 'namaḥ śivāya ca śivatarāya ca' supplies the Vedic seed of the five-syllabled Pañcākṣara mantra Oṃ Namaḥ Śivāya _(actors: Rudra–Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/sri-rudram-namakam-chamakam.md) — (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.5; Pañcākṣara tradition)
- **Parvati's Flood-Embrace of the Earth-Linga** — Shiva looses a flood to wash away Parvati's sand-linga; she embraces it with her whole body to shield it, leaving the imprint of her bangles, and a pleased Shiva marries her at Kanchi _(actors: Parvati, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-bhuta-sthalams.md) — (Ekambareswarar mahatmya)
- **Per-Varsha Avatara Worship Established in Jambudvipa** — Each of the nine varshas of Jambudvipa becomes the eternal heaven where a specific avatara (Hayagriva, Matsya, Kurma, Nrsimha, Varaha, Rama, Nara-Narayana) is worshipped by a chief devotee _(actors: avatara forms, Prahlada, Hanuman, Narada)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/bharatavarsha-and-puranic-geography.md) — (Bhagavata Purana canto 5.16-19)
- **Prajapati equated with the sacrifice and the year** — The PB identifies Prajapati with the sacrifice and the year; the year-sattra restores his dismembered body through chant _(actors: Prajapati)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/panchavimsha-brahmana.md) — (Panchavimsha (Tandya Maha-) Brahmana)
- **Prakriti unfolds the 23 evolutes (Samkhya emanation)** — Disturbed from equilibrium by Purusha's mere proximity, Prakriti evolves in fixed sequence into Mahat, ahamkara, manas, the eleven indriyas, the five tanmatras and the five gross elements — the cosmogonic emanation of the manifest world _(actors: Prakriti, Purusha)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/the-samkhya-tattvas.md) — (Samkhya-Karika 3, 22-25, 38)
- **Proto-karma reciprocity (the dead weighed and requited)** — JB passages on requital between this world and the next furnish one of the earliest pre-Upaniṣadic intimations of retributive reciprocity, a conceptual seed of karma _(actors: the dead, the gods)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/jaiminiya-brahmana.md) — (Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa)
- **Purañjana finds the City of Nine Gates** — The wandering king Purañjana (the embodied soul), accompanied by an unknown friend (Paramātman) he never recognizes, discovers a splendid nine-gated city (the body) in the Himālayan foothills _(actors: Purañjana (jīva), the Unknown Friend (Paramātman))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/puranjana-allegory.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.25.10–22)
- **Revelation of the tāraka (Rāma) mantra** — The two-syllable name Rāma is declared the tāraka that ferries souls across saṃsāra, grounding the Vārāṇasī death-bed tāraka tradition _(actors: Rāma, Śiva (Kāśī tradition), the dying devotee)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/ramatapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Rāma-tāpanī Up., Pūrva; Kāśī tāraka tradition)
- **Samjna Flees the Sun and Leaves Chhaya** — Samjna/Saranyu, unable to bear the Sun's heat, flees and leaves her shadow-double Chhaya in her place; Chhaya becomes mother of the future 8th Manu Savarni by Surya _(actors: Samjna/Saranyu; Chhaya; Surya/Vivasvan)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-08-savarni.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.2; Bhagavata Purana 8.13.1)
- **Sati weds Shiva against Daksha's will** — Sati performs tapas to win the ascetic Shiva and marries him, deepening Daksha's resentment of the cremation-ground bridegroom _(actors: Sati, Shiva, Daksha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana, Bhagavata Purana IV.2-4)
- **Surabhi Born from Dakṣa's Belch** — After Dakṣa drinks the churned amṛta, Surabhi is born from his belch, and from her spring the golden Kapilā cows, mothers of the world _(actors: Dakṣa, Surabhi)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/kamadhenu-and-divine-cattle.md) — (Mahābhārata Anuśāsana Parva)
- **Surabhi emanates from Kṛṣṇa in Goloka** — The wish-cow Surabhi/Kāmadhenu emanates from Kṛṣṇa in Goloka, grounding cow-worship and the cowherd cosmology _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Surabhi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmavaivarta-purana.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa (Brahma-khaṇḍa))
- **The agnicayana tortoise identified with Prajapati** — In the Vedic fire-altar rite a living tortoise is laid in the altar and identified with Prajapati the creator, the pre-Vishnu layer of the kurma motif _(actors: Prajapati, the ritual tortoise)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kurma-avatara.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana 7.5.1)
- **The Atharvaveda deifies Prana** — Atharvaveda 11.4 glorifies Prana as a cosmic deity, lord of all that breathes, present in wind, rain, trees and foetus — the earliest extended deification of breath as cosmic power _(actors: Prana)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/prana-and-the-vital-airs.md) — (Atharvaveda 11.4)
- **The exhausted Prajāpati restored by sacrifice** — Having emitted creation Prajāpati collapses, disjointed, and is re-membered and restored through the fire-altar sacrifice, which thereby sustains the cosmos _(actors: Prajāpati, Agni, the sacrificers)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/taittiriya-brahmana.md) — (Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 2; Śatapatha parallels)
- **The failed first creation: the four Kumaras refuse to procreate** — Brahma's first mind-sons, the four Kumaras, choose eternal childhood and celibacy, forcing Brahma to emit the procreating Prajapatis _(actors: Brahma, Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana, Sanatkumara)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.12.4-7; Vishnu Purana 1.7)
- **Theft of the Vedas** — At the dawn of the cycle the demons seize/scatter the Vedas, leaving Brahmā unable to begin creation _(actors: Madhu, Kaiṭabha, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/hayagriva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 2.7)
- **The Goddess Declares 'I Am Brahman'** — The Goddess answers in the first person 'ahaṃ brahma-svarūpiṇī' — I am of the nature of Brahman, from me proceed prakṛti and puruṣa, void and plenum _(actors: Mahādevī (Devī))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/devi-upanishad.md) — (Devī Upaniṣad v.2)
- **The Kumāras refuse to procreate** — As naiṣṭhika-brahmacārins fixed on mokṣa, the four decline Brahmā's command to beget offspring, the 'failed' first creation _(actors: Brahmā; the four Kumāras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-four-kumaras.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12.4–5)
- **The pantheon and praṇava collapsed into Gaṇeśa** — Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Indra, Agni, Vāyu, Sūrya, the Moon, the three worlds and Oṃ are all predicated of Gaṇeśa as the one reality _(actors: Gaṇeśa, the Trimūrti and Vedic gods)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/ganapati-atharvashirsha-upanishad.md) — (Gaṇapaty-atharvaśīrṣa Upaniṣad 2)
- **The prodigious growth of the fish** — The fish outgrows jar, pit, ground, and sea, revealing its supernatural nature _(actors: Manu, the fish)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/matsya-pralaya.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1; Mahābhārata Vana Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.24)
- **The triple-mother river triad** — RV 10.64.9 invokes Sarasvatī, Sarayū and Sindhu together as 'great mothers' summoned to the sacrifice _(actors: the ṛṣis; Sarasvatī, Sarayū, Sindhu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sapta-sindhu-and-the-indus-rivers.md) — (Ṛg Veda 10.64.9)
- **Vaiṣṇava counter — Narasiṃha as Gaṇḍabheruṇḍa** — Vaiṣṇava traditions reverse the outcome, with Narasiṃha taking the two-headed eagle Gaṇḍabheruṇḍa form to prevail over Śiva's Śarabha — a sectarian flashpoint _(actors: Narasiṃha (Viṣṇu, as Gaṇḍabheruṇḍa), Śarabha (Śiva))_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/mythic-beasts-and-composites.md) — (Vaiṣṇava Purāṇic & āgamic counter-traditions)
- **Varaha and Hamsa Seek the Pillar's Ends** — Vishnu descends as the boar Varaha to find the pillar's base and Brahma ascends on his swan to find its top, but neither reaches an end of the infinite linga _(actors: Vishnu (Varaha), Brahma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/12-jyotirlingas.md) — (Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Vishnu Stations the Dvādaśa Mādhava to Guard the Sangam** — At Brahma's yajna, Vishnu stations himself in twelve Madhava forms around the Prayaga kshetra to perpetually guard the confluence _(actors: Vishnu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/prayagraj-triveni-sangam.md) — (Matsya Purana; Padma Purana; Agni Purana)
- **Vāyu Hides Maināka in the Ocean** — Vāyu spirits away his friend Maināka and hides him in the ocean, so Maināka alone among mountains keeps his wings _(actors: Vayu, Mainaka)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/meru-kailash-and-cosmic-mountains.md) — (Brahmanda Purana; Kathasaritsagara)
- **Yama, the First Mortal to Die** — Yama becomes the first human to die, treading the path to the afterlife and so becoming lord and guide of the dead, welcoming souls to a sunlit Svarga _(actors: Yama)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yama.md) — (Rig Veda 10.14; Atharva Veda 18)
- **Aṅgiras seated among the Saptarṣi** — Aṅgiras takes his place among the Seven Sages, an office that recurs across manvantaras _(actors: Aṅgiras, the Saptarṣi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/angiras.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.1)
- **Agrarian fertility imagery and the children of Śrī** — Śrī is praised as moist and dung-rich (ārdrā, karīṣiṇī) and her sons Kardama, Ciklīta, and Ānanda are invited into the household _(actors: Śrī–Lakṣmī; Kardama; Ciklīta; Ānanda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/sri-suktam.md) — (Śrī Sūkta 9–12)
- **Bhairava severs Brahma's fifth head** — Shiva as Mahakala emanates Bhairava, who severs Brahma's arrogant fifth head with a thumbnail and is condemned to wander as Kapalika bearing the skull until released at Kashi _(actors: Bhairava (Shiva), Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Shiva Purana; Skanda Purana Kashi Khanda)
- **Brahma hymns Yoganidra to wake Vishnu** — Unable to wake Vishnu, Brahma praises the goddess Yoganidra/Mahamaya (the Brahma-stuti), begging her to withdraw so Vishnu can rouse _(actors: Brahma, Yoganidra, Vishnu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-mahatmya-and-the-great-goddess.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 1.73-87)
- **Brahmā and the Śatarūpā incest, cursed by Śiva** — Smitten by the goddess Śatarūpā he created, Brahmā grows extra heads to keep gazing at her, for which Śiva curses him to lack worship, explaining his absence of temples _(actors: Brahmā, Śatarūpā, Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/trimurti-and-tridevi.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa; Brahmā Purāṇa)
- **Brahma's Lie and Shiva's Curse on Brahma and the Ketaki** — Brahma falsely claims to have reached the summit using a ketaki flower as witness, and an enraged Shiva curses Brahma to have no worship and bars the ketaki flower from his worship while blessing the honest Vishnu _(actors: Brahma, Shiva, Vishnu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/12-jyotirlingas.md) — (Shiva Purana)
- **Brahmā's anger and the cascade of creation** — Frustrated by the refusal, Brahmā's wrath births Rudra from his brow and he emits the procreating Prajāpatis who carry creation forward _(actors: Brahmā; Rudra; the Prajāpatis (Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, etc.))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-four-kumaras.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12.4–7, 3.12.21–27)
- **Construction of the gaṇa-bīja mūla-mantra 'gaṃ'** — The text builds the Gaṇapati root-mantra by phonetic exegesis (ga + anusvāra + bindu, crowned with Oṃ), enshrining 'gaṃ' / 'oṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ' as Gaṇeśa's sound-body _(actors: Gaṇaka ṛṣi (tradition), Gaṇeśa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/ganapati-atharvashirsha-upanishad.md) — (Gaṇapaty-atharvaśīrṣa Upaniṣad 3)
- **Dakṣiṇāmūrti teaches the Kumāras in silence** — Śiva as the south-facing supreme guru expounds jñāna, yoga, and śāstra wordlessly through the cinmudrā to the four aged Kumāras, teaching ultimate truth through silence _(actors: Śiva, the four Kumāras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Śaṅkara's Dakṣiṇāmūrti Stotra)
- **Deity-as-Brahman identification (the shared thesis)** — Each sectarian Upaniṣad identifies its chosen deity (Viṣṇu, Śiva, or Devī) with the impersonal Brahman of the mukhya Upaniṣads _(actors: Viṣṇu / Śiva / Devī as Brahman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/vaishnava-shaiva-shakta-upanishads-overview.md) — (Vaiṣṇava, Śaiva, Śākta Upaniṣads passim)
- **Divine contest-myths and the seizing of soma** — Indra's exploits, the gods' quarrels with the Asuras, races and wagers, and the purchase/seizing of soma are told as etiologies attached to particular sāmans _(actors: Indra, the Devas, the Asuras)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/jaiminiya-brahmana.md) — (Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa)
- **Exposition of the Rāma ṣaḍakṣara** — The six-syllabled Rāma mantra built on the bīja rāṃ is given as the mūla-mantra of Rāma worship with its ṛṣi, chandas, devatā and ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa _(actors: Rāma, the worshipper)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/ramatapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Rāma-tāpanī Up., Pūrva)
- **Gayatri's flight for Soma** — The metre Gayatri takes bird-form and flies to heaven to seize Soma for the gods, bringing the soma-draught to earth _(actors: Gayatri (metre as bird), Soma, the gods)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/panchavimsha-brahmana.md) — (Panchavimsha Brahmana (and parallel Brahmanas))
- **Goddess Pratyaṅgirā/Śūlinī aids in quelling Narasiṃha** — The lion-faced goddess Pratyaṅgirā (Śūlinī Durgā) emerges from or fights alongside Śarabha to subdue Narasiṃha and is invoked in counter-sorcery _(actors: Pratyaṅgirā/Śūlinī, Śarabha (Śiva), Narasiṃha)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/mythic-beasts-and-composites.md) — (Kālikā Purāṇa; Tantric/āgamic Pratyaṅgirā traditions)
- **Hiranyagarbha golden egg splits into heaven and earth** — The golden womb-egg floats on the primordial waters for a cosmic year before splitting into heaven and earth, the Vedic antecedent of the Puranic Brahmanda _(actors: Hiranyagarbha)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahmanda-and-bhuvana-kosha.md) — (Rigveda 10.121; Manusmriti 1.5-13)
- **Indra releases the seven rivers** — Indra slays the serpent Vṛtra and frees the pent waters, setting loose the cosmic sapta sindhavaḥ — the seven rivers that double as the Punjab streams _(actors: Indra; Vṛtra; the seven rivers)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sapta-sindhu-and-the-indus-rivers.md) — (Ṛg Veda 1.32; 2.12)
- **Lakṣmī Becomes the Badrī Tree to Shelter Vishnu** — While Vishnu does austere tapas exposed to Himalayan cold, Lakshmi transforms into a badri (jujube) tree to shade him, giving Badrinath its name Badri-ka-ashrama _(actors: Vishnu, Lakshmi)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-kedar-pancha-badri.md) — (Skanda Purana (Badari-mahatmya))
- **Manu finds the fish (Matsya)** — Manu Vaivasvata finds a tiny fish in his washing water; the fish begs protection and promises to save him from a coming flood _(actors: Manu Vaivasvata, the fish (matsya))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/shatapatha-brahmana.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1.1–4)
- **Marriage of Heti and Bhayā** — Heti weds Bhayā, sister of Kāla (Time/Death), begetting Vidyutkeśa and continuing the rākṣasa line _(actors: Heti, Bhayā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rakshasas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Marriage to Dakṣa's thirteen daughters** — Dakṣa gives thirteen daughters (Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadru, Vinatā and others) to Kaśyapa, whose wombs become the matrix of every species _(actors: Dakṣa, Kaśyapa, his thirteen wives)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kashyapa.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.15; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 65)
- **Marriage to Queen Purañjanī** — At the seventh gate Purañjana meets and weds Purañjanī (buddhi/intelligence), guarded by a five-hooded serpent (prāṇa) and served by eleven attendants (ten senses plus the mind) _(actors: Purañjana, Queen Purañjanī (buddhi), the serpent (prāṇa), eleven senses/mind)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/puranjana-allegory.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.25.20–57)
- **Matsya preaches the Matsya Purāṇa to Manu** — At the start of the kalpa the fish-avatāra Matsya preaches the Matsya Purāṇa to Manu, making the deluge a frame for revelation itself _(actors: Matsya (Viṣṇu), Manu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/agni-purana.md) — (Agni Purāṇa)
- **Naciketas given to Yama (Death)** — The father Vājaśravasa, in anger during an all-goods sacrifice, consigns his son Naciketas to Yama; the boy goes to the house of Death _(actors: Naciketas, Vājaśravasa (Auddālaki Āruṇi), Yama)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/taittiriya-brahmana.md) — (Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 3.11.8)
- **Nārāyaṇa-anuvāka proclaims Nārāyaṇa as supreme Brahman** — The Nārāyaṇa Sūkta hails the thousand-headed Nārāyaṇa as the cosmic Self (viśvātman) and supreme refuge, the Vedic root of Vaiṣṇava-supremacy theology _(actors: Nārāyaṇa; reciting sages)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mahanarayana-upanishad.md) — (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad, Nārāyaṇa-anuvāka; cf. Ṛgveda 10.90 (Puruṣa-sūkta))
- **Prakṛti divides into the five primary goddesses** — On Kṛṣṇa's will Prakṛti divides into Rādhā, Durgā, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, and Sāvitrī, each assigned a cosmic office, with all other goddesses their portions _(actors: Prakṛti, Rādhā, Durgā, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Sāvitrī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmavaivarta-purana.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa (Prakṛti-khaṇḍa))
- **Pulastya begets Viśravas** — Pulastya fathers Viśravas, the hinge from which the Yakṣa (Kubera) and Rākṣasa (Rāvaṇa) dynasties branch _(actors: Pulastya; Viśravas; (Tṛṇabindu's daughter))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-mind-born-seers.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.8)
- **Purusha Sukta — creation by cosmic sacrifice** — The gods dismember the cosmic Man Purusha in a primal yajna, and from his parts arise the moon, sun, Indra, Agni, Vayu, the worlds, and the four varnas _(actors: Purusha, the gods)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Rigveda 10.90)
- **Rudra saluted as immanent in all beings and trades** — The middle anuvākas of the Namakam hail Rudra as present in every place, person, and profession — forests, paths, thieves, householders, artisans, hunters _(actors: Rudra–Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/sri-rudram-namakam-chamakam.md) — (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.5.2–9)
- **Saraswati's manifestation on Vasant Panchami** — Brahma brings forth Saraswati to give voice, melody, and order to a silent creation, honored on Magha Shukla Panchami as her birthday/appearance _(actors: Saraswati, Brahma)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Puranic tradition; Wikipedia (Vasant Panchami))
- **Sati's self-immolation at the Daksha-yajna** — Publicly humiliated by Daksha, who reviles Shiva at his great sacrifice, Sati renounces her body in yogic fire _(actors: Sati, Daksha, Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Bhagavata Purana IV.4, Shiva Purana)
- **Serpent-gems illuminate the sunless caverns** — Though sun and moon do not reach below the earth, the gem-crests on the hoods of the great Nagas (Vasuki and kin) dispel all darkness, giving constant light without day or night _(actors: Vasuki, the Nagas)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/bila-svarga-and-the-patalas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.24.9-10)
- **Shiva descends into matter (36-tattva emanation)** — In Kashmir Shaiva cosmogony a single divine consciousness Shiva, through Shakti, Sadashiva, Ishvara, Shuddhavidya, then Maya and the five kanchukas, contracts and descends into the individuated soul and the 24 tattvas of matter — the self-display of one consciousness as the universe _(actors: Shiva, Shakti)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/the-samkhya-tattvas.md) — (Tantraloka; Malinivijaya; Svacchanda Tantra)
- **Shiva severs Brahma's fifth head** — Condemning Brahma's pursuit of his own daughter, Shiva severs Brahma's fifth head _(actors: Shiva, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saraswati.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Soma's abduction of Tara and the Tarakamaya war** — Soma, swollen with pride after his Rajasuya, carries off Tara wife of Brihaspati, sparking the Tarakamaya war until Brahma forces her return; Tara then bears Budha, founder of the Lunar dynasty _(actors: Soma (Candra), Tara, Brihaspati, Shukra, Brahma, Budha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/matsya-purana.md) — (Matsya Purana (adhyaya 24))
- **Supremacy of the Brahman priest** — Argues the four chief priests culminate in the Brahman, who oversees and corrects the rite; a sacrifice without a true Brahman fails as 'one-winged.' _(actors: Brahman priest, Hotṛ, Udgātṛ, Adhvaryu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/gopatha-brahmana.md) — (Gopatha Brāhmaṇa Pūrvabhāga)
- **Surabhi Granted Goloka by Brahmā** — After ten thousand years of austerities to Brahmā at Kailāsa, Surabhi is made a goddess, decreed worthy of universal worship, and granted the cow-heaven Goloka _(actors: Surabhi, Brahmā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/kamadhenu-and-divine-cattle.md) — (Mahābhārata Anuśāsana Parva)
- **Sāvitrī's Curse on Brahmā** — Finding another woman in her ritual seat, the enraged Savitri curses Brahma to be worshipped nowhere in the universe (and curses the attendant gods), explaining Brahma's near-total absence from temples _(actors: Savitri, Brahma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pushkar-brahma-tirtha.md) — (Padma Purana (Pushkar-mahatmya))
- **Taittirīya-Prātiśākhya composed** — Phonetic manual in 24 chapters governing recitation of the Black Yajurveda's Taittirīya Saṃhitā _(actors: Taittirīya school of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/pratishakhyas.md) — (Taittirīya-Prātiśākhya)
- **The anatomy of the figure — planets and asterisms as limbs** — Sun, Moon, the five planets, Rāhu, the Aśvins, the nakṣatras and Nārāyaṇa (as the heart) are mapped onto specific limbs of the dolphin, with variant assignments in the Viṣṇu Purāṇa _(actors: the Navagraha, nakṣatra-deities, Nārāyaṇa, Yama/Mṛtyu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/shishumara-chakra.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.23.5-8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.9)
- **The Goddess as Source and Substrate of the Pantheon** — The Goddess enumerates herself as the all-gods — moving with the Rudras, Vasus, Ādityas and All-gods, bringing forth Heaven, bending Rudra's bow _(actors: Devī (as Vāc/Mahāśakti), the Vedic gods)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/devi-upanishad.md) — (Devī Upaniṣad v.3–7; Ṛgveda 10.125 (Devī-Sūkta / Vāk-Sūkta))
- **The Kumaras' curse on Jaya and Vijaya** — Barred from Vaikuntha by the gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya, the Kumaras curse them to three demonic births, engine of three Vishnu avatars _(actors: the four Kumaras, Jaya, Vijaya)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.15-16, 7.1)
- **The Mahāvrata rite expounded** — The great one-day Soma rite of the year-long Gavāmayana sattra is given esoteric exposition in the Rigvedic Āraṇyakas _(actors: Hotṛ priests; sattra participants)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/aranyakas.md) — (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 1; Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka 1–2)
- **The swan's reply on the one Self** — The swan answers that the question 'who are you?' is empty since the Self is one in all beings; any posited difference is unreal, all being made of the same elements _(actors: Viṣṇu as Haṃsa, the Four Kumāras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/hamsa-avatar.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.13.22-24)
- **Varāha emerges from Brahmā's nostril** — A thumb-sized boar issues from Brahmā's nostril and swells into a colossal cosmic form, hailed by the ṛṣis with Vedic hymns _(actors: Viṣṇu as Varāha, Brahmā, the gods and sages)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/varaha-hiranyaksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.13.18–34)
- **Viṣṇu assumes the Hayagrīva form** — Viṣṇu takes the horse-headed Hayagrīva/Hayaśiras descent to recover the Vedas and destroy the Madhu-class demons _(actors: Viṣṇu as Hayagrīva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/hayagriva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 2.7)
- **Viṣṇu speaks the Catuh-sloki to Brahma** — Viṣṇu speaks the four-verse seed of the Bhagavata to Brahma, the cosmogonic teaching treated as the text in miniature _(actors: Viṣṇu, Brahma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 2.9.33-36)
- **Wager of Kadrū and Vinatā; Vinatā Enslaved** — The sisters bet on the color of Uccaiḥśravas's tail; Kadrū's nāga sons blacken it by deceit, Vinatā loses the wager and becomes Kadrū's slave, rooting Garuḍa's hatred of serpents _(actors: Kadrū, Vinatā, nāgas, Uccaiḥśravas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/garuda.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Warning of the pralaya and order to build a boat** — The grown fish foretells the world-ending deluge and bids Manu build a ship and embark _(actors: the fish, Manu/Satyavrata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/matsya-pralaya.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1; Mahābhārata Vana Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.24)
- **Yama-Yami Dialogue and Rejected Union** — Yami proposes incestuous union with her twin Yama to propagate humankind, but Yama refuses on grounds of dharma, staging moral restraint winning over desire at humanity's origin _(actors: Yama, Yami)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yama.md) — (Rig Veda 10.10)
- **A hundred years of sense-enjoyment** — Purañjana lives ruled by his queen's moods, hunting and indulging the senses for a hundred years, forgetful of his eternal friend and his own nature _(actors: Purañjana, Purañjanī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/puranjana-allegory.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.25.62–4.26)
- **Atharvan and Angiras Hear the Atharvaveda at the Cosmic Dawn** — By the scripture clock, the rishis Atharvan, Angiras (and Bhrigu) 'hear' the eternal Atharvaveda — the twin streams of healing and aggressive magic — at the dawn of the cosmic order _(actors: Atharvan, Angiras, Bhrigu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/atharvaveda.md) — (Atharvaveda Samhita)
