- **Anasūyā's Trimūrti humbled** — Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva come to break Anasūyā's chastity-vow and are turned to infants, the tri-unity that the Sucīndram māhātmya reads as the origin of its one-liṅga-three-gods form _(actors: Anasūyā, Atri, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/suchindram-sthanumalayan.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; Sucīndra-sthala-māhātmya)
- **Aṅga Abandons the Throne over Vena** — King Aṅga weds Sunīthā, daughter of Death, whose evil grandson Vena is born; despairing of his wicked son, Aṅga abandons the throne for the forest _(actors: Aṅga, Sunīthā, Vena)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.13; Vishnu Purana 1.13)
- **Ajāmila's fall and life of sin** — The virtuous brāhmaṇa Ajāmila is ruined by lust for a dāsī, abandons his wife and dharma, and lives by theft and deceit, naming his youngest son Nārāyaṇa _(actors: Ajāmila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ajamila.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.1)
- **Atri and Anasūyā's austerity for a divine son** — The sage Atri and his wife Anasūyā perform severe tapas seeking a son equal to the Supreme, and the Trimūrti grant that portions of all three will be born to them _(actors: Atri, Anasūyā, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Avatar Satyasena destroys the evil spirits** — Vishnu's avatar Satyasena, born of Sunrita and Dharma, destroys the Yakshas, Rakshasas and lying bhutas, fighting beside Indra Satyajit _(actors: Satyasena, Sunrita, Dharma, Indra Satyajit)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-03-uttama.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.1.25)
- **Avatar Vaikuntha creates the realm of Vaikuntha** — Vishnu's avatar Vaikuntha, born of his own accord, creates his eternal abode Vaikuntha at the request of his consort Rama (Lakshmi) _(actors: Vaikuntha (Vishnu), Rama (Lakshmi))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5)
- **Bahulā recovered from the Nāga world; birth of Manu Auttama** — the mute Nāga princess Nandā, her speech restored by a Sarasvatī rite, blesses Uttama with a son who becomes the 3rd Manu, Auttama _(actors: Bahulā, Nāga princess Nandā, sage Garga, Manu Auttama)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/markandeya-manvantara-origin-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa LXXII)
- **Betrothal of Ruru and Pramadvarā** — The Bhārgava youth Ruru is betrothed to Pramadvarā, foundling daughter of the apsarā Menakā reared by sage Sthūlakeśa, and a wedding-day is fixed _(actors: Ruru, Pramadvarā, Pramati, Sthūlakeśa, Menakā, Viśvāvasu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ruru-pramadvara.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva (~1.8–12))
- **Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest, origin of the Śrīvatsa mark** — The sage Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu on the chest to test which of the three gods is greatest (the trimūrti-test). Far from angered, Viṣṇu honours and embraces the foot-mark; the auspicious whorl left on his breast becomes the Śrīvatsa, and Lakṣmī (Śrī), born of the milk-ocean, takes her seat there _(actors: Bhṛgu, Viṣṇu, Lakṣmī/Śrī)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-symbols-and-emblems.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.89)
- **Birth of Andhaka from Parvati's covering of Shiva's eyes** — Parvati playfully covers Shiva's three eyes, plunging the cosmos into darkness; a drop of her sweat becomes the blind, deformed boy Andhaka _(actors: Parvati, Shiva, Andhaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/andhakasura-vadha.md) — (Shiva Purana (Rudra-samhita); Matsya Purana; Kurma Purana)
- **Birth of Cyavana** — The Rākṣasa Puloman abducts the pregnant Pulomā, and the unborn Bhārgava child slips prematurely from the womb (hence 'Cyavana'), his radiance burning the Rākṣasa to ashes _(actors: Bhṛgu, Pulomā, Puloman, Cyavana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 5–6)
- **Birth of Jalandhara from Shiva's brow-fire** — The fire from Shiva's opened third eye is cast into the ocean and gestated into the asura Jalandhara _(actors: Shiva, Indra, Brahma, Samudra (ocean), Jalandhara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jalandhara-vrinda.md) — (Shiva Purana (Rudra-samhita, Yuddha-khanda))
- **Birth of Kakshivat from the substituted nurse** — Queen Sudeshna sends her shudra nurse to the blind sage in her place, and on her Dirghatamas begets eleven brahmin sons headed by the future rishi Kakshivat (Aushija) _(actors: Dirghatamas, Sudeshna, the dasi nurse, Kakshivat)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dirghatamas.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva ~104; Rigveda 1.116-126)
- **Birth of Kapila to Kardama and Devahuti** — Viṣṇu descends as the son of the patriarch Kardama and Devahūti in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara to teach Sāṃkhya-yoga _(actors: Kardama, Devahūti, Kapila (Viṣṇu avatāra), Svāyambhuva Manu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kapila-devahuti.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.22–24, 1.3.10)
- **Birth of Rishabhadeva from Merudevi** — King Nabhi and Merudevi perform a sacrifice longing for a son, and Vishnu descends, born as Rishabha (the bull), counted an avatara of Narayana _(actors: Nabhi, Merudevi, Vishnu/Rishabhadeva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.3; Vishnu Purana 2.1)
- **Birth of the avatar Vaikuntha** — In the Raivata Manvantara Vishnu manifests of his own accord as Lord Vaikuntha, born together with the deva-class called Vaikunthas _(actors: Vaikuntha, the Vaikuntha gods, Rama (Lakshmi))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5)
- **Birth of Vaivasvata Manu** — Vaivasvata, the 7th and current Manu, is born of Surya (Vivasvat) and Saranyu/Chhaya, becoming the present progenitor of humankind _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Surya, Saranyu/Chhaya)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.2; Bhagavata Purana 8.13)
- **Birth of Viśravas from Pulastya** — The rākṣasa line descends from Brahmā's mind-born son Pulastya, whose circumstance at Tṛṇabindu's hermitage produces the sage Viśravas _(actors: Pulastya, Viśravas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 2–3)
- **Birth of Yajña and Dakṣiṇā to Ākūti and Ruci** — Viṣṇu descends as the twin Yajña (a portion of Viṣṇu) alongside his sister-consort Dakṣiṇā, born to Ākūti (daughter of Svāyambhuva Manu) and the Prajāpati Ruci _(actors: Viṣṇu (as Yajña), Dakṣiṇā, Ākūti, Ruci, Svāyambhuva Manu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yajna-avatara.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.3.10, 4.1.4–7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **Brahma to Vaivasvata Manu Descent** — The cosmological spine runs Brahma to Marichi to Kashyapa to Vivasvan (Surya) to Vaivasvata Manu, whose children fork into the two royal dynasties _(actors: Brahma, Kashyapa, Surya, Vaivasvata Manu)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV; Bhagavata Purana IX)
- **Chakshusha Manu's previous-birth as Ananda** — Before becoming the sixth Manu, the future Chakshusha lives as Ananda, switched at birth by a cat into a royal household, and on learning the truth withdraws to the forest for tapas, whereupon Brahma blesses him to be reborn as Manu _(actors: Ananda/Chakshusha, Anamitra, King Vikranta, Brahma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Markandeya Purana; Puranic Encyclopaedia)
- **Daṇḍa violates Arajā** — Ikṣvāku's son Daṇḍa, king at Madhumanta, ravishes Arajā the daughter of Śukrācārya in the forest near the sage's hermitage _(actors: Daṇḍa, Arajā, Śukrācārya (Uśanas Kāvya))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dandakaranya-rama-forest.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 79–81)
- **Dadhīci teaches the Madhu-vidyā through a horse's head** — To evade Indra's curse, the Aśvins fit Dadhyañc with a horse's head so he can teach them the honey-doctrine, then restore his own head _(actors: Dadhīci (Dadhyañc), the Aśvins, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dadhichi.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2.5; Ṛgveda 1.116–117)
- **Daksha's Yajna and Snub of Shiva** — Daksha Prajapati holds a great sacrifice and deliberately omits to invite Shiva and Sati out of contempt for his ascetic son-in-law _(actors: Daksha, Sati, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/51-shakti-peethas.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana VII; Kalika Purana; Mahabhagavata Purana)
- **Descent of the Gomatī from Vasiṣṭha's tapas** — The river-goddess Gomatī is born as the daughter of the brahmarṣi Vasiṣṭha, flowing forth from his tapas to purify the earth; she wells up at the spring-tank Gomat Tāl (Fulhar Jheel) and becomes the river of Naimiṣāraṇya _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, Gomatī (nadī-devatā))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sacred-rivers-and-descent-myths.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.75.6 (Nadīstuti); Gomatī-māhātmya / Skanda Purāṇa; sthala-tradition)
- **Dhruva is slighted by his stepmother and vows penance** — The boy-prince Dhruva, pushed from his father's lap by queen Suruci's scorn, resolves to win the highest station and leaves for the forest _(actors: Dhruva, Suruci, Sunīti, Uttānapāda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.11)
- **Dirghatamas cast into the Ganga and rescued by King Bali** — Expelled by his wife Pradveshi and sons over the go-dharma scandal, the blind sage is set adrift on a raft, survives the dasa Traitana's attack, and is found and honoured by the eastern king Bali _(actors: Dirghatamas, Pradveshi, Traitana, King Bali, the Ashvins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dirghatamas.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva ~104; Rigveda 1.158.4-5; Brihaddevata 4)
- **Dirghatamas consecrates Bharata Daushyanti** — The blind seer Dirghatamas Mamateya performs the mahabhisheka royal consecration of Bharata son of Dushyanta, the emperor after whom Bharata-varsha is named _(actors: Dirghatamas, Bharata Daushyanti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dirghatamas.md) — (Aitareya Brahmana 8.23)
- **Founding of Ayodhya by Manu Vaivasvata** — Vaivasvata Manu lays out Ayodhya on the south bank of the Sarayu as the capital of Kosala, founding the Suryavamsha/Ikshvaku city _(actors: Manu Vaivasvata)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ayodhya.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Bala-kanda 1.5; Skanda Purana Ayodhya-mahatmya)
- **Founding of Ayodhyā by Manu Vaivasvata** — Ayodhya, the unconquerable city and Suryavamsha capital, is founded by Manu Vaivasvata himself as one of the oldest cities _(actors: Manu Vaivasvata)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sapta-puri-and-sacred-cities.md) — (Garuda Purana; Valmiki Ramayana)
- **Founding of Videha-Mithilā** — The bodiless king Nimi's churned-out son Mithi founds Mithilā, establishing the Videha/Janaka line that will rule from Janakpur _(actors: Nimi, Mithi, the Janaka dynasty)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/janakpur-mithila-sita-janmabhumi.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla-kāṇḍa 70-71; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Gajendra-moksha** — The elephant-king Gajendra, seized by a crocodile and dragged toward death over a thousand celestial years, surrenders to the Supreme and is rescued by Vishnu, who arrives on Garuda and severs the crocodile with his Sudarshana chakra _(actors: Gajendra, Vishnu (avatar Hari), the crocodile (Huhu), Garuda)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-04-tamasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.2-8.4)
- **Gajendra-moksha (liberation of Gajendra)** — The elephant-king Gajendra, seized by a crocodile, surrenders to the Supreme; Vishnu arrives on Garuda and severs the crocodile with his chakra _(actors: Gajendra, the crocodile (Huhu), Vishnu, Indradyumna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-04-tamasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.2-8.4)
- **Gaṇeśa counter-curses Tulasī: an asura husband, then a plant** — Gaṇeśa dooms Tulasī to marry a demon and thereafter become a plant, fixing the destiny fulfilled in the Śaṅkhacūḍa cycle _(actors: Gaṇeśa, Tulasī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tulasi-ganesha-curse.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa, Gaṇapati-khaṇḍa)
- **Gaṇeśa refuses the proposal on ascetic grounds** — Gaṇeśa declines, declaring marriage inimical to tapasyā and rebuking Tulasī as a breaker of meditation _(actors: Gaṇeśa, Tulasī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tulasi-ganesha-curse.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa, Gaṇapati-khaṇḍa)
- **Gaṇeśa tempers the curse with blessing but bars tulasī from his worship** — Propitiated, Gaṇeśa prophesies Tulasī will become the most sacred of plants, dearest to Nārāyaṇa, yet forever unacceptable in Gaṇeśa-pūjā _(actors: Gaṇeśa, Tulasī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tulasi-ganesha-curse.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa, Gaṇapati-khaṇḍa)
- **Ghosha continues the seer-line** — Kakshivat's daughter Ghosha, granddaughter of Dirghatamas, becomes a brahmavadini and seer of the twin Ashvin-hymns RV 10.39-40 _(actors: Ghosha, Kakshivat, the Ashvins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dirghatamas.md) — (Rigveda 10.39-40; Brihaddevata)
- **Jaḍa Bharata relates the parable to the Sauvīra king** — The brāhmaṇa Jaḍa Bharata, pressed into palanquin service, tells the Ṛbhu–Nidāgha story to the king of Sauvīra, who abandons his notion of difference and turns toward liberating knowledge _(actors: Jaḍa Bharata, the king of Sauvīra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ribhu-nidagha-vishnu-purana.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa, II.13–16)
- **Jahnu listed among the sons of Kuru** — Purāṇic rosters place Jahnu as a son of Kuru in the Pauravā throne-line, though son-lists vary by recension _(actors: Jahnu, Kuru)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jahnu.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.19; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.22)
- **Jaratkāru beholds his Pitṛs over the pit** — The celibate ascetic Jaratkāru finds his forefathers hanging head-down over an abyss, their lineage-rope gnawed by the rat of Time because he refuses to beget a son _(actors: Jaratkāru; his Pitṛs (ancestors))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaratkaru-and-manasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Āstīka sub-parva (~1.13–53))
- **Jyāmagha's daughter-in-law and the founding of Vidarbha** — The henpecked exile Jyāmagha declares a captive maiden his daughter-in-law before he has a son; the later-born Vidarbha marries her and founds the Vidarbha cousin-kingdom _(actors: Jyāmagha, Śaibyā, Vidarbha)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/yadava-vamsha.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.12; Bhāgavata IX.23)
- **Jyāmagha's exile to the Narmadā country** — Displaced when his brother Rukmeṣu takes the throne, Jyāmagha departs south, settles on Mount Ṛkṣavat at Mṛttikāvatī, and later takes Śuktimatī _(actors: Jyāmagha, Rukmeṣu)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jyamagha.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa 44; Vāyu Purāṇa; Harivaṃśa)
- **Kacha steals the Mṛtasañjīvanī vidyā** — Bṛhaspati's son Kacha serves Śukra to learn the dead-reviving mantra; killed thrice by the asuras and revived from Śukra's own belly, he masters it _(actors: Kacha, Śukrācārya, Devayānī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 71-72)
- **Kāmodā rises at the churning of the milk-ocean** — Third of four divine maidens (Ramā, Vāruṇī, Kāmodā, Varā) born of the Samudra Manthana, Kāmodā becomes the beloved of Hari, wedded to Viṣṇu in perpetual meditation _(actors: Kāmodā, Ramā, Vāruṇī, Varā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada-purana-ganga-tales.md) — (Nārada Purāṇa, Uttarabhāga 68)
- **Kapila descends and teaches Samkhya to Devahuti** — The sage Kapila, an avatara of Vishnu, descends and expounds the Samkhya tattva-system (the Kapila-gita) to his mother Devahuti, the foundational teaching of the school _(actors: Kapila, Devahuti)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/the-samkhya-tattvas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.25-33)
- **King Uttama banishes Queen Bahulā** — Uttama, son of Uttānapāda, casts his cold queen Bahulā into the forest after she spurns him at court, forfeiting (a rishi warns) all his righteousness _(actors: King Uttama, Queen Bahulā, the rebuking muni)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/markandeya-manvantara-origin-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa LXIX–LXX)
- **Krishna teaches the imperishable yoga to Vivasvan, Manu, and Ikshvaku** — Krishna recounts that at the dawn of the current Manvantara he first taught this imperishable yoga to the sun-god Vivasvan, who told Manu, who told Ikshvaku, a royal-sage lineage later lost and now restored _(actors: Krishna, Vivasvan, Manu, Ikshvaku)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavad-gita/03-to-06-karma-shatka.md) — (Bhagavad Gita 4.1-3)
- **Kubera's penance and Brahma's boons** — Kubera performs severe tapas standing on one leg and Brahma grants him immortality, lordship of all wealth and the nine nidhis, the office of Lokapala of the North, and the Pushpaka vimana _(actors: Kubera, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kubera.md) — (Ramayana; Puranic tradition)
- **Manu delegates the śāstra to Bhṛgu** — having composed the law, Manu teaches it to his mind-born son Bhṛgu, who recites chapters 2–12 to the assembled sages, fixing the code's nested narration _(actors: Svāyambhuva Manu, Bhṛgu, the maharṣis)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/manusmriti-map.md) — (Mānava-Dharmaśāstra 1.58–60)
- **Mṛkaṇḍu's Boon and Choice** — The childless sage Mṛkaṇḍu propitiates Shiva and chooses a virtuous son destined to live only sixteen years over a dull long-lived one _(actors: Mṛkaṇḍu, Marudvatī, Shiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva; Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Nārada liberates the Pracetas** — After ruling as their father wished, the Pracetas hear Nārada's discourse on bhakti as the essence of all duty and attain the Lord's abode _(actors: Nārada, the Pracetas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pracetas-rudra-gita.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.31)
- **Nidāgha attains liberation** — Recognizing his master and receiving the teaching of the one undivided Self, Nidāgha thereafter beholds all beings as non-different from himself and attains final mokṣa _(actors: Nidāgha, Ṛbhu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ribhu-nidagha-vishnu-purana.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa, II.16)
- **Niyoga fathering of Anga, Vanga, Kalinga, Pundra and Suhma** — At childless King Bali's request Dirghatamas begets upon Queen Sudeshna the five sons who become eponyms of the eastern kingdoms _(actors: Dirghatamas, King Bali, Sudeshna, Anga, Vanga, Kalinga)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dirghatamas.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva ~104; Bhagavata Purana 9.23)
- **Penance of Tāraka's sons** — Tārakākṣa, Vidyunmālī, and Kamalākṣa undertake fierce penance to avenge their slain father Tāraka _(actors: Tārakākṣa, Vidyunmālī, Kamalākṣa (sons of Tāraka))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-dahana.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa (Rudra-saṃhitā); Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Pippalāda's revenge pacified** — Dadhīci's tree-reared orphan vows to destroy the gods who cost him his parents, but the mare-demon from Śiva's third eye turns on him and Śiva pacifies him, the fire merging into the Gautamī _(actors: Pippalāda, Śiva, Dadhīci, the pippala trees, Soma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gautami-mahatmya-tales-catalog.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa, Gautamī-māhātmya, vulgate adh. 110)
- **Pravara rejects Varuthini** — The pious brahmana Pravara, stranded in the Himalayas after a flying-paste wears off, is propositioned by the lovesick apsaras Varuthini but refuses her, bound by his vow of one wife _(actors: Pravara, Varuthini)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana)
- **Ṛbhu instructs Nidāgha, who clings to duality** — Ṛbhu imparts the whole of divine knowledge to Nidāgha, son of the Prajāpati Pulastya, yet perceives his disciple remains inwardly attached to duality _(actors: Ṛbhu, Nidāgha, Pulastya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ribhu-nidagha-vishnu-purana.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa, II.15)
- **Ṛbhu's first visit — the meal at Vīranagara** — After a thousand divine years Ṛbhu arrives unrecognized as a guest at Nidāgha's house on the Devikā river and turns each courtesy question about food and dwelling into a lesson that hunger, satisfaction, coming and going do not belong to the omnipresent Self _(actors: Ṛbhu, Nidāgha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ribhu-nidagha-vishnu-purana.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa, II.15)
- **Ṛtavāc pulls the Revatī star from the sky** — cursing his wicked son's birth-nakṣatra, the rishi Ṛtavāc makes the constellation Revatī fall onto Mount Kumuda, which is thereby renamed Raivataka _(actors: rishi Ṛtavāc, the nakṣatra Revatī, Mount Kumuda/Raivataka)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/markandeya-manvantara-origin-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa LXXV)
- **Saraṇyū flees Vivasvat and the substitute is made** — After bearing Vivasvat twin children, Saraṇyū vanishes; the gods fashion a likeness (savarṇā) in her place, on whom the Aśvins are later begotten _(actors: Saraṇyū, Vivasvat, Tvaṣṭṛ)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/surya-and-his-family.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.17.1-2; Nirukta 12.10; Bṛhaddevatā 6.162ff)
- **Ṣaṣṭhī revives Priyavrata's stillborn son** — the goddess reveals herself to the grieving king (son of Svāyambhuva Manu, 1st Manvantara), revives the child Suvrata, and her sixth-day worship is instituted _(actors: Ṣaṣṭhī/Devasenā, Priyavrata, Mālinī, Suvrata)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/gramadevata-shashthi-cross-links.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata, IX.44–47)
- **Sati born as Daksha's daughter** — The Great Goddess consents to be born as a daughter of the Prajapati Daksha, named Sati, specifically to win Shiva as her husband _(actors: Adi Shakti (Sati), Daksha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita Sati Khanda; Devi-Bhagavata Purana VII)
- **Satīsaras, the lake of Satī, fills the Kashmir valley** — From the beginning of the kalpa the valley is the mountain-lake Satīsaras, remaining water through the first six manvantaras until the Vaivasvata age _(actors: Satī/Umā, the waters of Satīsaras)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/nilamata-purana.md) — (Nīlamata Purāṇa, cosmography)
- **Satīsaras, the six-manvantara lake** — the Kashmir basin is the mountain-lake Satīsaras, "the lake of Satī (Umā)," remaining water through the first six manvantaras _(actors: Satī/Umā, the primordial waters)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kashmir-tirthas-nilamata-geography.md) — (Nīlamata Purāṇa, cosmography)
- **Satyasena destroys the Yakshas and evil spirits** — Vishnu's avatar Satyasena, born of Sunrita and accompanied by the Satyavratas, destroys the Yakshas, Rakshasas, and lying evil spirits, fighting alongside Indra Satyajit in the Uttama manvantara _(actors: Satyasena, Sunrita, Satyavratas, Indra Satyajit)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-03-uttama.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.1.25)
- **Saudāsa's clash with Śakti and the curse of cannibalism** — Ikṣvāku king Saudāsa meets Vasiṣṭha's son Śakti on a narrow path, insults/strikes him, and is cursed to become a man-eating rākṣasa _(actors: Saudāsa (Mitrasaha), Śakti (Śaktri, son of Vasiṣṭha))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalmashapada-saudasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva (Vasiṣṭha upākhyāna))
- **Śiva rises from the lake to bless the Pracetas** — Rudra emerges from the water with his attendants and, declaring Viṣṇu's devotees most worshipful, offers the young ascetics a hymn to accomplish their purpose _(actors: Śiva/Rudra, the Pracetas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pracetas-rudra-gita.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.24.18–33)
- **Soma abducts Tara** — The moon-god Soma, proud after his Rajasuya, carries off Tara, the chaste wife of Brihaspati, and refuses to return her _(actors: Soma, Tara, Brihaspati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.6; Bhagavata Purana 9.14)
- **Soma abducts Tārā, igniting the Tārakāmaya War** — The moon-god Soma carries off Tārā, wife of Bṛhaspati, and refuses to return her, sparking the fifth Devāsura war _(actors: Soma (Chandra), Tārā, Bṛhaspati, Śukra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4.6; Devī-Bhāgavata 1.11)
- **Soma pacifies the Pracetas and gives Māriṣā** — The moon-god and lord of plants halts the burning and, to seal peace, presents the tree-nursed maiden Māriṣā as the brothers' shared bride _(actors: Soma, the Pracetas, Māriṣā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pracetas-rudra-gita.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.30.44–48)
- **Sukanyā pierces the anthill-sage Cyavana's eyes** — Princess Sukanyā blinds the anthill-buried sage Cyavana with a thorn; his tapas afflicts her father Śaryāti's army _(actors: Sukanyā, Cyavana, Śaryāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 122–123; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5)
- **Suruci humiliates the child Dhruva** — When five-year-old Dhruva climbs onto his father Uttānapāda's lap, the proud queen Suruci taunts that the royal lap is not for a rival's son unless he is reborn from her or wins it by propitiating Viṣṇu _(actors: Dhruva, Suruci, Uttānapāda, Uttama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.11)
- **Surya weds Saranyu and she flees as a mare** — Surya weds Saranyu, daughter of Vishvakarma, but unable to bear his blaze she leaves behind her shadow-double Chhaya and flees as a mare _(actors: Surya, Saranyu/Sanjna, Chhaya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/navagraha.md) — (Rig Veda 10.17; Markandeya & Matsya Puranas)
- **Sutapas and Pṛśni receive the icon** — Brahmā bestows the image on the austere couple, whose tapas wins Viṣṇu's boon to be born as their son in three successive lives _(actors: Brahmā, Sutapas, Pṛśni, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/guruvayur-krishna-kshetra.md) — (Guruvāyupura-māhātmya; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.3)
- **Svarāṣṭra dethroned by Vimarda** — the righteous king Svarāṣṭra, stripped of wives and kingdom by his rival Vimarda, withdraws to the forest as an ascetic _(actors: King Svarāṣṭra, rival king Vimarda)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/markandeya-manvantara-origin-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa LXXIII–LXXIV)
- **Ten thousand years of tapas and Viṣṇu's boon** — Chanting the Rudra-Gītā underwater for ten millennia, the Pracetas win Viṣṇu's darśana and boons of good progeny, enjoyment, and final release _(actors: the Pracetas, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pracetas-rudra-gita.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.30.1–34)
- **The Amṛta-manthana war (fourth saṅgrāma)** — The churning of the milk-ocean breaks into open battle over the nectar; Mohinī diverts the amṛta and Rāhu is beheaded _(actors: the devas, the asuras, Viṣṇu as Mohinī, Rāhu)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/twelve-devasura-battles.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa 47; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.5–12)
- **The Andhakāra war (eighth saṅgrāma)** — Śiva impales the blind asura Andhaka on the triśūla while the Mātṛkās drink his multiplying blood _(actors: Śiva, Andhaka, Pārvatī, the Mātṛkās)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/twelve-devasura-battles.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa 179, 47; Śiva Purāṇa, Rudra-saṃhitā)
- **The blurt: 'wife of your son yet unborn'** — Cornered, Jyāmagha declares the girl his daughter-in-law, bride of the son barren Śaibyā will yet bear, and the Viśvedevas and Pitṛs ratify the impossible word _(actors: Jyāmagha, Śaibyā, Viśvedevas, Pitṛs)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jyamagha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.23.36–38; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.12)
- **The burning of the tree-overgrown earth** — Emerging to find the earth choked with forest, the wrathful Pracetas breathe fire and wind from their mouths to reduce the trees to ash _(actors: the Pracetas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pracetas-rudra-gita.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.30.35–45)
- **The captive girl on the queen's chariot-seat** — Old and sonless, Jyāmagha returns from campaign with a captive maiden seated in the queen's place, and Śaibyā confronts him as a cheat _(actors: Jyāmagha, Śaibyā, the captive girl)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jyamagha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.23.35–36; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.12)
- **The demon rebirths of the six** — the cursed sons are born as offspring of Hiraṇyakaśipu (Devī-Bhāgavata: first of Kālanemi, then Hiraṇyakaśipu), fated to be slain by their own former father _(actors: the six Ṣaḍgarbha, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Kālanemi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/devaki-six-sons-shadgarbha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.85.49; Devī-Bhāgavata 4)
- **The doe-queen and the birth of Manu Tāmasa** — in a great flood Svarāṣṭra meets his cursed dead queen Utpalāvatī as a doe; her flood-born son becomes the 4th Manu, Tāmasa, and she is freed from Sutapas's curse _(actors: Svarāṣṭra, doe-queen Utpalāvatī, sage Sutapas, Manu Tāmasa)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/markandeya-manvantara-origin-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa LXXIV)
- **The king fashioned from the gods (rājadharma)** — the Lord creates the king from eternal particles of Indra, Vāyu, Yama, Sūrya, Agni, Varuṇa, Candra and Kubera so the strong do not devour the weak like fish _(actors: the eight lokapālas, the king, Daṇḍa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/manusmriti-map.md) — (Mānava-Dharmaśāstra 7.3–7, 7.14–31)
- **The king-and-elephant exchange** — Returning after another thousand years, Ṛbhu asks which is the king and which the elephant, and when Nidāgha leaps on his shoulders crying "I am above, you below," counters "which of us is you, and which is I?", collapsing his disciple's dualism _(actors: Ṛbhu, Nidāgha, the king of Vīranagara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ribhu-nidagha-vishnu-purana.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa, II.16)
- **The mocking of Brahmā (origin of the Ṣaḍgarbha)** — in the first (Svāyambhuva) Manvantara the six godling sons of Marīci and Ūrṇā laugh at Brahmā's passion for his own daughter and are cursed to fall into asura birth _(actors: Marīci, Ūrṇā, Brahmā, the six sons)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/devaki-six-sons-shadgarbha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.85.47–49)
- **The Pracetas set out to beget progeny** — Prācīnabarhi's ten sons, of one accord, journey west to a great lake to perform austerity as their father charged them to increase the world's population _(actors: Prācīnabarhi, the ten Pracetas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pracetas-rudra-gita.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.24)
- **The Rākṣasa who ate a shrew's temper** — a brahman's abducted wife is found in the Utpalāvataka forest, her ill-nature already consumed by the Rākṣasa Valāka, and her disposition is remade by rite _(actors: the brahman, his wife, Rākṣasa Valāka)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/markandeya-manvantara-origin-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa LXX–LXXI)
- **The rebirth of Dakṣa from Māriṣā** — The Prajāpati beheaded for reviling Śiva returns as the son of the ten Pracetas and Māriṣā — the "second Dakṣa" who re-seeds all progeny _(actors: Dakṣa, the Pracetas, Māriṣā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pracetas-rudra-gita.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.30.48–49; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.15)
- **The Rudra-Gītā — Śiva sings to Viṣṇu** — Śiva teaches the Pracetas a stotra glorifying Vāsudeva/Saṅkarṣaṇa, the Bhāgavata's Śaiva–Vaiṣṇava bridge in which the God of the Śaivas extols the God of the Vaiṣṇavas _(actors: Śiva, the Pracetas, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pracetas-rudra-gita.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.24.33–79)
- **The sages slay the tyrant Vena** — King Vena forbids all sacrifice and proclaims himself the sole god; the enraged brāhmaṇas kill him with charged mantras _(actors: Vena, the sages)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.14; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.13)
- **The star-maiden Revatī and the birth of Manu Raivata** — Pramuca fosters the girl born of the fallen star, Agni names King Durgama her husband, the star is restored for the wedding, and their son becomes the 5th Manu, Raivata _(actors: maiden Revatī, sage Pramuca, Agni, King Durgama, Manu Raivata)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/markandeya-manvantara-origin-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa LXXV–LXXVI)
- **The Tārakāmaya war (fifth saṅgrāma)** — Soma's abduction of Tārā splits gods and asuras into two armies; Viṣṇu slays Kālanemi before Brahmā halts the war _(actors: Soma, Tārā, Bṛhaspati, Śukra, Viṣṇu, Kālanemi)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/twelve-devasura-battles.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa 23–24, 47; Padma Purāṇa, Sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa 12)
- **The Traipura war (seventh saṅgrāma)** — Śiva as Tripurāntaka burns the three flying fortresses of Tāraka's sons with a single arrow at their alignment _(actors: Śiva, Tārakākṣa, Vidyunmālī, Kamalākṣa, Maya)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/twelve-devasura-battles.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa 129–140, 47; Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva)
- **The twelve-year drought and Varuṇa's boon** — During a long Deccan drought, sage Gautama propitiates Varuṇa and gains unfailing grain/water at Brahmagiri, feeding the starving sages _(actors: Gautama, Ahalyā, Varuṇa, gathered ṛṣis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/godavari-gautami-dakshina-ganga.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa (Gautamī-māhātmya))
- **The twelve-year sattra of Shaunaka at Naimisha** — 88,000 sages assemble in Naimisharanya for a perpetual long-session Soma-sacrifice led by Kulapati Shaunaka, the setting for hearing the Puranas _(actors: Shaunaka, the 88,000 rishis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.1.4; Vayu Purana 1.11-12)
- **Tāraka's tapas and boon** — The daitya Tāraka performs fierce penance and wins from Brahmā the boon that he can die only by a (seven-day-old) son of Śiva _(actors: Tāraka, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tarakasura-vadha.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa (Kumāra-khaṇḍa); Skanda Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Trimūrti test Anasūyā and are reborn as her sons** — Sent to break Anasūyā's chastity, Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Śiva are turned into infants by her power and reborn as Soma, Dattātreya, and Durvāsā _(actors: Anasūyā, Atri, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Tulasī curses Gaṇeśa to be married** — Humiliated by the rejection, Tulasī curses the celibate Gaṇeśa that he will certainly wed, vow or no vow _(actors: Tulasī, Gaṇeśa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tulasi-ganesha-curse.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa, Gaṇapati-khaṇḍa)
- **Tulasī departs for tapas toward her cursed destiny** — Tulasī leaves for austerities, her course bent toward the demon-marriage to Śaṅkhacūḍa and ultimate union with Nārāyaṇa _(actors: Tulasī, Nārāyaṇa, Śaṅkhacūḍa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tulasi-ganesha-curse.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa)
- **Tulasī interrupts Gaṇeśa's meditation with a proposal** — The ascetic maiden Tulasī, smitten by the young Gaṇeśa absorbed in meditation on Kṛṣṇa, breaks his tapas and proposes marriage _(actors: Tulasī, Gaṇeśa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tulasi-ganesha-curse.md) — (Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa, Gaṇapati-khaṇḍa)
- **Vidarbha weds the waiting bride** — Grown, Vidarbha marries the very captive girl long accepted as the household's daughter-in-law, and gives his name to the southern Vidarbha kingdom _(actors: Vidarbha, the captive girl (unnamed))_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jyamagha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.23.38–39; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.12)
- **Vidarbha's sons head the Kratha-Kaiśika and Cedi lines** — Vidarbha's sons (Kratha, Kaiśika, Romapāda; the Bhāgavata reads Kuśa for Kaiśika) head the Vidarbha king-line and, downstream, the Caidya kings _(actors: Vidarbha, Kratha, Kaiśika, Romapāda)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jyamagha.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.12; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.24)
- **Viṣṇu gifts Ambarīṣa the Sudarśana and the Ekādaśī vow** — Pleased by Ambarīṣa's total devotion, Viṣṇu awards him the Sudarśana-cakra as guardian; the king undertakes a year-long Ekādaśī vow _(actors: Ambarīṣa, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.4)
- **Yadu refuses his father's old age and is cursed** — Yayāti curses his eldest son Yadu that his descendants shall never hold imperial sovereignty, barring the senior Yādava branch from the Lunar throne _(actors: Yayāti, Yadu, Pūru)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/yadava-vamsha.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~84-85; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.10; Bhāgavata IX.18-19)
- **Yama becomes the first mortal to die and king of the dead** — Yama, son of Vivasvat and twin of Yami, is the first mortal to die and thereby becomes king of the dead, lord of Naraka in the southern quarter _(actors: Yama)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/narakas-and-afterlife.md) — (Rig Veda 10.14; Garuda Purana)
- **Yuvanāśva drinks the consecrated fertility-water** — The childless Ikṣvāku king Yuvanāśva, parched at night, accidentally drinks the mantra-charged conception-water the sages had prepared for his queen _(actors: Yuvanāśva, the ṛṣis (officiants of the Indra-yajña), the queen (intended drinker))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandhata.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva ~126; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.6.28–33)
- **Ajāmila cries 'Nārāyaṇa' and is saved by the Viṣṇudūtas** — Dying, Ajāmila calls his son's name 'Nārāyaṇa'; four Viṣṇudūtas stop the Yamadūtas and debate the saving power of the holy name _(actors: Ajāmila, Viṣṇudūtas, Yamadūtas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ajamila.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.1–6.2)
- **Anasūyā turns the Trimūrti into infants** — When the disguised Trimūrti demand to be served food naked to break her vow, Anasūyā by the power of her chastity transforms them into crying babies and serves them without sin _(actors: Anasūyā, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Andhaka adopted by Hiranyaksha and granted a boon** — Shiva gives the dark boy to the childless daitya Hiranyaksha, who rears him; Andhaka wins from Brahma a boon making him slayable only if he lusts after his own mother _(actors: Shiva, Hiranyaksha, Andhaka, Brahma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/andhakasura-vadha.md) — (Shiva Purana; Matsya Purana; Vamana Purana)
- **Atri serves as Saptarṣi of the Vaivasvata Manvantara** — Atri is installed among the Seven Sages presiding over the present Vaivasvata Manvantara _(actors: Atri, the Saptarṣi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/atri-anasuya.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.1)
- **Bharata gives the dynasty its name** — From Dushyanta and Shakuntala is born Bharata, after whom Bharata-varsha and the Mahabharata are named _(actors: Dushyanta, Shakuntala, Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/01-adi-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva 68-74)
- **Birth of Māndhātṛ from his father's side** — The child gestates within Yuvanāśva and is delivered by splitting open the king's flank, the father surviving by the sages'/Aśvins' grace _(actors: Yuvanāśva, the infant Māndhātṛ, the sages / Aśvins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandhata.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva ~126; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.6.34–36)
- **Birth of Mārkaṇḍeya** — The radiant son is born and named Mārkaṇḍeya, mastering the Vedas precociously while his parents conceal his death-date _(actors: Mārkaṇḍeya, Mṛkaṇḍu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Shiva Purana)
- **Birth of Nandi** — The bull-faced Nandi is born to sage Shilada by Shiva's grace and is made chief of Shiva's hosts and eternal gatekeeper and mount _(actors: Nandishvara (Shiva), Shilada)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Birth of Nara and Narayana** — The twin sage-incarnations of Vishnu, Nara and Narayana, are born as sons of Dharma and Murti/Ahimsa, becoming the perpetual ascetics of Badarikashrama (later reincarnated as Arjuna and Krishna) _(actors: Nara, Narayana, Dharma, Murti)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Puranic Encyclopaedia / Devi-Bhagavata; (variant: Bhagavata Purana 4.1 places in Svayambhuva))
- **Birth of the avatar Hari** — Vishnu manifests in the Tamasa Manvantara as the avatar Hari, son of sage Harimedha and his wife Harini, born expressly to liberate the devotee Gajendra _(actors: Hari, Harimedha, Harini)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-04-tamasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Brahma's prophecy and naming** — The infant grips Brahma's beard; Brahma names him Jalandhara and decrees he can be slain only by Shiva _(actors: Brahma, Jalandhara, Samudra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jalandhara-vrinda.md) — (Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda))
- **Brahmā restores Tārā; birth and naming of Budha** — Brahmā halts the war and recovers the pregnant Tārā; she confesses the child is Soma's, and Soma names the boy Budha, founder of the Lunar line _(actors: Brahmā, Soma, Tārā, Bṛhaspati, Budha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4.6; Bhāgavata 9.14)
- **Brahmā's boon of the three cities** — Brahmā grants three impregnable flying cities destructible only by a single arrow at a once-in-a-millennium alignment _(actors: Brahmā, the three asura brothers)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-dahana.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa)
- **Creation of Svayambhuva Manu and Shatarupa** — Brahma divides his own body into male and female halves, the male becoming Svayambhuva Manu and the female Shatarupa, the first human couple and progenitors of mankind _(actors: Brahma, Svayambhuva Manu, Shatarupa)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Manusmriti 1; Vishnu Purana 1; Bhagavata Purana 3-4)
- **Creation of Vaikuntha realm** — At the request of his consort the goddess Rama (Lakshmi), the avatar Vaikuntha creates the supreme eternal abode known as Vaikuntha to please her _(actors: Vaikuntha, Rama/Lakshmi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5)
- **Dadhīci gives his bones for Indra's vajra** — To slay Vṛtra, Dadhīci yields his life so his thunder-charged spine can be forged by Viśvakarman into the vajra _(actors: Dadhīci, Indra, Viṣṇu, Viśvakarman)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dadhichi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.9–10)
- **Dakṣa-prajāpati's daughters wed the gods** — Dakṣa's daughters marry Kaśyapa, Soma and others, seeding the gods, demons, and creatures in the standard Prajāpati genealogy _(actors: Dakṣa, Kaśyapa, Soma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahma-purana.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa)
- **Dattātreya teaches the 24 gurus of nature** — As the avadhūta sage, Dattātreya tells King Yadu how he learned liberation from twenty-four teachers drawn from the natural world _(actors: Dattātreya, Yadu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.7–9)
- **Devahuti's plea for liberation** — The aged, lonely Devahūti approaches her divine son Kapila and asks him to dispel the darkness of saṃsāra, opening the discourse _(actors: Devahūti, Kapila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kapila-devahuti.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.25.7–11)
- **Devi-Mahatmya frame: Suratha and Samadhi worship the Goddess** — In the Svarochisha manvantara King Suratha and the merchant Samadhi worship the Goddess, and Suratha is reborn as the future Savarni Manu _(actors: King Suratha, Samadhi, the Goddess)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/README.md) — (Markandeya Purana / Devi-Mahatmya)
- **Dhruva's great penance and Viṣṇu's darśana** — Instructed by Nārada in the Vāsudeva mantra, Dhruva's escalating austerity in Madhuvana chokes the worlds and wins Viṣṇu's appearance _(actors: Dhruva, Nārada, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8–4.9; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.12)
- **Dhruva's tapas and exaltation as the Pole Star** — The child prince Dhruva, slighted by his stepmother, performs extreme austerity, receives Vishnu's darshana, and is exalted as the immovable Dhruva-loka (Pole Star) _(actors: Dhruva, Uttanapada, Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 1); cf. Bhagavata 4)
- **Dhruva's vow and departure to the forest** — Consoled by his mother Sunīti to seek refuge in Viṣṇu, the boy Dhruva resolves to win a station higher than any being ever attained and leaves the palace alone for the forest _(actors: Dhruva, Sunīti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.11)
- **Durvāsā's wrath and the Sudarśana's pursuit** — Enraged over the Dvādaśī water-sip, Durvāsā hurls a fire-demon at Ambarīṣa; the Sudarśana burns it and chases the sage across the three worlds _(actors: Durvāsā, Ambarīṣa, Sudarśana, Brahmā, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.4)
- **Gaṅgā's descent floods Jahnu's sacrifice** — As Bhagīratha leads the descending Gaṅgā across the plains, her torrent drowns sage-king Jahnu's sacrificial enclosure _(actors: Gaṅgā, Bhagīratha, Jahnu)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jahnu.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 44)
- **Gajendra's hymn of surrender and rescue by Viṣṇu** — Helpless Gajendra offers the Gajendra-stuti to the unnamed Absolute; Viṣṇu flies on Garuḍa and severs the crocodile with the Sudarśana _(actors: Gajendra, Viṣṇu, Garuḍa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gajendra-moksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.3)
- **Gods Elect Nahuṣa as Indra** — The gods and sages install the earthly emperor Nahuṣa on heaven's throne for his unmatched tapas, augmenting his merit to hold the office _(actors: Nahuṣa, devas, ṛṣis)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nahusha.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva 11-12)
- **Ila/Sudyumna and the Founding of the Lunar Line** — Manu's gender-shifting child Ila/Sudyumna unites with Budha (son of Candra), and their son Pururavas founds the Candravamsha _(actors: Ila/Sudyumna, Budha, Pururavas)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana IX.1; Shatapatha Brahmana)
- **Śiva's axe severs Gaṇeśa's tusk (Ekadanta origin)** — When the boy Gaṇeśa barred Śiva's door, Śiva's axe (the paraśu later given to Paraśurāma) struck off one of Gaṇeśa's tusks, which he refused to dodge out of respect for his father's weapon — the origin of his epithet Ekadanta ('one-tusked') _(actors: Śiva, Gaṇeśa, (Paraśurāma in variant tellings))_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Purāṇic Gaṇeśa traditions)
- **Jaratkāru vows to marry on strict conditions** — Recognizing himself as the sonless descendant, Jaratkāru pledges to wed only a same-named bride given freely whom he need not support, reserving the right to leave at the first displeasure _(actors: Jaratkāru; his Pitṛs)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaratkaru-and-manasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Āstīka sub-parva)
- **Kakudmi and Revati visit Brahmaloka (time dilation)** — King Kakudmi takes his daughter Revati to Brahmaloka to seek a husband; Brahma reveals 27 chaturyugas have passed on Earth during the brief wait _(actors: Kakudmi (Raivata), Revati, Brahma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.3.27-36; Vishnu Purana 4.1)
- **King Janaka attains perfection through action** — Krishna cites King Janaka and others who reached liberation through action itself, the standing proof that ruling and self-realization can coexist _(actors: Janaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavad-gita/03-to-06-karma-shatka.md) — (Bhagavad Gita 3.20)
- **King Kuru Ploughs the Field of Dharma** — King Kuru ploughs the Kurukṣetra plain with a golden plough, sowing eight dharmic virtues to make it a Dharma-kṣetra _(actors: Kuru, Indra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kurukshetra-dharmakshetra.md) — (Vamana Purana, Kurukshetra-mahatmya)
- **Kubera made world-guardian and lord of Laṅkā** — Kubera, son of Viśravas, wins by austerity the lordship of the north, the yakṣas, and wealth, gaining the Puṣpaka chariot and the golden city of Laṅkā _(actors: Kubera, Brahmā, Viśravas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 13–15)
- **Marriage of Śaṅkhacūḍa and Tulasī; the double armor** — Śaṅkhacūḍa weds Tulasī, becoming invincible through her pativratya plus the Viṣṇu-Kavaca, and conquers the three worlds _(actors: Śaṅkhacūḍa, Tulasī, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shankhachuda-tulasi.md) — (Brahma-Vaivarta Purāṇa, Prakṛti-khaṇḍa)
- **Marriage of Kardama and Devahuti at Bindu-sarovara** — Svayambhuva Manu brings his daughter Devahuti to wed Kardama, who creates an aerial vimana for their ascetic married life _(actors: Kardama, Devahuti, Svayambhuva Manu, Shatarupa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/bindu-sarovar-siddhpur.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.22-23)
- **Marriage of Yajña and Dakṣiṇā and birth of the twelve Yāmas** — Yajña weds his twin Dakṣiṇā and they father the twelve Yāma gods, who become the deva-class of the Svāyambhuva Manvantara _(actors: Yajña, Dakṣiṇā, the twelve Yāmas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yajna-avatara.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1.7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **Pauloma and the birth of Cyavana** — A Rakshasa abducts the pregnant Puloma, causing the premature birth of Cyavana whose radiance burns the Rakshasa to ash, founding the Bhrigu line _(actors: Puloma, Cyavana, a Rakshasa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Pauloma Parva)
- **Pramadvarā killed by snakebite** — On the eve of the wedding Pramadvarā treads on a hidden snake and dies instantly, struck down by fate _(actors: Pramadvarā, a serpent)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ruru-pramadvara.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva)
- **Pṛthu churned from Vena's corpse and crowned first king** — The sages churn Niṣāda then the Viṣṇu-marked Pṛthu from Vena's body; Pṛthu is consecrated the first anointed king _(actors: Pṛthu, the sages, Niṣāda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.15; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.13)
- **Pulastya fathers Vaishravana (Kubera)** — The Prajapati Pulastya fathers Vaishravana/Kubera, who is granted lordship of wealth and the city of Lanka, angering his father's line _(actors: Pulastya, Kubera)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramopakhyana.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 257)
- **Rebirth of Vasishtha's seven sons as the Saptarishis of the Uttama manvantara** — The seven sons Vasishtha had by his wife Urja in the Svayambhuva manvantara are reborn as the Saptarishis of the third (Uttama) period, a clear sage-reincarnation statement _(actors: The seven sons of Vasishtha, Vasishtha, Urja)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-03-uttama.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.1)
- **Rishabha rains on his realm and fathers a hundred sons** — When envious Indra withholds rain, Rishabha rains by yoga-power on Ajanabha; he marries Jayanti and fathers a hundred sons, eldest Bharata, after whom the land becomes Bharata-varsha _(actors: Rishabha, Indra, Jayanti, Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.4; 5.7)
- **Sañjñā creates the shadow-wife Chhāyā and flees** — Scorched by Sūrya's blaze, Sañjñā creates an identical shadow-double Chhāyā to act as his wife, then flees to the northern forests in the form of a mare _(actors: Sañjñā, Sūrya, Chhāyā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/surya-and-his-family.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
- **Sati's Self-Immolation** — Sati attends Daksha's sacrifice uninvited, is insulted, and gives up her body in the sacrificial fire (or by yogic agni), the act that names sati _(actors: Sati)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/51-shakti-peethas.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana; Kalika Purana)
- **Sati's tapas and marriage to Shiva** — Sati performs the Nanda-vrata austerities to obtain the ascetic Shiva, who grants the boon and weds her against Daksha's will _(actors: Sati, Shiva, Daksha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita; Bhagavata Purana IV.2-4)
- **Sukanyā pierces Cyavana's eyes** — King Śaryāti's daughter Sukanyā pierces the glowing eyes of the anthill-buried sage Cyavana with a thorn, blinding him, whereupon his tapas afflicts the king's army with retention of urine and stool _(actors: Sukanyā, Cyavana, Śaryāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 122–123; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5)
- **Sukanyā wed to Cyavana; the Aśvins restore his youth** — Sukanyā is given in atonement to the aged Cyavana; refusing the Aśvins' advances, she correctly picks her husband from three identical youths after they rejuvenate him _(actors: Sukanyā, Cyavana, the Aśvins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 123–124; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5)
- **Suta Ugrashravas recites the Puranas to the assembly** — The bard Suta Ugrashravas (son of Romaharshana), in the transmission chain Vyasa to Romaharshana to Ugrashravas, narrates the eighteen Puranas to the Naimisha sages _(actors: Suta Ugrashravas, Romaharshana, Vyasa, the rishis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.1-1.4; Vayu Purana 1.16; Vishnu Purana 1.1)
- **The Atri-Anasuya triad: birth of Soma, Dattatreya, Durvasas** — From the chaste Anasuya the Trimurti take partial birth: Brahma as Soma, Vishnu as Dattatreya, Shiva as Durvasas _(actors: Atri, Anasuya, Soma, Dattatreya, Durvasas)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Markandeya Purana; Puranic Encyclopaedia)
- **The gandharva's deception and birth of Svarocis** — A spurned gandharva takes Pravara's form to seduce Varuthini; meditating on the true Pravara's radiance she bears the self-luminous Svarocis _(actors: the gandharva, Varuthini, Svarocis)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana)
- **The gandharva's deception and conception of Svarocis** — A spurned gandharva takes Pravara's exact form and unites with Varuthini; because she conceived meditating on the true Pravara's radiance, her son Svarocis is born self-luminous, giving the manvantara its name _(actors: The gandharva, Varuthini, Svarocis)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana)
- **The sages' jealousy and conspiracy** — When rains return, the other sages grow envious of Gautama's merit and honour and plot to drive him from his hermitage _(actors: Gautama, jealous ṛṣis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/godavari-gautami-dakshina-ganga.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa)
- **The thousand-year struggle and Gajendra's surrender** — After a thousand-year contest in which his herd abandons him and his strength fails, Gajendra at last lets go of pride and turns his whole mind to the Supreme, raising a lotus and pouring out the Gajendra-stuti of total surrender _(actors: Gajendra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gajendra-moksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.2–8.3)
- **Tāraka's oppression of the devas** — Tāraka conquers the three worlds, seizes Indra's heaven and the divine treasures, and inverts cosmic order _(actors: Tāraka, Indra, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tarakasura-vadha.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa; Vāmana Purāṇa)
- **Śukra's curse creates the wilderness** — Enraged Śukra curses Daṇḍa so Indra rains a seven-day dust-storm burying the kingdom for a hundred yojanas, making the desolate Daṇḍaka forest (Arajā's grove alone spared) _(actors: Śukrācārya, Daṇḍa, Indra, Arajā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dandakaranya-rama-forest.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 81; Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa)
- **Vasishtha-Vishvamitra cow rivalry and Vishvamitra's penance** — King Vishvamitra covets Vasishtha's wish-cow Kamadhenu, who conjures an army that routs his forces; humiliated, he renounces his throne and undertakes millennia of penance to rise from Rajarshi to Brahmarshi _(actors: Vishvamitra, Vasishtha, Kamadhenu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana Bala Kanda 51-65; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Vena's Misrule and Execution** — Crowned Vena forbids all sacrifice, proclaiming himself the sole object of worship; when he refuses the sages' appeal, the brāhmaṇas slay him with mantra-charged kuśa-grass _(actors: Vena, the ṛṣis)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.14; Vishnu Purana 1.13)
- **Vimāna passed to Ikṣvāku and the Sūryavaṃśa** — Brahmā grants the Raṅga-vimāna to Ikṣvāku, and it is worshipped down the Solar dynasty to Ayodhyā _(actors: Brahmā, Ikṣvāku, Sūryavaṃśa kings)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srirangam-ranganatha.md) — (Śrīraṅga-māhātmya)
- **Viśvāmitra sends a rākṣasa to possess the king** — Viśvāmitra, exploiting his feud with Vasiṣṭha, dispatches a rākṣasa to possess the cursed Saudāsa so the curse falls on Vasiṣṭha's sons _(actors: Viśvāmitra, Saudāsa, the rākṣasa Kiṃkara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalmashapada-saudasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Viśvāmitra waives the fee; Gālava insists** — Viśvāmitra dismisses his devoted pupil Gālava owing no guru-dakṣiṇā, but Gālava proudly insists on paying _(actors: Gālava, Viśvāmitra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/galava-madhavi.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva ~105–106)
- **Ajāmila's repentance and liberation at Haridvāra** — Restored to life and transformed, Ajāmila renounces all, practices bhakti-yoga at Haridvāra, and is borne to Vaikuṇṭha _(actors: Ajāmila, Viṣṇudūtas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ajamila.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.2)
- **Andhaka conquers the three worlds and lusts after Parvati** — The mighty blind asura overruns the devas and seizes the three worlds, then beholds Parvati on Kailasa and resolves to take her, not knowing she is his mother _(actors: Andhaka, Indra, devas, Parvati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/andhakasura-vadha.md) — (Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda); Matsya Purana; Kurma Purana)
- **Śarmiṣṭhā casts Devayānī into the well** — After a quarrel of precedence, Śarmiṣṭhā throws Devayānī into a dry well; King Yayāti rescues her by the hand, which she treats as betrothal _(actors: Devayānī, Śarmiṣṭhā, Yayāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 75-76; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Atri-Anasuya triad birth (Soma, Dattatreya, Durvasas)** — From the chaste Anasuya, wife of sage Atri, the Trimurti take partial birth — Brahma as Soma/Candra, Vishnu as Dattatreya, and Shiva as Durvasas — anchoring the great guru-avatar Dattatreya's origin here _(actors: Atri, Anasuya, Soma/Candra, Dattatreya, Durvasas)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Markandeya Purana; Puranic Encyclopaedia)
- **Bharata-varsha Named After King Bharata** — The southern karma-bhumi varsha is named after King Bharata, son of Rishabha (Bhagavata) or son of Dushyanta and Shakuntala (epic tradition) _(actors: Bharata, Rishabha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/bharatavarsha-and-puranic-geography.md) — (Vishnu Purana 2.3; Bhagavata Purana 5.19; Mahabharata)
- **Birth of Dattātreya, Soma, and Durvāsā** — Pleased by Anasūyā and restored by her, the Trimūrti are born as her sons — Soma (Brahmā-portion), Dattātreya (Viṣṇu-portion), and Durvāsā (Śiva-portion), the triple-deity avatar fused in three heads and six arms _(actors: Anasūyā, Atri, Dattātreya, Soma, Durvāsā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa, and Śūrpaṇakhā** — From the rākṣasī Kaikasī and Viśravas are born Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, the gentle Vibhīṣaṇa, and the sister Śūrpaṇakhā _(actors: Kaikasī, Viśravas, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 9–10)
- **Birth of the nine daughters and of Kapila; Kardama's renunciation** — Devahuti bears nine daughters wed to the rishis and a son Kapila, Vishnu incarnate; Kardama then takes sannyasa _(actors: Devahuti, Kardama, Kapila, the rishis (Marici, Atri, Anasuya))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/bindu-sarovar-siddhpur.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.24)
- **Birth of Vasiṣṭha and Agastya from Mitra-Varuṇa** — The sages Vasiṣṭha and Agastya are miraculously born from the seed of Mitra-Varuṇa at the sight of the apsaras Urvaśī, Agastya being pitcher-born _(actors: Mitra, Varuṇa, Urvaśī, Vasiṣṭha, Agastya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/varuna.md) — (Ṛgveda 7.33)
- **Birth of Vishravas from Pulastya's anger** — Slighted when Kubera attends Brahma over him, Pulastya produces the sage Vishravas from half his own being, into whom his wrath passes _(actors: Pulastya, Vishravas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramopakhyana.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 258)
- **Brahma's infatuation with Shatarupa and Shiva striking off his head** — In a variant, Brahma is infatuated with his daughter Shatarupa, sprouts extra heads to keep her in view, and Shiva later strikes one off _(actors: Brahma, Shatarupa, Shiva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Matsya Purana; Brahma Purana)
- **Chhāyā curses Yama and the deception is exposed** — Chhāyā curses Yama in anger, revealing she cannot be the true mother; Yama complains to Sūrya, who interrogates Chhāyā and uncovers the substitution _(actors: Chhāyā, Yama, Sūrya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/surya-and-his-family.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Churning of the Ocean of Milk (Ajita as Kurma)** — Vishnu's avatar Ajita bears Mount Mandara as the tortoise Kurma and distributes the amrita at the devas' churning of the milk-ocean _(actors: Ajita (Vishnu/Kurma), devas, asuras)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Churning of Vena's Body — Birth of Niṣāda** — From Vena's churned thigh emerges the dark hunter Niṣāda, ancestor of the forest peoples, carrying away all of Vena's accumulated sin _(actors: the sages, Niṣāda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.14; Vishnu Purana 1.13)
- **Cyavana creates Mada and wins the Aśvins their soma-share** — Cyavana paralyzes Indra's arm and creates the giant Asura Mada to force the Aśvins' admission to the soma-cult, then distributes Mada into the four kingly vices _(actors: Cyavana, Indra, the Aśvins, Mada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 125; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5)
- **Death of Vasishtha's hundred sons** — In the feud, Vishvamitra causes king Kalmashapada, possessed by a rakshasa, to devour all of Vasishtha's hundred sons; the grieving Vasishtha attempts suicide but is preserved _(actors: Vishvamitra, Kalmashapada, Vasishtha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva; Valmiki Ramayana)
- **Devouring of Śakti and Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons** — The possessed Kalmāṣapāda eats Śakti first and then all of Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons, extinguishing the sage's line of sons _(actors: Kalmāṣapāda, Śakti, Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalmashapada-saudasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Dhruva granted the immovable polar seat** — Viṣṇu grants Dhruva the Dhruva-pada, the fixed pole-star station enduring a full Kalpa, plus a long earthly reign _(actors: Dhruva, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.9, 4.12; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.12)
- **Founding of the royal lineages by Vaivasvata's sons** — Vaivasvata Manu's sons found the great dynasties, Ikshvaku seeding the Solar line and Ila/Sudyumna seeding the Lunar line through Pururavas _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Ikshvaku, Ila/Sudyumna, Pururavas)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.2, 4.1; Bhagavata Purana 9.1)
- **Gods dispossessed appeal to Śiva** — Driven from heaven, the devas petition Brahmā and Śiva, who agrees to destroy Śaṅkhacūḍa _(actors: Devas, Brahmā, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shankhachuda-tulasi.md) — (Brahma-Vaivarta Purāṇa; Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa, Book IX)
- **Gods petition Brahmā for a remedy** — The dispossessed devas approach Brahmā, who reveals that only a son of Śiva, born as war-general, can slay Tāraka _(actors: Indra, the devas, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tarakasura-vadha.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Kumārasambhava II; Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Indra names the child 'mām dhāsyati'** — Asked who will suckle the motherless infant, Indra answers 'he shall suckle me' and feeds him nectar from his finger, giving the name Māndhātṛ _(actors: Indra, the infant Māndhātṛ, the gods)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandhata.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva ~126; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.6.37–38)
- **Jahnu drinks the entire Gaṅgā** — Enraged at the ruined rite, Jahnu swallows the whole river in one draught by his ascetic power, undoing Bhagīratha's effort _(actors: Jahnu, Gaṅgā)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jahnu.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 44)
- **King Suratha Worships the Goddess and Is Reborn as Savarni** — King Suratha, having lost his kingdom, worships the Goddess Mahamaya/Durga in a forest hermitage alongside the merchant Samadhi and by Her boon is destined to be reborn as Savarni, son of Surya, the future 8th Manu _(actors: King Suratha; Samadhi; Mahamaya/Durga)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-08-savarni.md) — (Markandeya Purana 81-93 (Devi Mahatmya / Durga Saptashati); Devi Bhagavata)
- **Marriage of Atri and Anasūyā** — Anasūyā, daughter of Kardama and Devahūti and sister of Kapila, becomes Atri's wife and the archetypal pativratā _(actors: Atri, Anasūyā, Kardama, Devahūti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/atri-anasuya.md) — (Bhāgavata 3.24.22–24)
- **Marriage of Cyavana and Sukanyā** — To appease the wronged sage, Śaryāti bestows his young daughter Sukanyā in marriage on the aged blind ascetic Cyavana, and she devotedly serves him _(actors: Cyavana, Sukanyā, Śaryāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 123; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5.7)
- **Marriage of Jaratkāru and Manasā (Vāsuki's sister)** — Vāsuki offers his sister—herself named Jaratkāru (later Manasā)—freely and undertakes her maintenance, fulfilling every condition, so the sage weds her to fulfil Brahmā's promise of a serpent-deliverer _(actors: Jaratkāru; Manasā/Jaratkāru; Vāsuki; the nāgas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaratkaru-and-manasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Āstīka sub-parva)
- **Marriage to Vrinda** — Jalandhara, crowned king of the asuras, weds the supremely chaste Vrinda whose pativratya makes him invincible _(actors: Jalandhara, Vrinda, Kalanemi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jalandhara-vrinda.md) — (Shiva Purana; Padma Purana)
- **Maya builds Tripura** — The asura-architect Maya constructs the three fortresses of gold, silver, and iron in heaven, air, and earth _(actors: Mayāsura (architect), the three asura brothers)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-dahana.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva)
- **Mārkaṇḍeya Initiated into the Mahā-Mṛtyuñjaya Mantra** — Foreseeing his death, Mārkaṇḍeya is initiated into (or composes) the Mahā-Mṛtyuñjaya mantra and devotes himself to ceaseless Shiva worship _(actors: Mārkaṇḍeya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Shiva Purana; Rigveda 7.59.12)
- **Nahuṣa Covets Śacī** — Corrupted by power, Nahuṣa lusts after Indra's queen Śacī and demands her; she takes refuge with Bṛhaspati and sets a trap-condition _(actors: Nahuṣa, Śacī, Bṛhaspati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nahusha.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva 13-17)
- **Nārada initiates Dhruva with the Vāsudeva mantra** — The sage Nārada tests and then instructs Dhruva, directing him to Madhuvana and bestowing the twelve-syllable mantra 'Oṃ Namo Bhagavate Vāsudevāya' — a canonical first-giving of the dvādaśākṣara mantra _(actors: Nārada, Dhruva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.11–12)
- **Pṛthu inherits the bow Ājagava** — In the Pṛthu-narrative, Śiva's celestial bow Ājagava descends as the royal bow inherited by Pṛthu, the first consecrated king, who uses it to compel the Earth to yield her bounty _(actors: Pṛthu, (Śiva as bow-source))_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa (Pṛthu cycle))
- **Pṛthu milks the Earth-cow; origin of agriculture** — Pṛthu chases the fugitive Earth as a cow, levels the land, and milks her of grains and herbs, whence Earth is named Pṛthvī _(actors: Pṛthu, Pṛthvī (Earth))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.17–18; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.13)
- **Puru and the founding of the Paurava line** — Yayati's son Puru accepts his father's old age, founding the Paurava line from which the Kurus descend _(actors: Yayati, Puru, Kuru)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/01-adi-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva 75-95)
- **Ruru gives half his lifespan to revive her** — A messenger of the gods offers that Pramadvarā will live if Ruru surrenders half his remaining lifespan; he consents and she rises, and they wed _(actors: Ruru, deva-dūta, Yama/Dharma, the gods, Pramadvarā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ruru-pramadvara.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva)
- **Ruru Revives Pramadvarā** — The Bhārgava youth Ruru gives half his own lifespan to revive his betrothed killed by snakebite, then vows to slay snakes until a serpent preaches ahiṃsā _(actors: Ruru, Pramadvarā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/minor-upakhyanas-catalog.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva)
- **Shiva's Cosmic Grief-Dance** — Maddened with sorrow, Shiva takes up Sati's charred corpse and roams the worlds in a tandava of grief that threatens to unbalance creation _(actors: Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/51-shakti-peethas.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana VII.30; Kalika Purana 18)
- **Svarocis rescues and marries Manorama** — Grown Svarocis saves the maiden Manorama from a demon with mantric arrows and weds her, later marrying her two companions who teach him secret vidyas _(actors: Svarocis, Manorama, Vibhavari, Kalavati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana 64)
- **Svarocis rescues Manorama and marries her** — Grown and trained, Svarocis saves the maiden Manorama and her companions from a demon using mantric arrows, then marries her _(actors: Svarocis, Manorama)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana)
- **The curse-backstories of Indradyumna and Hūhū revealed** — The slain crocodile and freed elephant are revealed as the cursed king Indradyumna and gandharva Hūhū, both liberated by Viṣṇu _(actors: Indradyumna, Hūhū, Agastya, Devala, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gajendra-moksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.4)
- **The Daksha-yajna and the insult to Shiva** — Daksha organizes a colossal yajna deliberately omitting Shiva and Sati and, when Sati attends, reviles Shiva before the assembly as a skull-bearing cremation-ground madman _(actors: Daksha, Sati, Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Bhagavata Purana IV.2-4; Shiva Purana; Vayu Purana)
- **The impossible price of 800 horses** — Irritated, Viśvāmitra demands 800 moon-white horses each with a single black ear (śyāmakarṇa) as fee _(actors: Viśvāmitra, Gālava)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/galava-madhavi.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva ~106)
- **The Kapila-gita — theistic Sankhya taught to Devahuti** — Kapila delivers a nine-chapter discourse on bhakti-yoga, the tattvas subordinated to Īśvara, aṣṭāṅga-yoga meditating on Viṣṇu's form, grades of devotion, Kāla, and the wheel of rebirth _(actors: Kapila, Devahūti (within Maitreya–Vidura frame))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kapila-devahuti.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.25–32)
- **The Māṇḍavya curse on Yama** — Wrongly impaled and surviving, the sage Māṇḍavya curses Yama to be born a man, a Śūdra woman's son, for unjustly punishing a child's act — fulfilled as Vidura _(actors: Aṇī-Māṇḍavya, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vidura-niti.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **The phantom-cow ruse (māyā-dhenu)** — An illusory dying cow enters Gautama's field and collapses dead when he shoos it, framing him for go-hatyā (cow-slaughter) _(actors: Gautama, the jealous ṛṣis, the māyā-cow (variant: Gaṇeśa as the cow))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/godavari-gautami-dakshina-ganga.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa (Gautamī-māhātmya); sthala-tradition)
- **The Prachetasas and Daksha's re-creation** — The ten Prachetasa sons emerge from austerity in the waters and, with Daksha, repopulate the world in the secondary creation _(actors: Prachetasas, Daksha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 2))
- **The Rishabha-gita teaching to his sons** — Before renouncing, Rishabha delivers a celebrated discourse that the body is meant for tapas and self-realization, not sense gratification, and that sadhu-sanga liberates _(actors: Rishabha, his hundred sons)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.5)
- **Ugrashravas re-tells the Mahabharata at Naimisha (outermost frame)** — Arriving from Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice, Ugrashravas recites the entire Mahabharata to Shaunaka's sages, forming the epic's outermost narrative layer _(actors: Ugrashravas, Shaunaka, the rishis, (Vaishampayana, Janamejaya offstage))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 1.1-1.4)
- **Vena slain and Prithu churned forth** — The tyrant Vena is slain by the rishis, who churn from his body the first righteous king Prithu, a Vishnu amshavatara who milks the Earth (Prithvi) of grain and becomes the model cakravartin _(actors: Vena, rishis, Prithu, Prithvi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 1))
- **Vishnu's boon and the fixing of the Pole Star** — Vishnu grants Dhruva the immovable celestial Dhruva-loka, making the North Star the model bhakta _(actors: Vishnu, Dhruva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.9, 4.12)
- **Vishnu slays Kalanemi and Indra slays Virochana** — In the Tarakamaya fighting Vishnu kills the asura Kalanemi and Indra kills Virochana, son of Prahlada _(actors: Vishnu, Kalanemi, Indra, Virochana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Brahmanda Purana)
- **Viṣṇu declares 'I am subject to My devotees'** — Viṣṇu refuses to recall the discus, uttering the bhakta-vātsalya verse and sending Durvāsā back to beg Ambarīṣa's pardon _(actors: Viṣṇu, Durvāsā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.4.63)
- **Viṣṇu rescues Gajendra and slays the crocodile** — Hearing the unsectarian cry, Viṣṇu flies on Garuḍa to the lake, lifts the elephant, and severs the crocodile's head with his Sudarśana Cakra, liberating Gajendra _(actors: Viṣṇu, Garuḍa, Gajendra, the crocodile)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gajendra-moksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.3)
- **Viṣṇu Tests Kuru and Grants the Liberation-Boon** — Viṣṇu tests Kuru by severing his limbs and head; satisfied, he grants that the land be named Kurukṣetra forever and that bathing, dying, or being dusted by it confers mokṣa _(actors: Kuru, Viṣṇu, Indra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kurukshetra-dharmakshetra.md) — (Vamana Purana, Kurukshetra-mahatmya)
- **Yajña assumes the office of Indra of the Svāyambhuva Manvantara** — The Viṣṇu-aṃśa Yajña takes the rotating throne of Indra/king of the devas for the first Manvantara — a rare case of the deva-kingship being held by an incarnation of Viṣṇu _(actors: Yajña (Yajñeśvara), the Yāma devas, Svāyambhuva Manu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yajna-avatara.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1, 8.1.20; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **Agastya curses King Indradyumna to be an elephant** — The backstory revealed: the Pāṇḍya king Indradyumna, absorbed in a silent vow, failed to honor the sage Agastya, who cursed him to be reborn as a dull elephant — the prior birth of Gajendra _(actors: Agastya, Indradyumna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gajendra-moksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.4.6–10)
- **Agastya Curses Nahuṣa to Become a Python** — Yoking the Saptarṣis to his palanquin and kicking Agastya while crying 'sarpa, sarpa,' Nahuṣa is cursed to fall from heaven as a python _(actors: Nahuṣa, Agastya, Saptarṣis)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nahusha.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva 17; Vana Parva 178; Bhagavata 6.13)
- **Ajita as Kurma at the churning** — In the Bhagavata frame the avatar Ajita of this manvantara bears Mount Mandara as the tortoise Kurma and distributes the amrita at the devas' churning of the ocean _(actors: Ajita/Kurma, devas, asuras)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Ambarīṣa prays the Sudarśana to spare Durvāsā** — The wronged king prays to the discus to spare his persecutor; the Sudarśana relents and the two reconcile over a feast _(actors: Ambarīṣa, Durvāsā, Sudarśana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.5)
- **Anasūyā halts the river by her vow** — By the power of her chastity-vow Anasūyā stops a river's flow (or ends a drought), proving satya-saṃkalpa overrides nature _(actors: Anasūyā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/atri-anasuya.md) — (Purāṇic Anasūyā cycle; Padma Purāṇa [regional])
- **Asura misrule** — After a thousand years the empowered asuras abandon dharma and oppress the worlds, provoking the gods _(actors: The Tripura asuras, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-dahana.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa (Rudra-saṃhitā))
- **Aśvins restore Cyavana's youth** — The Aśvins, after Sukanyā refuses their seduction, enter a magical lake with Cyavana so all three emerge as identical youths; Sukanyā chooses rightly and Cyavana is restored to youth, beauty, and sight _(actors: Aśvins, Cyavana, Sukanyā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 124; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5.8–13; Ṛgveda 1.116–117)
- **Birth of Pṛthu from Vena's Arms** — From Vena's purified arms the sages draw forth the radiant Pṛthu (with his queen Arci), bearing the cakra and lotus marks of a Viṣṇu aṃśa-avatāra _(actors: Pṛthu, Arci, the sages)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.15; Vishnu Purana 1.13)
- **Birth of Yajna and Dakshina to Akuti** — Manu's daughter Akuti marries rishi Ruci and bears twins Yajna (the era's Indra and a Vishnu amsa) and Dakshina, who becomes Yajna's wife; their sons are the twelve Yama gods _(actors: Akuti, Ruci, Yajna, Dakshina)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.1)
- **Brahma halts the war and restores Tara** — Facing cosmic ruin, Brahma intervenes and compels Soma to surrender Tara, who is returned to Brihaspati already pregnant _(actors: Brahma, Soma, Tara, Brihaspati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.6; Bhagavata Purana 9.14)
- **Budha weds Ilā and founds the Lunar Dynasty** — Budha weds Ilā and fathers Pururavas, first king of the Candravaṃśa, so the adulterous Tārā union seeds an entire royal lineage _(actors: Budha, Ilā, Pururavas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/the-gurus-brihaspati-and-shukra.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Bhāgavata; Devī Bhāgavata)
- **Daksha's curse on Chandra and the Moon's waxing and waning** — Chandra marries the 27 Nakshatras but favors Rohini, so Daksha curses him to waste away; the relented cyclic curse becomes the waxing and waning of the Moon _(actors: Chandra, Daksha, Rohini)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/navagraha.md) — (Mahabharata; Puranas)
- **Dattātreya teaches the 24 gurus to King Yadu** — The avadhūta Dattātreya answers King Yadu by recounting how he took 24 gurus from the natural world — earth, wind, python, courtesan Piṅgalā, spider, wasp and more — each yielding one lesson, freeing Yadu of attachment _(actors: Dattātreya, Yadu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.7–9 (Uddhava Gītā))
- **Devahuti's liberation and Kapila's departure** — Devahūti takes up bhakti-yoga, attains realization at the Sarasvatī (Siddhapada), and Kapila departs north-east to abide in samādhi by the sea _(actors: Devahūti, Kapila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kapila-devahuti.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.33)
- **Dhruva's great penance suffocates the worlds** — Through six months of ever-intensifying fasting and breath-suspension on one leg, Dhruva's concentrated heat chokes the three worlds, prompting the alarmed gods to appeal to Viṣṇu _(actors: Dhruva, the gods)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8–4.9; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.12)
- **Dhruva's war on the Yakṣas and final ascent** — Avenging his slain brother, Dhruva wars on Alakā until Manu stays his wrath; in old age he ascends to Dhruva-loka with his mother Sunīti _(actors: Dhruva, Svāyambhuva Manu, Kubera, Sunīti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.10–4.12)
