- **Cyavana restored to youth by the Ashvins** — The aged Bhargava is restored to youth by the Ashvins, who in return gain a share of the soma _(actors: Cyavana, Sukanya, the Ashvins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra)
- **Descent of the Gaṅgā (Gaṅgāvataraṇa)** — Bhagīratha's austerities bring Gaṅgā from heaven to redeem Sagara's sons' ashes; Śiva breaks her fall in his hair as Gaṅgādhara _(actors: Bhagīratha, Gaṅgā, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 42–44)
- **Jada Bharata teaches King Rahugana (Bharata-gita and forest allegory)** — Conscripted to carry Rahugana's palanquin and rebuked for his erratic gait, Jada Bharata breaks his silence with the Bharata-gita and the bhavatavi forest-of-samsara allegory, humbling the king _(actors: Jada Bharata, King Rahugana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.10-14)
- **Prithu's 100 horse-sacrifices and clash with Indra** — Indra repeatedly steals Prithu's sacrificial horse in disguises until Brahma brokers peace, after which the four Kumaras and Vishnu instruct Prithu, who delivers a discourse and retires to the forest _(actors: Prithu, Indra, Brahma, the four Kumaras, Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.19-23)
- **Yayāti rescues Devayānī from the well** — King Yayāti, hunting and thirsty, finds Devayānī in the well and lifts her out by her right hand, which she construes as a betrothal _(actors: Yayāti, Devayānī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kacha-devayani.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 78-81; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Śarmiṣṭhā enslaved to Devayānī** — Threatened with abandonment by his indispensable preceptor, Vṛṣaparvan gives his daughter Śarmiṣṭhā with a thousand maidens as a servant to the woman she wronged _(actors: Śarmiṣṭhā, Devayānī, Vṛṣaparvan, Śukrācārya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kacha-devayani.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 81; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Aruna hatched prematurely as Surya's charioteer** — The legless dawn-deity Aruna, hatched prematurely from Vinata's egg, becomes the charioteer of Surya _(actors: Aruna, Vinata, Surya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/navagraha.md) — (Mahabharata; Garuda Purana)
- **Birth of Ganesha and his beheading** — Parvati creates Ganesha from the paste of her own body; his beheading and elephant-head restoration follows as a parallel myth _(actors: Parvati, Ganesha, Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita)
- **Narada Curses Daksha's Sons to Renunciation** — Narada turns Daksha's sons the Haryashvas and Savalashvas to renunciation, earning Daksha's counter-curse that Narada wander forever _(actors: Narada, Daksha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 6.5)
- **The ten Prachetas perform underwater tapas** — The ten Prachetas brothers undertake 10,000 years of underwater tapas, receiving from Vishnu the boon to be progenitors of mankind _(actors: The ten Prachetas, Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.14-15; Bhagavata Purana 4.24-30)
- **Dadhichi gives his bones for the Vajra** — The sage gives his bones to forge Indra's Vajra weapon _(actors: Dadhichi, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva, Tirtha-yatra)
- **Marriage of Yayāti and Devayānī** — Śukra weds Devayānī to Yayāti on the binding condition that he never summon Śarmiṣṭhā, who enters the palace as part of the dowry-train _(actors: Yayāti, Devayānī, Śukrācārya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kacha-devayani.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 81-82; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Parvati becomes Gauri** — Taunted as dark, Parvati performs tapas to shed her dark complexion and emerges radiant as Gauri, the sloughed dark sheath becoming the goddess Kaushiki/Kali _(actors: Parvati (Gauri), Kaushiki/Kali)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana; Devi Mahatmya context)
- **Shiva teaches the Prachetas the Rudra-Gita** — Shiva (Rudra) appears to the Prachetas as they begin their austerity and teaches them the hymn of self-realization, the Rudra-Gita _(actors: Shiva, the Prachetas)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.24)
- **The Prachetas' quarrel with the trees and birth of the second Daksha** — Emerging to find the Earth overgrown, the Prachetas nearly burn the forests until Soma mediates and gives them the tree-born maiden Marisha, from whom the reborn Daksha is born _(actors: The Prachetas, Soma, Marisha, Daksha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.15; Bhagavata Purana 4.30)
- **The two queens bear five sons** — Yayāti secretly fathers children on Śarmiṣṭhā despite the oath; Devayānī bears Yadu and Turvaśu, Śarmiṣṭhā bears Druhyu, Anu, and Pūru — the breach that later provokes the curse of old age and splits the Lunar dynasty _(actors: Devayānī, Śarmiṣṭhā, Yayāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kacha-devayani.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 83-84; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Viśvāmitra wars with Vasiṣṭha over the wish-cow** — The kṣatriya king Viśvāmitra covets Vasiṣṭha's wish-cow Śabalā, wars with him and loses, then begins millennia of tapas to become a brahmarṣi _(actors: Viśvāmitra, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 51–65)
- **Vīrabhadra destroys Dakṣa's sacrifice** — After Satī self-immolates at her father Dakṣa's yajña, the grief-maddened Śiva creates Vīrabhadra, who storms the sacrifice and beheads Dakṣa; Satī's scattered limbs become the Śakti Pīṭhas _(actors: Śiva, Satī, Dakṣa, Vīrabhadra)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Kālikā Purāṇa; Vāyu Purāṇa)
- **Triśaṅku raised to heaven and the counter-heaven** — Viśvāmitra raises the outcast king Triśaṅku bodily to heaven and, when the gods cast him down, creates a counter-heaven holding him mid-sky _(actors: Viśvāmitra, Triśaṅku)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 57–60)
- **Birth of Budha and the Tara Scandal** — Candra abducts Tara, wife of Brihaspati, triggering the Tarakamaya war; Tara bears Budha of disputed paternity, and the Moon's waning is linked to a resulting curse _(actors: Candra, Tara, Brihaspati, Budha)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.6; Bhagavata IX.14)
- **Śunaḥśepa saved from sacrifice** — The human-sacrifice victim Śunaḥśepa is saved by mantras Viśvāmitra gives him at Ambarīṣa's rite _(actors: Śunaḥśepa, Viśvāmitra, Ambarīṣa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 61–62)
- **Dhruva's Penance at Madhuvana** — The boy Dhruva performs tapas at Dhruva-ṭīlā in Madhuvana, one of the twelve forests of Braj _(actors: Dhruva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (Vraja-mahatmya)
- **Menakā breaks Viśvāmitra's penance; birth of Śakuntalā** — The apsarā Menakā seduces Viśvāmitra, begetting Śakuntalā; he later conquers desire and anger to win the title Brahmarṣi _(actors: Menakā, Viśvāmitra, Śakuntalā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 63–65)
- **Savitri wins back Satyavan from Yama** — The devoted wife out-argues Yama to win back her husband's life _(actors: Savitri, Satyavan, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva, Pativrata-mahatmya Parva)
- **Daksha populates the worlds through his daughters** — Daksha Prajapati's daughters, married to the sages and to Kashyapa, become mothers of the Adityas (gods), Daityas, Danavas, animals, nagas and all living kinds; he later resorts to sexual generation _(actors: Daksha, Kashyapa, Aditi, Diti, Danu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.15, 1.21; Bhagavata Purana 6.6)
- **Indra seduces Ahalyā and is cursed** — Indra, disguised as the sage Gautama, seduces his wife Ahalyā; Gautama curses Indra and condemns Ahalyā to penance to be released only by Rāma _(actors: Indra, Ahalyā, Gautama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 48)
- **Galava and Madhavi** — Sage Galava lends out the princess Madhavi, who bears a king to each of four lords while regaining her virginity each time, to gather the guru-dakshina horses _(actors: Galava, Madhavi, Vishvamitra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva, Bhagavadyana Parva)
- **Yayati's Exchange of Old Age** — Cursed with premature old age by Shukra for wronging Devayani, Yayati borrows youth from his son Puru, later returns it and crowns Puru over the elder Yadu _(actors: Yayati, Shukra, Devayani, Puru, Yadu)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva; Vishnu Purana IV.10; Bhagavata IX.18-19)
- **Pururavas and Urvasi** — The Lunar-line tale of Pururavas and the apsara Urvasi, a morality story on lust and renunciation _(actors: Pururavas, Urvasi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9)
- **Sudyumna/Ila's Monthly Sex-Change** — Vaivasvata Manu's child enters Shiva's forbidden grove and alternates monthly between man (Sudyumna) and woman (Ila), branching the solar and lunar lines _(actors: Sudyumna, Ila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.1)
- **Nahusa kicked from heaven into serpenthood** — The over-proud Nahusa, made temporary Indra, is kicked from heaven by Agastya into serpenthood _(actors: Nahusa, Agastya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Anushasana/Santi Parva)
- **Reign of Svayambhuva, the first Manu** — Svayambhuva, the self-born spiritual son of Brahma, rules the first manvantara and is the reputed promulgator of the Manu Smriti _(actors: Svayambhuva Manu, Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Manu Smriti 1, Vishnu Purana 3.1)
- **Vaivasvata's sons found the royal lineages** — Vaivasvata Manu's sons found the great dynasties — Ikshvaku begins the Solar line and Ila/Sudyumna seeds the Lunar line through Pururavas _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Ikshvaku, Ila/Sudyumna)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.2, 4.1, Bhagavata Purana 9.1)
- **Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest (the Trimūrti test)** — The sage Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest in the Bhṛgu-pada test to decide the supreme god, cursing and blessing the Trimūrti accordingly and earning the Śrīvatsa mark _(actors: Bhṛgu, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.89; Padma Purāṇa)
- **Soma Abducts Tara and the Birth of Budha** — Soma abducts Brihaspati's wife Tara, Budha is born of the union, and the lunar dynasty begins _(actors: Soma, Tara, Budha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.14)
- **Vamana subdues Bali in the Vaivasvata manvantara** — The dwarf-brahmin Vamana, manvantara-avatara of the present age, reclaims the three worlds from the demon-king Bali in three steps and restores them to Indra Purandara _(actors: Vamana, Bali, Indra Purandara)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.15-23, Vishnu Purana 3.1)
- **Birth of the submarine fire from Aurva's wrath** — The seer Aurva's world-burning wrath against the kṣatriyas produces the submarine fire (Vāḍava), which is restrained into the ocean-mare's-mouth _(actors: Aurva)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Rantideva's Fourfold Charity** — After a 48-day fast, King Rantideva gives away his last food and water to a brahmana, a shudra, a man with dogs, and a chandala, and the testing Trimurti grant him liberation _(actors: Rantideva, Trimurti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.21)
- **The caru-swap of Ṛcīka and Satyavatī** — The brahmin and kṣatriya rice-cakes are exchanged in the marriage of Ṛcīka and Satyavatī, producing a martial brahmin line and a priestly king _(actors: Ṛcīka, Satyavatī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Mahābhārata; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Soma, Dattātreya and Durvāsas to Atri** — By the Trimūrti's boon, the sage Atri and his wife Anasūyā father three deities as sons: Soma (Candra), Dattātreya and Durvāsas _(actors: Atri, Anasūyā, Soma, Dattātreya, Durvāsas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Chandra from Atri** — Chandra is born to the sage Atri and his chaste wife Anasuya, welling from Atri's penetrating gaze/tears of austerity (in some versions as an amsa of Brahma), and is placed in the sky by Brahma _(actors: Atri, Anasuya, Chandra, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/chandra-soma.md) — (Vishnu, Bhagavata 4, Brahmanda Puranas)
- **Budha weds Ila and Pururavas is born** — Budha marries Ila (originally Sudyumna, Vaivasvata Manu's son cursed to alternate sexes), and their son Pururavas begins the human lunar dynasty (Aila line) _(actors: Budha, Ila/Sudyumna, Pururavas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/chandra-soma.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4; Bhagavata 9.14)
- **Indra grants the Puṣpaka and Uparicara Vasu's vimāna** — Indra grants King Uparicara Vasu a crystalline aerial car letting him move godlike through the sky _(actors: Indra, Uparicara Vasu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/vahanas-and-celestial-vehicles.md) — (Vimana (Wikipedia); Mahabharata)
- **Dakṣa-yajña: Satī's self-immolation and Dakṣa's beheading** — Satī self-immolates at her father Dakṣa's sacrifice; in the catastrophe Dakṣa is beheaded by Vīrabhadra and later restored with a goat's head _(actors: Dakṣa, Satī, Vīrabhadra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1–7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **Nārada cursed by Dakṣa to wander ceaselessly** — For persuading Dakṣa's sons to renounce procreation, Nārada is cursed by Dakṣa to wander the worlds eternally _(actors: Nārada, Dakṣa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.5)
- **Nārada converts the Haryaśvas to renunciation** — Dakṣa's first thousand sons, the Haryaśvas, sent to procreate, are dissuaded by Nārada's riddle and renounce and disperse forever _(actors: Nārada, Haryaśvas, Dakṣa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.5; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Nārada converts the Śabalāśvas** — Dakṣa's next thousand sons, the Śabalāśvas, are likewise converted by Nārada, enraging Dakṣa into cursing him, after which Dakṣa begets daughters instead _(actors: Nārada, Śabalāśvas, Dakṣa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.5; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Dakṣa's daughters wed Kaśyapa and breed all beings** — Dakṣa's daughters married to Kaśyapa (Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadrū, Vinatā and others) produce every class of being — devas, daityas, dānavas, nāgas, birds, beasts and more _(actors: Dakṣa, Kaśyapa, Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kadrū, Vinatā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.21; Bhāgavata 6.6)
- **Dakṣa gives 27 nakṣatra-daughters to Candra; the Moon's curse** — Dakṣa marries 27 daughters (the lunar mansions) to Candra, whose neglect of all but Rohiṇī provokes Dakṣa's curse that the Moon waxes and wanes, partly relieved at Prabhāsa _(actors: Dakṣa, Candra, Rohiṇī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.14; Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Nara-Nārāyaṇa to Mūrti and Dharma** — Dakṣa's daughter Mūrti, married to Dharma, mothers the twin sage-avatāra Nara-Nārāyaṇa of Viṣṇu _(actors: Mūrti, Dharma, Nara-Nārāyaṇa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1)
- **Satī reborn as Pārvatī** — After self-immolating at the Dakṣa-yajña, Dakṣa's daughter Satī, wife of Śiva, is reborn as Pārvatī _(actors: Satī, Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Bhāgavata 4.2–7)
- **Agastya's curse of Indradyumna** — King Indradyumna, a Pandya/Dravida devotee, is cursed by sage Agastya to be reborn as an elephant for a lapse of courtesy, becoming Gajendra _(actors: Agastya, Indradyumna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-04-tamasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana)
- **Devala's curse of the gandharva Huhu** — The gandharva Huhu is cursed by sage Devala to become a crocodile for seizing his leg in the water, becoming the graha that attacks Gajendra _(actors: Devala, Huhu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-04-tamasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana)

## Satya (Kṛta) Yuga — current 28th Mahāyuga  ·  307 events

*Dharma on four legs. The early avatars and the churning of the ocean.*

- **Anasūyā restores the sun and revives Kauśika** — honouring the pativratā, Anasūyā releases the dawn with the arghya at the tenth midnight, so Kauśika dies by the curse and is at once raised up young, whole, and free of leprosy _(actors: Anasūyā, Kauśika's wife, Kauśika)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anasuya-halted-sunrise.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa XVI)
- **Anasūyā's boon: the Trimūrti as her sons** — grateful for the restored world-clock, the gods grant Anasūyā's request that Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva be born as her sons and that she and Atri attain liberation _(actors: Anasūyā, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anasuya-halted-sunrise.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa XVI)
- **Anasūyā's clay liṅga outweighs Atri's trance** — while Atri sits fifty-four years in prāṇāyāma-samādhi, Anasūyā fashions an earthen liṅga by mantra and worships without pause, her service adjudged by the gods greater than the sage's penance _(actors: Anasūyā, Atri, the devas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kotirudra-minor-linga-legends.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Koṭirudra-saṃhitā 3)
- **Apsarās arise from the Samudra Manthana** — The celestial nymphs arise from the churned waters between devas and asuras; claimed by neither side, they become common (sādhāraṇa) to all _(actors: Apsarās, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/apsaras.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.9; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 45; Mahābhārata)
- **Aurva arms Sagara with the Āgneyāstra** — The Bhārgava sage performs the exiled prince's rites, teaches him Veda and arms, and bestows the fire-weapon of his reconquest _(actors: Aurva, Sagara)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/sagara.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.3)
- **Avatara of Mahotkata Vinayaka** — Ganesha descends in Satya Yuga as the ten-armed lion-mounted Mahotkata Vinayaka and slays the demon-brothers Narantaka and Devantaka (and Dhumraksha) _(actors: Ganesha (Mahotkata Vinayaka), Narantaka, Devantaka, Dhumraksha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/ganesha-and-mudgala-upapuranas.md) — (Ganesha Purana (Krida-khanda))
- **Avīkṣit abducts Vaiśāliṇī** — Karandhama's son seizes the princess of Vaiśālī at her svayaṃvara and carries her off, defeating the assembled suitor-kings _(actors: Avīkṣit, Vaiśāliṇī/Vishālā, the suitor-kings)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karandhama-avikshit-marutta-dama.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, Canto CXXII)
- **Avīkṣit captured and rescued** — the humiliated suitor-kings combine, defeat Avīkṣit and take him prisoner, until his father Karandhama comes to the field and frees him _(actors: Avīkṣit, the suitor-kings, Karandhama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karandhama-avikshit-marutta-dama.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, Cantos CXXIII–CXXIV)
- **Bhagīratha renounces before bringing the Gaṅgā** — In the Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha telling Bhagīratha gives his kingdom away, begs unrecognized in his own capital, attains knowledge under Tritala, and only then performs the tapas that brings Gaṅgā to earth _(actors: Bhagīratha, Tritala, Gaṅgā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yoga-vasishtha-tales-catalog.md) — (Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha V–VI, Upaśama/Nirvāṇa)
- **Bhṛgu's boon and the gourd-birth of the 60,000** — After a hundred years' tapas Bhṛgu grants Keśinī one dynastic son (Asamañja) and Sumati sixty thousand sons, born from a gourd and reared in jars of ghee _(actors: Sagara, Bhṛgu, Keśinī, Sumati)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/sagara.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 38)
- **Bhū-Varāha lifts the Earth at Śrīmuṣṇam** — Viṣṇu as the Boar slays the demon Hiraṇyākṣa and lifts Bhū-devī from the cosmic ocean on his tusk, the deed the kṣetra localizes _(actors: Viṣṇu (Bhū-Varāha), Bhū-devī (Earth-goddess), Hiraṇyākṣa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/avatara-kshetras-srikurmam-srimushnam.md) — (Varāha Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.13–19; Śrīmuṣṇa-māhātmya)
- **Birth of Ekādaśī-devī and the slaying of Mura (Utpannā)** — a radiant śakti springs from the sleeping Viṣṇu at Badarikāśrama, slays the daitya Mura of Candrāvatī, and is granted the eleventh tithi as her own, founding the Ekādaśī fast _(actors: Viṣṇu, Ekādaśī-devī, Mura, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ekadashi-mahatmyas-catalog.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa 38) [late text]
- **Birth of Ekavīra the mare-born** — Śiva's boon lets Viṣṇu approach the mare-Lakṣmī as a horse; their son Ekavīra (Haihaya) is left on earth and raised by the childless king Śatajit _(actors: Viṣṇu, Lakṣmī, Śiva, Ekavīra, Śatajit)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ekavira-ekavali-haihaya-origin.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa VI.16–19)
- **Birth of Nara–Nārāyaṇa to Dharma and Mūrti** — The twin sage-avatāra of Viṣṇu are born to the prajāpati Dharma and his wife Mūrti (var. Ahiṃsā), among the ascetic offspring of Dharma's line _(actors: Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Dharma, Mūrti/Ahiṃsā, Dakṣa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nara-narayana.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1)
- **Birth of Soma, Dattātreya, and Durvāsas** — three sons are born to Anasūyā as guṇa-portions: Soma (Brahmā), Dattātreya the sattva-brahman (Viṣṇu), and Durvāsas the tamas-ascetic (Śiva) _(actors: Anasūyā, Atri, Soma, Dattātreya, Durvāsas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anasuya-halted-sunrise.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa XVII)
- **Cīnācāra from Viṣṇu-as-Buddha** — in Mahācīna Vasiṣṭha finds the Buddha (Viṣṇu's Buddha-form) amid the pañca-makāra and, past his brāhmaṇa revulsion, is initiated into Cīnācāra / Vāmācāra and at last attains Tārā's darśana and siddhi _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, Viṣṇu-Buddha, Tārā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tarapith-tara-vashishtha-bamakhepa.md) — (Rudrayāmala Tantra; Tārā Tantra) [tantra] [disputed]
- **Dama wins Sumanā of Daśārṇa** — Nariṣyanta's son Dama is chosen at the svayaṃvara of the Daśārṇa princess Sumanā and defeats the rival suitor-kings who unlawfully oppose the match _(actors: Dama, Sumanā, the suitor-kings, Nariṣyanta)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karandhama-avikshit-marutta-dama.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, Cantos CXXXIII–CXXXIV)
- **Dama's blood-libation śrāddha** — fulfilling his vow, Dama slays Vapuṣmat and performs his father's funeral rites with the murderer's own flesh and blood, feasting rākṣasa-descended brāhmaṇas — the Purāṇa's grim close _(actors: Dama, Vapuṣmat, Nariṣyanta's spirit)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karandhama-avikshit-marutta-dama.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, Canto CXXXVI)
- **Danda's curse and the origin of Dandakaranya** — Ikshvaku's son Danda violates Araja, daughter of guru Shukracharya, who buries his kingdom under seven days of dust, creating the wilderness named Dandaka-aranya _(actors: Danda, Araja, Shukracharya (Ushanas))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kamyaka-dvaita-pandava-exile-forests.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana Uttara-kanda 79-81; Brahmanda Purana; Vishnu Purana 4)
- **Dattātreya's Triloki-tilaka mantra** — the sage Dattātreya initiates Ekavīra into the Yogeśvarī-mahāmantra granting unobstructed travel through the three worlds _(actors: Dattātreya, Ekavīra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ekavira-ekavali-haihaya-origin.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa VI.20–21)
- **Dhanvantari rises from the Samudra Manthana** — When devas and asuras churn the Ocean of Milk with Mount Mandara and Vasuki, Dhanvantari rises bearing the pot of amrita, precipitating the deva-asura war over the nectar _(actors: Dhanvantari, devas, asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dhanvantari.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.8; Vishnu Purana 1.9; Ramayana Bala-kanda 45)
- **Durvāsā's curse launches the ocean-churning** — the spurned garland-curse drains the devas' strength, forcing the Samudra Manthana for amṛta _(actors: Durvāsā, Indra, the devas)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/tapas-boons-and-curses.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.9)
- **Ekavīra slays Kālaketu** — descending to Pātāla by the mantra's power, Haihaya breaks Kālaketu's army and strikes the daitya dead with his mace, freeing Ekāvalī _(actors: Ekavīra/Haihaya, Kālaketu, Ekāvalī)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ekavira-ekavali-haihaya-origin.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa VI.23)
- **Exile of Asamañja** — Sagara banishes his own heir for drowning the townsmen's children in the Sarayū, keeping the virtuous grandson Aṃśumān as successor _(actors: Sagara, Asamañja, Aṃśumān)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/sagara.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 38; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.4)
- **First jalabhisheka on Nilakantha** — After Shiva drinks the Halahala of the churning, the devas pour Ganga water over him to cool the poison's burning — the charter-act the Kanwar Yatra re-enacts [folk] _(actors: Shiva, Parvati, Devas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kanwar-yatra-and-shravan-shiva-observances.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7; devotional gloss)
- **Haihaya–Tālajaṅgha overthrow of Bāhu** — King Bāhu of Ayodhyā is dethroned by the Haihaya–Tālajaṅgha clans with their Śaka, Yavana, Kāmboja, Pārada and Pahlava confederates, and dies in forest exile _(actors: Bāhu, Haihayas, Tālajaṅghas)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/sagara.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.3; Harivaṃśa 13–14)
- **Hiraṇyakaśipu's boon and persecution of Prahlāda** — The daitya king Hiraṇyakaśipu wins a near-invincibility boon from Brahmā and persecutes his Vishnu-devoted son Prahlāda _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda, Brahmā, Vishnu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/simhachalam-varaha-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata-Purāṇa skandha 7; Vishnu Purāṇa 1)
- **Hiraṇyakaśipu's lattice boon** — anthill-buried tapas compels Brahmā to grant death by no man, beast, weapon, time or place, the loophole answered by Narasiṃha _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Brahmā, Narasiṃha, Prahlāda)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/tapas-boons-and-curses.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.3–8)
- **Ikṣvāku taught by Manu** — Rāma's ancestor, first Solar king, asks what lies beyond decay and receives from Manu the vision of one consciousness and the seven bhūmikās of knowledge _(actors: Ikṣvāku, Manu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yoga-vasishtha-tales-catalog.md) — (Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha VI.1, Nirvāṇa Pūrvārdha)
- **Ilā born of a flawed rite** — Vaivasvata Manu's sacrifice to Mitra-Varuṇa for a son miscarries and yields a daughter, Ilā, whom Vasiṣṭha's prayer then converts into the boy Sudyumna _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Vasiṣṭha, Mitra-Varuṇa, Ilā/Sudyumna)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ila-sudyumna.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.1; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.1)
- **Ila of Bāhlī and the kiṃpuruṣa origin** — in the Rāmāyaṇa's version Ila, son of Kardama, is feminised in Śiva's grove, and Budha turns Ila's transformed retinue into the kiṃpuruṣa people before an Aśvamedha to Rudra restores Ila to permanent maleness _(actors: Ila, Kardama, Budha, Rudra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ila-sudyumna.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Jalodbhava slain, Kashmir drained** — Kaśyapa's austerities bring the gods, the barrier at Varāhamūla (Baramulla) is breached, and Viṣṇu slays the water-demon Jalodbhava on drained ground, naming the land Kaśmīra _(actors: Kaśyapa, Jalodbhava, Viṣṇu, Nīla-nāga)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kashmir-tirthas-nilamata-geography.md) — (Nīlamata Purāṇa; Rājataraṅgiṇī 1.25–27)
- **Jaya–Vijaya born as Hiraṇyakaśipu (birth #1)** — Viṣṇu's cursed Vaikuṇṭha gatekeepers incarnate as the daitya brothers Hiraṇyākṣa and Hiraṇyakaśipu, the first of three demonic births _(actors: Jaya, Vijaya, Diti, Kaśyapa, Sanaka-kumāras, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.1–7.2; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.17)
- **Kālaketu abducts Ekāvalī** — the daitya Kālaketu seizes the Devī-devotee princess Ekāvalī, daughter of King Raibhya, and carries her to Pātāla _(actors: Kālaketu, Ekāvalī, Raibhya)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ekavira-ekavali-haihaya-origin.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa VI.22)
- **Karandhama's sigh-born army** — attacked with no host to defend him, King Balāsva exhales a whole phantom army out of his own body and routs his enemies, winning the name Karandhama by this "fanciful victory" _(actors: Balāsva/Karandhama, Khaninetra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karandhama-avikshit-marutta-dama.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, Canto CXXI)
- **Kavaṣa Ailūṣa followed by the Sarasvatī** — cast into the desert by ṛṣis as a slave-woman's son, Kavaṣa praises the Waters and the river Sarasvatī flows out after him, proving him a true seer _(actors: Kavaṣa Ailūṣa, the ṛṣis, Sarasvatī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/brahmana-legends-catalog.md) — (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 2.19)
- **Keśin Dārbhya and the ghost Kaupayeya** — the Pañcāla sage-king is taught hidden chant-knowledge and the fate of the dead by the preta of Kaupayeya, a spirit instructing the living _(actors: Keśin Dārbhya, the ghost Kaupayeya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/brahmana-legends-catalog.md) — (Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa 2.269–272)
- **Khanitra and the recoiling kṛtyā** — the minister Viśvavedin sets four rebel brothers' purohitas to raise a four-fold sorcery-deity against the beneficent king Khanitra, but his store of merit alone repels it and it falls back to destroy its own senders _(actors: Khanitra, Viśvavedin, Śauri, Suhotra, Kusāvartta, Pramati, Vāsiṣṭha)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/markandeya-vaivasvata-king-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 117–118)
- **Khanitra's grieving renunciation** — victorious without lifting a hand yet stricken that his kinsmen and their priests died on his account, Khanitra resigns the kingdom to his son and withdraws to the forest with his queen _(actors: Khanitra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/markandeya-vaivasvata-king-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 118)
- **Kilāta and Ākuli trick Manu** — two Asura priests con Manu into sacrificing first his demon-slaying bull, then his wife Manāvī, but the slaying-voice escapes into the sacrifice itself _(actors: Manu, Manāvī, Kilāta, Ākuli)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/brahmana-legends-catalog.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.1.4.14–17)
- **King Camatkāra founds Camatkārapura** — the Ānarta king Camatkāra builds and endows a town, gifting it to Brāhmaṇas, which is named Camatkārapura (later Vaḍnagar) after its royal donor _(actors: King Camatkāra of Ānarta, the Brāhmaṇas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/vadnagar-hatakeshvara-kshetra.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa, Nāgara-khaṇḍa)
- **Kubera's Rākṣasas rout the king's army** — Vaiśravaṇa looses a host of Rākṣasas that overwhelms and slaughters Mucukunda's forces, humbling the earth-conqueror against powers no weapon can touch _(actors: Vaiśravaṇa, the Rākṣasas, Mucukunda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mucukunda-vaishravana-shanti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Śānti Parva 12.75)
- **Lakṣmī cursed to a mare's body** — distracted by Revanta on Uccaiḥśravas, Lakṣmī ignores Viṣṇu and is cursed to be born on earth as a mare _(actors: Lakṣmī, Viṣṇu, Revanta, Uccaiḥśravas)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ekavira-ekavali-haihaya-origin.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa VI.16–19)
- **Madhu & Kaiṭabha Slain** — Two primordial Dānava brothers born from Viṣṇu's ear menace Brahmā and steal the Vedas, slain by Viṣṇu after the Goddess Yoganidrā withdraws her sleep-spell; their fat forms the earth _(actors: Madhu, Kaiṭabha, Viṣṇu, Yoganidrā, Brahmā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Devī Māhātmya 1; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; Mahābhārata)
- **Māṇḍavya's sunrise-curse on Kauśika** — the impaled sage Māṇḍavya, spurned by the leprous brahmin Kauśika of Pratiṣṭhāna on the night-road, curses him to die the instant the sun rises _(actors: Māṇḍavya, Kauśika)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anasuya-halted-sunrise.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa XVI)
- **Marriage and the seed of the Haihayas** — King Raibhya weds Ekāvalī to Ekavīra; she bears Kṛtavīrya, founding the Haihaya line that culminates in Kārtavīrya Arjuna _(actors: Ekavīra, Ekāvalī, Raibhya, Kṛtavīrya)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ekavira-ekavali-haihaya-origin.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa VI.23)
- **Marutta the universal monarch** — Avīkṣit's son is consecrated where his father refused, becoming a cakravartin, a great sacrificer and lavish patron of brāhmaṇas _(actors: Marutta, Avīkṣit)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karandhama-avikshit-marutta-dama.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, Cantos CXXVIII–CXXIX)
- **Marutta's golden sacrifice** — Marutta Āvīkṣita performs the enormous yajña (priest Saṃvarta) whose buried Himālayan gold the Pāṇḍavas later recover to fund Yudhiṣṭhira's horse-sacrifice _(actors: Marutta, Saṃvarta, Bṛhaspati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karandhama-avikshit-marutta-dama.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa CXXXI; Mahābhārata, Aśvamedhika Parva)
- **Marutta's Nāga war averted** — Marutta marches on the troublesome Nāgas, but his father Avīkṣit interposes on their behalf and the ṛṣis avert the battle, the Nāgas making reparation _(actors: Marutta, Avīkṣit, the Nāgas, the ṛṣis)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karandhama-avikshit-marutta-dama.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, Canto CXXX)
- **Matsya avatara and the great deluge** — Vishnu as a fish warns Vaivasvata Manu of the world-ending flood, tows his boat (Saptarshi, seeds, creatures) to safety via Vasuki tied to his horn, and slays Hayagriva to recover the stolen Vedas _(actors: Vishnu (Matsya), Vaivasvata Manu, Saptarshi, Vasuki, Hayagriva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana 8.24; Shatapatha Brahmana)
- **Matsya saves Manu from the deluge flood** — A tiny fish begging Manu's protection grows monstrous and reveals itself as Vishnu, warns of the deluge, and tows Manu's ark — loaded with the seeds of beings, the seven rishis and the Vedas — to safety, then narrates the Purana _(actors: Vishnu (Matsya), Manu Vaivasvata, the seven rishis)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/matsya-purana.md) — (Matsya Purana (frame))
- **Mithi churned from Nimi's body; Mithilā founded** — Fearing anarchy, the ṛṣis churn Nimi's preserved corpse and a son emerges — Janaka by birth, Vaideha as son of the bodiless, Mithila from the churning — who builds the city Mithilā _(actors: Mithi/Janaka the first, the ṛṣis)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/videha-mithila-line-janaka.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.13.13; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.5)
- **Mithi churned from the bodiless king** — fearing anarchy, the ṛṣis churn Nimi's preserved body to produce a son named Janaka (from birth), Vaideha (from the bodiless father), and Mithi (from churning), who founds Mithilā _(actors: the ṛṣis, Mithi/Janaka)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/nimi-vasishtha-mutual-curse.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.5; Bhāgavata IX.13)
- **Mucukunda challenges Vaiśravaṇa** — not content with the mortal world, Mucukunda sends a challenge to Kubera, lord of Alakā and guardian of the north, imagining kṣatra can measure itself against a lokapāla _(actors: Mucukunda, Vaiśravaṇa/Kubera)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mucukunda-vaishravana-shanti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Śānti Parva 12.75)
- **Mucukunda conquers the earth by his own arms** — the Ikṣvāku emperor Mucukunda subjugates the whole earth through personal prowess, priding himself on the might of his two arms _(actors: Mucukunda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mucukunda-vaishravana-shanti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Śānti Parva 12.75)
- **Mucukunda refuses the earth as a gift** — Vaiśravaṇa offers to bestow dominion, but Mucukunda declines sovereignty as charity, holding a Kṣatriya must enjoy rule won by his own valour _(actors: Vaiśravaṇa, Mucukunda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mucukunda-vaishravana-shanti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Śānti Parva 12.75)
- **Mucukunda reproaches Vasiṣṭha** — stung by defeat, the king turns on his purohita Vasiṣṭha, asking what use is a Brahmaṇa priest if the king is still crushed in war _(actors: Mucukunda, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mucukunda-vaishravana-shanti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Śānti Parva 12.75)
- **Mudāvatī renamed Sunandā** — after the kill the serpent-king Śeṣa takes the club Sunanda and gives the rescued princess Mudāvatī the new name Sunandā after it, whom Vatsaprī then weds _(actors: Śeṣa/Ananta, Mudāvatī, Vatsaprī)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/markandeya-vaivasvata-king-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 116)
- **Nābhāga's accepted caste-fall** — the kṣatriya prince Nābhāga abducts an unnamed vaiśya maiden by the Rākṣasa rite against the ṛṣis' counsel, and when a wandering muni rules he has thereby fallen to vaiśya-hood, he keeps the wife and wears the demotion without repenting _(actors: Nābhāga, Diṣṭa, the vaiśya maiden, a muni)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/markandeya-vaivasvata-king-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 113–115)
- **Nābhānediṣṭha and Rudra's leavings** — Manu's disinherited son wins cattle for teaching the Aṅgirases to reach heaven, then truthfully cedes them to a dark Rudra who, pleased, returns them _(actors: Nābhānediṣṭha, Manu, the Aṅgirases, Rudra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/brahmana-legends-catalog.md) — (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 5.14)
- **Namuci's loophole-boon and Indra's twilight betrayal** — The Dānava Namuci wins a boon making him slayable by neither wet nor dry, neither day nor night, by no weapon, on neither land nor water; Indra swears a truce/friendship with him, then betrays it by decapitating him at twilight on the shore using sea-foam (apām phena) wrapped on the vajra as the boon-evading instrument _(actors: Indra, Namuci)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Ṛgveda 5.30, 8.14; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 12.7.3; Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva; Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa)
- **Narasiṃha bursts from the pillar at Ahobilam** — Challenged to show Vishnu in the pillar, Hiraṇyakaśipu strikes it and Narasiṃha erupts on the Ahobilam hill to void the boon _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Narasiṃha (Vishnu), Prahlāda)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ahobilam-nava-narasimha.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Ahobila-māhātmya); Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7; Vishnu Purāṇa 1)
- **Nimi and Vasiṣṭha's mutual curse** — Supplanted at Nimi's sacrifice, Vasiṣṭha curses the king's body to fall and Nimi curses him back, leaving both bodiless _(actors: Nimi, Vasiṣṭha, Indra, Gautama)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/videha-mithila-line-janaka.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.13; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.5)
- **Nimi refuses re-embodiment** — his corpse kept in unguents through the sattra, Nimi declines the gods' offer to restore his body, calling embodiment bondage, and asks instead to dwell among living beings _(actors: Nimi, the devas)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/nimi-vasishtha-mutual-curse.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 57; Bhāgavata IX.13)
- **Nimi refuses re-embodiment and dwells in the blink** — Offered his body back by the gods, Nimi declines embodiment as bondage and is granted residence in the eyes of all creatures — the blink (nimeṣa) etymology _(actors: Nimi, the gods)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/videha-mithila-line-janaka.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.13.8–12)
- **Nimi's thousand-year sattra and Vasiṣṭha's prior retainer** — Ikṣvāku's son Nimi engages the family priest Vasiṣṭha, who is already retained by Indra and bids him wait; Nimi, holding life fleeting, begins the rite with Gautama instead _(actors: Nimi, Vasiṣṭha, Indra, Gautama)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/nimi-vasishtha-mutual-curse.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 55–56)
- **Poison-birth of Sagara at Aurva's āśrama** — Aurva stops Bāhu's poisoned widow from ascending the pyre; her son is born together with the poison and named Sa-gara, "with the gara" _(actors: Sagara, Aurva, Bāhu's queen)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/sagara.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.3; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.8)
- **Prahlāda charges the armed ascetics with hypocrisy** — finding two matted-haired sages in antelope skins beside the divine bows Śārṅga and Ājagava, Prahlāda condemns their mixing of tapas and weapons as dambha; Nara replies that for the truly capable the two are one authority _(actors: Prahlāda, Nara, Nārāyaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-nara-narayana-battle.md) — (Vāmana Purāṇa; Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa IV.9)
- **Prahlāda's pilgrimage to Naimiṣa** — counseled by Cyavana that inner purity outranks any tīrtha, the Daitya sovereign Prahlāda leads the Daityas and Dānavas from Rasātala to Naimiṣāraṇya to bathe in the Sarasvatī _(actors: Prahlāda, Cyavana, the Daityas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-nara-narayana-battle.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa IV.8; Vāmana Purāṇa)
- **Prahlāda's self-awakening (Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha version)** — Prahlāda attains realization by his own inquiry and sinks into nirvikalpa absorption so deep the asura realm falls into disorder, until Viṣṇu wakes him and bids him rule as a jīvanmukta _(actors: Prahlāda, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yoga-vasishtha-tales-catalog.md) — (Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha V, Upaśama prakaraṇa)
- **Prahlāda's submission at Badarikāśrama** — the humbled asura renounces his kingdom to Andhaka, journeys to Badarī, hymns Nārāyaṇa as Acyuta, Varāha and Narasiṃha, and is granted freedom from karmic bondage _(actors: Prahlāda, Nārāyaṇa, Andhaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-nara-narayana-battle.md) — (Vāmana Purāṇa)
- **Prahlāda's yajña at Manchāle (Mantrālayam)** — Mādhva tradition holds the Tuṅgabhadrā site of Rāghavendra's future bṛndāvana to be the ground where Prahlāda performed a sacrifice in Kṛta Yuga [traditional] _(actors: Prahlāda)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/raghavendra-tirtha-and-the-dvaita-line.md) — (Mantrālayam maṭha tradition)
- **Rājyavardhana's ten-thousand-year youth** — after a grey hair at seven thousand years his subjects win him a Sun-boon of ten millennia of enduring youth, but the king despairs at outliving everyone until a second penance extends the long life to all his people together _(actors: Rājyavardhana, Sūrya, queen Māninī, his subjects)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/markandeya-vaivasvata-king-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 109–110)
- **Sagara installs Aṃśumān and departs to heaven** — After a reign of thirty thousand years, with his 60,000 sons still unredeemed ash, Sagara enthrones his grandson and ascends, leaving the Gaṅgā-labor to Bhagīratha's generation _(actors: Sagara, Aṃśumān, Bhagīratha)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/sagara.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 42; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.4)
- **Sagara's Aśvamedha and Indra's theft of the horse** — Emperor Sagara performs a horse-sacrifice; Indra, fearing his merit, steals the horse and hides it at Kapila's āśrama in Pātāla _(actors: Sagara, Indra, Kapila, queens Keśinī and Sumati)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gangasagar-sagara-dvipa-kapila-ashram.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 38–40; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.8)
- **Sagara's reconquest of Ayodhyā** — Sagara all but exterminates the Haihaya–Tālajaṅgha power and recovers the Ikṣvāku empire, fulfilling his vow of vengeance _(actors: Sagara, Haihayas, Tālajaṅghas)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/sagara.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.3; Harivaṃśa 14)
- **Samudra Manthana and the Spilling of Amṛta** — The churning of the ocean of milk produces the kumbha of amrita; in the ensuing fight, drops spill at four earthly sites that become the Kumbh Mela cities _(actors: devas, asuras, Viṣṇu, Garuḍa, Dhanvantari)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kumbh-mela-and-pilgrimage-cycles.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana; Britannica)
- **Samudra Manthana — emergence of the fourteen ratnas** — The Devas and Asuras churn the milk-ocean using Mt. Mandara and the serpent Vāsuki, drawing up the fourteen ratnas including Amṛta, Kāmadhenu, Kalpavṛkṣa, Kaustubha, Airāvata, Uccaiḥśravas and Lakṣmī _(actors: Devas, Asuras, Vāsuki, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.9)
- **Śiva roots as Atrīśvara and Gaṅgā fills the kuṇḍa** — Śiva manifests from the clay liṅga and stays permanently as Atrīśvara, while Gaṅgā, given a year of Anasūyā's worship-merit, abides in the sacred pit, ending the drought _(actors: Śiva, Atrīśvara, Gaṅgā, Anasūyā, Atri)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kotirudra-minor-linga-legends.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Koṭirudra-saṃhitā 4.43–56)
- **Sudyumna's abdication and liberation** — deemed unfit to reign as a half-time woman, Sudyumna cedes the throne to Purūravas and retires to the forest to attain liberation _(actors: Sudyumna, Purūravas, Nārada)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ila-sudyumna.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.1)
- **Sudyumna's three regional sons** — in his male months Sudyumna fathers Utkala, Gaya, and Vinatāśva (Bhāgavata: Vimala), eponyms of Utkala/Odisha, Gayā, and the western marches _(actors: Sudyumna, Utkala, Gaya, Vinatāśva)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ila-sudyumna.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.1; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.1.42)
- **Surabhi Churned from the Ocean of Milk** — Surabhi/Kāmadhenu rises among the fourteen ratnas churned from the Ocean of Milk, and Brahmā assigns her to yield the milk and ghee of Vedic sacrifice, giving her to the seven ṛṣis _(actors: Surabhi/Kāmadhenu, Brahmā, seven ṛṣis)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/kamadhenu-and-divine-cattle.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu and Bhāgavata Purāṇas)
- **The Devī names the rescuer** — Ekāvalī's companion Yaśovatī worships Caṇḍikā, who appears in a dream and directs her to the Goddess's devotee King Ekavīra/Haihaya _(actors: Yaśovatī, Caṇḍikā/Devī, Ekāvalī, Ekavīra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ekavira-ekavali-haihaya-origin.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa VI.22)
- **The Gaupāyanas recall Subandhu's soul** — after Āsura sorcerers hired by king Asamāti kill Subandhu, his three brothers chant his departed life-breath back from Yama and the sky, and he revives _(actors: Bandhu, Subandhu, Śrutabandhu, Viprabandhu, Asamāti, Kirāta, Ākuli)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/brahmana-legends-catalog.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.57–60; Bṛhaddevatā 7.83–102)
- **The gods beg Brahmā, who sends them to Anasūyā** — with sacrifices and seasons collapsing, the gods appeal to Brahmā, who cannot overrule a faithful wife and directs them to propitiate Atri's wife Anasūyā _(actors: the devas, Brahmā, Anasūyā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anasuya-halted-sunrise.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa XVI)
- **The hundred-year drought in the Kāmada forest** — a century-long drought parches the forest of Kāmada by Citrakūṭa, driving the saptarṣi Atri and his wife Anasūyā to penance for relief _(actors: Atri, Anasūyā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kotirudra-minor-linga-legends.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Koṭirudra-saṃhitā 3)
- **The imposed marks on the Śakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas** — At Vasiṣṭha's intercession Sagara spares the foreign hosts but strips their dharma and brands them with shaven heads, half-shaven heads, loose hair and beards, making them mlecchas _(actors: Sagara, Vasiṣṭha, Śakas, Yavanas, Pahlavas)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/sagara.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.3; Vāyu Purāṇa 88)
- **The king who refused his crown** — so shamed by having been captured, Avīkṣit refuses to be consecrated king; the impasse breaks only when his son Marutta is born to succeed him _(actors: Avīkṣit, Vaiśāliṇī, Marutta)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karandhama-avikshit-marutta-dama.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, Cantos CXXV–CXXVII)
- **The Matsya flood and Manu's survival** — Vishnu as the Fish warns Vaivasvata Manu of a world-dissolving deluge, has him build a boat carrying the seven sages, seeds, and creatures, and tows it to a Himalayan peak by a horn on the fish's head, preserving the seeds of life into the new age _(actors: Matsya/Vishnu, Vaivasvata Manu (Satyavrata), the Saptarishi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/README.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1; Mahabharata Vana Parva 3.186; Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **The monthly alternation granted** — Vasiṣṭha propitiates Śiva, who cannot revoke his decree but compromises: Sudyumna will be male one month and female the next for life _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, Śiva, Sudyumna/Ilā)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ila-sudyumna.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.1.38–40; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.1)
- **The Nārasiṃha war (first saṅgrāma)** — Viṣṇu as the Man-Lion slays the boon-armored Daitya emperor Hiraṇyakaśipu at twilight for his devotee-son Prahlāda _(actors: Viṣṇu as Narasiṃha, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/twelve-devasura-battles.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa 47; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7)
- **The Nava-Yogendras arrive at Nimi's sattra** — Ṛṣabha's nine avadhūta sons appear at the Videha king's sacrifice and answer his nine questions on bhāgavata-dharma _(actors: Nimi, Kavi, Havi, Antarīkṣa, Prabuddha, Pippalāyana, Āvirhotra, Drumila, Camasa, Karabhājana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nimi-nava-yogendra-samvada.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa, 11.2–5)
- **The Nimi–Vasiṣṭha mutual curse** — the slighted Vasiṣṭha curses the sleeping king to bodilessness, and the guiltless Nimi curses his guru back in kind, so both their bodies fall away _(actors: Nimi, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/nimi-vasishtha-mutual-curse.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 56; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.5)
- **The pativratā halts the dawn** — to save her cursed husband, Kauśika's faithful wife decrees "the sun verily shall not arise," and by her fidelity the sun fails to rise, throwing the worlds into continual night _(actors: Kauśika's wife, Sūrya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anasuya-halted-sunrise.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa XVI)
- **The Śiva-grove transformation** — Sudyumna rides into a forbidden reed-grove (Śaravaṇa/Sukumāra) at Meru's foot where Śiva sports with Pārvatī, and is turned female — becoming Ilā again — along with his companions and horse _(actors: Sudyumna, Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/ila-sudyumna.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.1.23–26)
- **The soma-sacrifice performed in a pit** — trapped in the well, Trita turns pebbles into soma-grains and the water into ghee and mentally performs an entire soma-rite, whose chants reach the gods led by Bṛhaspati, who lift him out _(actors: Trita, Bṛhaspati, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/trita-aptya.md) — (Mahābhārata, Śalya Parva ~36)
- **The thousand-year battle of Prahlāda and Nārāyaṇa** — the boon-armored asura fights Nara-Nārāyaṇa for a thousand divine years, archery escalating without result until the Brahmāstra and Māheśvarāstra cancel each other _(actors: Prahlāda, Nārāyaṇa, Nara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-nara-narayana-battle.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa IV.9; Vāmana Purāṇa)
- **The Vārtraghna war (tenth saṅgrāma)** — Indra slays the drought-serpent Vṛtra with the vajra forged from Dadhīci's bones, releasing the pent-up waters _(actors: Indra, Vṛtra, Dadhīci)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/twelve-devasura-battles.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa 47; Ṛgveda 1.32)
- **The Vitastā brought down** — Śiva opens a trident-channel one vitasti (span) deep and Pārvatī flows forth as the river Vitastā (Jhelum) to purify the piśāca-defiled valley, taking her name from the span _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī/Vitastā, Kaśyapa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kashmir-tirthas-nilamata-geography.md) — (Nīlamata Purāṇa)
- **Trita betrayed into the well** — journeying with cattle earned by sacrifice, the brothers Ekata and Dvita covet the herd and abandon Trita when he falls into a deep dry well at Udapāna on the Sarasvatī _(actors: Trita, Ekata, Dvita)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/trita-aptya.md) — (Mahābhārata, Śalya Parva ~36)
- **Trita's curse on his brothers** — freed from the well, Trita curses the greedy Ekata and Dvita to become wolves and beasts of prey, so the wolf that scattered the herd becomes their own descendants' fate _(actors: Trita, Ekata, Dvita)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/trita-aptya.md) — (Mahābhārata, Śalya Parva ~36)
- **Vamana measures the three worlds (Trivikrama)** — Born as a dwarf brahmana to Aditi and Kashyapa, Vishnu begs three paces from the asura-king Bali, swells into cosmic Trivikrama, and presses Bali to the netherworld, restoring Indra's sovereignty _(actors: Vamana/Vishnu, Bali, Aditi, Kashyapa, Indra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vamana-purana.md) — (Vamana Purana; cf. Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Vapuṣmat murders Nariṣyanta** — Vapuṣmat, one of the suitors Dama had beaten, waylays and kills King Nariṣyanta in the forest _(actors: Vapuṣmat, Nariṣyanta, Dama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karandhama-avikshit-marutta-dama.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa, Canto CXXXV)
- **Vasiṣṭha Journeys to Mahācīna** — directed that Tārā yields only to another ācāra, Vasiṣṭha travels to Mahācīna (the trans-Himalayan Buddhist north) seeking her secret mode of worship _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, Tārā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tarapith-tara-vashishtha-bamakhepa.md) — (Rudrayāmala Tantra; Brahmayāmala) [tantra]
- **Vasiṣṭha reborn from the kumbha** — directed by Brahmā, the bodiless Vasiṣṭha lodges in the seed of Mitra and Varuṇa spilled at the sight of Urvaśī and is reborn womblessly from a pot, gaining his Maitrāvaruṇi and Kumbhayoni names _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, Brahmā, Mitra, Varuṇa, Urvaśī)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/nimi-vasishtha-mutual-curse.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 56–57)
- **Vasiṣṭha's Failed Tārā Worship** — the Brahmā-born ṛṣi Vasiṣṭha undertakes ages of Vedic/Dakṣiṇācāra austerity to Tārā at Tārāpīṭha and gains no vision of the goddess _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, Tārā, Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tarapith-tara-vashishtha-bamakhepa.md) — (Rudrayāmala Tantra; Brahmayāmala) [tantra]
- **Vasiṣṭha's tapas vanquishes the Rākṣasas** — the ṛṣi brings his brahma-tejas to bear through severe penance, and the enemy that kṣatra could not touch is dissolved by brahman power _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, the Rākṣasas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mucukunda-vaishravana-shanti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Śānti Parva 12.75)
- **Vatsaprī slays Kujṛmbha in Pātāla** — descending with scimitar and bow, Vatsaprī kills the Daitya Kujṛmbha — whose Prajāpati-forged club Sunanda gapes the earth open to Pātāla — with his fire-weapon after the captive princess secretly drains the club's power by touching it _(actors: Vatsaprī, Kujṛmbha, Mudāvatī, Vidūratha)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/markandeya-vaivasvata-king-tales.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 116)
- **Videgha Māthava carries Agni east to found Videha** — Agni Vaiśvānara flashes from the mouth of king Videgha Māthava at his priest's ghee-verse and burns eastward over the rivers to the Sadānīrā, granting the king his abode east of it — the founding charter of Videha/Mithilā _(actors: Videgha Māthava, Agni Vaiśvānara, Gotama Rāhūgaṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/shatapatha-brahmana.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.4.1.10–17)
- **Vishnu-as-Kurma bears Mount Mandara at the churning** — Vishnu descends as the tortoise Kurma to support sinking Mount Mandara during the Samudra-manthana, and from within that episode discourses the whole Purana to King Indradyumna _(actors: Vishnu (Kurma), King Indradyumna, the rishis)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana (opening))
- **Viṣṇu becomes Mohinī to recover the amṛta** — Viṣṇu takes the form of the enchantress Mohinī after the asuras seize the nectar pot from Dhanvantari at the churning _(actors: Viṣṇu (as Mohinī), Dhanvantari, the asuras, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mohini-avatara.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8–8.9; Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Vāsuki the Churning-Rope at Samudra Manthana** — The nāga-king Vāsuki serves as the churning-rope wound round Mount Mandara at the Samudra Manthana, vomiting the Hālāhala poison that Śiva drinks, and is worn by Śiva as a neck-ornament _(actors: Vāsuki, Śiva, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata; Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
- **Dhanvantari rises last bearing the Amṛta-kumbha** — The divine physician Dhanvantari, patron of Āyurveda, rises last from the churning bearing the pot (kumbha) of amṛta, the nectar of immortality _(actors: Dhanvantari, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8)
- **Durvasa's curse and Lakshmi's withdrawal** — Durvasa gives Indra a divine garland which Indra slights and Airavata tramples; the offended Lakshmi abandons the three worlds, which lose their lustre, prompting the churning to recover her _(actors: Durvasa, Indra, Lakshmi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lakshmi.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **Durvasa's curse triggers the churning** — Durvasa's garland is trampled by Indra's elephant Airavata; he curses the Devas to lose their shri, Lakshmi withdraws into the ocean, and the Asuras rout the weakened Devas _(actors: Durvasa, Indra, Airavata, Lakshmi, Bali)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5; Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **Eternal tapas at Badarīkāśrama** — Nara and Nārāyaṇa retire to the Himālayan hermitage of Badarī (Badrīnāth) and perform unbroken, cyclically-renewed austerity for the welfare of the worlds _(actors: Nara, Nārāyaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nara-narayana.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Mahābhārata Śānti Parva)
- **Hiraṇyakaśipu's vow of vengeance** — After Hiraṇyākṣa is slain by Varāha, Hiraṇyakaśipu swears to destroy Viṣṇu and all his devotees _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Diti, Hiraṇyākṣa (slain), Varāha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.2)
- **Hiraṇyākṣa Slain by Varāha** — The daitya Hiraṇyākṣa drags the Earth down into the cosmic ocean and is slain by Viṣṇu as the Boar Varāha, who lifts Earth back on his tusks _(actors: Hiraṇyākṣa, Viṣṇu (Varāha))_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.13-19; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Matsya saves Manu and recovers the Vedas from Hayagrīva** — Viṣṇu's fish-avatāra grows enormous, warns Vaivasvata Manu of the deluge, tows his boat with the seven ṛṣis and the seeds/Vedas to safety, and recovers the Vedas from the demon Hayagrīva _(actors: Matsya (Viṣṇu), Vaivasvata Manu, Hayagrīva, seven ṛṣis)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/agni-purana.md) — (Agni Purāṇa 2)
- **Matsya slays Hayagriva and recovers the Vedas** — In the Puranic version the Matsya avatar slays the demon Hayagriva and recovers the Vedas he had stolen _(actors: Matsya/Vishnu, Hayagriva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/README.md) — (Matsya Purana)
- **Mohinī distributes the amṛta to the devas** — After the ocean-churning Viṣṇu takes his only female form, Mohinī, beguiling the asuras and distributing the nectar of immortality to the devas alone _(actors: Mohinī (Viṣṇu), devas, asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vishnu-forms-and-vyuhas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8-9, 8.12; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Mohini Tricks the Asuras for the Amṛta** — Viṣṇu takes the form of the enchantress Mohini to seize the pot of amrita and trick the asuras out of immortality _(actors: Viṣṇu (Mohini), asuras)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kumbh-mela-and-pilgrimage-cycles.md) — (Bhagavata Purana)
- **Mohinī's unfair distribution of the nectar** — Mohinī seats devas and asuras separately and serves the amṛta only to the devas, beguiling the asuras with delay _(actors: Mohinī, the devas, the asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mohini-avatara.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.9.14–25)
- **Namuci steals Indra's strength and Soma** — In the Brāhmaṇa version Namuci drinks away Indra's strength together with the Soma/Surā, carrying off Indra's vigour in the intoxicant; the weakened Indra makes a truce to recover it, the Aśvins and Sarasvatī supply the foam as the loophole-weapon, and the strength is restored upon Namuci's slaying _(actors: Namuci, Indra, Aśvins, Sarasvatī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 12.7.3; Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 1.7)
- **Origin of Mahalakshmi at the churning** — Lakshmi (Sri) rises among the treasures churned from the milk-ocean and chooses Vishnu, exalted as the supreme Shakti _(actors: Lakshmi (Sri), Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana)
- **Prahlada counsels Andhaka and undertakes a tirtha-circuit** — The Vishnu-devotee Prahlada counsels his kinsman Andhaka against lust for Gauri and later makes an extended pilgrimage circuit, serving as a vehicle for the text's pilgrimage doctrine _(actors: Prahlada, Andhaka)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vamana-purana.md) — (Vamana Purana)
- **Prahlāda cast from the Lion-Hill and rescued** — Prahlāda is hurled into the sea from the mountain on his father's order, rescued by Vishnu, and builds the first shrine on the hill _(actors: Prahlāda, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Vishnu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/simhachalam-varaha-narasimha.md) — (Siṃhācala-kṣetra-māhātmya; Narasiṃha-Purāṇa tradition)
- **Raivata Kakudmin and Revatī's domain** — Folk etymology of the hill ties it to the Ānarta king Raivata Kakudmin, whose daughter Revatī wed Balarāma _(actors: Raivata Kakudmin, Revatī, Balarāma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/girnar-raivataka-datta-tirtha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.3; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Samudra Manthana — churning of the ocean** — Gods and asuras churn the milk-ocean with Mandara and Vasuki over Kurma, producing the fourteen ratnas (Lakshmi, Dhanvantari with amrita, the poison Shiva swallows, etc.), and Mohini tricks the asuras out of the nectar _(actors: devas, asuras, Vishnu (Kurma, Mohini), Vasuki, Shiva, Dhanvantari, Lakshmi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/matsya-purana.md) — (Matsya Purana)
- **Slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu at the Jvālā / Rakta-kuṇḍa spot** — Narasiṃha in flaming form tears Hiraṇyakaśipu apart, his blood reddening the Rakta-kuṇḍa pool below _(actors: Narasiṃha, Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ahobilam-nava-narasimha.md) — (Ahobila-kṣetra-māhātmya)
- **The 60,000 sons dig to the sea (Sāgara etymology)** — Sumati's 60,000 sons excavate the earth seeking the horse, hollowing the ocean-bed — whence the sea is called sāgara, 'of Sagara' _(actors: Sagara's 60,000 sons)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gangasagar-sagara-dvipa-kapila-ashram.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 38–40)
- **The Matsya flood and rescue of Vaivasvata Manu** — Vishnu as Matsya the fish warns Vaivasvata of a coming deluge; the Manu builds a boat tied to the fish's horn and carries the seven sages, seed of all creatures, and the Vedas across the pralaya, founding current humanity _(actors: Matsya (Vishnu), Vaivasvata Manu, Saptarishis)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana 8.24; Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1; Mahabharata Vana Parva)
- **Varāha remains permanently manifest at Śrīmuṣṇam** — After the Earth-rescue the Boar does not vanish but stays eternally visible at the spot, sometimes at Bhū-devī's petition, founding the perpetual-presence claim _(actors: Viṣṇu (Bhū-Varāha), Bhū-devī)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/avatara-kshetras-srikurmam-srimushnam.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, Śrīmuṣṇa-māhātmya)
- **Vishnu takes Mohini form to recover the amrita** — After the asuras seize the amrita-pot, Vishnu takes the enchantress Mohini form to recover and redistribute the nectar to the devas _(actors: Vishnu/Mohini, devas, asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dhanvantari.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.9)
- **Vāruṇī Emerges at the Churning** — Vāruṇī, goddess of wine and consort of Varuṇa, emerges among the treasures churned from the ocean at the Samudra Manthana _(actors: Vāruṇī, Varuṇa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/dikpalas-and-lokapalas.md) — (Samudra Manthana tradition)
- **Vāsuki serves as the churning-rope at the Samudra Manthana** — The Nāga-king Vāsuki serves as the churning-rope wound round Mt. Mandara at the Samudra Manthana _(actors: Vāsuki, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md (cross-ref))
- **Viṣṇu reveals the twins' invincibility** — Viṣṇu discloses that Nara and Nārāyaṇa are his own aṃśas doing tapas for the worlds and tells Prahlāda he can conquer the Lord by devotion but never by battle _(actors: Viṣṇu, Prahlāda, Nara-Nārāyaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-nara-narayana-battle.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa IV.9; Vāmana Purāṇa)
- **Vṛśa Jāna revives the boy under the chariot** — after king Tryaruṇa's chariot kills a brāhmaṇa boy and the blood-guilt is apportioned, the purohita Vṛśa restores the dead child to life with an Agni-hymn _(actors: Tryaruṇa Traivṛṣṇa, Vṛśa Jāna, the boy)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/brahmana-legends-catalog.md) — (Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa 13.3.12; Bṛhaddevatā 5.14–23)
- **Yogeśvarī Emitted Against Andhaka's Blood** — When Śiva spears Andhaka and each blood-drop becomes a new demon, Śiva emits Yogeśvarī from his mouth-flame and the gods send their śaktis to follow and drink the blood, checking the flood _(actors: Śiva, Yogeśvarī, Andhaka, the gods' śaktis)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/matrikas-and-64-yoginis.md) — (Īśānaśivagurudevapaddhati; Matsya Purāṇa 179; Vāmana Purāṇa)
- **Beheading of Svarbhānu and the birth of Rāhu and Ketu** — Svarbhānu infiltrates the deva row to drink the nectar; Sūrya and Candra expose him and Mohinī beheads him with the Sudarśana Cakra, creating the immortal shadow-grahas Rāhu and Ketu _(actors: Svarbhānu (Rāhu/Ketu), Mohinī/Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Candra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mohini-avatara.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.9.24–26, 8.10; Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Consecration of Yoga-Narasiṃha on the summit** — The summit Yoga-Narasiṃha shrine, Narasiṃha in seated meditative posture, is held the original guardian deity, consecrated in legend by Prahlāda _(actors: Yoga-Narasiṃha, Prahlāda)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/melkote-tirunarayanapuram.md) — (kṣetra-māhātmya; local tradition)
- **Cursed devas churn the Milk Ocean** — The weakened devas lose to the asuras and are told to churn the Milk Ocean in alliance with them to recover amṛta and lost treasures, from which Airāvata and Uccaiḥśravas re-emerge _(actors: Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.6; Mahābhārata Ādiparva)
- **Dhanvantari emerges at the Samudra Manthana** — The divine physician Dhanvantari rises from the churned ocean bearing the pot of amṛta, hailed as deva of medicine and aṃśa-avatāra of Viṣṇu _(actors: Dhanvantari, devas and asuras, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/ayurveda-and-the-science-of-life.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.9)
- **Emergence of Lakshmi from the Samudra Manthana** — When devas and asuras churn the milk-ocean, Lakshmi rises seated on a lotus among the ratnas, is bathed by the celestial elephants, and garlands Vishnu as her eternal consort _(actors: Lakshmi, Vishnu, devas, asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lakshmi.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.9; Bhagavata Purana 8.8; Mahabharata)
- **Hiraṇyakaśipu Slain by Narasiṃha** — Granted a loophole-bound boon of invulnerability, Hiraṇyakaśipu tortures his devotee-son Prahlāda and is slain by Viṣṇu as the man-lion Narasiṃha at twilight on a threshold _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Viṣṇu (Narasiṃha), Prahlāda)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Ikshvaku Founds Ayodhya** — Ikshvaku, eldest son of Manu, establishes the Solar dynasty and the kingdom of Kosala at Ayodhya after the deluge _(actors: Ikshvaku)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.2; Bhagavata IX.6)
- **Kapila's glance burns the 60,000 sons to ash** — The sons find the horse by the meditating Kapila and abuse him; Kapila's opened eyes incinerate all 60,000, leaving their un-rited ashes restless _(actors: Kapila, Sagara's 60,000 sons)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gangasagar-sagara-dvipa-kapila-ashram.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 40–41; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.8 (Kapila as Viṣṇu-avatāra); Mahābhārata Vana Parva (Agastya narration))
- **Kurma avatara supports Mount Mandara** — As Mandara (churning rod) wound with Vasuki sinks into the ocean of milk, Vishnu incarnates as the tortoise Kurma to bear the mountain on his back as the pivot for churning _(actors: Vishnu (Kurma), Vasuki, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Mahabharata Adi Parva; Vishnu Purana)
- **Manu and the Flood (Matsya rescue)** — Viṣṇu as the fish (Matsya) warns Manu of the pralaya-flood and saves him and the seeds of life across the deluge — the earliest extant Hindu flood account _(actors: Matsya (Viṣṇu), Manu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shruti-vedas-and-upanishads.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1; Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Marriage of Śiva and Pārvatī** — The Śiva Purāṇa narrates the marriage of Śiva and Pārvatī among the central cosmic Śaiva events _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Maya builds Tripura's three cities** — Maya constructs the gold, silver and iron flying fortresses for Tāraka's three sons, later burned by Śiva Tripurāntaka _(actors: Maya, Tārakākṣa, Vidyunmālī, Kamalākṣa, Śiva)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/maya-danava.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā; Matsya Purāṇa 129–140; Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva 8.24)
- **Narasiṃha slays Hiraṇyakaśipu at the threshold** — Vishnu bursts from the pillar as the Man-Lion at twilight on the threshold and kills Hiraṇyakaśipu, voiding the boon; the kṣetra claims the deed for Siṃhācalam _(actors: Narasiṃha (Vishnu), Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/simhachalam-varaha-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata-Purāṇa 7; Siṃhācala sthala-purāṇa)
- **Nārāyaṇa produces Urvaśī from his thigh to humble Indra's apsarās** — When Indra sends Kāmadeva and apsarās to break their penance, the unmoved Nārāyaṇa creates the nymph Urvaśī from his thigh, shaming Indra's nymphs, then gifts her to the gods _(actors: Nārāyaṇa, Nara, Indra, Kāmadeva, the apsarās, Urvaśī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nara-narayana.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Devī Bhāgavata)
- **Samudra Manthana (Churning of the Ocean of Milk)** — Devas and asuras use Mandara as the churning-rod and Vasuki as the rope to churn the ocean; Vishnu as Kurma bears the sinking mountain, and the fourteen ratnas including amrita and Lakshmi rise _(actors: Devas, Asuras, Vishnu (Kurma), Vasuki)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/meru-kailash-and-cosmic-mountains.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.6-8; Mahabharata Adi-parva; Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **The boon of near-invulnerability** — Through extreme tapas Hiraṇyakaśipu wins from Brahmā a death hedged by impossibilities — no created being, no weapon, not day or night, not inside or outside, not earth or sky, not man or beast _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.3)
- **The devas name the hill (Ahō-balam / Ahō-bilam)** — Watching the deed, the gods cry 'Ahō balam!' (what strength) or 'Ahō bilam!' (what a cave), naming the kṣetra _(actors: The devas, Narasiṃha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ahobilam-nava-narasimha.md) — (Ahobila-kṣetra-māhātmya)
- **The Mātṛkās' Rampage and Pacification** — Drunk on power after drinking the demon-blood, the Mātṛkās begin devouring gods, demons and creatures indiscriminately until Viṣṇu/Śiva must pacify them _(actors: Mātṛkās, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/matrikas-and-64-yoginis.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa; Vāmana Purāṇa)
- **The white-boar (Śveta-Varāha) self-manifestation at the tank** — The svayam-vyakta icon reveals itself via a white boar appearing at the Nitya-puṣkariṇī tank, sometimes drawn by a sage's tapas; the lost-and-refound motif also attaches _(actors: Viṣṇu (Śveta-Varāha); an unnamed sage/king)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/avatara-kshetras-srikurmam-srimushnam.md) — (Śrīmuṣṇa-māhātmya; temple tradition)
- **Vaivasvata Manu begets the ten progenitor children** — Through a son-yielding sacrifice, Manu and his wife Shraddha beget ten children who found the two great royal lines, including Ikshvaku and Ila/Sudyumna _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Shraddha, Ikshvaku, Ila/Sudyumna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9; Vishnu Purana 4)
- **Airāvata emerges from the churning** — The white elephant-king Airāvata rises from the Samudra-manthana as one of the ratnas and is seized by Indra as his vāhana and East-guardian _(actors: Airāvata, Indra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.9; Mahābhārata)
- **Amṛta Falls at Brahmakund (Haridwar)** — A drop of amṛta from the celestial kumbha spills at Brahmakund within Har-ki-Pauri during the flight after the Samudra Manthana, making it Haridwar's holiest bathing point and a Kumbh site _(actors: Garuḍa, devas, asuras)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/haridwar-rishikesh-ganga-dwara.md) — (Wikipedia, Haridwar Kumbh Mela; Puranic Kumbh sources)
- **Births of Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya** — The Śiva Purāṇa records the births of Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya (Skanda) _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī, Gaṇeśa, Kārttikeya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Conquest of the three worlds** — Armoured by the boon, Hiraṇyakaśipu usurps the realms of the devas and rules heaven, earth, and underworld as universal tyrant _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Indra, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.4; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.17)
- **Dhanvantari rises from the ocean with the amṛta** — The divine physician Dhanvantari rises from the churned ocean bearing the pot of amṛta, founding and patronizing Āyurveda _(actors: Dhanvantari (Viṣṇu))_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vishnu-forms-and-vyuhas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.3, 8.8; Garuḍa Purāṇa)
- **Drops of amṛta fall at the four Kumbh Mela sites** — During the deva-asura scramble for the kumbha, drops of nectar fall at Prayāg, Haridvāra, Ujjain and Nāsik — the etiology of the Kumbh Mela _(actors: Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Puranic/folk tradition)
- **Halahala poison and Shiva Nilakantha** — The world-destroying Halahala poison rises first from the churn; Shiva drinks it and Parvati holds his throat so it lodges there, turning it blue and earning him the name Nilakantha _(actors: Shiva, Parvati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Shiva Purana; Vishnu Purana)
- **Śiva beholds the Mohinī form and is overpowered by māyā** — Śiva asks to see the enchantress form; Viṣṇu reappears as Mohinī and Śiva, maddened with desire, demonstrates that even he is not beyond Viṣṇu's māyā _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī, Viṣṇu (as Mohinī))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mohini-avatara.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.12.12–35)
- **Kūrma supports the churning of the ocean** — The tortoise-avatāra Kūrma serves as the support beneath Mount Mandara during the churning of the ocean _(actors: Kūrma (Viṣṇu))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/agni-purana.md) — (Agni Purāṇa 3)
- **Narasiṃha teaches yoga to Prahlāda (Yōgānanda form)** — His fury cooled after the slaying, Narasiṃha instructs Prahlāda in yoga, fixed as the Yōgānanda Narasiṃha shrine _(actors: Narasiṃha, Prahlāda)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ahobilam-nava-narasimha.md) — (Ahobila-māhātmya; Ahobila Maṭha tradition)
- **Nityakalyāṇa — the eternal auspiciousness/wedding** — The Lord is invoked as Nityakalyāṇa, conferring perpetual marital weal; read also as Varāha eternally 'wedded' to the rescued Earth on his body _(actors: Viṣṇu (Nityakalyāṇa-perumāḷ), Bhū-devī)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/avatara-kshetras-srikurmam-srimushnam.md) — (temple tradition; sthala usage)
- **Prahlāda Survives His Father's Attempts** — Prahlāda, a Viṣṇu-devotee from the womb, miraculously survives poison, fire and the pillar, becoming the paradigmatic bhakta and a righteous asura-king _(actors: Prahlāda, Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Sharabha pacifies Narasimha** — Shiva assumes the colossal part-lion part-bird Sharabha form to pacify Vishnu's Narasimha when his fury threatens the cosmos _(actors: Sharabha (Shiva), Narasimha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Shiva Purana; Sharabha Upanishad)
- **The Churning of the Ocean (Amrita-manthana)** — The churning of the milk-ocean to win amrita, told within the Astika frame to explain the gods' immortality _(actors: devas, asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Astika Parva)
- **The condition for redemption revealed** — Aṃśumān recovers the horse and learns that only the celestial Gaṅgā brought down over the ashes can liberate the burnt sons _(actors: Aṃśumān, Garuḍa, Kapila)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gangasagar-sagara-dvipa-kapila-ashram.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 41–42)
- **Vikukshi Shashada Eats the Sacrificial Hare** — Sent to fetch sacrificial meat, Vikukshi eats a hare himself, earning the nickname Shashada and a brief exile _(actors: Vikukshi)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.2)
- **Vishnu descends as Ajita and becomes Kurma** — During the churning Vishnu descends as Ajita and, when Mandara sinks, becomes the tortoise to bear the mountain on his shell as the pivot _(actors: Vishnu/Ajita as Kurma, Devas, Asuras, Mount Mandara, Vasuki)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kurma-avatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5-8.8; Vishnu Purana 1.9; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Vṛtra slain by Indra** — Indra slays the drought-serpent Vṛtra, who withheld the cosmic waters, with the Vajra forged from sage Dadhīci's bones, releasing the seven rivers _(actors: Indra, Vṛtra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Dadhīci)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Ṛgveda 1.32, Mahābhārata, Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.9-13)
- **Birth and devotion of Prahlāda** — Prahlāda, son of Hiraṇyakaśipu, is a perfected Viṣṇu-devotee from the womb (taught by Nārada), rejecting demon-schooling and preaching bhakti _(actors: Prahlāda, Nārada, Ṣaṇḍa, Amarka, Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.4–7.5, 7.7)
- **Dakṣa's sacrifice** — The Śiva Purāṇa narrates Dakṣa's sacrifice and its destruction, a key cosmic Śaiva event _(actors: Dakṣa, Śiva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Descent of the Ganga (Gangavataran) at Gangotri** — The Ganga descends from heaven at Gangotri to liberate the ancestors of King Bhagiratha, the headstream named Bhagirathi after him _(actors: Ganga, Bhagiratha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/char-dham-and-chota-char-dham.md) — (Ramayana/Mahabharata Gangavataran legend)
- **Emergence of Lakshmi from the ocean** — The goddess of fortune re-emerges radiant from the churned ocean and of her own choice garlands and weds Vishnu, restoring shri to the cosmos _(actors: Lakshmi, Vishnu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.8; Vishnu Purana 1.9)
