- **First demonic birth: Hiranyaksa and Hiranyakasipu slain** — Jaya and Vijaya are reborn as the asura brothers Hiranyaksa (slain by Varaha) and Hiranyakasipu (torn open by Narasimha) in Satya-yuga _(actors: Hiranyaksa, Hiranyakasipu, Varaha, Narasimha, Prahlada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaya-vijaya.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.17-19; 7.2-8)
- **Ila/Sudyumna roots the Lunar Dynasty** — Ila/Sudyumna, who shifts between female and male after entering a Shiva-sacred grove, becomes root of the Chandra Vamsha via the child Pururavas, descending to the Kurus, Pandavas, and Krishna's kin _(actors: Ila/Sudyumna, Pururavas, Budha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/README.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana; Mahabharata)
- **Kakutstha Rides Indra-as-Bull** — Puranjaya rides into battle against the Asuras seated on Indra's hump in bull form, earning the patronymic Kakutstha later applied to Rama _(actors: Kakutstha/Puranjaya, Indra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Ramayana)
- **Kāmadhenu given to the Saptarṣi and Vasiṣṭha** — The wish-cow Kāmadhenu emerges from the churning and is given to the seven sages, passing into the keeping of Vasiṣṭha _(actors: Kāmadhenu, Saptarṣi, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Kamadhenu (Wikipedia); Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8)
- **Kurma named in the Bhagavata avatara-list (1.3.16)** — The kurma/kacchapa tortoise descent that supported Mandara is enumerated in the Bhagavata's master list of Vishnu's avataras _(actors: Vishnu as kurma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kurma-avatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.3.16)
- **Marriage of Narasiṃha to Chenchu-Lakṣmī** — Lingering on the hill, Narasiṃha falls in love with and weds the Chenchu tribal maiden Chenchu-Lakṣmī, making the Chenchus his in-laws _(actors: Narasiṃha, Chenchu-Lakṣmī (Lakṣmī), the Chenchu tribe)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ahobilam-nava-narasimha.md) — (Ahobila-kṣetra-māhātmya; Chenchu oral tradition)
- **Namuci beheaded by Indra** — Indra circumvents Namuci's boon by decapitating him at twilight with sea-foam wrapped on the vajra, neither wet nor dry, by day nor night _(actors: Indra, Namuci)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Ṛgveda, Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, Mahābhārata)
- **Nārada turns Dakṣa's sons to renunciation; cursed to wander** — Nārada counsels Dakṣa's sons toward renunciation so they never beget subjects, and Dakṣa curses him to wander ceaselessly without rest, feeding the Dakṣa–Satī cycle _(actors: Nārada, Dakṣa, the Haryaśvas and Śabalāśvas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.5)
- **Sanaka-kumaras curse Jaya and Vijaya** — Vishnu's gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya are cursed by the four child-sages to three demonic births each ending in death at the Lord's hand, of which Shishupala is the third _(actors: Sanaka-kumaras, Jaya, Vijaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shishupala.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.1)
- **Shiva Drinks the Hālāhala Poison at Alangudi** — During the Samudra Manthana the world-destroying halahala poison rises first and Shiva drinks it to save creation, his throat turning blue; Alangudi is held to be the spot, making Shiva Apatsahaya, savior in distress _(actors: Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/navagraha-temples.md) — (Sthala-purana; Samudra Manthana cycle)
- **Three generations of failed penance** — Aṃśumān and his son Dilīpa perform austerities to draw Gaṅgā down but die without success, passing the task to Bhagīratha _(actors: Aṃśumān, Dilīpa, Bhagīratha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gangasagar-sagara-dvipa-kapila-ashram.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 42–43)
- **Varaha avatara slays Hiranyaksa** — The Boar avatara lifts the Earth from the cosmic waters and slays the demon Hiranyaksa, the first life of the Jaya-Vijaya curse _(actors: Varaha/Viṣṇu, Hiranyaksa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3)
- **Varaha Stays on Venkata Hill After Slaying Hiranyaksha** — In a variant, the Varaha avatar remains on the hill as guardian after lifting the earth and slaying Hiranyaksha, and Shrinivasa must obtain his permission to settle there _(actors: Varaha, Hiranyaksha, Shrinivasa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Sthala Purana of Tirumala)
- **Agastya drinks the ocean to expose the Kālakeyas** — To destroy the ocean-hiding Kālakeyas who devoured sages by night, the gods enlist Agastya, who drinks the entire ocean dry _(actors: Agastya, the Kālakeyas, the devas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva)
- **Bhagīratha's penance and Brahmā's boon** — Bhagīratha renounces his throne for vast tapas; Brahmā grants Gaṅgā's descent but warns only Śiva can bear her fall _(actors: Bhagīratha, Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gangasagar-sagara-dvipa-kapila-ashram.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 43)
- **Birth of Mandhatr from His Father's Side** — Mandhatr is born from his father Yuvanashva's side after the king drinks consecrated water meant for his queen, and becomes a universal emperor _(actors: Mandhatr, Yuvanashva, Indra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.2; Mahabharata)
- **Daksha's yajna and Sati's self-immolation** — Prajapati Daksha holds a grand sacrifice snubbing his daughter Sati and her husband Shiva; insulted when she attends uninvited, Sati immolates herself in the sacrificial fire _(actors: Daksha, Sati, Shiva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.2-4.4; Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Dhanvantari rises with the amrita** — The divine physician Dhanvantari, patron of Ayurveda and an aspect of Vishnu, rises last from the ocean bearing the kalasha of amrita, the goal of the entire churning _(actors: Dhanvantari)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.8; Mahabharata; Vishnu Purana)
- **Garuḍa's vision of the nine Narasiṃhas** — Garuḍa does tapas in the Nallamala and is shown all nine self-manifest Narasiṃha forms across the hill _(actors: Garuḍa, Narasiṃha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ahobilam-nava-narasimha.md) — (Ahobila-kṣetra-māhātmya)
- **Hālāhala / Nīlakaṇṭha — Śiva drinks the world-poison** — During the churning of the milk-ocean Vāsuki disgorges the all-destroying Hālāhala poison; Śiva drinks it and Pārvatī halts it at his throat, making him the blue-throated saviour of creation _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī, Vāsuki)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Indra bears the Kalpavṛkṣa to Svarga** — The wish-fulfilling tree Kalpavṛkṣa emerges at the churning and Indra carries it to his paradise, rooting it in the Nandana-vana _(actors: Indra, Kalpavṛkṣa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Kalpavriksha (Wikipedia); Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8)
- **Jyeshtha/Alakshmi rises from the churning** — Alakshmi as Jyeshtha, elder sister of Lakshmi, rises from the churning before the nectar and is later married off to the sage Duhsaha, dwelling wherever inauspiciousness is found _(actors: Jyeshtha (Alakshmi), Duhsaha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lakshmi.md) — (Linga Purana; Padma Purana)
- **Kapila teaches Devahuti (Kapilopadesa)** — The Kapila avatara, born to Kardama and Devahuti, teaches his mother devotional Sankhya and bhakti-yoga, a primary scriptural Sankhya source _(actors: Kapila, Devahuti)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.24-33)
- **King Indradyumna Seeks Nila-Madhava** — Satya-Yuga Malava king Indradyumna sends brahmin Vidyapati (who weds the Shabara chief's daughter Lalita) to find the secret Nila-Madhava image; it vanishes, directing the king to worship a sacred floating log instead _(actors: Indradyumna, Vidyapati, Vishvavasu, Lalita)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Madala Panji; Skanda Purana)
- **Markandeya conquers death at the Shiva-linga** — At his destined hour of death the boy Markandeya clasps the Shiva-linga chanting the Maha-mrityunjaya mantra; Shiva bursts forth, defeats Yama, and grants him eternal youth _(actors: Markandeya, Shiva, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-chiranjivis.md) — (Skanda/Linga/Padma Puranas; Markandeya Purana)
- **Mohinī's Muktanṛtya dance-trap of Bhasmāsura** — Viṣṇu as Mohinī lures the ash-demon Bhasmāsura into mirroring her dance and touching his own head, reducing him to ashes (regional/folk version of the Vṛkāsura kernel) _(actors: Mohinī (Viṣṇu), Bhasmāsura, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mohini-avatara.md) — (Regional / folk tradition; Kathakali Bhasmāsura Mohinī (cf. Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.88 Vṛkāsura))
- **Nārada initiates the child Dhruva** — Nārada meets the boy Dhruva, tests his resolve, sends him to Madhuvana, and bestows the dvādaśākṣara mantra that ignites Dhruva's penance _(actors: Nārada, Dhruva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.11–12)
- **Prahlāda expounds navadhā bhakti** — Confronting his father, Prahlāda declares Hari is everywhere and teaches the ninefold path of devotion, sealing his father's murderous resolve _(actors: Prahlāda, Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.5.23–24, 7.8)
- **The Kurma Purana spoken from the tortoise** — Vishnu in tortoise form narrates the Kurma Purana to sages and Devas/Asuras during the churning, the only Mahapurana named for its avatara-narrator _(actors: Vishnu as Kurma, the sages, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kurma-avatara.md) — (Kurma Purana (framing chapters))
- **Gaṅgādhara — Śiva bears the descent of Gaṅgā** — When Bhagīratha's penance brings the celestial Gaṅgā down to redeem Sagara's 60,000 sons, Śiva catches her world-shattering fall in his matted locks and releases her as a tamed stream, humbling her pride _(actors: Śiva, Gaṅgā, Bhagīratha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa; Mahābhārata)
- **Śiva catches Gaṅgā in his locks (Gaṅgādhara)** — Śiva traps the plunging Gaṅgā in his matted hair to tame her, releasing her in a thinned stream — the Gaṅgādhara icon _(actors: Śiva, Gaṅgā, Bhagīratha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gangasagar-sagara-dvipa-kapila-ashram.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 43–44)
- **Mohini distributes the nectar to the Devas** — The Asuras seize the amrita; Vishnu takes the enchantress form Mohini, beguiles them, and serves the nectar only to the Devas _(actors: Vishnu (Mohini), Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.9; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Nārada's prenatal instruction of Prahlāda** — Kayādhu shelters in Nārada's hermitage during the deva-asura war and the unborn Prahlāda absorbs Nārada's teaching on Viṣṇu-bhakti, the root of his invincible devotion _(actors: Nārada, Kayādhu, the unborn Prahlāda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.7)
- **The failed killings of Prahlāda** — Hiraṇyakaśipu has Prahlāda trampled, bitten, hurled from cliffs, burned, poisoned, and cast into the sea; Viṣṇu shields him each time. Folk tradition adds the Holikā fire-ordeal (etiology of Holī) _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda, Holikā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.5; later Purāṇic/festival tradition (Holikā))
- **The Unfinished Carving of Jagannatha** — A divine carpenter carves the Puri triad on condition of being undisturbed; the door is opened early, so the images remain armless and legless, and Brahma is brought to consecrate the temple _(actors: Vishnu/Vishvakarma, Indradyumna, Gundica, Brahma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Madala Panji; Skanda Purana; Brahma & Narada Puranas)
- **Virabhadra destroys Daksha's sacrifice** — Enraged at Sati's death, Shiva creates Virabhadra and Bhadrakali from a lock of his hair, who destroy the yajna and behead Daksha; Shiva later revives Daksha with a goat's head _(actors: Shiva, Virabhadra, Bhadrakali, Daksha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.5-4.7; Shiva Purana)
- **Viṣṇu claims the Kaustubha jewel from the churning** — The supreme jewel Kaustubha emerges from the Samudra Manthana and Viṣṇu claims it, wearing it on his chest alongside the Śrīvatsa and Vaijayantī _(actors: Viṣṇu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8; Vishnu Purana; Kaustubha (Wikipedia))
- **Beheading of Svarbhānu (Origin of Rāhu and Ketu)** — During the Samudra Manthana the asura Svarbhanu disguises himself to sip the amrita; exposed by Sun and Moon, Vishnu as Mohini beheads him with the Sudarshana Chakra, and his immortal head becomes Rahu and body becomes Ketu, who cause eclipses _(actors: Svarbhanu, Vishnu (Mohini), Surya, Chandra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/navagraha-temples.md) — (Samudra Manthana cycle)
- **Founding of the Shakti Pithas** — Shiva wanders bearing Sati's corpse; Vishnu's Sudarshana cuts it into pieces that fall across the land, founding the Shakti Pithas, and Sati reincarnates as Parvati _(actors: Shiva, Sati, Vishnu, Parvati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Devi Bhagavata; Kalika Purana; Tantra literature)
- **Harishchandra's Truth-Test** — Harishchandra sells himself, wife, and son to honor a debt to Vishvamitra and is tested mercilessly but never lies, restored and ascending to heaven as the archetype of satya _(actors: Harishchandra, Vishvamitra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Markandeya Purana; Aitareya Brahmana; Devi-Bhagavata)
- **Indra Slays Vṛtra with the Vajra** — The drought-serpent Dānava Vṛtra withholds the cosmic waters and is slain by Indra with the vajra forged from sage Dadhīci's bones, releasing the seven rivers — the foundational Vedic combat _(actors: Indra, Vṛtra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Dadhīci)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Ṛgveda 1.32; Mahābhārata; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.9-13)
- **The descent reaches the sea and redeems the ashes at Gaṅgāsāgar** — Gaṅgā follows Bhagīratha's chariot to the ocean and over the ashes of the 60,000 at Sāgara-dvīpa, granting them heaven — establishing the first ancestral water-rite tīrtha _(actors: Gaṅgā, Bhagīratha, the 60,000 sons)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gangasagar-sagara-dvipa-kapila-ashram.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 44; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.9)
- **The pillar challenge and Narasiṃha bursting forth** — Hiraṇyakaśipu strikes a pillar to disprove Viṣṇu's omnipresence; Narasiṃha, the man-lion, erupts from it roaring _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda, Narasiṃha (Viṣṇu))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.8.12–22; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.20; Narasiṃha Purāṇa)
- **Varāha lifts the Earth** — Viṣṇu as the boar (Varāha) raises the Earth from the cosmic waters — a Satya-Yuga / Manvantara-boundary avatāra event framing the Varāha Purāṇa _(actors: Varāha (Viṣṇu), Earth (Bhūmi))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Varāha Purāṇa)
- **Indra Decapitates Namuci with Sea-Foam** — Bound by a truce and a no-wet-no-dry boon, Indra beheads the asura Namuci at twilight with sea-foam wrapped on the vajra — the loophole-archetype and origin of his brahmahatyā guilt-stain _(actors: Indra, Namuci)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Ṛgveda; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa; Mahābhārata)
- **Nārada instructs Prahlāda in the womb** — Nārada teaches the unborn Prahlāda (via Kayādhu), seeding the Vaiṣṇava devotion of the Narasiṃha cycle _(actors: Nārada, Prahlāda, Kayādhu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7)
- **Skanda slays Tārakāsura** — The Skanda Purāṇa records Skanda/Kārttikeya's birth and his slaying of the demon Tārakāsura _(actors: Skanda/Kārttikeya, Tārakāsura)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa)
- **The threshold disembowelment of Hiraṇyakaśipu** — At twilight, on the doorway threshold, on his lap, with bare claws, Narasiṃha disembowels Hiraṇyakaśipu — voiding every loophole of the boon _(actors: Narasiṃha, Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.8.23–29)
- **Uccaiḥśravas emerges from the churning** — The seven-headed snow-white horse-king Uccaiḥśravas arises at the Samudra-manthana, born of the amṛta, and is seized by Indra (or claimed by Bali) _(actors: Uccaiḥśravas, Indra, Bali)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādiparva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8)
- **War over the nectar and Indra restored** — Strengthened by the amrita, the Devas with Vishnu defeat the Asuras in the post-churning war and Indra is reinstated to Svarga _(actors: Indra, Devas, Asuras, Vishnu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.10-8.11; Mahabharata)
- **Agastya Drinks the Ocean Dry, Kālakeyas Slain** — The ocean-hiding Kālakeyas devour sages by night until the gods beg Agastya, who drinks the entire ocean dry, exposing and enabling the slaughter of the Kālakeya asuras _(actors: Agastya, Kālakeyas, Devas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva)
- **Bhagiratha Brings Down the Ganga** — Through epic tapas Bhagiratha brings Ganga from heaven to liberate the ashes of Sagara's sons, with Shiva catching her in his locks; the river is named Bhagirathi for him _(actors: Bhagiratha, Ganga, Shiva)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Ramayana Balakanda; Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata IX.9)
- **Curse of the Sanaka-kumaras on Jaya and Vijaya** — Brahma's four child-sages curse Vishnu's gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya to three demonic births, setting off the Hiranyaksha/Hiranyakashipu and later demon incarnations _(actors: Sanaka-kumaras, Jaya, Vijaya)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.12, 3.15-3.16, 7.1)
- **Kāmadahana — the burning of Kāma** — Sent by the gods to kindle Śiva's desire for Pārvatī so a son can slay Tārakāsura, Kāmadeva fires his arrow and Śiva's third eye burns him to ash; Śiva later restores him bodiless (Ananga) _(actors: Śiva, Kāmadeva, Rati, Pārvatī)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā; Matsya Purāṇa; Kālidāsa's Kumārasaṃbhava)
- **Prahlāda pacifies Narasiṃha's wrath** — Narasiṃha's fury terrifies even the gods and Lakṣmī; the child Prahlāda alone calms him with the Nṛsiṃha-stuti and is offered any boon _(actors: Narasiṃha, Prahlāda, Brahmā, Rudra, Indra, Lakṣmī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.9–7.10)
- **Samudra Manthana - the curse that triggers it** — Sage Durvasa gives Indra a divine garland which Indra's elephant Airavata tramples; Durvasa curses the devas to lose their fortune and strength, and Lakshmi withdraws into the ocean _(actors: Durvasa, Indra, Airavata, Lakshmi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5; Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **Varaha rescues Bhudevi from the cosmic ocean** — As Bhudevi, the Earth goddess is rescued by the boar Varaha from the cosmic ocean _(actors: Varaha, Bhudevi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kamadeva-and-minor-deities.md) — (Daskavatara tradition)
- **Hiraṇyakaśipu liberated; Prahlāda enthroned** — Slain by the Lord's own hand, Hiraṇyakaśipu attains liberation (dveṣa-bhakti), discharging curse-birth #1; Narasiṃha enthrones Prahlāda as righteous daitya king, whose line leads to Bali _(actors: Narasiṃha, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda, Bali (descendant))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.1, 7.10)
- **Kurma supports Mount Mandara** — As the churning rod Mount Mandara sinks, Vishnu becomes the giant tortoise Kurma and bears the mountain on his back as the pivot for churning the Ocean of Milk for amrita _(actors: Kurma/Vishnu, devas, asuras, Vasuki, Mandara)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Vishnu Purana)
- **The Kadrū–Vinatā wager over the horse's tail** — Kadrū and Vinatā wager over the colour of Uccaiḥśravas's tail with the loser to become slave; Kadrū's nāga sons coil as black hairs to deceive, winning and enslaving Vinatā _(actors: Kadrū, Vinatā, the nāgas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata Āstīkaparva)
- **Tārakāsura Slain by Skanda** — The daitya Tāraka, boon-protected to die only by a son of Śiva, forces the gods to engineer Śiva's marriage to Pārvatī, whose son Kārttikeya/Skanda slays him in the Tārakāmaya war _(actors: Tārakāsura, Skanda, Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa; Kumārasambhava; Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Varaha avatara rescues the Earth and slays Hiranyaksha** — The Asura Hiranyaksha drags Bhumi to the bottom of the cosmic ocean; Vishnu as the boar Varaha dives in, slays him in a thousand-year duel, and lifts the Earth on his tusks _(actors: Vishnu (Varaha), Hiranyaksha, Bhumi/Prithivi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.13, 3.17-3.19; Vishnu Purana 1.4)
- **Emergence of the fourteen ratnas** — During the churning fourteen treasures rise from the ocean — including Kamadhenu, Uccaihshravas, Airavata, Kaustubha, Parijata, the Apsaras, Lakshmi, Varuni, Candra, Shankha, and Dhanvantari with the amrita _(actors: the churning devas and asuras)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7-8.8; Vishnu Purana; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Śiva Burns the Three Cities (Tripurāntaka)** — Three sons of Tāraka win three indestructible flying fortresses destroyable only by a single aligned arrow; Śiva as Tripurāntaka burns all three with one shaft from his earth-chariot _(actors: Śiva, Tārakākṣa, Vidyunmālī, Kamalākṣa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva; Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Kadrū curses the reluctant nāgas** — The serpents who refuse to deceive the tail are cursed by their mother Kadrū to perish in King Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice, driving the Mahābhārata's nāga frame-story _(actors: Kadrū, the nāgas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata Āstīkaparva)
- **Matsya saves Manu from the pralaya-flood** — Viṣṇu as the fish Matsya saves Manu and the seeds of life across the deluge — the Manvantara-transition framing the Matsya Purāṇa _(actors: Matsya (Viṣṇu), Manu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Andhaka Impaled by Śiva** — The blind asura Andhaka, born of Pārvatī covering Śiva's eyes, lusts after Pārvatī and is impaled on Śiva's triśūla until his clone-spawning blood dries, drunk by the Mātṛkās; redeemed, he becomes the gaṇa-chief Bhṛṅgi _(actors: Andhaka, Śiva, Pārvatī, Mātṛkās)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Garuḍa ransoms Vinatā by stealing the amṛta** — To redeem his enslaved mother Vinatā, Garuḍa is forced to fetch the amṛta from Indra's heaven, originating his nectar-theft, his enmity with the serpents and his recruitment as Viṣṇu's vāhana _(actors: Garuḍa, Vinatā, Indra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādiparva, Garuḍa cycle)
- **Narasiṃha slays Hiraṇyakaśipu** — Viṣṇu as the man-lion Narasiṃha kills the demon Hiraṇyakaśipu to protect the devotee Prahlāda — a Satya-Yuga avatāra event _(actors: Narasiṃha (Viṣṇu), Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Nṛsiṃha (Narasiṃha) Upapurāṇa)
- **Prahlada's devotion survives every attempt to kill him** — Hiranyakashipu's son Prahlada, taught Vishnu-bhakti by Narada in the womb, becomes a supreme devotee and survives poison, elephants, weapons, and fire _(actors: Prahlada, Hiranyakashipu, Narada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.5)
- **Saptarishi carried across the flood by Vaivasvata Manu** — In the Matsya flood, Vaivasvata Manu carries the seven sages, the seed of all creatures, and the Vedas across the pralaya, re-seeding knowledge for the current humanity _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, the Saptarishi, Matsya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana 8.24)
- **Shiva drinks the Halahala poison (Nilakantha)** — To save the cosmos from the world-destroying Halahala poison that first rises, Shiva drinks it; Parvati holds his throat so it lodges there, turning it blue and earning him the name Nilakantha _(actors: Shiva, Parvati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Shiva Purana)
- **Holika burns in the fire - origin of Holi** — Prahlada's fire-proof aunt Holika sits with him in flames to burn him but perishes while he survives, the origin myth of the festival of Holi _(actors: Holika, Prahlada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; folk/festival tradition)
- **Jalandhara Slain by Śiva** — Jalandhara, born of Śiva's third-eye fire and shielded by his wife Vṛndā's chastity, is undone when Viṣṇu deceives Vṛndā in his form, and Śiva slays him with a toe-carved cakra; Vṛndā self-immolates and becomes the Tulsī plant _(actors: Jalandhara, Śiva, Viṣṇu, Vṛndā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Mohini distributes the amrita** — Vishnu takes the form of the enchantress Mohini, beguiles the Asuras who had seized the nectar pot, and distributes the amrita only to the Devas _(actors: Mohini/Vishnu, Devas, Asuras, Dhanvantari)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.8-8.9)
- **Beheading of Svarbhanu (origin of Rahu and Ketu)** — The Asura Svarbhanu disguises himself among the Devas to drink amrita; exposed by Surya and Candra, he is beheaded by the Sudarshana chakra, his immortal head and body becoming Rahu and Ketu who cause eclipses out of grudge _(actors: Svarbhanu/Rahu/Ketu, Surya, Candra, Mohini/Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.9; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Hiranyakasipu's boon of near-invincibility** — Hiranyakasipu obtains a boon of near-invincibility (not by man or beast, day or night, indoors or out), the second life of the Jaya-Vijaya curse _(actors: Hiranyakasipu, Brahma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7)
- **Mahalakshmi born at the Samudra Manthana** — The supreme Lakshmi, consort of Vishnu, is born from the churning of the Ocean of Milk _(actors: Mahalakshmi, Vishnu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-forms-and-navadurga.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Sri Sukta)
- **Narasimha avatara slays Hiranyakashipu** — Vishnu bursts from a pillar as the man-lion Narasimha and kills Hiranyakashipu at twilight on the threshold upon his lap with claws, voiding every clause of the boon _(actors: Vishnu (Narasimha), Hiranyakashipu, Prahlada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.8)
- **Sudarśana severs Rāhu at the churning** — Viṣṇu's Sudarśana Cakra severs the asura Rāhu's head at the Samudra Manthana after he steals a sip of amṛta _(actors: Viṣṇu, Rāhu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Sudarshana Chakra (Wikipedia))
- **The Matsya and Manu flood narrative** — Manu rears a tiny fish that grows into the giant Matsya, who tows his boat to safety through the deluge _(actors: Manu, Matsya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/03-vana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 185)
- **Churning of the Ocean (Samudra Manthana)** — Viśvāmitra tells the Bāla-Kāṇḍa version of devas and asuras churning the Milk-Ocean with Mandara and Vāsuki, yielding the Hālāhala poison, Dhanvantari, apsarases, and Amṛta _(actors: Devas, Asuras, Śiva, Vāsuki)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 45)
- **Narasimha disembowels Hiranyakasipu** — The Man-Lion avatara bursts from a pillar at twilight to disembowel Hiranyakasipu, threading every clause of the boon, and saves Prahlada _(actors: Narasimha/Viṣṇu, Hiranyakasipu, Prahlada)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7)
- **Prahlada enthroned as righteous Asura king** — Narasimha's fury is pacified by Prahlada's prayers; Prahlada is enthroned as a virtuous Asura king and becomes ancestor of Bali _(actors: Narasimha, Prahlada, Bali)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.9-7.10)
- **War over the nectar and Indra's reinstatement** — Devas and Asuras battle over the nectar; with strength restored the Devas prevail and Indra is reinstated as king of the gods _(actors: Indra, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.10-8.11)
- **Dhruva becomes the Pole Star** — Rebuffed by his stepmother, the boy Dhruva performs intense tapas guided by Narada; Vishnu appears and fixes him as the immovable Dhruva Nakshatra around which the Saptarshi revolve _(actors: Dhruva, Uttanapada, Suniti, Suruci, Narada, Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.11-1.12; Bhagavata Purana 4.8-4.12 (canonically Svayambhuva Manvantara))
- **Varaha lifts the Earth and slays Hiranyaksha** — When the Asura Hiranyaksha drags Earth (Bhumi) to the bottom of the cosmic ocean, Vishnu becomes the colossal boar Varaha, slays Hiranyaksha in a thousand-year duel, and lifts the Earth back on his tusks _(actors: Varaha/Vishnu, Hiranyaksha, Bhumi/Prithivi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.13, 3.17-3.19; Vishnu Purana 1.4)
- **Daksha Yajna and Sati's self-immolation** — Prajapati Daksha snubs his daughter Sati and her husband Shiva at a grand yajna; the insulted Sati immolates herself in the sacrificial fire _(actors: Daksha, Sati, Shiva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.2-4.4; Shiva Purana; Kalidasa Kumarasambhava)
- **Hiranyakashipu's boon of near-invulnerability** — Enraged at his brother's death, Hiranyakashipu performs extreme tapas and wins from Brahma a boon that he cannot be slain by man or beast, day or night, indoors or outdoors, on earth or sky, by any weapon, then tyrannizes the three worlds _(actors: Hiranyakashipu, Brahma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.3-7.4; Harivamsha)
- **Nimi and Vasishtha's Mutual Curse** — Nimi and his purohita Vasishtha curse each other to bodilessness over a sacrifice dispute; from Nimi's churned body is born Janaka, founding the Videha/Mithila line _(actors: Nimi, Vasishtha, Janaka)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.5; Bhagavata IX.13)
- **Samudra-manthana (churning of the milk-ocean)** — Devas and asuras churn the milk-ocean with the Kurma avatara as pivot, producing amṛta, Dhanvantari, and Lakṣmi _(actors: Devas, Asuras, Kurma/Viṣṇu, Dhanvantari, Lakṣmi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Manu and the Flood (Matsya Avatara)** — The fish-avatara (Matsya) saves Manu from the cosmic deluge in the earliest extant Hindu flood narrative recorded in the Shatapatha Brahmana _(actors: Manu, Matsya/Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/yajurveda.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1)
- **Mohini tricks the asuras out of the nectar** — The Mohini avatara enchants the asuras and distributes the amṛta to the devas, denying the demons immortality _(actors: Mohini/Viṣṇu, Asuras, Devas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Prahlada's devotion and survival** — Hiranyakashipu's son Prahlada, taught Vishnu-devotion by Narada in the womb, becomes a supreme devotee and survives his father's repeated murder attempts by poison, elephants, weapons, and fire _(actors: Prahlada, Hiranyakashipu, Narada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.5)
- **Virabhadra's rampage and beheading of Daksha** — Enraged Shiva creates Virabhadra and Bhadrakali from a lock of hair; they destroy the yajna and behead Daksha, who is later revived with a goat's head _(actors: Shiva, Virabhadra, Bhadrakali, Daksha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.5-4.7; Shiva Purana)
- **Founding of the Shakti Pithas and Sati's rebirth as Parvati** — Shiva wanders bearing Sati's corpse, which Vishnu's Sudarshana cuts into pieces that fall across the land founding the 51 Shakti Pithas; Sati reincarnates as Parvati _(actors: Shiva, Sati/Parvati, Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Devi Bhagavata; Kalika Purana; Tantra literature)
- **Holika burned (origin of Holi)** — Prahlada's fire-proof aunt Holika sits with him in flames to burn him but herself perishes while he survives — the origin myth of Holi _(actors: Holika, Prahlada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; folk tradition)
- **Narasimha Bursts from the Pillar to Slay Hiranyakashipu** — In defense of the boy-devotee Prahlada, the man-lion Narasimha bursts from a pillar at dusk and slays the demon-king Hiranyakashipu _(actors: Narasimha, Prahlada, Hiranyakashipu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.1-10)
- **Ikshvaku founds the Solar dynasty** — Vaivasvata Manu's eldest son Ikshvaku, granted Aryavarta/Kosala, becomes progenitor of the Suryavamsha, the line of Mandhata, Sagara, Bhagiratha, Raghu, and Rama _(actors: Ikshvaku, Vaivasvata Manu, Nimi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.2-4.4; Harivamsha)
- **Matsya saves Satyavrata and the Vedas from the flood** — The Fish avatara saves Satyavrata (Manu), the seeds of life, and the Vedas from the dissolution-flood, the manvantara-transition par excellence _(actors: Matsya/Viṣṇu, Satyavrata/Manu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Narasimha slays Hiranyakashipu** — When challenged whether Vishnu is in a pillar, Hiranyakashipu smashes it and Vishnu bursts out as the man-lion Narasimha, seizing the Asura at twilight on the threshold upon his lap and disemboweling him with claws — voiding every clause of the boon _(actors: Narasimha/Vishnu, Hiranyakashipu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.8)
- **Pururavas and Urvashi** — The first mortal king of the Lunar line loves the apsara Urvashi under conditions, loses her when they break, and is eventually reunited _(actors: Pururavas, Urvashi)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Rigveda X.95; Shatapatha Brahmana XI; Vishnu Purana)
- **Dhanvantari Emerges at the Churning Bearing Amrita** — The divine physician Dhanvantari rises from the Samudra Manthana carrying the pot of amrita, linking the churning of the ocean to the origin of Ayurveda _(actors: Dhanvantari, devas, asuras)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upavedas-vedangas-darshanas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; Vishnu Purana)
- **Ila/Sudyumna and the founding of the Lunar dynasty** — From Vaivasvata Manu's gender-shifting child Ila/Sudyumna springs the Lunar dynasty (Chandravamsha) via Budha _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Ila/Sudyumna, Budha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.1; Bhagavata Purana 9.1)
- **Prahlada enthroned as Asura king** — After Narasimha's fury is pacified by Prahlada's prayers, Prahlada is enthroned as a righteous Asura king and ancestor of Bali _(actors: Prahlada, Narasimha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.9-7.10)
- **Kapila burns the 60,000 sons of Sagara** — Sage Kapila incinerates King Sagara's 60,000 sons for accusing him of stealing the ashvamedha horse, the curse later driving Bhagiratha's bringing-down of the Ganga _(actors: Kapila, Sagara's sons, Bhagiratha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.8; Ramayana Bala Kanda)
- **Kapila burns the sons of Sagara** — Sage Kapila incinerates the 60,000 sons of King Sagara for accusing him of stealing the sacrificial horse — the curse that later drives Bhagiratha's bringing-down of the Ganga _(actors: Kapila, the 60,000 sons of Sagara)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.8; Ramayana Bala Kanda)
- **Markandeya granted a short brilliant life** — The childless sage Mrkandu propitiates Shiva and chooses a virtuous son fated to die at sixteen; the radiant boy Markandeya is born and masters the Vedas _(actors: Mrkandu, Marudvati/Manasvini, Markandeya, Shiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva; Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Matsya Rescues Manu and the Vedas** — The fish-avatara Matsya rescues Manu and the Vedas from the deluge at the pralaya _(actors: Matsya, Manu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.24)
- **Descent of Ganga (Gangavatarana)** — Ganga is brought to earth by Bhagiratha's austerities, her fall broken by Shiva's matted hair, to liberate the ashes of Sagara's sons _(actors: Ganga, Bhagiratha, Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yamuna-and-river-goddesses.md) — (Ramayana Balakanda; Bhagavata; Mahabharata)
- **Shiva as Kalantaka conquers Death for Markandeya** — When Yama casts his noose around the boy clinging to a Shiva-linga, Shiva bursts forth as Kalantaka/Mrtyunjaya, strikes down Death, and blesses Markandeya to remain eternally sixteen and deathless _(actors: Markandeya, Shiva (Kalantaka/Mrtyunjaya), Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Sudarshana Chakra beheads Rahu** — Vishnu's time-disc the Sudarshana Chakra (Kala-chakra) beheads the demon Rahu who stole the amrita, the weapon-face of Time cutting off every form at its appointed moment _(actors: Vishnu, Rahu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/kalachakra-wheel-of-time.md) — (Mahabharata; Bhagavata Purana; Vishnu Purana)
- **Rishabhadeva avatara born to Nabhi and Merudevi** — Vishnu descends as Rishabha, son of King Nabhi and Merudevi of the Priyavrata line, an avatara of Narayana who fathers a hundred sons, the eldest being Bharata _(actors: Rishabhadeva, Nabhi, Merudevi, Jayanti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.3-5.4; Vishnu Purana 2.1)
- **Rishabha's renunciation and death by forest fire** — After delivering the Rishabha-gita to his sons and crowning Bharata, Rishabha wanders as a naked avadhuta and quits his body, consumed by a wildfire, absorbed in the Self _(actors: Rishabhadeva, Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.5-5.6)
- **Emperor Bharata's reign and renunciation** — Bharata rules Bharata-varsha righteously while inwardly detached, then divides the empire among his sons and retires to Pulaha-ashrama on the Gandaki to meditate _(actors: Bharata, Panchajani)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.7)
- **Bharata's attachment to the deer and rebirth as a deer** — The ascetic Bharata becomes attached to an orphaned fawn he rescues; dying with the deer in his mind, he is reborn as a conscious deer remembering his past life _(actors: Bharata, the fawn/deer)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.8)
- **Jada Bharata the silent sage and the Rahugana teachings** — Reborn as a brahmana, the soul feigns idiocy as Jada Bharata, is nearly sacrificed to Bhadra Kali (who saves him), then teaches King Rahugana the forest-of-samsara allegory and attains liberation _(actors: Jada Bharata, King Rahugana, Bhadra Kali)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.9-5.14)
- **Satya Yuga — the Age of Truth** — Dharma stands on all four legs; humans live ~100,000 years in spontaneous righteousness, with meditation as the path to liberation _(actors: humanity)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/yugas-and-mahayuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.3, Bhagavata Purana 12.3)
- **Soma emerges from the churning of the ocean** — In the Samudra Manthana the Moon (Soma/Chandra) emerges among the fourteen ratnas and is taken by Shiva onto his head, fusing the soma-as-nectar and soma-as-moon ideas _(actors: Soma/Chandra, Shiva, devas and asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/chandra-soma.md) — (Bhagavata, Vishnu, Matsya Puranas)
- **Kapila born to Kardama and Devahuti** — Kapila, an avatara of Viṣṇu and founder-sage of Sankhya, is born to the Prajapati Kardama and Devahuti to impart self-knowledge to his mother _(actors: Kapila, Kardama, Devahuti)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/darshanas/samkhya-karika.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.24-33)
- **Matsya rescues Manu and the Vedas from the deluge** — Vishnu as the fish Matsya warns Manu of the coming pralaya, has him build a boat loaded with the seeds of life and the seven sages, tows it through the flood, and (in variants) slays the demon Hayagriva to restore the stolen Vedas — marking the start of our Manvantara _(actors: Matsya (Vishnu), Manu, the saptarshi, Hayagriva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1; Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana 8.24)
- **Kurma supports Mount Mandara at the churning** — As devas and asuras churn the ocean of milk for amrita using Mount Mandara and the serpent Vasuki, the sinking mountain is supported on the back of Vishnu as the giant tortoise Kurma _(actors: Kurma (Vishnu), devas, asuras, Vasuki)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7-8; Vishnu Purana 1.9; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Dhanvantari and Mohini emerge at the churning** — During the Samudra Manthana the physician-god Dhanvantari emerges bearing the nectar pot, and Vishnu takes the Mohini form to trick the asuras out of the amrita _(actors: Dhanvantari, Mohini (Vishnu), devas, asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8; Vishnu Purana)
- **Narasimha slays Hiranyakashipu and saves Prahlada** — To evade the demon-king Hiranyakashipu's boon, Vishnu bursts from a pillar as the man-lion Narasimha at twilight on a threshold, and disembowels him with his claws while saving his devotee-son Prahlada _(actors: Narasimha (Vishnu), Hiranyakashipu, Prahlada)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.2-10; Vishnu Purana 1.16-20)
- **Rahu beheaded at the churning** — At the Samudra Manthana the asura Rahu steals the amrita and is beheaded by Vishnu as Mohini, becoming the eclipse-node _(actors: Rahu, Mohini (Vishnu))_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devas-asuras-and-the-lokas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8; Vishnu Purana)
- **Exile of the Daityas and Danavas** — In Krita/Satya Yuga the Daityas and Danavas are exiled from heaven by the devas and take refuge in the Vindhya mountains and the sea (Patala) _(actors: Daityas, Danavas, the devas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devas-asuras-and-the-lokas.md) — (Puranas)

## Tretā Yuga  ·  1166 events

*Dharma on three legs. Vāmana, Paraśurāma, and the Rāmāyaṇa.*

- **"I desire not the eight siddhis"** — giving away the last water, Rantideva renounces even liberation, asking only to enter into and bear the suffering of all embodied beings so they be freed from misery _(actors: Rantideva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rantideva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.21.12)
- **A Brāhmaṇa Is Adaṇḍya** — Rāma's councillors Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Kutsa, Vasiṣṭha and Kaśyapa rule that a brāhmaṇa cannot be corporally punished, forcing Rāma to let the plaintiff dog name the sentence _(actors: Rāma, Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Vasiṣṭha, Kaśyapa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramas-justice-the-dog-and-the-mendicant.md) — (Uttara Kāṇḍa, prakṣipta) [scholarly]
- **Agastya finds the corpse-eater at the empty lake** — wandering the deserted future-Daṇḍaka, Agastya sees a radiant heaven-dweller descend from a swan-chariot to devour a human corpse floating in a pristine lake _(actors: Agastya, King Śveta, apsarās)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shveta-corpse-king-and-agastya.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 77)
- **Ahalyā's śāpa-mokṣa** — Gautama's curse on Ahalyā is capped with an end-condition and released by Rāma's presence, the classic curse-liberation _(actors: Ahalyā, Gautama, Indra, Rāma)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/tapas-boons-and-curses.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 1.48–49)
- **Aṅgada crowned king of Kiṣkindhā** — at Rāma's final departure Sugrīva follows him into retirement, first enthroning his nephew Aṅgada so the once-disinherited prince inherits his father Vālī's throne in full _(actors: Aṅgada, Sugrīva, Rāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/angada.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa tradition) [late text]
- **Aṅgada leads the fast unto death on the southern shore** — deadline broken and Sītā unfound, the despairing prince, recalling his father's killing and dreading Sugrīva's wrath, resolves with his party on prāyopaveśa rather than return in disgrace _(actors: Aṅgada, Hanumān, Jāmbavān)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/angada.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Kiṣkindhā-kāṇḍa 55–56)
- **Aṅgada leads the southern search-party** — Sugrīva entrusts the decisive southern quarter to Aṅgada, commanding Hanumān, Jāmbavān, Nīla and others to seek Sītā across the Vindhyas and the southern ocean within one month _(actors: Aṅgada, Hanumān, Jāmbavān, Sugrīva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/angada.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Kiṣkindhā-kāṇḍa 41)
- **Aṅgada made crown prince of Kiṣkindhā** — at Sugrīva's consecration by Lakṣmaṇa, Vālī's orphaned son Aṅgada is installed as yuvarāja (heir-apparent), fulfilling his father's dying wish and securing the succession without civil war _(actors: Aṅgada, Sugrīva, Lakṣmaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/angada.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Kiṣkindhā-kāṇḍa 25–26)
- **Aṅgada plants his immovable foot (Aṅgada-Rāyabāram)** — in vernacular retelling Aṅgada roots his foot in the assembly and challenges the whole court to lift it; every rākṣasa champion and Rāvaṇa himself fail, and he taunts the emperor to bow at Rāma's feet instead _(actors: Aṅgada, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/angada.md) — (Kamba Rāmāyaṇam; Rāmcaritmānas, Laṅkā-kāṇḍa) [folk]
- **Aṅgada slays the rākṣasa Vajradaṃṣṭra** — in the successive sorties before Laṅkā's gates the crown prince kills the commander Vajradaṃṣṭra, fighting as the foremost vānara duellist after Hanumān _(actors: Aṅgada, Vajradaṃṣṭra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/angada.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha-kāṇḍa 51–58)
- **Aṅgada's defiant embassy to Rāvaṇa's court** — sent as Rāma's envoy demanding Sītā's release on pain of death and Vibhīṣaṇa's enthronement, Aṅgada is ordered seized, but leaps to the palace roof wrecking a turret and returns unharmed _(actors: Aṅgada, Rāvaṇa, Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/angada.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha-kāṇḍa 41)
- **Aśokasundarī curses Huṇḍa** — inviolate and enraged, she dooms the demon to die at the hands of the very Nahuṣa she is destined to marry, converting prophecy into fate _(actors: Aśokasundarī, Huṇḍa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ashokasundari-nahusha-hunda.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Bhūmi-khaṇḍa 108)
- **Bharata looses the Saṃvarta weapon** — unable to break the Gandharvas by ordinary arms, Bharata discharges the pralaya-scaled Saṃvarta astra and annihilates the host in a single stroke — three hundred thousand slain _(actors: Bharata, the Gandharvas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bharata-gandharva-conquest-takshashila.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 101; the three-crore host under Śailūṣa is the Agni Purāṇa's, ch. 11)
- **Birth of Kuśanābha's hundred daughters** — King Kuśanābha of Mahodaya begets one hundred daughters of unmatched beauty on the apsarā Ghṛtācī _(actors: Kuśanābha, Ghṛtācī)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kushanabha-daughters-and-brahmadatta.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 32)
- **Birth of Mandodarī to Maya and Hemā** — the asura-architect Maya and the apsarā Hemā have a daughter, Mandodarī, left in Maya's care when Hemā is recalled to the celestial sphere _(actors: Mandodarī, Maya Dānava, Hemā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/mandodari.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 12)
- **Birth of Śala, Dala and Vala** — Suśobhanā bears Parikṣit three sons under her father's curse, the eldest Śala succeeding to the Ikṣvāku throne _(actors: Suśobhanā, Parikṣit, Śala, Dala, Vala)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/manduka-frog-princess-sushobhana.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva CXCII)
- **Birth of Śūrpaṇakhā** — Śūrpaṇakhā is born to the sage Viśravas and the rākṣasī Kaikasī, youngest sibling of Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa and Vibhīṣaṇa _(actors: Śūrpaṇakhā, Viśravas, Kaikasī, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/shurpanakha.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 9–10)
- **Brahmā commands the creation of the vānara host** — the devas beget shape-shifting monkey-sons (and Jāmbavān springs from Brahmā's yawn) as an army for the coming Rāma-avatāra _(actors: Brahmā, the devas, Jāmbavān)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/vanaras-and-rikshas.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 17)
- **Brahmā parts them and ends the feud** — the Grandfather descends, dissolves their brute-nature, restores the sages to human form, declares Viśvāmitra's ordeal had won Hariścandra heaven, and reconciles the rivals in an embrace _(actors: Brahmā, Vasiṣṭha, Viśvāmitra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/adi-baka-bird-war.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa IX; Devī-Bhāgavata VI.13)
- **Brahmā's oracle names Raji the pivot of the devāsura war** — Deadlocked devas and asuras both ask Brahmā who will win, and he answers: whichever side the mortal king Raji joins _(actors: Brahmā, Raji, devas, asuras)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/raji-and-his-sons.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.9; Matsya Purana 24)
- **Brahmā's rebuke: tapas without dāna** — reaching Brahmaloka yet stricken by impossible hunger, Śveta is told by Brahmā that he gave no gifts, and is sentenced to eat his own endlessly-regenerating flesh daily _(actors: Śveta, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shveta-corpse-king-and-agastya.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 78)
- **Brahmadatta's marriage heals the hundred hunchbacked daughters** — Kuśanābha gives all hundred daughters to King Brahmadatta of Kāmpilya, and at the touch of his hand in the wedding rite each maiden's crookedness vanishes and her beauty returns _(actors: Brahmadatta, the hundred daughters, Kuśanābha, Somadā)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kushanabha-daughters-and-brahmadatta.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 33)
- **Breaking of Śiva's bow and wedding of Sītā** — escorted by Viśvāmitra to Mithilā, Rāma snaps the bow of Śiva and wins Sītā's hand in the quadruple wedding of Daśaratha's sons _(actors: Rāma, Sītā, Viśvāmitra, Janaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/rama.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa)
- **Bṛhaspati's heterodox-delusion rites corrupt the Rājeyas** — The destitute Indra begs Bṛhaspati, who performs strengthening rites and promulgates a deluding anti-Vedic teaching that makes Raji's sons fall from dharma _(actors: Bṛhaspati, Indra, sons of Raji)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/raji-and-his-sons.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.9; Matsya Purana 24; Bhagavata Purana 9.17)
- **Cirakārī deliberates too slowly to kill his mother** — ordered by the enraged Gautama to slay the adulterous Ahalyā, the habitually slow-acting son Cirakārī deliberates until his father repents, and slowness redeems them both _(actors: Gautama, Ahalyā, Cirakārī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shanti-parva-minor-upakhyanas.md) — (MBh, Śānti Parva 12.258)
- **Cūlī grants Somadā a mind-born son, Brahmadatta** — The gandharvī Somadā, daughter of Ūrmilā, serves the ascetic Cūlī and, being husbandless, asks as her boon a son by his tapas; the sage brings forth the mānasa son Brahmadatta, who rules Kāmpilya _(actors: Cūlī, Somadā, Brahmadatta)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kushanabha-daughters-and-brahmadatta.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 33)
- **Dala's poisoned arrow kills prince Senajit** — the defiant heir Dala aims a poisoned shaft at Vāmadeva, but by the sage's word it turns and slays his own ten-year-old son Senajit, and a second arrow freezes in his hand _(actors: Dala, Vāmadeva, Senajit)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/manduka-frog-princess-sushobhana.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva CXCIII)
- **Daśaratha rides into the sky** — by kingly merit and tapas Daśaratha mounts his war-chariot and ascends past the winds into the region of the nakṣatras to confront Saturn where he approaches Rohiṇī _(actors: Daśaratha, Śani)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dasharatha-shani-stotra-legend.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa, Nāgara-khaṇḍa)
- **Death of Dhruvasandhi and the Kosala usurpation** — the Solar-line king is killed by a lion while hunting, and Yudhājit of Ujjayinī slays Vīrasena of Kaliṅga to crown the younger prince Śatrujit at Ayodhyā _(actors: Dhruvasandhi, Yudhājit, Vīrasena, Śatrujit)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sudarshana-shashikala-navaratri.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa, III.14–15)
- **Devarāta receives Śiva's bow in trust** — The gods deposit Śiva's colossal bow (Pināka) as a nyāsa with king Devarāta of Videha, the heirloom on which the Rāmāyaṇa marriage-plot turns _(actors: Devarāta, the gods)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/videha-mithila-line-janaka.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 66)
- **Durgā worship instituted at Vārāṇasī and Ayodhyā** — Subāhu wins the boon that the Goddess remain forever as Kāśī's guardian Durgā, and the restored King Sudarśana establishes her worship throughout Kosala — the text's charter of royal Devī cult _(actors: Subāhu, Sudarśana, the Devī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sudarshana-shashikala-navaratri.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa, III.25–26)
- **Fall of Rāvaṇa and the agni-parīkṣā** — Rāma slays Rāvaṇa at Laṅkā, then publicly repudiates Sītā, who is returned unscathed from the fire by Agni before Rāma accepts her _(actors: Rāma, Rāvaṇa, Sītā, Agni)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/rama.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa)
- **Founding of Puṣkalāvatī for Puṣkala** — in the adjacent Gandharva country Bharata founds Puṣkalāvatī (Charsadda) and installs his younger son Puṣkala, then dwells in the two cities five years before returning to Ayodhyā _(actors: Bharata, Puṣkala)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bharata-gandharva-conquest-takshashila.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 101)
- **Founding of Takṣaśilā for Takṣa** — on the conquered Gāndhāra land Bharata raises the city of Takṣaśilā (Taxila) and consecrates his elder son Takṣa as its king _(actors: Bharata, Takṣa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bharata-gandharva-conquest-takshashila.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 101)
- **Gaṇeśa grounds the Raṅganātha vimāna** — bearing the vimāna south after the Laṅkā war, Vibhīṣaṇa entrusts it at Tiruvaraṅgam to a cowherd boy (Gaṇeśa in disguise) who sets it on the earth, rooting Raṅganātha at Śrīraṅgam forever _(actors: Vibhīṣaṇa, Gaṇeśa, Raṅganātha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tiruchirappalli-rockfort-thayumanavar.md) — (Śrīraṅga-māhātmya)
- **Gaṇeśa installs Mahābala at Gokarṇa** — after Rāvaṇa wins Śiva's liṅga by penance and is tricked into setting it down, Gaṇanāyaka roots it at Gokarṇa as Mahābala, its power reaching to the seven nether worlds _(actors: Gaṇeśa, Rāvaṇa, Mahābala/Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kotirudra-minor-linga-legends.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Koṭirudra-saṃhitā 8)
- **Gaṅgā is named at Devprayag** — the Bhāgīrathī of Bhagīratha's descent meets the Alaknandā, and from this confluence the united river is first called Gaṅgā _(actors: Gaṅgā, Bhagīratha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/panch-prayag-alaknanda-confluences.md) — (Wikipedia, Panch Prayag/Devprayag; Kedāra-khaṇḍa tradition)
- **Haihaya–Kāśī wars and Pratardana's vengeance** — After the Vītahavyas/Haihayas crush Haryaśva, Sudeva and Divodāsa of Kāśī, Bharadvāja's putrakāmeṣṭi yields Pratardana, who exterminates the Vītahavyas; Vītahavya is made a brāhmaṇa by Bhṛgu _(actors: Divodāsa, Bharadvāja, Pratardana, Vītahavya, Bhṛgu)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kashi-line-divodasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva 30)
- **Hanumān mistakes Mandodarī for Sītā** — searching Rāvaṇa's sleeping palace, Hanumān momentarily takes the radiant queen Mandodarī for Sītā, then reasons the captive could never sleep amid luxury _(actors: Hanumān, Mandodarī, Sītā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/mandodari.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Sundara Kāṇḍa 9–11)
- **Hariścandra restored by the Ajā Ekādaśī** — the truth-king, enslaved at the cremation ground, keeps the Ajā fast on Gautama's counsel and regains son, wife, and kingdom _(actors: Hariścandra, Gautama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ekadashi-mahatmyas-catalog.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa 39–63) [late text]
- **Huṇḍa abducts Aśokasundarī** — the daitya lord of Mahodaya carries her off and tries to win her by conjured illusion, an āśrama and false ascetic she sees through _(actors: Huṇḍa, Aśokasundarī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ashokasundari-nahusha-hunda.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Bhūmi-khaṇḍa 106–108)
- **Huṇḍa kidnaps the infant Nahuṣa** — learning his destined slayer is born to King Āyu, Huṇḍa steals the newborn and orders him killed and cooked, but the cook's compassion spares the child _(actors: Huṇḍa, Nahuṣa, Āyu, the cook)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ashokasundari-nahusha-hunda.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Bhūmi-khaṇḍa 110–112)
- **Indra declares himself Raji's son to keep the throne** — Owing Raji the rank of Indra, Indra bows at his feet claiming 'you are my father,' and the gratified Raji leaves him functioning as king of heaven _(actors: Indra, Raji)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/raji-and-his-sons.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.9; Matsya Purana 24)
- **Indra purified at Suchindram** — sin-stained from seducing Ahalyā and cursed by Gautama, Indra travels to the far-southern liṅga and is washed pure (*śuci*), giving the town its name *Śuci-Indram* _(actors: Indra, Gautama, Ahalyā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/suchindram-sthanumalayan.md) — (Sucīndra-sthala-māhātmya; cf. Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla 48–49)
- **Indra slays the apostate sons of Raji and regains heaven** — Once the deluded Rājeyas abandon the Veda and dharma, Indra kills all five hundred with the thunderbolt and recovers his station and sacrificial shares _(actors: Indra, sons of Raji, Bṛhaspati)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/raji-and-his-sons.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.9; Bhagavata Purana 9.17; Matsya Purana 24)
- **Indra surrenders heaven to Raji for his lifetime** — In the Bhāgavata's variant, Indra, terrified of Prahlāda, hands the celestial kingdom back to Raji and clasps his feet, and Raji holds heaven until his death _(actors: Indra, Raji, Prahlāda)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/raji-and-his-sons.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.17)
- **Indra's endless night-watch** — because his cleansing is held to continue, the temple's late-night *ardhajāma* pūjā is understood as Indra's own worship, kept invisibly each night _(actors: Indra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/suchindram-sthanumalayan.md) — (Sucīndra-sthala-māhātmya; temple custom)
- **Initiation into the inverted mantra "marā marā"** — too sin-laden for the Name itself, the penitent robber is set to repeating Rāma's name in reverse, which becomes Rāma on the tongue _(actors: the robber (Vālmīki-to-be), the Saptarṣi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/valmiki-ratnakara-conversion.md) — (Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa 6)
- **Instigation of Khara and the battle of Janasthāna** — the mutilated Śūrpaṇakhā rouses Khara, whose fourteen champions and then full host of 14,000 with Dūṣaṇa and Triśiras are annihilated by Rāma single-handed _(actors: Śūrpaṇakhā, Khara, Dūṣaṇa, Triśiras, Rāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/shurpanakha.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya Kāṇḍa 19–30)
- **Jāmbavān awakens Hanumān's forgotten powers** — the aged bear-king, who once circumambulated Trivikrama, rouses Hanumān to leap the ocean to Laṅkā _(actors: Jāmbavān, Hanumān)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/vanaras-and-rikshas.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Kiṣkindhā-kāṇḍa 65–66)
- **Janaka gives Yājñavalkya the Videhas and himself** — Taught the Self as one's own light through waking, dream and deep sleep, and told 'you have attained the fearless, Janaka,' the king answers: 'I give you the Videhas, and myself with them, into servitude' _(actors: Janaka Vaideha, Yājñavalkya)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/videha-mithila-line-janaka.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 4.1–4.4)
- **Janaka passes the agnihotra test to Yājñavalkya** — Janaka of Videha quizzes three brāhmaṇas on the agnihotra and drives off; Yājñavalkya pursues him, and the king wins the boon of unlimited questions — 'thenceforth Janaka was a brahman' _(actors: Janaka Vaideha, Yājñavalkya, Śvetaketu Āruṇeya, Somaśuṣma)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/videha-mithila-line-janaka.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 11.6.2)
- **Kārtavīrya Arjuna's thousand-armed empire and fall** — The Haihaya-Yādava emperor of Māhiṣmatī, boon-armed by Dattātreya, seizes Jamadagni's wish-cow and is slain by Paraśurāma, triggering the twenty-one Kṣatriya exterminations _(actors: Kārtavīrya Arjuna, Dattātreya, Jamadagni, Paraśurāma)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/yadava-vamsha.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.11; Bhāgavata IX.15-16, IX.23; Mahābhārata)
- **Kaśyapa and Aditi worship the icon** — reborn as Kaśyapa and Aditi, the couple keep the image and Viṣṇu is born to them as Upendra/Vāmana, the second of the three births _(actors: Kaśyapa, Aditi, Vāmana)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/guruvayur-krishna-kshetra.md) — (Guruvāyupura-māhātmya; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.3)
- **Khaṭvāṅga wins the devas' war** — the unconquerable Ikṣvāku king Khaṭvāṅga, son of Viśvasaha and ancestor of Rāma, is summoned by the demigods to fight the asuras, secures their victory, and is offered any boon he wishes _(actors: Khaṭvāṅga, the devas, the asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/khatvanga-one-muhurta.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.9.41–42)
- **King Śveta of Vidarbha renounces for tapas** — Sudeva's son Śveta, after a thousand-year righteous reign, sets his brother Suratha on the throne and withdraws to austerities by the forest lake _(actors: Śveta, Sudeva, Suratha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shveta-corpse-king-and-agastya.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 78)
- **Kuśa's four sons found their cities** — The Brahmā-born king Kuśa's sons Kuśāmba, Kuśanābha, Ādhūrtarajasa, and Vasu build Kauśāmbī, Mahodaya, Dharmāraṇya, and Girivraja respectively _(actors: Kuśa, Kuśāmba, Kuśanābha, Vasu)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kushanabha-daughters-and-brahmadatta.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 32)
- **Kuśanābha's putrakāmeṣṭi and the birth of Gādhi** — The sonless Kuśanābha performs a son-yielding sacrifice at which his father Kuśa promises a supremely righteous son, and Gādhi — Viśvāmitra's father — is born _(actors: Kuśanābha, Kuśa, Gādhi)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kushanabha-daughters-and-brahmadatta.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 34)
- **Kuśanābha's teaching of kṣamā** — Rather than avenging the god's assault, Kuśanābha praises his daughters' forbearance, declaring that on kṣamā the universe is established, and takes counsel on their marriage _(actors: Kuśanābha, the hundred daughters)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kushanabha-daughters-and-brahmadatta.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 33)
- **Liberation in a single muhūrta** — returning at once to earth, Khaṭvāṅga declares nothing dearer to him than Nārāyaṇa, casts off queens, kingdom and the guṇa-swayed senses, and merges in Vāsudeva/Brahman before the 48-minute hour is out _(actors: Khaṭvāṅga, Nārāyaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/khatvanga-one-muhurta.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.9.44–49)
- **Makarākṣa slain by the Āgneyāstra** — Rāma fits the fire-weapon of Agni to his bow and pierces Makarākṣa through the chest, felling Khara's son as his father had fallen _(actors: Rāma, Makarākṣa, Agni)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/makaraksha-son-of-khara.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa 79)
- **Makarākṣa's vow of vengeance** — the son of Khara joyfully accepts the charge, vowing to avenge his father slain by Rāma at Janasthāna _(actors: Makarākṣa, Rāvaṇa, Khara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/makaraksha-son-of-khara.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa 78)
- **Māṇḍakarṇi yields and weds all five** — unlike the wrathful Viśvāmitra, the sage succumbs to desire and takes the five apsaras as his wives rather than cursing them _(actors: Māṇḍakarṇi, five apsaras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandakarni-and-panchapsaras-lake.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya Kāṇḍa 11)
- **Māṇḍakarṇi's ten-thousand-year immersion** — the sage stands submerged in the lake living on air alone for ten thousand years, heaping up ascetic power that alarms the gods _(actors: Māṇḍakarṇi, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandakarni-and-panchapsaras-lake.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya Kāṇḍa 11)
- **Mandodarī bears Meghanāda (Indrajit)** — Laṅkā's crown prince is born to Rāvaṇa and Mandodarī, named for his thundercloud birth-cry _(actors: Mandodarī, Rāvaṇa, Meghanāda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/mandodari.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Mandodarī counsels Rāvaṇa to return Sītā** — with Vibhīṣaṇa and Mālyavān, Mandodarī urges restoring Sītā and peace with Rāma, declaring him no mere man; Rāvaṇa refuses _(actors: Mandodarī, Rāvaṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/mandodari.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa tradition; Rāmcaritmānas, Sundara–Laṅkā Kāṇḍa)
- **Mandodarī remarries Vibhīṣaṇa (later tradition)** — at Rāma's counsel the widowed queen weds the newly crowned Vibhīṣaṇa, securing Laṅkā's throne; absent from the Vālmīki critical edition [late text] [disputed] _(actors: Mandodarī, Vibhīṣaṇa, Rāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/mandodari.md) — (later Purāṇic/regional Rāmāyaṇa tradition)
- **Mandodarī's lament over the slain Rāvaṇa** — widowed on the battlefield, Mandodarī names lust for Sītā as the cause of Laṅkā's ruin and recognises Rāma as the eternal Viṣṇu _(actors: Mandodarī, Rāvaṇa, Rāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/mandodari.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa 111)
- **Manoramā's flight to Bharadvāja's hermitage** — the widowed queen escapes Ayodhyā with the child-heir Sudarśana and the minister Vidalla, taking refuge under the sage's protection against Yudhājit's pursuit _(actors: Manoramā, Sudarśana, Vidalla, Bharadvāja, Yudhājit)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sudarshana-shashikala-navaratri.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa, III.15–17)
- **Nahuṣa fostered by Vasiṣṭha** — the rescued infant is laid in Vasiṣṭha's hermitage, where the sage and Arundhatī raise him and school him in the Vedas and arms _(actors: Nahuṣa, Vasiṣṭha, Arundhatī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ashokasundari-nahusha-hunda.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Bhūmi-khaṇḍa 112–115)
- **Nahuṣa weds Aśokasundarī** — blessed by Śiva and Pārvatī, the Candravaṃśa king marries the Kalpavṛkṣa-born maiden, who in this Padma frame (not Virajā of the epics) becomes mother of Yayāti _(actors: Nahuṣa, Aśokasundarī, Yayāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ashokasundari-nahusha-hunda.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Bhūmi-khaṇḍa 119–120)
- **Nala bridges the sea to Laṅkā** — Viśvakarman's vānara son directs the building of the Setu in five days for Rāma's army _(actors: Nala, Rāma, the vānara host)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/vanaras-and-rikshas.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha-kāṇḍa 22)
- **Nārada boasts against Śiva's warning** — ignoring Śiva's counsel to tell no one, Nārada brags of his victory over lust to Brahmā and then to Viṣṇu, who resolves to humble him by māyā _(actors: Nārada, Śiva, Brahmā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada-moha-svayamvara.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Rudra-saṃhitā, Sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa 2)
- **Nārada curses the mocking Rudra-gaṇas** — the two attendants of Śiva who laughed at his monkey face are cursed to be born as demons from a rākṣasa womb, with the mitigation that they will return to Śiva's side _(actors: Nārada, the two Rudra-gaṇas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada-moha-svayamvara.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Rudra-saṃhitā, Sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa 4)
- **Nārada recites the saṃkṣipta-Rāmāyaṇa to Vālmīki** — asked who is the perfectly virtuous man, Nārada answers "Rāma" and plants the seed of the epic _(actors: Vālmīki, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/valmiki-ratnakara-conversion.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 1)
- **Nārada's penance and the false conquest of Kāma** — Kāmadeva, sent by Indra, fails to break Nārada's Himalayan tapas at Śiva's hallowed spot, and the sage swells with pride _(actors: Nārada, Kāmadeva, Indra, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada-moha-svayamvara.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Rudra-saṃhitā, Sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa 2)
- **Nārada's three-fold curse on Viṣṇu** — the enraged sage curses Viṣṇu to a mortal birth, to grief in separation from his wife, and to monkey companions — the Śaiva seed of the Rāma avatāra, which Viṣṇu gladly accepts _(actors: Nārada, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada-moha-svayamvara.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Rudra-saṃhitā, Sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa 4)
- **Nikumbha's curse empties Vārāṇasī** — Dishonored by King Divodāsa, the gaṇa Nikumbha curses Vārāṇasī to stand deserted a thousand years, and Śiva and Pārvatī dwell in the emptied city while the king removes to the Gomatī _(actors: Nikumbha, Divodāsa, Suyaśā, Śiva)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kashi-line-divodasa.md) — (Harivaṃśa ~29; Vāyu Purāṇa)
- **Parashurama founds the Pura Mahadev yatra** — Parashurama carries Ganga water on foot from Garhmukteshwar to worship Shiva at Pura Mahadev, an alternative founding of the kanwar vow [folk] [regional] _(actors: Parashurama, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kanwar-yatra-and-shravan-shiva-observances.md) — (Pura Mahadev/Garhmukteshwar temple tradition)
- **Paraśurāma reclaims Gomāntaka** — the axe-bearing avatar shoots an arrow into the sea, forces the waters back, and settles Brahmin gotras on the uncovered Konkan strip that becomes Goa _(actors: Paraśurāma, the ocean, Brahmin settlers)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/goa-shantadurga-mangeshi-kuladevatas.md) — (Sahyādri-khaṇḍa, Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Paraśurāma seeks out Dattātreya** — sick at heart after exterminating the kṣatriyas twenty-one times, the axe-wielder comes to his guru Dattātreya asking what world, bondage, and release truly are, and receives the Tripurā Rahasya _(actors: Paraśurāma, Dattātreya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-rahasya.md) — (Tripurā Rahasya, Māhātmya-khaṇḍa)
- **Paraśurāma's axe releases the Lauhitya** — bathing in the Brahmakuṇḍa frees Paraśurāma's axe and matricide-sin, and he cleaves the mountain wall to loose the river into the world _(actors: Paraśurāma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/lauhitya-brahmaputra-origin.md) — (Kālikā Purāṇa, 84–85)
- **Puruṣottama appears in the guise of an ascetic** — after Ratnagrīva's five-day fast at the Gaṅgā-ocean confluence the Lord comes disguised, promising darśana at noon and naming five who will reach the highest place _(actors: Puruṣottama/Viṣṇu, Ratnagrīva, Karamba the weaver)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ratnagriva-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Pātāla-khaṇḍa 21)
- **Raji destroys the asura host for the devas** — Fighting for the gods under the Indra-ship bargain, the Aila king Raji slays the asura armies and wins the war the devas could not _(actors: Raji, devas, asuras)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/raji-and-his-sons.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.9; Bhagavata Purana 9.17; Matsya Purana 24)
- **Rājñā Devī carried from Laṅkā** — displeased with Rāvaṇa who first installed her, the goddess Rājñā (Ragnya) asks Hanumān to bear her seat north from Laṅkā to Tulmul, where she settles as Kṣīr Bhavānī _(actors: Rājñā/Ragnya Devī, Rāvaṇa, Hanumān)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kashmir-tirthas-nilamata-geography.md) — (Kṣīr Bhavānī sthala tradition)
- **Rāma accepts fourteen years' exile** — honouring Daśaratha's boons to Kaikeyī, Rāma renounces the throne without protest and departs for the forest with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa _(actors: Rāma, Kaikeyī, Daśaratha, Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/rama.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā Kāṇḍa)
- **Rāma appoints Bharata over the Gandharva war** — Rāma assents to the conquest and dispatches Bharata with his two sons Takṣa and Puṣkala, the campaign framed from the outset as a city-founding for the next generation _(actors: Rāma, Bharata, Takṣa, Puṣkala)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bharata-gandharva-conquest-takshashila.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 100)
- **Rāma breaks the bow; the quadruple wedding at Mithilā** — Rāma snaps Śiva's bow and the Videha and Ikṣvāku houses are knit fourfold: Rāma–Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa–Ūrmilā, Bharata–Māṇḍavī, Śatrughna–Śrutakīrti _(actors: Rāma, Sītā, Janaka, Daśaratha, Kuśadhvaja)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/videha-mithila-line-janaka.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 67–73)
- **Rama carries water from Sultanganj to Baidyanath** — Eastern tradition holds Rama himself bore Ganga water from the uttaravahini Ganga at Sultanganj to the Vaidyanath Jyotirlinga at Deoghar, chartering the Shravani Mela route [folk] [regional] _(actors: Rama, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kanwar-yatra-and-shravan-shiva-observances.md) — (Shravani Mela/Baidyanath tradition)
- **Rāma keeps the Vijayā Ekādaśī at the ocean** — counselled before the crossing to Laṅkā, Rāma keeps the Vijayā fast by whose merit the ocean is crossed and Rāvaṇa defeated _(actors: Rāma, Vakadālbhya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ekadashi-mahatmyas-catalog.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa 39–63) [late text]
- **Rāma recognizes Satī and dispels her doubt** — Undeceived, Rāma salutes Satī by name as Dakṣa's daughter and asks why she wanders alone in Sītā's guise; her doubt collapses in shame _(actors: Rāma, Satī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sati-tests-rama.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Satī-khaṇḍa 24; Rāmcaritmānas, Bāl-kāṇḍa)
- **Rāma's akāl-bodhan founds the autumn Durgā Pūjā calendar** — Rāma awakens Durgā out of season in autumn and worships her from Ṣaṣṭhī to Daśamī before the Laṅkā war, the charter of Bengal's Śāradīyā festival days _(actors: Rāma, Durgā, Brahmā)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/durga-puja-bengal.md) — (Kṛttivāsī Rāmāyaṇ; Kālikā/Bṛhaddharma Purāṇa)
- **Rāma's Aśvamedha and the capture of the horse by Lava and Kuśa** — after the return to Ayodhyā the sacrificial horse wanders under Śatrughna's guard until Sītā's twin sons seize it at Vālmīki's āśrama, forcing recognition and reunion _(actors: Rāma, Śatrughna, Lava, Kuśa, Sītā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/padma-purana-khanda-map.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Pātāla-khaṇḍa)
- **Rāma's aśvamedha horse nears the Nīla mountain** — Śatrughna's army reaches the Puruṣottama region and the minister Sumati recounts the old tale of Ratnagrīva of Kāñcī _(actors: Śatrughna, Sumati, Śeṣa, Vātsyāyana)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ratnagriva-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Pātāla-khaṇḍa 17, 22–23)
- **Rāma's enlightenment and the charter of jīvanmukti** — Rāma attains repose in the Self, is roused from absorption, and chooses to rule and act while inwardly free, recasting the coming Rāmāyaṇa as a jīvanmukta's career _(actors: Rāma, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yoga-vasishtha-tales-catalog.md) — (Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha, Nirvāṇa Uttarārdha VI.2, final sargas)
- **Rāma's expiation at Devprayag** — Rāma performs penance at the Bhāgīrathī–Alaknandā confluence to cleanse the brahma-hatyā of killing Rāvaṇa; the Raghunāthjī temple marks the site [regional] _(actors: Rāma, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/panch-prayag-alaknanda-confluences.md) — (Wikipedia, Devprayag; regional sthala-purāṇa)
- **Rāma's Navarātri before the war on Rāvaṇa** — after Sītā's abduction, Nārada prescribes the autumn Navarātra-vrata; Rāma performs it and the Devī grants victory, the recovery of Sītā, and long rule _(actors: Rāma, Nārada, the Devī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sudarshana-shashikala-navaratri.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa, III.28–30)
- **Rāma's offered eye (akāl-bodhan)** — the Śākta twin of the tale: worshipping Durgā before Laṅkā with 108 blue lotuses, Rāma finds one hidden and prepares to give his own lotus-eye until the Goddess stays his hand _(actors: Rāma, Durgā, Hanumān, Vibhīṣaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vishnu-lotus-eye-sudarshana.md) — (Kṛttivāsī Rāmāyaṇ)
- **Rāma's retort and the arrow-duel** — Rāma recalls slaying Khara, Dūṣaṇa, Triśiras and fourteen thousand rākṣasas alone at Janasthāna, then breaks Makarākṣa's chariot and horses in a shaft-storm _(actors: Rāma, Makarākṣa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/makaraksha-son-of-khara.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa 79)
- **Rāma-paṭṭābhiṣeka and Rāma-rājya** — Rāma is crowned at Ayodhyā and his reign becomes the proverbial ideal polity of dharma, without untimely death or want _(actors: Rāma, Sītā, Bharata, Hanumān)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/rama.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha/Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Rāmavaradāyinī — the boon to Rāma** — southbound in search of Sītā, Rāma is blessed by the goddess at Tuljapur, folding the kṣetra into Rāmāyaṇa geography _(actors: Rāma, the Devī)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tuljapur-tulja-bhavani.md) — (sthala-tradition) [folk] [regional]
- **Rantideva keeps nothing for the morrow** — the Bhārata-line king, son of Saṅkṛti, gives away all that comes to him and lives in voluntary poverty, he and his household bearing want with perfect equanimity _(actors: Rantideva, Saṅkṛti's line)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rantideva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.21.3–4)
- **Ratnagrīva proclaims the pilgrimage to Puruṣottama** — minister Uttama announces the yātrā through Kāñcī and all four varṇas and occupational groups march east singing of Kṛṣṇa and Viṣṇu _(actors: Ratnagrīva, Uttama, the people of Kāñcī)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ratnagriva-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Pātāla-khaṇḍa 19–20)
