- **Karṇa born with the Kavaca-Kuṇḍala; Indra extracts it** — Karṇa is born with invulnerable golden armor and earrings fused to his body, the gift of his father Sūrya; Indra extracts them by guile to make Karṇa killable _(actors: Karṇa, Sūrya, Indra)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana/Karṇa Parvas)
- **The Mahabharata war and Krishna's departure mark the Dvapara-Kali transition** — The great Mahabharata war and Krishna's departure mark the turn from Dvapara into Kali Yuga, traditionally dated to 3102 BCE _(actors: Krishna, Pandavas, Kauravas)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/yugas-and-mahayuga.md) — (Mahabharata; Bhagavata Purana 1.18, 11.31, 12.2)
- **The Sauptika night massacre** — Ashvatthama raids the sleeping camp, killing Draupadi's five sons; his Brahmashiras aimed at Parikshit's womb is countered by Krishna, who curses him _(actors: Ashvatthama, Draupadi's sons, Krishna, Parikshit)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Sauptika Parva)
- **Yadava civil war at Prabhasa** — On pilgrimage the drunken Yadavas quarrel, the reeds turn to iron clubs in their hands, and the entire clan slaughters itself _(actors: the Yadavas, Satyaki, Kritavarma, Pradyumna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva)
- **Death of Balarama** — Balarama withdraws into yoga at the seashore and Shesha-naga issues from his mouth into the ocean as he departs the world _(actors: Balarama, Shesha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva; Bhagavata Purana 11.30)
- **Death of Shakuni** — Sahadeva beheads Shakuni, the dice-master architect of the war, fulfilling his own dice-hall vow _(actors: Sahadeva, Shakuni, Uluka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/09-shalya-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Shalya Parva)
- **Garga names Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma** — The Yādava family-priest Garga performs the naming rite for Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma _(actors: Garga, Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.8; Garga Saṃhitā)
- **Planets align in conjunction at the start of Kali Yuga** — The Surya Siddhanta sets all planets in conjunction at the start of Kali Yuga (18 Feb 3102 BCE), synchronizing the planetary clock with the cosmological clock _(actors: the grahas (planets))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/jyotisha-and-the-zodiac.md) — (Surya Siddhanta)
- **Submersion of Dwaraka** — As Krishna departs the sea reclaims Dwaraka; Arjuna evacuates the surviving women and children, who are raided by bandits en route _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Mausala Parva 7-8)
- **Death of Krishna** — Krishna sits in meditation under a pipal tree and the hunter Jara, mistaking his reddish sole for a deer, shoots an arrow piercing it; Krishna ascends to his abode, ending the avatar and marking the onset of Kali Yuga _(actors: Krishna, Jara)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva; Bhagavata Purana 11.30-11.31)
- **Onset of Kali Yuga at Krishna's departure** — Krishna's departure (traditionally 3102 BCE) marks the start of Kali Yuga and the Pandavas' final journey _(actors: Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana XI; Mausala Parva)
- **The mace-duel and fall of Duryodhana** — In the gada-yuddha Bhima, cued by Krishna, breaks Duryodhana's thighs with a foul below-the-belt blow, effectively ending the war _(actors: Bhima, Duryodhana, Krishna, Balarama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/09-shalya-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Shalya Parva)
- **The Uddhava-Gita** — Krishna gives his last great discourse to his devotee Uddhava on jnana, bhakti, and the avadhuta's 24 gurus before the end _(actors: Krishna, Uddhava)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-lila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.7-11.29)
- **Viṣṇu slays the demon Pañcajana and takes the conch** — In the Mahābhārata/Skanda variant, Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa slays the demon Pañcajana (in whale-form, who had swallowed Sāndīpani's son) and seizes the conch he dwelt in, naming it Pāñcajanya _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Pañcajana, Sāndīpani)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Mahābhārata; Skanda Purāṇa; Panchajanya (Wikipedia))
- **Ashvatthama's night massacre** — Empowered by Shiva, Ashvatthama with Kripa and Kritavarman slaughters the sleeping Pandava camp, killing Dhrishtadyumna, Shikhandin and the Upapandavas _(actors: Ashvatthama, Kripa, Kritavarman, Dhrishtadyumna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/10-sauptika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sauptika Parva)
- **Curse of the sages on Samba** — Krishna's son Samba is dressed as a pregnant woman to mock sages, who curse the clan to be doomed by an iron club _(actors: Samba, Vishvamitra, Durvasa, Narada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva)
- **Krishna's Vishvarupa theophany — 'I am Time'** — At the climax of the universal-form vision Krishna declares 'kalo'smi' — I am Time, the world-destroyer — revealing the cosmic person as the cosmic clock and Arjuna as its instrument _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/kalachakra-wheel-of-time.md) — (Bhagavad Gita 11.32-33)
- **Submergence of Dvaraka** — As Krishna leaves, the sea swallows Dvaraka; Arjuna evacuates the survivors but is robbed en route, his powers fading with the age _(actors: Arjuna, the survivors)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva)
- **Sudarśana Cakra beheads Śiśupāla** — Kṛṣṇa's Sudarśana Cakra beheads Śiśupāla after his hundred offenses are exhausted _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Śiśupāla)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Sudarshana Chakra (Wikipedia); Mahābhārata)
- **Brahmashiras duel and curse of Ashvatthama** — Ashvatthama aims the Brahmashiras at Uttara's womb; Krishna vows to revive the child Parikshit, takes Ashvatthama's gem and curses him to wander 3,000 years _(actors: Ashvatthama, Arjuna, Krishna, Uttara, Vyasa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/10-sauptika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sauptika Parva)
- **Brahma-vimohana-lila (Bewilderment of Brahma)** — Doubting child-Krishna, the Brahma of our universe steals Krishna's cowherd boys and calves; Krishna duplicates them all for a year and reveals countless universes each with its own Brahma, humbling his pride _(actors: Brahma, Krishna)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahma-lifetime.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.13-14; Brahma Samhita 5.40-48)
- **Draupadī demands Aśvatthāman's head after the night-raid** — After all five Draupadeyas are slain in the night-raid, Draupadī demands Aśvatthāman's head but accepts the gem from his crest instead _(actors: Draupadī, Aśvatthāman)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/draupadi.md) — (Mahābhārata Sauptika/Strī Parvas)
- **Karṇa loses his Nāgāstra against Arjuna** — Karṇa looses the nāgāstra (the serpent Aśvasena) at Arjuna's head, but Kṛṣṇa presses the chariot into the earth so it strikes only Arjuna's crown _(actors: Karṇa, Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa, Aśvasena)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Karṇa Parva)
- **Krishna delivers the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna** — Krishna answers Arjuna's crisis by teaching svadharma, niskama-karma, and the imperishable atman, reconciling the warrior's duty with ahimsa _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/ahimsa-and-hindu-ethics.md) — (Bhagavad Gita 2.19-25, 2.47-48, 3.35, 18.47)
- **Krishna slays Narakasura (Naraka Chaturdashi)** — Krishna with Satyabhama slays the asura Narakasura of Pragjyotishapura and frees 16,000 captives, the South Indian Deepavali charter _(actors: Krishna, Satyabhama, Narakasura)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Harivamsha)
- **Posthumous revelation of Karna's birth** — After the war Kunti reveals Karna was the eldest Pandava; the anguished Yudhishthira curses all women never to keep a secret _(actors: Kunti, Yudhishthira, Karna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karna.md) — (Mahabharata Stri/Shanti Parva)
- **Bhagadatta's Vaiṣṇavāstra absorbed by Kṛṣṇa** — Bhagadatta looses the infallible Vaiṣṇavāstra at Arjuna, but Kṛṣṇa absorbs it onto his own chest, where it becomes the Vaijayantī garland _(actors: Bhagadatta, Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Droṇa Parva)
- **Draupadī's death on the Himālayan ascent** — On the great departure toward heaven, Draupadī is the first of the six to fall dead, attributed by Yudhiṣṭhira to her partiality for Arjuna _(actors: Draupadī, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/draupadi.md) — (Mahābhārata Mahāprasthānika Parva)
- **Sage's curse on Samba's iron club** — Yadava princes mock rishis with Samba dressed as a pregnant woman; the cursed iron club is ground to powder that becomes the deadly eraka grass _(actors: Samba, Vishvamitra, Narada, Kanva, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva; Vishnu Purana)
- **Aśvatthāman looses the Nārāyaṇāstra; Pāṇḍavas survive by submission** — Aśvatthāman discharges Viṣṇu's Nārāyaṇāstra, and Kṛṣṇa has the Pāṇḍava host drop their weapons and dismount so the auto-multiplying barrage finds no resistance _(actors: Aśvatthāman, Kṛṣṇa, the Pāṇḍavas)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Droṇa Parva)
- **Draupadī restored as Śrī in heaven** — In heaven Yudhiṣṭhira finds Draupadī revealed as the goddess Śrī/Lakṣmī, closing her prior-birth incarnation _(actors: Draupadī, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/draupadi.md) — (Mahābhārata Svargārohaṇa Parva)
- **Submergence of Dwaraka** — As Krishna leaves, the sea swallows Dwaraka; Arjuna evacuates survivors but is robbed en route as his powers fade _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva)
- **The Yadava clan self-destructs at Prabhasa** — Thirty-six years after the war the drunken Vrishni-Andhakas slay one another with eraka-turned-iron clubs, fulfilling Gandhari's and the sages' curses _(actors: Satyaki, Kritavarman, Pradyumna, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva)
- **Death of Balarama and Krishna; sinking of Dvaraka** — Balarama departs as Shesha; the hunter Jara's arrow pierces Krishna's foot and he ascends, after which the sea swallows Dvaraka, ending the Dvapara Yuga _(actors: Krishna, Balarama, Jara, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Mausala Parva; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Śeṣa incarnates as Balarāma** — When Viṣṇu descends as Kṛṣṇa, Śeṣa descends as his elder brother Balarāma, whose serpent-nature departs his mouth as a white nāga at his death _(actors: Śeṣa, Balarāma, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/shesha-ananta.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Indra gives Karṇa the Vāsava-śakti for his kavaca-kuṇḍala** — Indra trades his one-use infallible dart, the Vāsava-śakti, to Karṇa in exchange for his birth-armor and earrings (kavaca-kuṇḍala) _(actors: Indra, Karṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Karṇa/Droṇa Parva)
- **Karṇa spends the Vāsava-śakti on Ghaṭotkaca** — Forced by Ghaṭotkaca's rampage, Karṇa expends his one-use Vāsava-śakti dart (reserved for Arjuna) to kill Bhīma's son Ghaṭotkaca _(actors: Karṇa, Ghaṭotkaca, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Droṇa Parva)
- **Arjuna beheads Karṇa with the Añjalikāstra** — Arjuna uses Indra's crescent-bladed Añjalikāstra to behead Karṇa, who had lost his Bhārgavāstra knowledge to a curse at the decisive moment _(actors: Arjuna, Karṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Karṇa Parva)
- **Śiva grants Barbarīka the three infallible arrows** — Śiva grants Ghaṭotkaca's son Barbarīka three infallible arrows able to end the entire war in a moment — one marks targets to destroy, one to save, the third destroys/binds the marked _(actors: Śiva, Barbarīka)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (folk Mahābhārata traditions (Khāṭū Śyām))
- **Sudarśana obscures the sun to trap Jayadratha** — Kṛṣṇa's Sudarśana Cakra obscures the sun at Kurukṣetra to trick Jayadratha into the open so Arjuna can fulfill his vow _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna, Jayadratha)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Sudarshana Chakra (Wikipedia); Mahābhārata)
- **Brahmaśiras duel of Arjuna and Aśvatthāman; killing and revival of Parīkṣit** — After Kurukṣetra, Arjuna and Aśvatthāman loose Brahmaśiras at each other; Vyāsa and Nārada intervene, Arjuna withdraws his but Aśvatthāman cannot, redirecting it at Uttarā's womb to kill the unborn Parīkṣit, whom Kṛṣṇa revives _(actors: Arjuna, Aśvatthāman, Vyāsa, Nārada, Kṛṣṇa, Parīkṣit, Uttarā)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Sauptika Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1)
- **Aśvatthāman cursed for the Brahmaśiras misuse** — For aiming the unwithdrawable Brahmaśiras at the Pāṇḍava line, Aśvatthāman is cursed with the loss of his head-jewel and a festering wound enduring for millennia _(actors: Aśvatthāman, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Sauptika Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1)
- **Burning of the Khāṇḍava forest and gift of the Gāṇḍīva to Arjuna** — When Agni begs Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa to help him consume the Khāṇḍava forest, Varuṇa gives Arjuna the bow Gāṇḍīva (made by Brahmā) with two inexhaustible quivers _(actors: Agni, Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa, Varuṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva; Gandiva (Wikipedia))
- **Pārijātaharaṇa — Kṛṣṇa steals the Pārijāta from Indra** — Kṛṣṇa uproots the Pārijāta tree from Indra's heaven and plants it in Satyabhāmā's courtyard, provoking a brief war with Indra _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Satyabhāmā, Rukmiṇī, Indra)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Hari-vaṃśa / Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10; Parijata (Wikipedia))
- **Sūrya gifts the Syamantaka gem to Satrājit** — The sun-gem Syamantaka, source of Sūrya's brilliance and yielding eight bhāras of gold daily, is gifted by Sūrya to the Yādava king Satrājit _(actors: Sūrya, Satrājit)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Syamantaka (Wikipedia); Vishnu Purana; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.56)
- **The Syamantaka affair — Kṛṣṇa fights Jāmbavān and weds Jāmbavatī** — Falsely accused of stealing the Syamantaka after Prasena is killed by a lion and the gem taken by Jāmbavān, Kṛṣṇa fights the bear-king for 28 days (or 21), who yields the gem and his daughter Jāmbavatī in marriage; Kṛṣṇa returns it and weds Satyabhāmā _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Jāmbavān, Jāmbavatī, Prasena, Satrājit, Satyabhāmā)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.56–57; Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Syamantaka (Wikipedia))
- **Kṛṣṇa sounds the Pāñcajanya to open the Kurukṣetra war** — Kṛṣṇa blows his conch Pāñcajanya, with Arjuna's Devadatta and the Pāṇḍava conches, to open the Bhagavad-gītā and the Kurukṣetra war _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna, the Pāṇḍavas)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Bhagavad-gītā 1.15–18; Panchajanya (Wikipedia))
- **Sūrya gives Yudhiṣṭhira the Akṣaya-pātra** — After Yudhiṣṭhira's penance in the Gaṅgā, Sūrya gives the Pāṇḍavas the inexhaustible food-vessel Akṣaya-pātra, yielding unlimited food each day until Draupadī takes her own meal _(actors: Sūrya, Yudhiṣṭhira, Draupadī, Dhaumya)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva; Akshaya Patra (Wikipedia))
- **Kṛṣṇa sates Durvāsā with a single rice-grain from the Akṣaya-pātra** — When Durvāsā and his thousand disciples arrive after Draupadī has eaten, Kṛṣṇa eats a single clinging rice-grain from the empty pot and thereby sates the sage's whole party _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Durvāsā, Draupadī)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva)
- **Kāliya-mardana — Kṛṣṇa dances on the serpent Kāliya** — The boy Kṛṣṇa leaps into the Yamunā at Vṛndāvana, is coiled by the venomous Nāga Kāliya, then dances on his hoods until he submits and departs, sparing him at his wives' plea _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Kāliya)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (tell-a-tale, Kaliya Daman; Wikipedia)
- **Kṛṣṇa masters the 64 kalās and 14 vidyās in 64 days** — After slaying Kaṃsa and his upanayana, Kṛṣṇa (with Balarāma) studies under guru Sāndīpani at Avantī/Ujjayinī and masters the 14 vidyās and 64 kalās within 64 days _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma, Sāndīpani)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sixty-four-kalas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.45)
- **Kṛṣṇa restores Sāndīpani's drowned son as guru-dakṣiṇā** — As guru-dakṣiṇā, Kṛṣṇa restores Sāndīpani's drowned son from the sea/Yama's realm _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Sāndīpani)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sixty-four-kalas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.45)
- **Krishna's life and the Bhagavad Gita** — Krishna slays his tyrant uncle Kamsa, lifts Govardhana hill, and as Arjuna's charioteer at Kurukshetra delivers the Bhagavad Gita; his departure in 3102 BCE marks the start of Kali Yuga _(actors: Krishna, Kamsa, Arjuna)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Mahabharata; Bhagavata Purana 10-11; Harivamsa)
- **Balarama's deeds** — Balarama, incarnation of the serpent Shesha and Krishna's elder brother, slays the asuras Dhenuka and Pralamba and drags the Yamuna river with his plow _(actors: Balarama, Dhenuka, Pralamba)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10; Vishnu Purana)
- **Kṛṣṇa destroys Śālva's flying fortress Saubha** — Kṛṣṇa destroys Saubha, the airborne fortress-city of the asura king Śālva, after it attacks Dvārakā _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Śālva)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/vahanas-and-celestial-vehicles.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva)
- **Vyāsa redacts the Vedas at the Dvapara–Kali junction** — Vyāsa (Krishna Dvaipayana) arranges and redacts the four Vedas at the Dvapara–Kali junction (~3102 BCE in the scriptural frame), earning the title Veda-Vyāsa _(actors: Vyāsa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/README.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Vayu Purana)
- **Vyāsa composes the Mahābhārata** — Vyāsa composes the Mahābhārata, chronicling the Kuru succession war at Kurukṣetra and containing the Bhagavad Gītā, with Krishna's departure marking the start of Kali Yuga _(actors: Vyāsa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/README.md) — (Mahabharata (Vyasa); Itihasa (Wikipedia))
- **The eight Vasus steal Vasiṣṭha's cow Nandinī** — The eight Vasus, led by Prabhāsa at his wife's urging, steal the wish-cow Nandinī from the sage Vasiṣṭha and are cursed to be born among mortals _(actors: Vasus, Prabhāsa, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-thirty-three-devas.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva (Sambhava Parva 1.99))
- **Gaṅgā drowns seven Vasu-newborns; the eighth becomes Bhīṣma** — The river-goddess Gaṅgā bears the cursed Vasus by King Śāntanu and drowns the first seven at birth to release them; Śāntanu stays her hand at the eighth, Prabhāsa, who lives on as Bhīṣma _(actors: Gaṅgā, Śāntanu, Prabhāsa, Bhīṣma)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-thirty-three-devas.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Arjuna requests the Gita teaching again (Anugita frame)** — After the Kurukshetra war, as Krishna prepares to leave for Dvaraka, Arjuna confesses he has forgotten the supreme teaching of Kurukshetra and begs Krishna to repeat it _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anugita.md) — (Mahabharata 14.16 (Ashvamedhika Parva))
- **Krishna smears color on Radha and the gopis (Holi)** — Krishna playfully smears color on Radha and the gopis in Vrindavan, the devotional origin of Holi's play of colors _(actors: Krishna, Radha, gopis)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Krishna Lila)
- **Krishna declines to repeat the Gita verbatim** — Krishna rebukes Arjuna's lapse and declares he cannot reproduce the original discourse word-for-word since it was uttered in a yogic trance, choosing instead to convey the same truths through an old narrative _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anugita.md) — (Mahabharata 14.16)
- **Krishna speaks the Anugita to Arjuna** — In peacetime after the war, Krishna delivers the Anugita, a jnana-and-Samkhya seminar restating the Gita through embedded ancient stories, within the Ashvamedhika Parva _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anugita.md) — (Mahabharata 14, Anugita (Telang, SBE vol. 8))
- **Yudhishthira performs the Ashvamedha horse-sacrifice** — To expiate the slaughter of the war, Yudhishthira performs the ashvamedha (horse-sacrifice) that gives Book 14 of the Mahabharata its name _(actors: Yudhishthira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anugita.md) — (Mahabharata, Ashvamedhika Parva)
- **Nalakūbara and Maṇigrīva cursed to become trees** — Kubera's sons Nalakūbara and Maṇigrīva are cursed by Nārada to become trees, later liberated by the infant Kṛṣṇa in the yamalārjuna episode _(actors: Nalakūbara, Maṇigrīva, Nārada, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/yakshas-and-guhyakas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.10)
- **The Yakṣa Praśna and revival of the Pāṇḍavas** — A yakṣa guarding a lake kills the four younger Pāṇḍavas who drink without answering him; Yudhiṣṭhira alone answers the dharma-catechism, and the yakṣa — revealed as Yama-Dharma — restores his brothers to life _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Yama-Dharma, Pāṇḍavas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/yakshas-and-guhyakas.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva)
- **Sthūṇa exchanges sex with Śikhaṇḍin** — The yakṣa Sthūṇa compassionately exchanges his sex with Śikhaṇḍinī so she can become male; Kubera curses the exchange permanent, enabling the fall of Bhīṣma _(actors: Sthūṇa, Śikhaṇḍin, Kubera, Bhīṣma)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/yakshas-and-guhyakas.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva)
- **Astika halts Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice (Nag Panchami)** — The sage Astika stops King Janamejaya's sarpa-satra and saves the serpent race, the Adi Parva frame-story commemorated at Nag Panchami _(actors: Astika, Janamejaya)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
- **Krishna subdues the serpent Kaliya** — Krishna subdues the serpent Kaliya in the Yamuna, recalled in western Nag Panchami strands _(actors: Krishna, Kaliya)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Krishna Lila)
- **Birth of Krishna (Janmashtami)** — Krishna, the 8th avatar, is born at midnight in Mathura's prison to Devaki and Vasudeva, commemorated by Krishna Janmashtami _(actors: Krishna, Devaki, Vasudeva)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Krishna Lila; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Krishna lifts Govardhan Hill (Govardhan Puja)** — Krishna lifts Govardhan Hill on one finger to shelter Vrindavan from Indra's rains, teaching worship of nature over Indra; commemorated as Annakut _(actors: Krishna, Indra)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana)
- **Vyasa dictates the Mahabharata to Ganesha** — Ganesha serves as scribe to whom Vyasa dictates the Mahabharata, invoked at Ganesh Chaturthi as lord of letters and beginnings _(actors: Vyasa, Ganesha)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Mahabharata tradition)
- **Bhishma chooses death at Uttarayana (Makar Sankranti)** — Bhishma, lying on his bed of arrows with the boon of icchamrityu, waits for Uttarayana before releasing his life, commemorated at Makar Sankranti _(actors: Bhishma)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Mahabharata, Anushasana Parva)
- **Draupadi binds her sari on Krishna's finger** — Draupadi binds her torn sari on Krishna's bleeding finger and he vows lifelong protection, repaid at the vastra-haran; a Raksha Bandhan charter _(actors: Draupadi, Krishna)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Mahabharata, Sabha Parva)
- **Krishna speaks the Gita on Mokshada Ekadashi** — Vaikuntha/Mokshada Ekadashi marks the day the Bhagavad Gita was spoken by Krishna to Arjuna _(actors: Krishna, Arjuna)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Bhagavad Gita tradition)
- **Birth of Vyasa / division of the Veda (Guru Purnima)** — Guru Purnima honors the birth and Veda-division day of Veda Vyasa, the Adi Guru who split the one Veda into four and composed the Mahabharata and Puranas _(actors: Veda Vyasa)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Vyasa tradition)
- **The Avantī Brāhmaṇa's Song of Forbearance (Bhikṣu-gītā)** — Recited by Kṛṣṇa to Uddhava in his farewell teaching: a rich but miserly brāhmaṇa of Avantī (Ujjain), who hoarded wealth and neglected gods, guests, and ancestors, is stripped of everything by fate (relatives, thieves, time, fire, accident); reduced to begging he is mocked, beaten, and reviled by the townsfolk, yet bears it without anger. Reflecting, he realizes that neither other people, the body, the planets (graha), time (kāla), nor fate/karma cause his suffering — the mind alone (manas) is the cause of bondage and liberation; he vows forbearance (titikṣā), crosses the ocean of material existence, and attains peace _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava, the unnamed miserly brāhmaṇa of Avantī (Ujjain), the townspeople of Avantī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uddhava-gita.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.23 (Bhikṣu-gītā / Avantī-brāhmaṇa-gītā), within the Uddhava-gītā (11.6.40–11.29))

## Kali Yuga — Scriptural & Prophetic  ·  492 events

*Dharma on one leg. The current age (from 3102 BCE) and its prophesied end with Kalki.*

- **Acyutānanda's Mālikā foretells Kali's end** — palm-leaf Bhaviṣya Mālikā prophecies of calamity, the sea entering Purī, Jagannātha leaving the Śrīmandira, and Kalki's advent [folk] [disputed] _(actors: Acyutānanda Dāsa, Jagannātha, Kalki)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/odia-literature-sarala-and-panchasakha.md) — (Bhaviṣya Mālikā corpus)
- **Aśvatthāman's weapon against the embryo** — After Kurukṣetra, Aśvatthāman hurls the Brahmaśiras/Aiṣīka weapon to abort the unborn last Kuru heir in Uttarā's womb _(actors: Aśvatthāman, Uttarā, the unborn Parīkṣit)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Mahābhārata Sauptika Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.7–8)
- **Ātmadeva retires to the forest with the Tenth Skandha** — Counselled in vairāgya by Gokarṇa, the grieving Ātmadeva renounces home at sixty, daily recites the Bhāgavata's Tenth Skandha, and attains the Lord _(actors: Ātmadeva, Gokarṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-mahatmya-gokarna-dhundhukari.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa, Bhāgavata-Māhātmya 4)
- **Bhakti revived by Bhāgavata recitation** — Bhakti personified, wandering with her fainting sons Jñāna and Vairāgya, is restored in Kali-yuga by recitation of the Bhāgavata, with the Gokarṇa–Dhundhukārī ghost-liberation tale _(actors: Bhakti, Jñāna, Vairāgya, Gokarṇa, Dhundhukārī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/padma-purana-khanda-map.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa, Bhāgavata-māhātmya)
- **Bharata ascends by one funeral-rite merit and Puṣkara's grace** — the sinner, saved by having once carried a stranger's dead child to the Gaṅgā bank and performed its funeral rites, rises to heaven in a celestial vehicle, crediting the grace of Puṣkara _(actors: Bharata, Puṇḍarīka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pundarika-of-pushkara.md) — (Padma Purana, Uttara-khanda 218–219)
- **Bharata dies confessing at Puṣkara** — Puṇḍarīka finds his sinful younger brother mortally wounded at the lake and hears his confession of the prostitute Prabhāvatī, gambling, theft, and a brāhmaṇa's killing _(actors: Puṇḍarīka, Bharata, Prabhāvatī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pundarika-of-pushkara.md) — (Padma Purana, Uttara-khanda 218)
- **Bhartṛhari and the immortality-fruit** — given an amṛta-phala, Bhartṛhari watches it circle from queen to stable-master to courtesan and back to him, grasps the vanity of desire, cedes the throne of Ujjayinī to Vikramāditya, and turns yogin _(actors: Bhartṛhari, Piṅgalā, the kotwāl, a courtesan, Vikramāditya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/simhasana-dvatrimshika-vikramaditya-cycle.md) — (Ujjain / Bhartṛhari tradition) [folk]
- **Bhīmā glorified as Candrabhāgā** — the Pāṇḍuraṅga-māhātmya sanctifies the crescent bend of the Bhīmā at Pandharpur as the Candrabhāgā tīrtha whose bath destroys sins, with Puṇḍalīka's shrine on its sands _(actors: Puṇḍalīka, the river-goddesses)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pandharpur-vitthala-wari.md) — (Pāṇḍuraṅga-māhātmya) [late text]
- **Binduga forsakes Cañculā** — a base brahmin of the seaside village Bāṣkala abandons his faithful, beautiful wife Cañculā for a prostitute, squandering himself in a courtesan's house _(actors: Binduga, Cañculā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shiva-purana-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Śivapurāṇa-Māhātmya 3)
- **Binduga the wind-eating piśāca** — Pārvatī reveals that Binduga, after death and hell, has become a piśāca bound to the Vindhya mountains, feeding only on wind, from the residue of his sins _(actors: Pārvatī, Cañculā, Binduga)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shiva-purana-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Śivapurāṇa-Māhātmya 5)
- **Binduga's salvation by recitation** — at Cañculā's intercession the Gandharva-king Tumburu recites the whole Śiva Purāṇa (saṃhitās 1–7) to the bound ghost, who sheds his sins and piśāca-body and ascends by aerial chariot to Śiva's abode _(actors: Cañculā, Tumburu, Binduga)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shiva-purana-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Śivapurāṇa-Māhātmya 5)
- **Birth of Naravāhanadatta** — from the restored marriage of Udayana and Vāsavadattā is born the son destined to become cakravartin of the Vidyādharas, the frame-hero of the rest of the ocean of story _(actors: Udayana, Vāsavadattā, Naravāhanadatta)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/udayana-vasavadatta.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara IV, Naravāhanadattajanana)
- **Bṛhadratha's Renunciation** — King Bṛhadratha, judging body and world impermanent, installs his son and retires to the forest for austerity _(actors: King Bṛhadratha, his son)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/maitrayaniya-upanishad.md) — (Maitrī Upaniṣad 1.1)
- **Bhīma's unforgiving taunt drives the elders to renounce** — During fifteen years of concord, Bhīma alone cannot forgive and openly boasts of slaying the Kaurava sons and drinking Duḥśāsana's blood, wounding Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī and pushing them toward renunciation _(actors: Bhīma, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Ashramavasa))
- **Brahman identified as Kṛṣṇa-Gopāla** — The Upaniṣad opens by declaring the supreme Brahman to be Kṛṣṇa, the eternal cowherd (Gopāla) of Vṛndāvana, cause of all causes _(actors: Kṛṣṇa-Gopāla, Brahman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/gopala-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Pūrva-tāpanī)
- **Cañculā's adultery and the pimping contract** — neglected, the once-chaste Cañculā takes a paramour; discovering it, Binduga strikes a nefarious mutual contract, profiting from his wife's adultery until her youth fades _(actors: Cañculā, Binduga, her paramour)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shiva-purana-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Śivapurāṇa-Māhātmya 3)
- **Cañculā's disillusion at Gokarṇa** — at the Gokarṇa temple Cañculā chances to hear a discourse describing the tortures of adulterous women, trembles with fear, and falls at the reciting brahmin's feet begging to be lifted from her plight _(actors: Cañculā, the reciting brahmin)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shiva-purana-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Śivapurāṇa-Māhātmya 3)
- **Cañculā's salvation** — instructed in the Śiva Purāṇa she takes up Śaiva asceticism — bark, matted hair, ash, rudrākṣa, Śiva's names — casts off her body, assumes the form of Gaurī, and becomes an attendant of Pārvatī in Śiva's city _(actors: Cañculā, Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shiva-purana-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Śivapurāṇa-Māhātmya 4)
- **Caṇḍamahāsena's artificial elephant** — the Ujjayinī king traps the elephant-charmer Udayana of Vatsa by a mechanical wooden elephant hiding armed men in the Vindhya forest, carrying him captive to Ujjayinī _(actors: Caṇḍamahāsena, Udayana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/udayana-vasavadatta.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara II, Kathāmukha)
- **Citraketu's sonlessness** — The mighty emperor of Śūrasena grieves that none of his many wives bears him a son _(actors: Citraketu, his queens)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/citraketu.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.14.10–17)
- **Codification of the tālamāna unit system** — The śilpa-śāstras define the aṅgula, mānāṅgula and the face-based tāla (12 aṅgulas) as the modular units of all image-measure _(actors: śilpins (image-makers); compilers of the Mānasāra and Mayamata)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/murti-lakshana-and-iconometry.md) — (Mānasāra; Mayamata; Śilpa Śāstra tradition)
- **Composition of the Nṛsiṃha-anuṣṭubh (Mantrarāja)** — After Narasiṃha slays Hiraṇyakaśipu, the terrified gods and ṛṣis compose the thirty-two-syllable anuṣṭubh 'king of mantras' to pacify and praise the Man-Lion _(actors: Narasiṃha, the Devas, ṛṣis (in the slaying of Hiraṇyakaśipu))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/nrisimha-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Nṛsiṃha-pūrva-tāpanīya Upaniṣad; Nṛsiṃha-anuṣṭubh / Mantrarāja)
- **Coronation of Parīkṣit at Hastināpura** — Renouncing the throne, Yudhiṣṭhira installs Parīkṣit, the lone Kuru heir revived by Kṛṣṇa in the womb, as King of Hastināpura with Kṛpa as his preceptor, and leaves Yuyutsu as regent _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Parīkṣit, Kṛpa, Yuyutsu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.1)
- **Devarāja's catalogue of sins** — a Kirāta brahmin turned liquor-seller robs all four varṇas by murder, kills his own mother, father, and first wife for wealth, and dissipates the family fortune with the courtesan Śobhāvatī _(actors: Devarāja, Śobhāvatī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shiva-purana-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Śivapurāṇa-Māhātmya 2)
- **Devasmitā and the red lotus of fidelity** — armed with Śiva's chastity-token, a merchant's wife sees through the nun Yogakaraṇḍikā's weeping-bitch ruse, brands four seducers with a dog's-foot mark, and reclaims her honor disguised as a merchant _(actors: Devasmitā, Guhasena, Yogakaraṇḍikā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kathasaritsagara-famous-tales.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara II.13)
- **Dhaneśvara saved by a single Kārtika lamp** — a lifelong sinner is present when a lamp is lit before Viṣṇu in Kārtika, and that one accidental dīpa outweighs his sins so his soul is saved at death _(actors: Dhaneśvara, Yama's messengers, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kartika-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Skanda P., Kārttikamāsa-māhātmya; Padma P., Uttara-khaṇḍa)
- **Dharmadatta frees the piśācī Kalahā** — a drop of Tulasī-sanctified water from the brāhmaṇa's Kārtika worship cleanses the quarrel-ghost Kalahā and releases her from ghost-hood _(actors: Dharmadatta, Kalahā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kartika-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Padma P., Uttara-khaṇḍa)
- **Dhundhukārī murdered by the five harlots; becomes a preta** — His prostitutes strangle him with ropes and kill him with burning coals, burying the body secretly; dead by violence without rites, he becomes a tormented wind-form ghost _(actors: Dhundhukārī, the five harlots)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-mahatmya-gokarna-dhundhukari.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa, Bhāgavata-Māhātmya 5)
- **Durvāsas commissioned to revive the Śaiva teaching** — the śāstras lost in deepening Kali Yuga, Śiva as Śrīkaṇṭha orders Durvāsas to restore them; his mind-born son Tryambaka founds the non-dual line claimed by Kashmir Śaivism _(actors: Śrīkaṇṭha/Śiva, Durvāsas, Tryambaka)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/kashmir-shaiva-texts.md) — (lineage account with Tantrāloka 36, Jayaratha's Viveka)
- **Founding of the Four Vaishnava Sampradayas** — To anchor valid initiation in Kali Yuga, four authorized disciplic lines are inaugurated by Shri, Brahma, Rudra and the Kumaras, whose acharyas are prophesied to appear at Purushottama-kshetra _(actors: Shri/Lakshmi, Brahma, Rudra, the four Kumaras)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/four-vaishnava-sampradayas.md) — (Padma Purana (attributed); Prameya-ratnavali)
- **Gāṇḍīva surrendered at the Lauhitya waters** — on the Pāṇḍavas' final journey Agni bars the way and Arjuna casts the Gāṇḍīva and quivers back into the Lauhitya sea for Varuṇa _(actors: Arjuna, Agni, Varuṇa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/lauhitya-brahmaputra-origin.md) — (Mahābhārata, Mahāprasthānika Parva)
- **Gayā-śrāddha fails and Sūrya counsels the saptāha** — Gokarṇa's śrāddha at Gayā and every tīrtha cannot free the preta, who appears in shifting terrible forms; appealed to, the Sun-god prescribes a seven-day hearing of the Bhāgavata _(actors: Gokarṇa, Dhundhukārī, Sūrya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-mahatmya-gokarna-dhundhukari.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa, Bhāgavata-Māhātmya 5)
- **Gokarṇa born of the cow** — The cow that ate the sannyāsī's fruit gives birth to a perfect human child with cow's ears, named Gokarṇa, raised alongside the wicked Dhundhukārī _(actors: Gokarṇa, Ātmadeva, Dhundhukārī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-mahatmya-gokarna-dhundhukari.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa, Bhāgavata-Māhātmya 4)
- **Guru and Vāyu install Kṛṣṇa at Guruvāyūr** — as Dvārakā sinks at the Dvāpara–Kali hinge, Bṛhaspati and Vāyu recover the floating icon, are guided by Paraśurāma, and enshrine it by Rudratīrtha where Śiva cedes the spot and withdraws to Mammiyūr _(actors: Bṛhaspati, Vāyu, Paraśurāma, Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/guruvayur-krishna-kshetra.md) — (Guruvāyupura-māhātmya) [late text]
- **Indra's dance-contest & the gift of the throne** — summoned to Amarāvatī to judge whether Rambhā or Urvaśī dances better, Vikramāditya renders a flawless verdict and Indra rewards him with the jewelled lion-throne borne by thirty-two apsara statuettes _(actors: Vikramāditya, Indra, Rambhā, Urvaśī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/simhasana-dvatrimshika-vikramaditya-cycle.md) — (Siṃhāsana-dvātriṃśikā, frame)
- **Janamejaya questions Vaiśampāyana about Kashmir** — In the generation after the war, Janamejaya asks why no Kashmir king fought at Kurukṣetra, and Vaiśampāyana's answer unfolds into the whole Nīlamata — Kashmir's origins and Nīla's ordinances _(actors: Janamejaya, Vaiśampāyana)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/nilamata-purana.md) — (Nīlamata Purāṇa, frame narrative)
- **Kali Yuga Begins** — Kali Yuga starts at 3102 BCE the moment Kali fully enters, reckoned from Krishna's departure from earth _(actors: Kali (personified age), Krishna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.15.36, Vishnu Purana 5.38, Surya Siddhanta 1.15-20)
- **Katamaraju crowned Pasuvulanna** — the Yadava cattle-chief, reckoned 74th from Vishnu and 23rd from Krishna and himself an incarnation of Vishnu, is crowned sovereign over all the Yadava herds and vows lifelong brahmacarya _(actors: Katamaraju, Bhaktiranna, Sridevi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/katamaraju-katha.md) — (Katamaraju Kathalu, Coronation of Katama Raju)
- **Katamaraju's duel with Goddess Ganga at the Paleru** — driven south by drought, the herder-king argues with the goddess Ganga who bars his herds at the Paleru, finally salutes and worships her, and is blessed to cross _(actors: Katamaraju, Ganga, Peyyala Yerrayya, Padma Raghava)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/katamaraju-katha.md) — (Katamaraju Kathalu, Ballad of Paleru)
- **King Cola vs Viṣṇudāsa & the freed brahma-rākṣasa** — rich king and poor bhakta each donate a Kārtika-observance to liberate a tree-haunting brahma-rākṣasa, then quarrel to the edge of war over whose merit freed him until Viṣṇu judges their bhakti equal _(actors: Cola, Viṣṇudāsa, a brahma-rākṣasa, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kartika-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Skanda P., Kārttikamāsa-māhātmya, chs. ~26–29)
- **King Tuṅgadhvaja spurns the cowherds' prasāda** — the king refuses the vrata prasāda of cowherds worshipping under a tree, loses his hundred sons and wealth, and regains all by joining the vrata and eating the prasāda _(actors: King Tuṅgadhvaja, the gopas, Satyanārāyaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/satyanarayana-vrata-katha.md) — (Skanda P. [attrib.], Revā-khaṇḍa appendix, ch. 5) [late text]
- **Kṣāntiśīla's gem-fruits oblige the king** — The mendicant Kṣāntiśīla presents King Trivikramasena a fruit daily for years, each hiding a priceless gem, and summons him to the cremation ground by night _(actors: Trivikramasena, Kṣāntiśīla)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vetala-panchavimshati-vikram-and-betal.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara XII, Taraṅga 75)
- **Lakṣmī chooses Karavīra as her earthly seat** — Mahālakṣmī takes up permanent earthly residence at Karavīra, glorified by the māhātmya as the foremost of all tīrthas _(actors: Mahālakṣmī / Śrī)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kolhapur-mahalakshmi-karavira.md) — (Karavīra-māhātmya (Padma Purāṇa / Skanda Purāṇa))
- **Lakṣmī expelled from the Śrīmandira** — Balabhadra brands the goddess polluted for entering a caṇḍāla's house and Jagannātha, deferring to his elder brother, casts her out _(actors: Balabhadra, Jagannātha, Lakṣmī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/lakshmi-purana-shriya-chandaluni.md) — (Lakṣmī Purāṇa of Balarāma Dāsa)
- **Lakṣmī's conditions and the Mahāprasād charter** — Lakṣmī returns to the temple only after Jagannātha concedes that no caste distinction shall attach to his food, the story Odia tradition tells for Purī's caste-free Mahāprasād _(actors: Lakṣmī, Jagannātha, Balabhadra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/lakshmi-purana-shriya-chandaluni.md) — (Lakṣmī Purāṇa of Balarāma Dāsa, conclusion)
- **Lakṣmī's Gurubāra inspection of Purī** — on a Mārgaśira Thursday Lakṣmī leaves the Śrīmandira, finds high-caste houses negligent, and accepts the worship of the outcaste devotee Śriyā _(actors: Lakṣmī, Śriyā the Caṇḍāluṇī, Jagannātha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/lakshmi-purana-shriya-chandaluni.md) — (Lakṣmī Purāṇa of Balarāma Dāsa, opening)
- **Lavaṇāsura tyrannises the Lonār country** — The salt-asura Lavaṇāsura/Lonāsura oppresses the region, sages and gods from his lair in the crater basin _(actors: Lavaṇāsura / Lonāsura, local sages and gods)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/lonar-sarovar-daityasudana.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa Lonar-māhātmya tradition; Lonar sthala-purāṇa)
- **Lineage transmission from Brahmā to Śaunaka** — Brahmā teaches Brahma-vidyā to Atharvan, passed down through Aṅgiras and Satyavaha until Śaunaka the householder asks Aṅgiras what, once known, makes all known _(actors: Brahmā, Atharvan, Aṅgir(as), Bhāradvāja Satyavaha, Śaunaka)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mundaka-upanishad.md) — (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 1.1.1–3)
- **Lohajaṅgha impersonates Viṣṇu at Mathurā** — a cast-off Brāhmaṇa lover, enriched from a jewel-island after riding a dead elephant's carcass, disguises as four-armed Viṣṇu on a Garuḍa to disgrace the greedy bawd and reclaim the courtesan Rūpiṇikā _(actors: Lohajaṅgha, Rūpiṇikā, the kuṭṭinī, a rākṣasa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kathasaritsagara-famous-tales.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara II.12)
- **Madanavega deceives Kaliṅgasenā and Madanamañcukā is born** — the Vidyādhara Madanavega weds Kaliṅgasenā in Udayana's borrowed form after minister Yaugandharāyaṇa blocks the real match, fathering Madanamañcukā, future chief queen of Naravāhanadatta _(actors: Kaliṅgasenā, Madanavega, Udayana, Madanamañcukā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kathasaritsagara-famous-tales.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara VI, Madanamañcukā)
- **Mahidasa Aitareya redacts the Aitareya Brahmana** — The sage Mahidasa Aitareya, favoured by the Earth-goddess Mahi, is credited with redacting the Hotr's Rigvedic Brahmana _(actors: Mahidasa Aitareya, Itara, Mahi (Earth-goddess))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/aitareya-brahmana.md) — (Aitareya Brahmana; Aitareya school tradition)
- **Mahānārāyaṇa = Taittirīya Āraṇyaka prapāṭhaka 10** — The Mahānārāyaṇa (Yājñikī) Upaniṣad is identified as prapāṭhaka 10, the concluding theistic forest-layer of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda _(actors: Taittirīya śākhā compilers; Yajurvedic tradition)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mahanarayana-upanishad.md) — (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 10; Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad; Muktikā Upaniṣad)
- **Mālava's gift to Puṇḍarīka at the Godāvarī** — the Viṣṇu-devoted brāhmaṇa of Vidarbha, bathing at the Godāvarī with ten thousand palas of gold, gives half to his sister's son Puṇḍarīka as the "crest-jewel of worthy recipients," and Puṇḍarīka gives a fourth of it onward to learned brāhmaṇas _(actors: Mālava, Puṇḍarīka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pundarika-of-pushkara.md) — (Padma Purana, Uttara-khanda 218)
- **Malayadhvaja's putra-kāmeṣṭi** — The childless Pāṇḍya king Malayadhvaja and queen Kāñcanamālai perform a son-desiring fire-sacrifice at Madurai _(actors: Malayadhvaja, Kāñcanamālai)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **Mandodarī fixed in the Pañcakanyā verse** — the sin-destroying remembrance verse *Ahalyā Draupadī Kuntī Tārā Mandodarī tathā…* enshrines her among the five ideal women [late text] _(actors: Mandodarī, Ahalyā, Draupadī, Kuntī, Tārā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/mandodari.md) — (later subhāṣita / smṛti tradition)
- **Mantroddhāra — coded extraction of mantras** — The Tantric manuals encode mantras in coded epithets and prastāra syllable-grids so they must be decoded by an initiate rather than read plainly _(actors: Lakṣmaṇadeśika, Mahīdhara, Tantric sādhakas)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mantra-shastra.md) — (Śāradā-tilaka Tantra; Mantra-mahodadhi; Varivasyā-rahasya)
- **Mārkaṇḍeya instructs King Vajra** — at the dawn of Kali the deathless sage Mārkaṇḍeya answers the young king's plea with a total curriculum — cosmology, statecraft, the sciences, and the arts of divine image-making _(actors: Mārkaṇḍeya, Vajra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnudharmottara-purana.md) — (Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa, three khaṇḍas)
- **Muktikā groups the ~20 Yoga Upaniṣads** — The Muktikā Upaniṣad's 108-text canon contains a cluster of about twenty minor Śruti texts unified by yoga practice rather than pure Brahman-metaphysics _(actors: Muktikā Upaniṣad; Upaniṣad-Brahma-Yogin; A. Mahadeva Sastri)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/yoga-upanishads-overview.md) — (Muktikā Up.; Mahadeva Sastri, The Yoga Upaniṣads (1920))
- **Naciketas Questions His Father's Gift** — Watching his father give away useless cattle, the boy Naciketas asks three times to whom he himself will be given _(actors: Naciketas, Vājaśravasa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1; Taittiriya Brahmana 3.11.8)
- **Naciketas sent to the house of Death** — Vājaśravasa angrily gives his son Naciketas to Yama; the boy waits three nights and is granted three boons _(actors: Naciketas, Vājaśravasa, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.1; Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 3.11.8)
- **Nāma-saṅkīrtana declared the yuga-dharma of Kali** — the intelligent worship the kṛṣṇa-varṇa yet non-black-lustered Lord with His associates by sacrifices consisting chiefly of congregational chanting, the Gauḍīya proof-text for Caitanya _(actors: Karabhājana, Nimi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nimi-nava-yogendra-samvada.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa, 11.5.32)
- **Namuci slain and the panakam-offering origin** — The asura Namuci, unslayable by dry or wet weapon, is destroyed by Vishnu/Indra through foam/stratagem, the 'neither dry nor wet' theme read into the liquid panakam rite _(actors: Namuci (asura), Vishnu, Indra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mangalagiri-panakala-narasimha.md) — (Maṅgalagiri regional sthala-purāṇa)
- **Narada chides Vyasa, Bhagavata composed** — Despondent after compiling the Vedas and Mahabharata, Vyasa is told by Narada to glorify Hari directly, and so composes the Bhagavata Purana _(actors: Vyasa, Narada)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.5-7)
- **Nārada finds Bhakti with her aged sons on the Yamunā** — Touring a Kali-ridden earth, Nārada meets the young mother Bhakti beside her decrepit sons Jñāna and Vairāgya at Vṛndāvana, who recounts her Draviḍa-to-Gujarat journey _(actors: Nārada, Bhakti, Jñāna, Vairāgya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-mahatmya-gokarna-dhundhukari.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa, Bhāgavata-Māhātmya 1)
- **Nārada's petition and the vrata's revelation** — grieved by earthly suffering, Nārada asks Viṣṇu for an easy remedy, and Nārāyaṇa prescribes the Satyanārāyaṇa vrata as the fit rite for the Kali age _(actors: Nārada, Viṣṇu/Satyanārāyaṇa, Sūta, Śaunaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/satyanarayana-vrata-katha.md) — (Skanda P. [attrib.], Revā-khaṇḍa appendix, ch. 1) [late text] [interpolation]
- **Nārada–Pañcacūḍā saṃvāda** — The sage Nārada encounters the apsarā Pañcacūḍā and interrogates her about the true inner nature and conduct of women; her unsparing reply on strī-svabhāva becomes a much-cited and contested gnomic discourse, later reported by Bhīṣma to Yudhiṣṭhira from the bed of arrows _(actors: Nārada, Pañcacūḍā, Bhīṣma, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/apsaras.md) — (Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva (Nārada-Pañcacūḍā saṃvāda))
- **Onset of Kali Yuga** — Kali Yuga begins at midnight 17/18 February 3102 BCE, the moment of Krishna's departure, when the bull of Dharma is reduced to standing on one leg _(actors: Krishna, Kali (personified))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Surya Siddhanta; Vishnu Purana 5.38; Bhagavata Purana 1.15.36)
- **Parāśara teaches Maitreya the exemption** — asked how a man may be exempt from Yama, the sage Parāśara transmits to his pupil the layered Yama-Gītā he had from Bhīṣma through Nakula _(actors: Parāśara, Maitreya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yama-gita.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa III.7)
- **Parīkṣit liberated at Takṣaka's bite** — after Śuka's final teaching that the self cannot be burned, Parīkṣit fixes his mind on Kṛṣṇa and attains liberation at the instant of the serpent's strike _(actors: Śuka, Parīkṣit, Takṣaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shuka-shukadeva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 12.5–6)
- **Pratardana storms Indra's abode** — Pratardana, son of Divodāsa of Kāśī, reaches Indra's world by fighting and virility and receives the teaching that Indra is prāṇa, the conscious self _(actors: Pratardana, Indra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kashi-line-divodasa.md) — (Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad 3.1–8)
- **Puṇḍalīka's brick halts the Lord** — the devoted son, unwilling to interrupt service to his parents, tosses a brick for the visiting Lord to wait on, and Viṣṇu-Kṛṣṇa remains standing on it as Viṭṭhala of Pandharpur for the whole Kali Yuga _(actors: Puṇḍalīka, Viṭṭhala/Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pandharpur-vitthala-wari.md) — (Pāṇḍuraṅga-māhātmya, Skanda Purāṇa / Padma Purāṇa) [late text]
- **Puṇḍarīka's sāyujya at Puṣkara** — on the Māgha full moon Viṣṇu promises absorption, carries the devotee back to Puṣkara on Garuḍa, and a flash with Puṇḍarīka's vital breath leaves his body and merges into Viṣṇu's own form _(actors: Puṇḍarīka, Viṣṇu, Garuḍa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pundarika-of-pushkara.md) — (Padma Purana, Uttara-khanda 219)
- **Rain of golden lotuses and the founding of Madurai** — Nectar drips from Śiva's locks over the new city, naming it Madhurā/Maturai; Madurai laid out as a lotus around the svayambhū liṅga _(actors: Śiva, King Kulaśekhara, merchant Dhanañjaya, Indra)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **Rājadharma taught for the new age** — Mārkaṇḍeya lays out for Vajra the duties of a sovereign — law and punishment, judicial procedure, army and diplomacy, expiation and gift — the governance of the remnant Yādava world as Kali opens _(actors: Mārkaṇḍeya, Vajra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnudharmottara-purana.md) — (Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa, Khaṇḍa II)
- **Redaction of the Kauṣītaki (Śāṅkhāyana) Brāhmaṇa** — The second Brāhmaṇa of the Ṛgveda is preserved and arranged by the Kauṣītaki/Śāṅkhāyana school as a 30-adhyāya prose manual of the Hotṛ's ritual _(actors: Kauṣītaki / Kuṣītaka teacher-line; Śāṅkhāyana school; Hotṛ priesthood)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/kaushitaki-brahmana.md) — (Kauṣītaki (Śāṅkhāyana) Brāhmaṇa; Keith HOS 25)
- **Sādhu's deferred vow and imprisonment at Ratnasārapura** — the merchant Sādhu vows the vrata for a child, twice defers it, and is framed for the theft of King Candraketu's treasure until Līlāvatī's vrata prompts the king's dream and his release with doubled wealth _(actors: Sādhu, Līlāvatī, Kalāvatī, King Ulkāmukha, King Candraketu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/satyanarayana-vrata-katha.md) — (Skanda P. [attrib.], Revā-khaṇḍa appendix, ch. 3) [late text]
- **Sahadeva and Nakula fall on the final journey** — On the mahāprasthāna Sahadeva falls second for thinking none his equal in wisdom and Nakula third for believing none equalled him in beauty, Yudhiṣṭhira naming each flaw without looking back _(actors: Sahadeva, Nakula, Yudhiṣṭhira, Draupadī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/nakula-sahadeva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.2)
- **Śani puts Vikramāditya through the sāḍe-sātī** — slighted in the Ujjain court, Saturn strands the king maimed and nameless at an oil-press for 7½ years, then restores him and grants that Saturday worshippers who hear the Māhātmya pass his transits lightly _(actors: Śani, Vikramāditya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vrata-kathas-catalog.md) — (Śani Māhātmya, Marathi/Hindi text) [late text] [folk]
- **Sannyāsa listed among the kalivarjyas** — medieval smṛti digests declare the acceptance of sannyāsa forbidden in the Kali Yuga, a ruling the living monastic orders reject [disputed] [late text] _(actors: Dharmaśāstra digest authors)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/sannyasa-and-the-renunciate-tradition.md) — (kalivarjya lists, per Kane, History of Dharmaśāstra II)
- **Śiva becomes the mother (Thāyumānavar)** — with the Kāverī in flood stranding her real mother on the far bank, the devotee Ratnāvatī goes into labour, and Śiva of the Rock Fort takes the exact form of her absent mother to comfort and midwife the childbirth _(actors: Śiva as Mātṛbhūtēśvara, Ratnāvatī, the mother)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tiruchirappalli-rockfort-thayumanavar.md) — (Tiruchirāppaḷḷi sthala-purāṇa)
- **Six seekers approach Pippalāda** — Six Brahman-devoted seekers come fuel-in-hand to sage Pippalāda, who bids them dwell a year in austerity and faith before questioning _(actors: Pippalāda; Sukeśā Bhāradvāja, Śaibya Satyakāma, Sauryāyaṇī Gārgya, Kausalya Āśvalāyana, Bhārgava Vaidarbhi, Kabandhī Kātyāyana)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/prashna-upanishad.md) — (Praśna Upaniṣad 1.1–1.2)
- **Śṛṅgi's seven-day curse on Parīkṣit** — the death-countdown by Takṣaka's bite creates the frame-audience for the Bhāgavata Purāṇa's recitation _(actors: Parīkṣit, Śṛṅgi, Takṣaka, Śuka)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/tapas-boons-and-curses.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.18–19)
- **Story of Uttanka and the snake-sacrifice trigger** — Uttanka's quest for his guru's wife's earrings and duel with Takshaka leads him to urge Janamejaya to the snake-sacrifice, the hinge that triggers the epic's recitation _(actors: Uttanka, Takshaka, Janamejaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Paushya Parva)
- **Śuka cites Khaṭvāṅga to the doomed Parīkṣit** — instructing the king who has seven days to live, Śuka names Khaṭvāṅga — freed with only a muhūrta left — as the charter of taking shelter of Vāsudeva at the last hour _(actors: Śuka, Parīkṣit)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/khatvanga-one-muhurta.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 2.1.13)
- **Sundarar Claimed as Bondsman at Tiruvennainallur** — At Tiruvennainallur, Shiva claims the saint Sundarar as his bondsman (the tozhan episode), beginning Sundarar's career _(actors: Shiva, Sundarar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md) — (Periya Puranam)
- **Taṇḍula-kusuma-balivikāra named in the 64 Kalās** — Vātsyāyana lists rice-and-flower offering-designs as the 7th of the sixty-four classical arts, the textual anchor of the floor-art tradition _(actors: Vātsyāyana)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/rangoli-kolam-floor-art.md) — (Kāmasūtra 1.3 (Vidyā-samuddeśa))
- **The curse ripens in the Kali age** — the cursed brāhmaṇas are sentenced to Kumbhīpāka hell until Kṛṣṇa's incarnation, then reborn in the Kali age devoid of the three sandhyās and of Gāyatrī-devotion — the Devī-Bhāgavata's charter for why brāhmaṇas neglect the Goddess _(actors: the cursed brāhmaṇas, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gautama-curse-on-the-brahmins.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata XII.9)
- **The cursed cirañjīvi wanders Kali Yuga** — First-named of the eight immortals and the only one whose deathlessness is a punishment, Aśvatthāman is held by folk tradition to roam still, offering a daily flower to Śiva at Asirgarh fort and seeking oil for his unhealing wound [folk] _(actors: Aśvatthāman)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/ashvatthama.md) — (Cirañjīvi śloka; Asirgarh folk legend)
- **The Draviḍa-rivers devotee prophecy** — great devotees of Vāsudeva will abound in Kali along the Tāmraparṇī, Kṛtamālā, Payasvinī, Kāverī and Mahānadī, read by Śrīvaiṣṇavas as foretelling the Āḻvārs _(actors: Karabhājana, Nimi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nimi-nava-yogendra-samvada.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa, 11.5.38–40)
- **The elopement from Ujjayinī** — contrived by minister Yaugandharāyaṇa, Udayana and Vāsavadattā flee on the swift she-elephant Bhadravatī to Kauśāmbī, while her father Caṇḍamahāsena secretly consents to the match he had engineered _(actors: Udayana, Vāsavadattā, Yaugandharāyaṇa, Caṇḍamahāsena)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/udayana-vasavadatta.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara II, Kathāmukha)
- **The first Bhāgavata saptāha at Haridvāra revives Bhakti's sons** — The Four Kumāras conduct the seven-day Bhāgavata recitation at Ānanda-ghāṭ on the Gaṅgā, Bhakti and her sons appear rejuvenated, and Bhakti is installed in the hearts of devotees _(actors: Four Kumāras, Nārada, Bhakti, Jñāna, Vairāgya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-mahatmya-gokarna-dhundhukari.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa, Bhāgavata-Māhātmya 2–3)
- **The goddess's boycott strips the temple** — departing, Lakṣmī vows the brothers will find neither food nor water, and all wealth and abundance leave the Śrīmandira with her _(actors: Lakṣmī, Jagannātha, Balabhadra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/lakshmi-purana-shriya-chandaluni.md) — (Lakṣmī Purāṇa of Balarāma Dāsa)
- **The Great Puzzle silences the king** — The kinship-tangle of the father and son who married a daughter and her mother defeats even Trivikramasena, and the satisfied vetāla reveals Kṣāntiśīla's plot to sacrifice him _(actors: Trivikramasena, the vetāla, Kṣāntiśīla)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vetala-panchavimshati-vikram-and-betal.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara XII, Taraṅga 98)
- **The Jagannātha Triad and Sudarśana Pillar** — Purī's sanctum holds the abstract wooden busts of Jagannātha (Kṛṣṇa), Balabhadra, Subhadrā and the Sudarśana post — deliberately armless and unfinished _(actors: Jagannātha, Balabhadra, Subhadrā, Sudarśana)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa (Puruṣottama-kṣetra Māhātmya); Brahma Purāṇa)
- **The liberation of Devarāja** — dying of fever at Pratiṣṭhāna, Devarāja involuntarily overhears a Śiva-discourse; Yama's messengers seize him but four ash-smeared trident-bearing gaṇas drive them off and bear him to Kailāsa, instantly liberated _(actors: Devarāja, Yama's dūtas, Śiva's gaṇas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shiva-purana-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Śivapurāṇa-Māhātmya 2)
- **The lie to the sannyāsī and Kalāvatī's abandoned prasāda** — Sādhu calls his cargo "leaves and creepers" before the disguised god and finds it so, and Kalāvatī's uneaten prasāda sinks her husband's boat until she returns and eats it _(actors: Sādhu, Kalāvatī, Satyanārāyaṇa as daṇḍī sannyāsī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/satyanarayana-vrata-katha.md) — (Skanda P. [attrib.], Revā-khaṇḍa appendix, ch. 4) [late text]
- **The lute behind the curtain** — set to teach Vāsavadattā the vīṇā while each is told the other is deformed, Udayana and the princess break the screen, behold each other, and fall in love _(actors: Udayana, Vāsavadattā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/udayana-vasavadatta.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara II, Kathāmukha)
- **The poor brahmin of Kāśī and the woodcutter** — Satyanārāyaṇa in disguise teaches the vrata to a starving brahmin, and a woodcutter who copies it sells his load at double price; both rise to wealth _(actors: the Kāśī brahmin, the woodcutter, Satyanārāyaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/satyanarayana-vrata-katha.md) — (Skanda P. [attrib.], Revā-khaṇḍa appendix, ch. 2) [late text]
- **The revelation and reunion** — his purpose secured, Yaugandharāyaṇa discloses the ruse and produces Vāsavadattā alive, restored as senior queen with Padmāvatī her junior co-wife _(actors: Yaugandharāyaṇa, Vāsavadattā, Udayana, Padmāvatī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/udayana-vasavadatta.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara III, Lāvāṇaka)
- **The sannyāsī's fruit and Dhundhulī's fraud** — Childless Ātmadeva receives a son-granting fruit, but his wife Dhundhulī feeds it to the cow and passes off her sister's newborn as her own son Dhundhukārī _(actors: Ātmadeva, Dhundhulī, Dhundhukārī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-mahatmya-gokarna-dhundhukari.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa, Bhāgavata-Māhātmya 4)
- **The seven knots burst and Dhundhukārī is liberated** — Listening from inside a seven-knotted bamboo as Gokarṇa reads the Bhāgavata seven days, the preta bursts one knot per day and emerges in divine form, borne to Vaikuṇṭha by the Lord's attendants _(actors: Dhundhukārī, Gokarṇa, the pārṣadas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-mahatmya-gokarna-dhundhukari.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa, Bhāgavata-Māhātmya 5)
- **The seven-day Bhāgavata recitation** — the sixteen-year-old Śuka arrives unbidden at Parīkṣit's fast unto death on the Gaṅgā and recites the entire Bhāgavata over the king's last seven days _(actors: Śuka, Parīkṣit, the assembled ṛṣis)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shuka-shukadeva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.19–12.6)
- **The Śīkṣā-vallī convocation charge** — A teacher dismisses the graduating student with the famous injunctions to speak truth, practise dharma, neglect not study, and revere mother, father, teacher and guest as gods _(actors: the ācārya (teacher) and the graduating Vedic student (snātaka); the four 'gods': mother, father, teacher, guest)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/taittiriya-upanishad.md) — (Taittirīya Upaniṣad I.11 (Śīkṣā-vallī))
- **The Opening Question (Keneṣitaṃ patati preṣitaṃ manaḥ)** — A disciple asks by whose will the mind, breath, speech, eye and ear go forth to their objects _(actors: Unnamed disciple and teacher)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 1.1)
- **The Sannyāsa Upaniṣad group within the Muktikā canon** — A thematic cluster of ~17–19 minor Upaniṣads, grouped by the subject of renunciation rather than parent Veda, forms the Śruti charter of Hindu monasticism _(actors: Muktikā tradition; later Vedānta compilers)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/sannyasa-upanishads-overview.md) — (Muktikā Upaniṣad; Olivelle, Saṃnyāsa Upaniṣads (1992))
- **The Self Alone in the Beginning** — The Ātman alone exists before creation and resolves to bring forth the worlds _(actors: Ātman (the Self))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad I.1.1)
- **The Śivapurāṇa-Māhātmya frame** — Sūta expounds to Śaunaka at Naimiṣāraṇya the seven-chapter Glory of the Śiva Purāṇa, three phala-śruti tales proving that merely hearing the Purāṇa liberates the vilest Kali-age sinner _(actors: Sūta, Śaunaka)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/shiva-purana-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Śivapurāṇa-Māhātmya 1)
- **The Śrāvaṇa saptāha takes the whole town to Goloka** — Gokarṇa repeats the seven-day reading with disciplined listeners, the Lord himself appears and embraces him, and the entire assembly ascends in divine form to Goloka _(actors: Gokarṇa, the Lord Hari, the townspeople)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-mahatmya-gokarna-dhundhukari.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa, Bhāgavata-Māhātmya 5)
- **The starving brothers eat in the outcaste's house** — begging in vain through Purī, Jagannātha and Balabhadra finally eat rice cooked by Lakṣmī herself in a caṇḍāluṇī's home, the very act for which she was expelled _(actors: Jagannātha, Balabhadra, Lakṣmī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/lakshmi-purana-shriya-chandaluni.md) — (Lakṣmī Purāṇa of Balarāma Dāsa)
- **The tale told to Janamejaya** — within the Devī Bhāgavata's Book III celebration of the Devī-yajña and Navarātra, the Satyavrata story is narrated to King Janamejaya as an exhortation to worship the Goddess _(actors: Vyāsa, Janamejaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/satyavrata-aim-bija.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa III.10–11)
- **The treacherous mendicant beheaded** — Asked to prostrate before the corpse, the king makes Kṣāntiśīla demonstrate and beheads him; the vetāla grants the tales world-fame and apotropaic power, and Śiva bestows the sword Aparājita and future Vidyādhara emperorship _(actors: Trivikramasena, Kṣāntiśīla, the vetāla, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vetala-panchavimshati-vikram-and-betal.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara XII, Taraṅga 99)
- **The twelve-year sattra of Śaunaka at Naimiṣa** — 88,000 ṛṣis led by Kulapati Śaunaka assemble in Naimiṣa forest for a perpetual sacrificial session, hearing the old stories during ritual intervals _(actors: Śaunaka, the 88,000 ṛṣis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 1.1; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.1.4; Vāyu Purāṇa 1.11–12)
- **The twins seated among the Aśvins in heaven** — Touring heaven in the epic's last book, Yudhiṣṭhira beholds Nakula and Sahadeva shining in the station of the Aśvins, their divine fathers _(actors: Nakula, Sahadeva, Yudhiṣṭhira, the Aśvins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/nakula-sahadeva.md) — (Mahabharata, Svargarohana Parva)
- **The Two Paths After Death (devayāna/pitṛyāna)** — Citra Gāṅgyāyani questions Uddālaka/Śvetaketu; the dead pass to the moon, which sorts souls to the upward path of the gods or rebirth as rain _(actors: Citra Gāṅgyāyani, Uddālaka Āruṇi, Śvetaketu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaushitaki-upanishad.md) — (Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad 1.1–2)
- **The vanishing and the naming** — when the flood subsides and the true mother arrives, the Śiva-form disappears, and the Lord is thereafter called Thāyumānavar / Mātṛbhūtēśvara, 'he who became even the mother' _(actors: Śiva, Ratnāvatī, the mother)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tiruchirappalli-rockfort-thayumanavar.md) — (Sirappaḷḷi sthala-purāṇa)
- **The vetāla's twenty-four riddle-tales** — Carrying the corpse from the śiṃśapā tree in silence, the king answers dilemma after dilemma (transposed heads, three suitors, Unmādinī, Vīravara) and each answer sends the corpse flying back _(actors: Trivikramasena, the vetāla)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vetala-panchavimshati-vikram-and-betal.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara XII, Taraṅgas 75–98)
- **Udayana's grief and the Padmāvatī marriage** — believing his queen dead, the inconsolable Udayana is counselled to wed Padmāvatī of Magadha, sealing the alliance and army with which he recovers Vatsa _(actors: Udayana, Padmāvatī, Darśaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/udayana-vasavadatta.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara III, Lāvāṇaka)
- **Upakośā and the chest of blackened dignitaries** — the faithful wife of Vararuci lures four would-be seducers into a dark chest, has them smeared with lamp-black, and exposes them at the Nanda king's court to recover her husband's deposit _(actors: Upakośā, Vararuci, banker Hiraṇyagupta)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kathasaritsagara-famous-tales.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara I.4)
- **Vaṭapatraśāyī enshrined as a Divya Desam** — Viṣṇu reclines as Vaṭapatraśāyī on a banyan leaf at Srivilliputhur, counted among the 108 Divya Desams hymned in the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham _(actors: Vaṭapatraśāyī Viṣṇu, the Āḻvārs)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srivilliputhur-vatapatrasayi-andal-kshetra.md) — (Sthala-purāṇa of Srivilliputhur; Nālāyira Divya Prabandham)
- **Āśvalāyana petitions Brahmā for brahma-vidyā** — The sage Āśvalāyana approaches Brahmā the Grandsire asking to be taught the highest secret knowledge of Brahman by which the wise cast off evil and attain the supreme Puruṣa _(actors: Āśvalāyana; Brahmā (Parameṣṭhin))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaivalya-upanishad.md) — (Kaivalya Upaniṣad 1-2)
- **Vedas and Gītā fail; the ākāśavāṇī prescribes a sat-karma** — Nārada's recitation of Vedas, Vedānta and Gītā cannot rouse Jñāna and Vairāgya, and a bodiless voice announces that only a specific good work will revive them _(actors: Nārada, Jñāna, Vairāgya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-mahatmya-gokarna-dhundhukari.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa, Bhāgavata-Māhātmya 1–2)
- **Vikrama gives away the philosopher's stone** — granted the pāras-maṇi that turns iron to gold, Vikramāditya hands it at once to a poor Brahmin, the recurring pattern by which he acquires only to give _(actors: Vikramāditya, a mendicant, a poor Brahmin)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/simhasana-dvatrimshika-vikramaditya-cycle.md) — (Siṃhāsana-dvātriṃśikā, tale of the touchstone)
- **Vikramāditya offers his own head to the Goddess** — to fulfil another man's vow of a perfect human sacrifice, Vikrama lays his own head on Devī's altar and is restored to life by the awestruck Goddess, the cycle's chief proof of his fearless self-sacrifice _(actors: Vikramāditya, Devī/Kālī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/simhasana-dvatrimshika-vikramaditya-cycle.md) — (Siṃhāsana-dvātriṃśikā, tale of the head-gift)
- **Vikramāditya vs. Śālivāhana and the two eras** — the child Śālivāhana of Pratiṣṭhāna, son of the nāga Śeṣa, animates a clay army to repel Vikrama's invasion, the folk etiology of the Vikrama Saṃvat (57 BCE) and Śālivāhana Śaka (78 CE) reckonings _(actors: Vikramāditya, Śālivāhana, Śeṣa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/simhasana-dvatrimshika-vikramaditya-cycle.md) — (Śālivāhana folk cycle) [folk]
- **Vipula guards Ruci from Indra by yoga** — The sage Devaśarman, leaving on a sacrifice and knowing Indra covets his beautiful wife Ruci, charges his disciple Vipula to guard her chastity. Vipula enters Ruci's body by yoga, binding her senses from within so she cannot respond to a seducer; when Indra arrives in disguise he finds her warded and Vipula's tapas blazing, and departs foiled. Vipula withdraws, restores Ruci unaware, and reports his success to his returning guru. A didactic inset on guarding a teacher's trust, the burdens of a guru-kārya, and yogic self-mastery, with contested ethics read variously as pious devotion or as coercive violation of Ruci's consent _(actors: Vipula (Bhārgava disciple), Devaśarman (guru), Ruci (Devaśarman's wife), Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/minor-upakhyanas-catalog.md) — (Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana-parva 40–43 (Vipula-Upākhyāna))
- **Viṣṇu dwells a month in Puṇḍarīka's house** — answering Puṇḍarīka's bath-wish at Puṣkara, Viṣṇu in his original form resides in the devotee's adorned home for the whole month of Māgha, worshipped with tulasī, flowers and incense while two hundred brāhmaṇas are fed _(actors: Puṇḍarīka, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pundarika-of-pushkara.md) — (Padma Purana, Uttara-khanda 219)
- **Viṣṇu's Kali-yuga refuge promise on Veṅkaṭa hill** — At the dawn of Kali-yuga Viṣṇu agrees to remain standing and visible on the Seven Hills so the merit-poor may win liberation by darśana alone, making Tirumala Bhū-Vaikuṇṭha _(actors: Viṣṇu/Śrīnivāsa, the sages)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya (Varāha/Bhaviṣyottara/Skanda Purāṇa))
- **Vājaśravasa's flawed Viśvajit sacrifice** — The father Vājaśravasa gives away only old, barren cows in the all-giving Viśvajit sacrifice, a defective dāna noticed by his son _(actors: Vājaśravasa (Auddālaki / 'son of Vājaśravas'), Naciketas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad I.1.1–3; cf. Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 3.11.8)
- **Īśāvāsyam idaṃ sarvam — all is pervaded by the Lord** — The opening mantra declares the whole moving universe pervaded by the Lord (Īśa), to be enjoyed by renunciation and non-coveting _(actors: Īśa (the Lord); the seeker)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/isha-upanishad.md) — (Īśa Upaniṣad 1 (Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā 40))
- **Viṣṇudāsa cooks his own flesh** — the poor Vaiṣṇava, bound by a Kārtika vow of hospitality and with no food, cuts and cooks flesh from his own body to honour an arriving guest _(actors: Viṣṇudāsa, the guest)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kartika-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Skanda P., Kārttikamāsa-māhātmya, chs. ~24–29)
- **Vyāsa composes the Purāṇas, recited by the Sūta at Naimiṣa** — All 18 Mahāpurāṇas and 18 Upapurāṇas are ascribed to Vyāsa and recited by the sūta Ugraśravas/Romaharṣaṇa to the sages at the Naimiṣa forest in this Kali Yuga _(actors: Vyāsa, Ugraśravas, Romaharṣaṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/README.md) — (Purāṇa frame-story)
- **Vyāsa on the ego of the enlightened** — answering Janamejaya's paradox of why sages fought for a thousand years, Vyāsa teaches that even liberated beings retain ahaṃkāra, bridging to the tale of Bhṛgu's curse on Viṣṇu _(actors: Vyāsa, Janamejaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-nara-narayana-battle.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa IV.10)
- **Vyāsa teaches Jaimini the kriyā-yoga for Kali-yuga** — asked how beings of the degenerate age can reach Viṣṇu, Vyāsa prescribes devotional action (pūjā, Gaṅgā-snāna, Ekādaśī, tulasī) illustrated by the Manobhadra, Mādhava–Sulocanā, Kālakalpa, Indra–Padmagandhā, Cakrikā and Bhadratanu tales _(actors: Vyāsa, Jaimini, Sūta)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/padma-purana-khanda-map.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Kriyāyogasāra-khaṇḍa 1–26)
- **Yaugandharāyaṇa's fire-ruse at Lāvāṇaka** — to force the Magadha alliance, the minister stages a fire and reports Vāsavadattā and himself burned, secretly hiding the disguised queen under rival princess Padmāvatī's own protection _(actors: Yaugandharāyaṇa, Vāsavadattā, Padmāvatī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/udayana-vasavadatta.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara III, Lāvāṇaka)
- **Yoga Narasiṃha cooled on Ghaṭikācala** — After slaying Hiraṇyakaśipu the fierce Narasiṃha withdraws to the Periya-malai and settles into yoga-mudrā as the pacified Yoga Narasiṃha _(actors: Narasiṃha (Viṣṇu), Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sholingur-tirukkadigai-yoga-narasimha.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, Ghaṭikācala-māhātmya)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira finds Duryodhana enthroned in heaven** — Carried to Svarga, Yudhiṣṭhira sees his arch-enemy Duryodhana enthroned in glory; he recoils, but Nārada explains that earthly hatred ceases in heaven and Duryodhana earned the seat by dying bravely on the field of Kurukṣetra _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Duryodhana, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/18-svargarohana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 18.1)
- **Aṅgiras's son-boon** — Sage Aṅgiras performs a Tvaṣṭṛ sacrifice for the king, warning the son will bring both joy and grief _(actors: Aṅgiras, Citraketu, Queen Kṛtadyuti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/citraketu.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.14.17–28)
- **Bhāskararāya's uddhāra of the Śrīvidyā pañcadaśākṣarī** — Bhāskararāya's Varivasyā-rahasya decodes the fifteen-syllable Lalitā-Tripurasundarī mantra from its coded designations, differing by Kādi and Hādi schools _(actors: Bhāskararāya Makhin, Śrīvidyā lineage)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mantra-shastra.md) — (Varivasyā-rahasya; Hindupedia, Sri Vidya)
- **Birth of Taḍātakai (Mīnākṣī) from the fire** — A three-breasted, fish-eyed girl rises fully formed from the yajña fire, born to rule, named Taḍātakai/Mīnākṣī _(actors: Taḍātakai/Mīnākṣī, Malayadhvaja, Kāñcanamālai)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **Birth of Taḍātakai/Mīnākṣī from the sacrificial fire** — A three-breasted girl, the future Mīnākṣī, rises from the Pāṇḍya fire-altar, born crowned to rule, with a prophecy of her third breast vanishing at meeting her lord _(actors: Malayadhvaja Pāṇḍya, Kāñcanamālai, Taḍātakai/Mīnākṣī)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **Birth of Viṣṇucitta (Periyāḻvār) and his garland service** — The brahmin Viṣṇucitta is born at Srivilliputhur and weaves daily garlands from his tulasī garden for Vaṭapatraśāyī _(actors: Periyāḻvār (Viṣṇucitta))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srivilliputhur-vatapatrasayi-andal-kshetra.md) — (Periyāḻvār hagiography; Guruparamparā)
- **Brahman as the Ear of the Ear** — The teacher answers that Brahman is the mind of the mind, speech of speech, eye of the eye and breath of breath — the unseen ground of all faculties _(actors: Teacher (Kena Upaniṣad voice))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 1.2–8)
- **Brahmā teaches the path of renunciation** — Brahmā answers that immortality is won not by works, progeny or wealth but by renunciation (tyāga) joined with faith, devotion and meditation, practised by forest ascetics _(actors: Brahmā; Āśvalāyana)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaivalya-upanishad.md) — (Kaivalya Upaniṣad 2-3 (renunciation half-verse shared with Mahānārāyaṇa Up.))
- **Definition of Brahman as Satyaṃ jñānam anantaṃ Brahma** — The Brahmānanda-vallī declares Brahman to be the Real, Knowledge and the Infinite, set in the cave of the heart, and unfolds the elements from the Self _(actors: the Upaniṣadic teacher; Brahman/Ātman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/taittiriya-upanishad.md) — (Taittirīya Upaniṣad II.1 (Brahmānanda-/Ānanda-vallī))
- **Demons made invincible by Vedic dharma** — The daityas defeat the devas because their rigorous Vedic observance and tapas make them unconquerable; the gods appeal to Vishnu _(actors: Daityas/asuras, devas, Vishnu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/buddha-avatara.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.17)
