- **Dharma Bull Stands on One Leg** — With Kali's onset only one quarter of virtue remains; Earth and Dharma lament as cow and bull _(actors: Dharma (bull), Earth (cow))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.16-17, Manusmriti 1.81-86)
- **Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and Kuntī depart for the forest** — Grief-worn, the blind king and Gāndhārī take leave to retire as vānaprasthas; to the Pāṇḍavas' shock Kuntī chooses to accompany them, and the elders cast off royal robes for bark and deerskin at Vyāsa's hermitage on the Gaṅgā _(actors: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī, Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15)
- **End of the Barhadratha line** — The last Barhadratha king Puranjaya (Ripunjaya) is assassinated by his minister Shunaka, who enthrones his own son, beginning the prophesied Kali dynasties of Magadha _(actors: Puranjaya, Shunaka)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1.2-3)
- **Establishment of the tāla-schemes ranking deities by height** — The aṣṭa-, nava- and daśa-tāla schemes assign taller, more elongated proportions to higher deities and squatter ones to lesser/fierce beings _(actors: Varāhamihira; Citrasūtra tradition; Mānasāra compilers)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/murti-lakshana-and-iconometry.md) — (Bṛhat Saṃhitā 58; Viṣṇudharmottara Citrasūtra; Mānasāra 65; Śukranīti 4)
- **Exposition of the haviryajña fire-rites** — Chapters 1–6 lay out the Agnyādheya, Agnihotra, Darśapūrṇamāsa, Cāturmāsya and Agrayaṇa offerings in a single systematic sequence _(actors: Hotṛ and assistant priests; sacrificer (yajamāna))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/kaushitaki-brahmana.md) — (Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa 1–6)
- **Indradyumna founds the Jagannath deities** — King Indradyumna, instructed in a dream, recovers Krishna's imperishable remains (a sacred daru log washed ashore) and has Vishvakarma carve the three stub-armed deities from neem wood, the carving left unfinished _(actors: Indradyumna, Vishvakarma, Krishna)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (Skanda Purana)
- **Kṛṣṇa revives Parīkṣit in the womb** — Born stillborn and scorched, the infant is revived by Kṛṣṇa entering the womb, the Bhāgavata's proof-text of Kṛṣṇa as protector of the embryo _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, the infant Parīkṣit, Uttarā)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.8.13–33; Mahābhārata Āśvamedhika Parva)
- **King Indradyumna's Quest for Nīla Mādhava** — The pious king Indradyumna seeks the hidden forest form of Viṣṇu, Nīla Mādhava, and sends Brahmins to find it _(actors: Indradyumna)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa (Puruṣottama-kṣetra Māhātmya))
- **Kurvann eveha karmāṇi — action-renunciation synthesis** — The text endorses doing works while wishing to live a hundred years, holding that disinterested action does not bind _(actors: the active seeker / householder)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/isha-upanishad.md) — (Īśa Upaniṣad 2)
- **Lakṣmī departs Vaikuṇṭha** — Śrī-Lakṣmī leaves Vaikuṇṭha after estrangement from Viṣṇu and descends to dwell at Karavīra _(actors: Lakṣmī, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kolhapur-mahalakshmi-karavira.md) — (Karavīra-māhātmya)
- **Naciketas Consigned to Death** — Provoked, the father angrily declares 'To Death I give you,' and the boy must go to Yama's house _(actors: Vājaśravasa, Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.4; Taittiriya Brahmana 3.11.8)
- **Naciketas demands the secret of death from Yama** — Rejecting all worldly bribes, Naciketas holds firm to his third boon and Yama teaches him the deathless Self, śreyas/preyas, OM and yoga _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.1–2.6)
- **Naciketas given to Death** — Naciketas thrice asks 'to whom will you give me?'; the angry father vows 'Unto Death (Yama) I give you,' and the boy goes willingly to Yama's abode _(actors: Naciketas, Vājaśravasa, Yama (Death))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad I.1.4–6)
- **Parikshit Cursed by Shringi** — Abhimanyu's son Parikshit, last of the Kuru line, garlands a meditating sage with a dead snake and the sage's son curses him to die of Takshaka's bite in seven days, occasioning the Bhagavata's recitation _(actors: Parikshit, Shringi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.18-19)
- **Prahlāda and the Man-Lion descent localized at the hill** — The māhātmya draws the Prahlāda–Hiraṇyakaśipu cycle and the Narasiṃha descent onto the auspicious hill as the seat of the Lord's grace _(actors: Prahlāda, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Narasiṃha (Vishnu))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mangalagiri-panakala-narasimha.md) — (Maṅgalagiri sthala-māhātmya; Bhāgavata-Purāṇa skandha 7)
- **Praśna 1 — origin of creatures from rayi and prāṇa** — Pippalāda teaches Kabandhī that Prajāpati produced the pair rayi (matter/moon) and prāṇa (life/sun), from whose union all creatures arise _(actors: Pippalāda, Kabandhī Kātyāyana; Prajāpati)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/prashna-upanishad.md) — (Praśna Upaniṣad 1.3–1.16)
- **Projection of the Four Worlds** — The Self emits the four worlds ambhas, marīci, mara, and āpas _(actors: Ātman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad I.1.2)
- **Revelation of the Gopāla (eighteen-syllable) mantra** — The Pūrva-tāpanī expounds the eighteen-syllable Gopāla-mantra syllable by syllable as the supreme means of realizing Kṛṣṇa _(actors: Kṛṣṇa-Gopāla, the seers/Brahmā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/gopala-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Pūrva-tāpanī)
- **Revelation of the Narasiṃha-Sāvitrī and Yajus with nyāsa** — The Pūrva-tāpanī supplies the Narasiṃha gāyatrī/Sāvitrī, the Yajus formula, and the six aṅga-mantras for installing the Mantrarāja's syllables on the body _(actors: Narasiṃha; the worshipper-practitioner)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/nrisimha-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Nṛsiṃha-pūrva-tāpanīya Upaniṣad)
- **Self-manifestation of the Kūrma tortoise-icon at Śrīkūrmam** — The sage/king Śveta performs tapas and Vishnu reveals himself as the svayam-vyakta tortoise-stone on the Bay of Bengal shore, with the icon later lost and refound _(actors: Vishnu (Kūrmanātha), Śveta-mahārṣi/king)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/avatara-kshetras-srikurmam-srimushnam.md) — (Śrīkūrma-māhātmya (Padma/Skanda/Brahmāṇḍa material))
- **Shiva Grants Sundarar the Padikasu at Tiruvarur** — Shiva grants Sundarar a daily gold coin (padikasu) at the Tiruvarur Thyagaraja temple, dramatizing his intimate friend-of-Shiva status _(actors: Shiva, Sundarar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md) — (Periya Puranam; Tevaram)
- **Suta recites Bhagavata at Naimisa** — The bard Ugrasrava (Suta Gosvami) recites the entire Bhagavata to the sages of the Naimisa forest during Kali Yuga, opening the outer frame _(actors: Ugrasrava/Suta, Naimisa sages)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.1)
- **The 28 Yogeshvaras incarnate to teach Pashupata-yoga** — Shiva incarnates once in every Kali Yuga across the 28 mahayugas of the present manvantara as the 28 Yogeshvaras, each with four disciples, transmitting the yoga of liberation _(actors: Shiva (Pashupati), the 28 Yogeshvaras)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/linga-purana.md) — (Linga Purana (ch. 24))
- **The ghaṭikā boon of mental clarity** — Worship on the hill bears fruit within one ghaṭikā (~24 min), granting clarity of intellect and relief from mental affliction — naming the hill Ghaṭikācala / Tirukkaḍigai _(actors: Yoga Narasiṃha, devotees)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sholingur-tirukkadigai-yoga-narasimha.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa, Ghaṭikācala-māhātmya; Śrī Vaiṣṇava tradition)
- **The Lament on Transience** — Bṛhadratha pours out a vanitas lament: the body is a foul frame and even great kings, seas, mountains and gods perish _(actors: King Bṛhadratha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/maitrayaniya-upanishad.md) — (Maitrī Upaniṣad 1.4)
- **The Paryaṅka-vidyā — ascent to Brahmaloka and dialogue at the throne** — The liberated soul travels the devayāna up through cosmic worlds, crosses the river Vijarā and reaches Brahmā's couch Amitaujas, where Brahmā asks 'Who are you?' and the soul answers with self-identification as Brahman _(actors: The liberated soul, Brahmā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaushitaki-upanishad.md) — (Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad 1.3–7)
- **The saṃnyāsa renunciation rite (praiṣa)** — The candidate performs his own symbolic funeral, recites the praiṣa formula freeing all beings of fear of him, and discards sacred fire, thread, and tuft _(actors: the renouncer (sannyāsin); officiating tradition)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/sannyasa-upanishads-overview.md) — (Jābāla Up.; Āruṇi Up.; Sannyāsa group)
- **The two knowledges: parā vs. aparā vidyā** — Aṅgiras teaches that two knowledges exist — the lower (aparā: the four Vedas and Vedāṅgas) and the higher (parā) by which the imperishable Brahman is known _(actors: Aṅgiras, Śaunaka)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mundaka-upanishad.md) — (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 1.1.4–6)
- **Tirumūlar enters the cowherd's corpse** — The Kailāsa-yogī Sundaranātha animates the dead cowherd Mūlan's body to tend cattle, cannot return, and becomes the Siddhar Tirumūlar _(actors: Sundaranātha/Tirumūlar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/tamil-siddhars.md) — (Periya Purāṇam; Wikipedia (Tirumular))
- **Two recensions (Āndhra/Drāviḍa vs Atharvan)** — The Upaniṣad survives in a longer South-Indian Āndhra recension (~64 anuvākas) and a shorter Northern/Atharvan recension, causing anuvāka numbering to vary by edition _(actors: regional recensional traditions)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mahanarayana-upanishad.md) — (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad recensions)
- **Ugraśravas Sauti recites the epic at Naimiṣa Forest** — The bard Ugraśravas arrives at the Naimiṣa Forest where ṛṣis led by Śaunaka perform a 12-year sacrifice and recites the whole Mahābhārata as he heard it at Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice (the outer frame narrative) _(actors: Ugraśravas Sauti, Śaunaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/README.md) — (Mahabharata 1 (Adi Parva))
- **Ugraśravas Sūta recites the Mahābhārata and Purāṇas** — The bard Ugraśravas (son of Romaharṣaṇa), Vyāsa's disciple, narrates the Mahābhārata and the eighteen Purāṇas to Śaunaka's sages — the outermost narrative frame of the corpus _(actors: Ugraśravas Sūta, Romaharṣaṇa/Lomaharṣaṇa, Vyāsa, Śaunaka's sages)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 1.1–1.5; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.1; Vāyu Purāṇa 1.16)
- **Vajra crowned at Indraprastha** — Yudhiṣṭhira enthrones Vajra, the surviving Yādava prince and great-grandson of Kṛṣṇa, over Indraprastha and the Śūrasena lands, preserving the Yādava line after the Mausala fratricide _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Vajra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.1)
- **Varāha's prior ownership of the hill** — Varāha already owns Veṅkaṭa hill from a prior age; Śrīnivāsa must ask his leave to settle and ordains Varāha's darśana be taken first _(actors: Varāha (Viṣṇu boar-avatāra), Śrīnivāsa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Viṣṇu-Daityasūdana slays the asura** — Viṣṇu descends as Daityasūdana and slays the asura, burying him in the crater basin _(actors: Viṣṇu (as Daityasūdana), Lavaṇāsura/Lonāsura)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/lonar-sarovar-daityasudana.md) — (Lonar sthala-purāṇa; Daityasūdana temple tradition)
- **Yogatattva names the four yogas** — The Yogatattva Upaniṣad gives the earliest neat Śruti statement of mantra-, laya-, haṭha- and rāja-yoga, the eight aṅgas, āsanas, prāṇāyāma and the siddhis in a Viṣṇu/Hiraṇyagarbha frame _(actors: Viṣṇu/Hiraṇyagarbha (teacher))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/yoga-upanishads-overview.md) — (Yogatattva Up.)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira descends into hell and chooses to remain** — Led down a foul path through the iron-thorned hells (Asipatravana, Vaitaraṇī), Yudhiṣṭhira hears the agonized voices of his brothers, Karṇa and Draupadī and, declaring his presence eases their suffering, resolves to stay in hell with them rather than enjoy heaven with their tormentors _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Karṇa, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/18-svargarohana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 18.2)
- **Astika halts the snake-sacrifice** — Janamejaya's serpent-sacrifice burns thousands of Nagas until the boy-brahmin Astika wins a boon and halts the rite, the frame at which the epic is recited _(actors: Janamejaya, Astika, Takshaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Astika Parva)
- **Birth of Mayamoha the deluder** — Vishnu emits Mayamoha, a mendicant deluder, and sends him to the asuras on the Narmada banks _(actors: Vishnu, Mayamoha (Mayamoha), asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/buddha-avatara.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.17-18)
- **Birth of Sambandar at Sirkazhi** — The child-prodigy saint Sambandar, largest contributor of pathigams to the Tevaram canon, is born at Sirkazhi (Brahmapureeswarar) _(actors: Sambandar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md) — (Periya Puranam / Tevaram)
- **Birth of the prince** — Kṛtadyuti bears a son; the king's possessive love provokes the co-wives' jealousy _(actors: Kṛtadyuti, Citraketu, co-wives)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/citraketu.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.14.28–43)
- **Boon and Request for Ātma-vidyā** — The sage Śākāyanya, pleased by the austerities, grants a boon; the king asks for knowledge of the Self rather than the body _(actors: Sage Śākāyanya, King Bṛhadratha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/maitrayaniya-upanishad.md) — (Maitrī Upaniṣad 1.2–1.4)
- **Brahmā's penance on the hill** — Brahmā performs tapas on the hill and gains darśana of the yogic Narasiṃha, marking the kṣetra as divinely revealed _(actors: Brahmā, Yoga Narasiṃha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sholingur-tirukkadigai-yoga-narasimha.md) — (Ghaṭikācala-māhātmya (folk strand))
- **Chanakya uproots the Nandas and enthrones Chandragupta** — A brahmana (Chanakya/Kautilya) uproots the Nanda dynasty and enthrones Chandragupta, founding the Maurya dynasty in the Puranic king-prophecy _(actors: Chanakya, Chandragupta, the Nandas)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1.12; Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **Dhyāna on Śiva in the heart-lotus** — The seeker is instructed to meditate in a pure secret place on the Lord (Īśa) of the nature of Oṃ within the heart-lotus, contemplating the three-eyed, blue-throated, tranquil Śiva _(actors: the meditator/seeker; Śiva (Īśa, trilocana, nīlakaṇṭha))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaivalya-upanishad.md) — (Kaivalya Upaniṣad 5-7)
- **Doctrine of the five sheaths (pañca-kośa)** — Man is described as enveloped in five nested sheaths — food, breath, mind, intellect and bliss — each inner and other than the last, leading to the bliss-Self _(actors: the Upaniṣadic teacher; the embodied self)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/taittiriya-upanishad.md) — (Taittirīya Upaniṣad II.1–II.5)
- **Drawing Forth of the Cosmic Puruṣa** — The Self draws a cosmic Person from the waters and shapes him as the matrix of the organs _(actors: Ātman; the cosmic Puruṣa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad I.1.3-4)
- **Exposition of the Soma sacrifices** — Chapters 7–30 expound the Agniṣṭoma/jyotiṣṭoma Soma rites, multi-day ahīna and sattra sessions, the Gavām-ayana and Mahāvrata, and the Hotṛ's śastras _(actors: Hotṛ, Udgātṛ, Adhvaryu; sacrificer)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/kaushitaki-brahmana.md) — (Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa 7–30)
- **Formulation of the āyādi ṣaḍvarga calculations** — Six divinatory formulae (āya, vyaya, yoni, ṛkṣa, vāra, tithi) test an icon's or temple's dimensions for auspicious remainders before construction _(actors: śilpa architects; Mānasāra and Mayamata compilers)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/murti-lakshana-and-iconometry.md) — (Mānasāra (āyādi-ṣaḍvarga); Mayamata)
- **Lakulisha as the 28th avatara founds the Pashupata sect** — Shiva descends at Kayavarohana as the wandering ascetic Lakulisha, the 28th Yogeshvara, with four disciples Kushika, Garga, Mitra, and Kaurushya who spread the Pashupata cult _(actors: Shiva (Lakulisha), Kushika, Garga, Mitra, Kaurushya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/linga-purana.md) — (Linga Purana (ch. 24); Vayu; Kurma)
- **Markandeya's Kali Prophecy** — Sage Markandeya foretells the apocalyptic decline of Kali: mleccha kings, 16-year lifespans, cannibalism, barren earth _(actors: Markandeya)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 188-190)
- **Meditation on the Vṛndāvana maṇḍala** — Meditation locates Kṛṣṇa at the centre of a lotus/maṇḍala in Vṛndāvana-Goloka, surrounded by gopas, gopīs, cows and wish-trees, beyond the material worlds _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, gopas, gopīs, cows)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/gopala-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Pūrva-tāpanī)
- **Naciketas Waits Three Nights in Yama's House** — Yama being absent, Naciketas waits three nights unfed; to atone for the un-hosted guest Yama grants three boons _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.7-9; Taittiriya Brahmana 3.11.8)
- **Naming and birth-omens** — The child is named Parīkṣit (and Viṣṇurāta) and astrologers foretell a pious Ikṣvāku-like Aśvamedha-king devoted to Kṛṣṇa _(actors: Parīkṣit, the Pāṇḍavas, assembled sages and astrologers)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.12; Mahābhārata)
- **Panguni Uthiram divine marriages** — On the Uttara-phalguni (Uthiram) full moon of Tamil Panguni, a cluster of celestial weddings is solemnized across South Indian temples on a single day — Shiva-Meenakshi/Parvati, Murugan-Deivanai, Rama-Sita, and Andal-Ranganatha — the nakshatra of marital union (ruled by Bhaga/Aryaman); also a great kavadi day at the Murugan abodes _(actors: Shiva, Parvati/Meenakshi, Murugan, Deivanai, Rama, Sita, Andal, Ranganatha)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (Wikipedia (Panguni Uthiram); Tamil temple calendars [traditional])
- **Pānakāla Narasiṃha drinks only panakam (half left)** — The open-mouthed hilltop Narasiṃha accepts only jaggery-water poured in, gurgles as he drinks, and mysteriously leaves about half uncons­umed however much is offered _(actors: Pānakāla Lakṣmī-Narasiṃha (Vishnu), temple priests, pilgrims)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mangalagiri-panakala-narasimha.md) — (Maṅgalagiri sthala-māhātmya; Wikipedia (Panakala Narasimha Swamy Temple))
- **Praśna 2 — supremacy of prāṇa** — Answering Bhārgava, Pippalāda shows via the bee-king parable that prāṇa is chief among the body's powers, sustaining all the faculties _(actors: Pippalāda, Bhārgava Vaidarbhi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/prashna-upanishad.md) — (Praśna Upaniṣad 2.1–2.13)
- **Prāṇa-upāsanās and the father-to-son transmission rite** — Meditations worshipping prāṇa as Brahman, the inter-sensory internal offering, and the dying father's sampradāna handing of his powers to his son _(actors: Dying father, son)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaushitaki-upanishad.md) — (Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad 2.1–15)
- **Prophecy of the vanishing third breast** — A divine voice foretells the supernumerary breast will disappear when she meets her destined consort, making it a recognition device _(actors: Taḍātakai, divine oracle)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **Self-manifestation of the Mūla-virāṭ mūrti** — The standing four-armed Veṅkaṭeśvara image arises svayam-vyakta, not carved by human hands, with Śrī resting on his chest; later fixed as Viṣṇu by Rāmānuja _(actors: Veṅkaṭeśvara, Lakṣmī, Rāmānuja)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya; Vaiṣṇava tradition)
- **Shrinivasa Weds Padmavati at Tirumala** — Vishnu as Shrinivasa dwells in a termite-mound on Venkata hill, meets Padmavati (reborn Lakshmi) while hunting, and weds her, founding the Tirumala-Tirupati cult _(actors: Vishnu-Shrinivasa, Padmavati)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Venkatacala-Mahatmya)
- **Spark-from-fire creation simile** — As thousands of sparks of like form leap from a blazing fire, so manifold beings arise from and return into the Imperishable Brahman _(actors: Aṅgiras (teacher); Brahman/Akṣara)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mundaka-upanishad.md) — (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 1.1.7–9; 2.1.1)
- **Sudarśana-cakra association and protective kavaca** — The Pūrva links the Mantrarāja to the Sudarśana-cakra and a protective maṇḍala/yantra, founding the apotropaic Sudarśana-Narasiṃha worship _(actors: Narasiṃha-with-Sudarśana; devotees seeking protection)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/nrisimha-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Nṛsiṃha-pūrva-tāpanīya Upaniṣad)
- **That Which the Mind Cannot Think** — The text declares Brahman to be that which the mind cannot think but by which the mind thinks, unknown to those who know and known to those who do not _(actors: Teacher (Kena Upaniṣad voice))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 1.4–8; 2.1–3)
- **The asura's being becomes the saline water** — The blood/dissolved being of the slain asura becomes the lake's saline (lavaṇa) water, explaining the brine and the name Lonār _(actors: Lavaṇāsura/Lonāsura (slain), Viṣṇu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/lonar-sarovar-daityasudana.md) — (Lonar sthala-purāṇa)
- **The Bhāgavata's opening question on the dawning Kali Yuga** — Troubled by the onset of Kali Yuga, the Naimiṣa sages ask Sūta for the essence of all scriptures; he answers with the Bhāgavata he heard from Śuka _(actors: Naimiṣa sages, Ugraśravas Sūta, Śuka)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.1.9–23)
- **The Bhṛgu-kick trigger (separated-couple variant)** — Sage Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest, the offended Lakṣmī quits Vaikuṇṭha and settles at Kolhapur while Viṣṇu settles at Tirupati, reading the two shrines as the separated divine couple _(actors: Bhṛgu, Viṣṇu, Lakṣmī, Śrīnivāsa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kolhapur-mahalakshmi-karavira.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala-Māhātmya; regional Śrī-Vaiṣṇava tradition)
- **The four (and six) grades of renouncer** — Ascetics are graded as kuṭīcaka, bahūdaka, haṃsa, and paramahaṃsa, with later texts adding turīyātīta and avadhūta above _(actors: Nārada; Prajāpati; mendicant orders)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/sannyasa-upanishads-overview.md) — (Bhikṣuka Up.; Nāradaparivrājaka Up.; Turīyātītāvadhūta Up.)
- **The hell dissolves as māyā; the final test passed** — At Yudhiṣṭhira's choice Indra, Yama and the gods appear and the hell instantly vanishes as illusion; Dharma reveals this was the third and last trial, explains that all must briefly taste hell to exhaust residual karma (his caused by the half-lie about Aśvatthāmā), and Yudhiṣṭhira bathes in the celestial Ganges to shed his human body _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Indra, Yama/Dharma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/18-svargarohana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 18.3)
- **The joyless asura-worlds and the slayers of the Self** — Those who slay the Self go after death to sunless worlds wrapped in blind darkness _(actors: ātma-han (Self-slayers))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/isha-upanishad.md) — (Īśa Upaniṣad 3)
- **The Madurai debate and the Tiruppallāṇḍu** — Viṣṇucitta wins the Pāṇḍya court debate on Viṣṇu's supremacy and sings the Tiruppallāṇḍu, earning the title Periyāḻvār _(actors: Periyāḻvār, the Pāṇḍya king (Vallabhadeva/Śrīvallabha), Viṣṇu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srivilliputhur-vatapatrasayi-andal-kshetra.md) — (Periyāḻvār hagiography; Nālāyira Divya Prabandham)
- **The Pāṇḍavas and Draupadī begin the mahāprasthāna** — After final rites and distribution of wealth, the five brothers and Draupadī cast off royalty for ascetic garb and set out walking north toward death with no intention of return, a faithful dog attaching itself to the company _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadī, the dog)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.1)
- **The six-limbed viniyoga (anatomy of a mantra)** — Every mantra is specified by ṛṣi, chandas, devatā, bīja, śakti and kīlaka, each touched to a body-point before recitation as a prerequisite for efficacy _(actors: Tantric ritualists)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mantra-shastra.md) — (Śāradā-tilaka Tantra; Mantra-mahodadhi; Agni Purāṇa)
- **Three nights unhosted at Yama's house** — Naciketas waits three nights without food or welcome while Yama is absent, an unhonoured Brahmin guest who 'burns up' the host's merit _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad I.1.7–9)
- **Uttaṅka incites Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice** — Uttaṅka's grudge against Takṣaka goads King Janamejaya into the sarpa-satra, the frame at which the Mahābhārata is first recited _(actors: Uttaṅka, Janamejaya, Takṣaka, Āstīka, Vaiśampāyana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttanka.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Āstīka sub-parva)
- **Vaiśampāyana narrates the epic at Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice** — At King Janamejaya's Sarpa Satra, held to avenge his father Parīkṣit's death by the serpent Takṣaka, Vyāsa's pupil Vaiśampāyana narrates the Mahābhārata at Vyāsa's bidding (the middle frame narrative) _(actors: Vaiśampāyana, Janamejaya, Vyāsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/README.md) — (Mahabharata 1 (Adi Parva))
- **Vidura merges into Yudhiṣṭhira and dies** — Found wasted by tapas, Vidura by yogic power casts his life-breaths and being into Yudhiṣṭhira's body and drops dead, the two merged because both are portions of Dharma; Vyāsa forbids cremating his body and explains the Aṇī-Māṇḍavya curse that made Dharma born as Vidura _(actors: Vidura, Yudhiṣṭhira, Vyāsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Ashramavasa))
- **Vidyāpati, Viśvāvasu and the Mustard-Seed Trail** — The Brahmin Vidyāpati finds Nīla Mādhava worshipped by the Śabara chief Viśvāvasu, marries his daughter Lalitā, and traces the secret path with mustard seeds _(actors: Vidyāpati, Viśvāvasu, Lalitā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa; Brahma Purāṇa)
- **World-conquest and the Tirukalyāṇam (divine wedding)** — Mīnākṣī's dig-vijaya reaches Kailāsa, her third breast vanishes at sight of Śiva, who weds her at Madurai as Sundareśvara with Viṣṇu giving her away _(actors: Mīnākṣī, Śiva/Sundareśvara, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **Yogaśikhā: Śiva teaches integrated haṭha-rāja yoga** — The longest Yoga Upaniṣad has Śiva expound the union of prāṇa and mind, the nāḍīs, chakras and kuṇḍalinī, integrating haṭha and rāja yoga toward the jīvan-mukta _(actors: Śiva (teacher))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/yoga-upanishads-overview.md) — (Yogaśikhā Up.)
- **Appar Reconverts from Jainism to Shaivism** — Appar (Tirunavukkarasar), formerly the Jain Dharmasena, reconverts to Shaivism and composes Tirumurai 4–6, famed for his hoe-service temple cleaning _(actors: Appar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md) — (Periya Puranam / Tevaram)
- **Arjuna surrenders the Gāṇḍīva to Agni** — At the red-watered sea Agni appears blocking the path and demands Arjuna return the celestial bow Gāṇḍīva and quivers to Varuṇa; Arjuna casts them into the waters, formally ending the kṣatriya phase of their lives _(actors: Arjuna, Agni)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.1)
- **Bhṛgu's kick and Lakṣmī's departure from Vaikuṇṭha** — Sage Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest in a test; affronted that her seat was struck, Lakṣmī leaves Vaikuṇṭha and descends to earth _(actors: Bhṛgu, Viṣṇu, Lakṣmī)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Brahmā receives and transmits the Gopāla knowledge** — Brahmā receives the highest secret of the Gopāla-mantra and transmits it down through a divine paramparā _(actors: Brahmā, divine teachers)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/gopala-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Pūrva-tāpanī)
- **Coronation as reigning Pāṇḍya queen** — On Malayadhvaja's death Taḍātakai is crowned queen regnant of Madurai, ruling and bearing the sword in her own name _(actors: Taḍātakai/Mīnākṣī)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **Critique of sacrifice — the leaky boats** — The fire-sacrifices are declared unsteady boats (plavā hy ete adṛḍhā yajña-rūpāḥ); those who hail them as highest return to old age and death, like the blind led by the blind _(actors: Aṅgiras (teacher))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mundaka-upanishad.md) — (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 1.2.7–8, 12–13)
- **Divergence from the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa** — As the Bāṣkala/Kauṣītaki śākhā's manual it preserves an independent, more unified Hotṛ tradition, omitting the Aitareya's Rājasūya block and Śunaḥśepa legend _(actors: Kauṣītaki school vs. Aitareya/Śākala school)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/kaushitaki-brahmana.md) — (Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa vs. Aitareya Brāhmaṇa; Keith HOS 25)
- **Emergence of Organs and Presiding Deities** — From the brooded-over Puruṣa break forth the organs, their faculties, and the cosmic deities (Agni, Vāyu, Āditya, the Quarters, herbs, Moon, Death, Waters) _(actors: Ātman; Puruṣa; Agni, Vāyu, Āditya, the Quarters, Candra, Mṛtyu, the Waters)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad I.1.4)
- **Establishment of the Daityasūdana temple cult** — Viṣṇu under the epithet Daityasūdana is enshrined beside the crater, commemorating the slaying and anchoring the māhātmya to a living shrine _(actors: Viṣṇu (Daityasūdana), pilgrims)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/lonar-sarovar-daityasudana.md) — (Daityasūdana temple sthala-purāṇa tradition)
- **First Boon — A Reconciled Father** — Naciketas asks that his father be freed of anger and welcome him gladly on his return, and Yama grants it _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.10-11)
- **Āṇḍāḷ found in the tulasī garden** — Periyāḻvār discovers the infant Gōdai beneath a tulasī plant and raises her as Āṇḍāḷ, held to be an avatāra of Bhū-devī _(actors: Periyāḻvār, Āṇḍāḷ (Gōdā Devī), Bhūmi-devī)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srivilliputhur-vatapatrasayi-andal-kshetra.md) — (Āṇḍāḷ hagiography; Guruparamparā)
- **Installation on the Hāstinapura throne** — On the Pāṇḍavas' mahāprasthāna, Yudhiṣṭhira installs the boy Parīkṣit as emperor at Hāstinapura _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Parīkṣit, Vajra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Mahābhārata Mahāprasthānika Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.15)
- **Śiva identified with the entire pantheon** — The text declares the meditated Śiva to be Brahmā, Indra, Viṣṇu, the imperishable supreme self-ruler, breath, time, fire and moon — collapsing the Trimūrti and all gods into one _(actors: Śiva; Brahmā; Viṣṇu; Indra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaivalya-upanishad.md) — (Kaivalya Upaniṣad 8)
- **Jaratkāru sees his ancestors hanging in the pit** — The celibate ascetic Jaratkāru finds his forefathers dangling over a chasm and is told his line will end unless he marries and begets a son _(actors: Jaratkāru, his pitṛs)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 13, 41–44)
- **Jābāla Upaniṣad teaches immediate renunciation** — Yājñavalkya rules that the very day detachment dawns one may go forth (yad ahar eva virajet tad ahar eva pravrajet), bypassing the āśrama sequence; the only text of the group cited in the corpus _(actors: Yājñavalkya; Bṛhaspati; Janaka; Atri)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/sannyasa-upanishads-overview.md) — (Jābāla Upaniṣad)
- **King's tapas and the self-manifest Pānakāla form** — A royal devotee's penance on the hill draws the Lord to manifest svayam in the open-mouthed Pānakāla form, establishing the hilltop worship _(actors: An unnamed royal devotee, Pānakāla Narasiṃha (Vishnu))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mangalagiri-panakala-narasimha.md) — (Maṅgalagiri regional sthala-purāṇa (late text))
- **Śākāyanya's Teaching of the Two-Fold Brahman** — Śākāyanya expounds Brahman in two forms — the guṇa-bound bhūtātman and the supreme tranquil Self _(actors: Sage Śākāyanya, King Bṛhadratha, (Vālakhilyas/Kratu in variants))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/maitrayaniya-upanishad.md) — (Maitrī Upaniṣad 2.1–3.5; 6.3)
- **Lakṣmī waits for Viṣṇu (tāyār theology)** — Karavīra is the place where Lakṣmī abides awaiting Viṣṇu's reconciliation, linking Kolhapur and Tirupati darśana _(actors: Lakṣmī, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kolhapur-mahalakshmi-karavira.md) — (Regional tāyār / folk tradition)
- **Muktinath sung as Tiru Śālagrāmam by the Ālvārs** — The Ālvār poet-saints give the maṅgalāśāsanam of Tiru Śālagrāmam, fixing Muktinath as the only Divya Deśam outside India _(actors: the twelve Ālvārs, Śrī Mūrti Perumāḷ)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/muktinath-gandaki-shalagrama-kshetra.md) — (Nālāyira Divya Prabandham)
- **Nama-Sankirtana — Kali's One Virtue** — Though an ocean of faults, Kali offers liberation through mere chanting of God's name, hard-won in earlier ages _(actors: Vyasa/Shuka (narrators))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.3.51-52, Vishnu Purana 6.2)
- **Nārada counsels Vyāsa to compose the Bhāgavata** — The despondent Vyāsa is visited by Nārada, who diagnoses his lack and prompts him to compose the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, telling his own life-story as encouragement _(actors: Nārada, Vyāsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.5–6)
- **Nyāsa — installation of sound on the body** — Through ṣaḍaṅga-, kara-, aṅga-, vyāpaka- and mātṛkā-nyāsa the practitioner installs mantra-syllables onto the body to become the deity before worship _(actors: Tantric sādhakas; Śākta upāsakas)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mantra-shastra.md) — (Śāradā-tilaka Tantra; Lakṣmī-tantra; Mantra-mahodadhi)
- **Poisoning of the heir** — The jealous co-wives poison the infant prince to death, collapsing the king into grief _(actors: co-wives, the prince, Citraketu, Kṛtadyuti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/citraketu.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.14.43–60)
- **Praśna 3 — origin, five-fold division and departure of prāṇa** — Pippalāda tells Kausalya that prāṇa arises from the Ātman, divides into five vital airs, moves in 101 nāḍīs, and departs upward via udāna at death _(actors: Pippalāda, Kausalya Āśvalāyana)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/prashna-upanishad.md) — (Praśna Upaniṣad 3.1–3.10)
- **Pratardana and Indra — prāṇa as prajñā** — Pratardana son of Divodāsa wins a boon from Indra, who reveals himself as prāṇa and the conscious self (prajñātman), teaching that life-breath and consciousness are one and the lord of all the senses _(actors: Pratardana, Indra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaushitaki-upanishad.md) — (Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad 3.1–8)
- **Pūrva phala-śruti** — The knower-reciter of the Mantrarāja is promised protection from fear, demons, untimely death, and saṃsāra, purified as by all Vedic sacrifices _(actors: the reciter of the Mantrarāja)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/nrisimha-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Nṛsiṃha-pūrva-tāpanīya Upaniṣad)
- **Śrīmuṣṇam reckoned among the Aṣṭa svayam-vyakta kṣetras** — Vaiṣṇava tradition counts Śrīmuṣṇam among the eight self-manifest abodes of Vishnu alongside Tirumala, Śrīraṅgam, Naimiṣāraṇya, Puṣkara, Badari, Śālagrāma and Toṭādri _(actors: Vishnu (Bhū-Varāha), Vaiṣṇava tradition)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/avatara-kshetras-srikurmam-srimushnam.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa Śrīmuṣṇa-māhātmya; Vaiṣṇava tradition)
- **Seduction of the asuras off the Vedic path** — Mayamoha preaches non-Vedic (Jain/Buddhist) heterodoxy until the asuras abandon the Veda, lose protective merit, and are destroyed by the devas _(actors: Mayamoha, asuras, devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/buddha-avatara.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.18)
- **Selling bangles to the women of Madurai** — Śiva walks the streets disguised as a bangle-seller to grace the cowherd women of Madurai _(actors: Śiva, women of Madurai)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam)
- **Shrinivasa Borrows Wedding Wealth from Kubera** — To pay the bride-price Shrinivasa borrows immense wealth from the treasurer-god Kubera, a perpetual divine debt that devotees' Tirumala offerings repay _(actors: Shrinivasa, Kubera)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Venkatacala-Mahatmya)
- **Specification of aṅga-pratyaṅga proportions and bhaṅga flexions** — Texts fix limb-by-limb sub-measures, the three-part face division, canonical eye-shapes, and the postural axes sama-/ā-/tri-/ati-bhaṅga _(actors: Citrasūtra and śilpa authorities)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/murti-lakshana-and-iconometry.md) — (Bṛhat Saṃhitā 58; Viṣṇudharmottara III (Citrasūtra); Mānasāra)
- **Tad-vanam Doctrine** — Brahman is named Tad-vanam, the Yearned-for that all beings long for, and is to be worshipped under that name _(actors: Teacher (Kena Upaniṣad voice))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 4.6 / closing verses)
- **The calculus of bliss (ānanda-mīmāṃsā)** — A graded scale measures bliss a hundredfold up through human, gandharvas, pitṛs, devas, Indra, Bṛhaspati, Prajāpati to Brahman, equating it with the desireless Veda-knower's joy _(actors: the Upaniṣadic teacher; ranks of gandharvas, pitṛs, devas, Indra, Bṛhaspati, Prajāpati, Brahman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/taittiriya-upanishad.md) — (Taittirīya Upaniṣad II.8)
- **The Devī-Bhāgavata recited at Naimiṣa** — The Śākta Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa is framed as recited at Naimiṣa, binding the Goddess-tradition to the same recitation-forest _(actors: Sūta, the Naimiṣa sages)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.1)
- **The heroes reunited and dissolved into their source deities** — In his new divine body Yudhiṣṭhira beholds each hero returned to source: Bhīma to the Maruts, Arjuna among Indra's host (as Nara), Nakula and Sahadeva to the Aśvins, Draupadī as Śrī/Lakṣmī, Karṇa into Sūrya, Bhīṣma to the Vasus, Droṇa into Bṛhaspati, Abhimanyu to Soma, and Kṛṣṇa beheld in his supreme Viṣṇu/Nārāyaṇa form _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadī, Karṇa, Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Abhimanyu, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/18-svargarohana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 18.4-5)
- **The nadir king Vishvasphurji abolishes caste** — The prophesied king Vishvasphurji abolishes caste, shows no reverence to Vedas or brahmanas, and reduces the twice-born to outcaste status — the symbolic floor of the dynastic prophecy _(actors: Vishvasphurji)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1; Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **The three boons granted** — Yama offers three boons in amends: reconciliation with the father, knowledge of the heaven-leading Naciketas-fire (named after the boy), and the secret of what survives death _(actors: Yama, Naciketas, Vājaśravasa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad I.1.9–20)
- **The unmoving mover and the indwelling Ātman** — The Self is described as immanent-yet-transcendent — unmoving yet swifter than mind, far and near, within and outside all; the seer of oneness transcends grief _(actors: the Ātman/Brahman; the seer)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/isha-upanishad.md) — (Īśa Upaniṣad 4–8)
- **The Vanished Deity and the Floating Dāru-brahma** — Nīla Mādhava disappears into the sand before the king arrives; a divine voice promises return as a fragrant log (Dāru-brahma) that washes ashore at Purī _(actors: Nīla Mādhava, Indradyumna)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa (Puruṣottama Māhātmya))
- **The Vratya-stomas** — Four soma-chants prescribed to consecrate roving outsider Vratya bands and absorb them into the orthodox sacrificial community, redistributing their distinctive gear _(actors: Vratyas, Udgatr priests, Magadha bard, brahmana recipients)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/panchavimsha-brahmana.md) — (Panchavimsha Brahmana 17.1-4 (cf. Atharvaveda 15))
- **Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār sings Tirukkaḍigai** — Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār offers maṅgalāśāsanam on Tirukkaḍigai, enrolling it among the 108 Divya Desams in the Tondai-nāḍu group _(actors: Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār, Yoga Narasiṃha, Amṛtavalli Thāyār)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sholingur-tirukkadigai-yoga-narasimha.md) — (Nālāyira Divya Prabandham, Periya Tirumoḻi)
- **Vyāsa raises the slain warriors from the Gaṅgā for one night** — At Gāndhārī's and Kuntī's plea, Vyāsa by ascetic power calls up all the slain warriors of both armies from the river for one reconciled night with the living; Dhṛtarāṣṭra is granted celestial sight to behold his hundred sons, and at dawn the dead re-enter the Gaṅgā _(actors: Vyāsa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the slain warriors)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Putradarshana))
- **Yogacūḍāmaṇi maps the six chakras** — A concise manual lays out the ṣaṭ-cakra, nāḍīs, prāṇas, bandhas, mudrās and the haṃsa (so'ham) mantra — an early chakra-list text _(actors: —)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/yoga-upanishads-overview.md) — (Yogacūḍāmaṇi Up.)
- **Aniconic yoni-cleft worship** — The Goddess is worshipped not as an image but as a natural yoni-shaped rock cleft kept moist by an underground spring _(actors: Kāmākhyā Devī, pilgrims)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kamakhya-nilachala-kamarupa.md) — (Yoginī Tantra; Kālikā Purāṇa)
- **Attachment of the Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka and Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad** — The Brāhmaṇa's school-corpus extends into the Śāṅkhāyana (Kauṣītaki) Āraṇyaka, which embeds the Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad with its Paryaṅka-vidyā and Pratardana–Indra dialogues _(actors: Kauṣītaki school; Pratardana; Indra; Bālāki; Ajātaśatru)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/kaushitaki-brahmana.md) — (Śāṅkhāyana/Kauṣītaki Āraṇyaka; Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad)
- **Avatara of Dhumraketu** — Ganesha will descend as the smoke-colored horse-mounted Dhumraketu at the end of Kali Yuga to destroy the wicked mleccha hordes, a Ganapatya parallel to Kalki _(actors: Ganesha (Dhumraketu))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/ganesha-and-mudgala-upapuranas.md) — (Ganesha Purana (Krida-khanda))
- **Barhadratha Line Ends** — Last Barhadratha king Puranjaya (Ripunjaya) is assassinated by his minister Shunaka, who enthrones his own son _(actors: Puranjaya/Ripunjaya, Shunaka)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1.2-3)
- **Becoming a fish-seller** — Śiva takes the guise of a fisherman/fish-vendor, echoing Mīnākṣī's fish-eyed name and the Pāṇḍya fish-emblem _(actors: Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam)
- **Bālāki and Ajātaśatru — the king teaches a brahmin** — Proud Gārgya Bālāki offers to expound Brahman to King Ajātaśatru of Kāśī, names a series of cosmic/bodily 'persons' each rejected as mere aspects, then is taught the prajñātman via a sleeping man — a parallel of Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.1 _(actors: Gārgya Bālāki, Ajātaśatru of Kāśī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaushitaki-upanishad.md) — (Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad 4.1–20; cf. Bṛhadāraṇyaka 2.1)
- **Brahman Wins a Victory; the Gods Grow Proud** — Brahman secures a victory for the devas, who exult thinking the glory was their own _(actors: Brahman; the devas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 3.1)
- **Brahmā's hurled discus names the forest (nemi/cakra)** — Brahmā releases his mind-made wheel and bids the sages settle where its rim (nemi) falls; the rim sinks here, naming the forest Naimiṣa and opening the Chakra-tīrtha spring _(actors: Brahmā, the ṛṣis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa; Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa; Naimiṣāraṇya-māhātmya)
- **Definition of the identity-grammar (āsana, mudrā, āyudha, vāhana, dhyāna-śloka)** — Pratimā-lakṣaṇa rules fix a deity's identity through posture, gesture, held attributes, mount and meditation-verse, generating named forms by attribute-permutation _(actors: Purāṇic compilers; Mārkaṇḍeya–Vajra dialogue of the Citrasūtra)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/murti-lakshana-and-iconometry.md) — (Agni Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Garuḍa Purāṇa pratimā-lakṣaṇa chs.; Viṣṇudharmottara III)
- **Deities Afflicted by Hunger Seek an Abode** — The emitted deities fall into the cosmic ocean, suffer hunger and thirst, and ask the Self for a dwelling _(actors: Ātman; the presiding deities; hunger and thirst)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad I.2.1-2)
- **Descent of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (Closing-Age Teacher)** — In Gaudiya tradition the next descent after Krishna in this Mahayuga is Chaitanya Mahaprabhu within the present Kali Yuga, propagating the nama-sankirtana yuga-dharma _(actors: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.5.32; Chaitanya Charitamrita)
- **Digvijaya conquest of the eight directions** — As warrior-queen she conquers the eight quarters, subduing kings, the dik-pālas, Indra and the devas _(actors: Mīnākṣī, Indra, the Lokapālas, the dik-pālas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **Durvāsas, the gopīs, and the parting of the Yamunā** — The gopīs cross the Yamunā to feed Durvāsas after the river parts at the claim that Kṛṣṇa is a perpetual brahmacārin, dramatizing His transcendence of His own līlā _(actors: Durvāsas, the gopīs, Kṛṣṇa, the Yamunā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/gopala-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Uttara-tāpanī)
- **Kṛṣṇa's Viśvarūpa Darśana to Janamejaya** — Viṣṇu as Kṛṣṇa the Pāṇḍava-envoy grants the cosmic-form darśana to king Janamejaya, commemorated at the Pāṇḍava Dūta temple of Kāñcī _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Janamejaya)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kanchipuram-city-of-temples.md) — (divyadesam.com)
- **Marriage of Jaratkāru and Vāsuki's sister (Manasā)** — Vāsuki gives his sister, also named Jaratkāru (later Manasā), to the ascetic so her son can halt the snake-sacrifice _(actors: Jaratkāru, Vāsuki, Jaratkāru/Manasā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 13, 45–47; Manasā-maṅgal tradition)
- **Nārada and Aṅgiras console** — The two sages come to teach the king that worldly relations are transient configurations of karma _(actors: Nārada, Aṅgiras, Citraketu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/citraketu.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.15.1–26)
- **Oṃkāra-turīya identification of Narasiṃha-Brahman** — The Uttara analyses AUM and its fourth soundless mātrā, mapping the four states of consciousness to Narasiṃha as turīya, the supreme non-dual Self _(actors: Narasiṃha as Brahman/Ātman/antaryāmin)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/nrisimha-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Nṛsiṃha-uttara-tāpanīya Upaniṣad)
- **Praśna 4 — sleep, dream and deep sleep** — Pippalāda explains to Sauryāyaṇī how the senses rest in the mind in sleep, the mind projects dreams, and in deep sleep all merge in the imperishable Ātman _(actors: Pippalāda, Sauryāyaṇī Gārgya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/prashna-upanishad.md) — (Praśna Upaniṣad 4.1–4.11)
- **Śrīnivāsa's descent and the anthill austerity** — Viṣṇu follows Lakṣmī to earth as Śrīnivāsa and dwells in austerity on Veṅkaṭa hill, in some tellings nursed within an anthill _(actors: Śrīnivāsa (Viṣṇu))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Āruṇi questions Prajāpati on abandoning rites** — The sage Āruṇi (Uddālaka) asks Prajāpati how to relinquish all rites, and is told the physical renunciations (sons, wealth, sacred thread, study) _(actors: Āruṇi (Uddālaka); Prajāpati)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/sannyasa-upanishads-overview.md) — (Āruṇeya Upaniṣad)
- **Sambandar's Confrontation with the Jains at Madurai** — At the Meenakshi/Madurai shrine, Sambandar confronts the Jains in the legends focused on the Pandya capital _(actors: Sambandar, Jains)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md) — (Periya Puranam)
- **Second Boon — The Nāciketa Fire** — Naciketas asks the heavenward fire-sacrifice; Yama expounds the Nāciketa fire-altar, names it after the boy, and adds a necklace _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.12-19; Taittiriya Brahmana 3.11.8)
- **Slaying of Kolhāsura** — The Goddess slays the demon Kolhāsura, who dying begs that the city bear his name and that she remain as Mahālakṣmī of Kolhāpura _(actors: Mahālakṣmī, Kolhāsura)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kolhapur-mahalakshmi-karavira.md) — (Karavīra-māhātmya; Wikipedia: Kolhapur)
- **The Bhṛgu–Varuṇa inquiry into Brahman** — Bhṛgu asks his father Varuṇa to teach Brahman and, through repeated tapas, ascends from food to breath, mind, knowledge and finally bliss as Brahman — that from which beings are born, live, and into which they return _(actors: Bhṛgu (Vāruṇi) and his father Varuṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/taittiriya-upanishad.md) — (Taittirīya Upaniṣad III.1–III.6 (Bhṛgu-vallī))
- **The Bhūtātman Bound by the Guṇas** — The elemental self, overcome by prakṛti's three guṇas, fails to perceive the indwelling Lord and wanders through births _(actors: the bhūtātman (embodied self), the inner Lord)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/maitrayaniya-upanishad.md) — (Maitrī Upaniṣad 3.2)
- **The bow-and-arrow praṇava meditation** — Oṃ is the bow, the self the arrow, Brahman the target; drawn by a mind absorbed in That, one strikes the Imperishable _(actors: Aṅgiras (teacher))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mundaka-upanishad.md) — (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 2.2.3–4)
- **The epic closes with its phala-śruti** — The book declares Vyāsa composed a six-million-verse poem distributed across the worlds, proclaims the merit of reciting the Mahābhārata, and gives the closing self-praise that what is here is found elsewhere and what is not here is nowhere, with benediction to Nārāyaṇa, Nara and Sarasvatī _(actors: Vyāsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/18-svargarohana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 18.5)
- **The five fall one by one on the slopes of Meru** — As they cross the high snow, Draupadī, Sahadeva, Nakula, Arjuna, and Bhīma each fall in turn, Yudhiṣṭhira naming the single fault (partiality, pride in wisdom, vanity of beauty, arrogance in prowess, gluttony and boasting) that bars each from bodily ascent, never looking back _(actors: Draupadī, Sahadeva, Nakula, Arjuna, Bhīma, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.2)
- **The Hidden Carpenter and the Unfinished Images** — Viśvakarmā (or Ananta-mahārāṇā) carves the log behind locked doors; the door is opened early, leaving Jagannātha armless and unfinished, and Brahmā consecrates the temple _(actors: Viśvakarmā / Ananta-mahārāṇā, Indradyumna, Guṇḍicā, Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa; Brahma Purāṇa)
- **The 'I am Śiva' (śivo'ham) realization** — The meditator declares his identity with Śiva-Brahman — all is born, established and dissolved in Me; that non-dual Brahman am I; for Me there is no death, fear, caste, birth, father or mother _(actors: the realized meditator (kevalin); Śiva-Brahman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaivalya-upanishad.md) — (Kaivalya Upaniṣad 16-24)
- **The righteous reign** — Parīkṣit rules as a cakravartin at the Dvāpara→Kali cusp, marries Irāvatī, fathers Janamejaya, and performs three Aśvamedhas _(actors: Parīkṣit, Irāvatī, Janamejaya)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.16; Mahābhārata)
- **The sixteen mantra-saṃskāras and mantra-caitanya** — A received mantra is purified by sixteen saṃskāras and 'awakened' (caitanya), since a mantra may be asleep or cursed and thus inert without it _(actors: Guru and initiate)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mantra-shastra.md) — (Śāradā-tilaka Tantra; Prapañcasāra Tantra; Mantra-mahodadhi)
- **The vidyā/avidyā and saṃbhūti/asaṃbhūti balanced pairs** — Devotion to either knowledge or ignorance alone leads to darkness; one crosses death by holding both vidyā and avidyā (and saṃbhūti and asaṃbhūti) together _(actors: the integrating knower)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/isha-upanishad.md) — (Īśa Upaniṣad 9–14 (Kāṇva & Mādhyandina recensions; Śaṅkara bhāṣya))
- **The worn-garland miracle (Cūḍikkoḍutta Nācciyār)** — Gōdai secretly wears the Lord's garlands; Viṣṇu declares he will accept only garlands she has first worn, giving her the epithet Cūḍikkoḍutta Nācciyār _(actors: Āṇḍāḷ, Periyāḻvār, Vaṭapatraśāyī Viṣṇu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srivilliputhur-vatapatrasayi-andal-kshetra.md) — (Āṇḍāḷ hagiography)
- **War-widows enter the Gaṅgā to rejoin their husbands** — Vyāsa tells the widows that any who wish to rejoin their dead husbands may enter the river; women who do so cast off their bodies in the Gaṅgā and ascend to their husbands' worlds _(actors: Vyāsa, the war-widows)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Putradarshana))
- **Yama's test — wealth offered and refused** — Yama tries to deflect the third boon with sons, herds, gold, long life and apsarases; Naciketas rejects all fleeting pleasures and holds Yama to the knowledge of the Self _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad I.1.21–29)
- **Yogakuṇḍalinī rouses the serpent power** — The text describes rousing kuṇḍalinī by bhastrikā breath and bandhas, the khecarī-mudrā and drinking cranial amṛta, culminating in union with Śiva at the sahasrāra _(actors: —)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/yoga-upanishads-overview.md) — (Yogakuṇḍalinī Up.)
- **Ambubāchī Melā — annual menstruation** — Each Āṣāḍha the Goddess menstruates; the temple closes three days and reopens with red-cloth prasāda, drawing tantric pilgrims _(actors: Kāmākhyā Devī, tāntrikas and ascetics, pilgrims)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kamakhya-nilachala-kamarupa.md) — (regional festival tradition (Ambubachi Mela))
- **Birth of Āstīka** — After Jaratkāru abandons his pregnant wife, the half-brahmin half-nāga boy Āstīka is born and reared by Vāsuki to save the snakes _(actors: Āstīka, Jaratkāru, Jaratkāru/Manasā, Vāsuki, Cyavana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 13, 47–48)
- **Brahma founds the Tirumala Brahmotsavam** — Brahma is said to have first performed the nine-day utsavam on Venkatachala hill to thank Vishnu for descending as Venkateshwara in the Kali Yuga, establishing the paradigm South-Indian brahmotsava form with its sequence of daily vahana processions culminating in Garuda Seva, Rathotsavam and the Chakra-snanam _(actors: Brahma, Vishnu/Venkateshwara (Malayappa Swami))_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (Venkatachala Mahatmya / Varaha Purana; Vaikhanasa-Pancharatra Agama; TTD)
- **Composition of the Tiruppāvai and Nācciyār Tirumoḻi** — At Srivilliputhur Āṇḍāḷ composes the thirty-verse Tiruppāvai and the 143-verse Nācciyār Tirumoḻi, vowing to wed only Raṅganātha _(actors: Āṇḍāḷ)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srivilliputhur-vatapatrasayi-andal-kshetra.md) — (Nālāyira Divya Prabandham — Tiruppāvai, Nācciyār Tirumoḻi)
- **Cow and Horse Rejected, Man Accepted** — The deities reject cow and horse as dwellings but accept the human form, exclaiming su-kṛtam ('well made') _(actors: Ātman; the deities)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad I.2.3)
- **Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and Kuntī die in the forest fire** — After two more years of harsh tapas, a wildfire sweeps the wood; too weak to flee, the three elders choose not to escape and the blind king sits in yoga as the flames take all three; Nārada announces their deaths to Yudhiṣṭhira _(actors: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī, Kuntī, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Naradagamana))
- **Divergence of sectarian Āgamic iconometric canons** — Śaiva, Vaikhānasa and Pāñcarātra Āgamas establish sect-specific bera/pratimā-lakṣaṇa distinguishing dhruva-bera from utsava icons by distinct measures _(actors: Vaikhānasa and Śaiva Āgama lineages)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/murti-lakshana-and-iconometry.md) — (Vaikhānasa Āgama; Śaiva Āgama kriyāpāda)
- **Doctrine of the Good vs. the Pleasant (śreyas/preyas)** — Satisfied by the test, Yama teaches that the wise choose the Good (śreyas) over the Pleasant (preyas), and that the Self is gained only by the one it chooses _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad I.2.1–23)
- **Dvā suparṇā — two birds on one tree** — Two companion birds on one tree: the jīva eats the sweet fruit while the witnessing Self looks on; seeing the Lord, the grieving jīva's sorrow departs _(actors: jīva (embodied self), the witnessing Ātman/Īśa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mundaka-upanishad.md) — (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 3.1.1–2)
- **Enrollment among the 18 Mahā Śakti Pīṭhas** — Mahālakṣmī of Kolhapur is fixed as the seventh of the Aṣṭādaśa Śakti Pīṭhas in the stotram attributed to Ādi Śaṅkara _(actors: Mahālakṣmī, Ādi Śaṅkara (attrib.))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kolhapur-mahalakshmi-karavira.md) — (Aṣṭādaśa Śakti Pīṭha Stotram)
- **Gokarna-Dhundhukari ghost-liberation (Bhagavata-Mahatmya)** — The allegory of Bhakti as a mother with sons Jnana and Vairagya, with the ghost Dhundhukari liberated by recitation of the Bhagavata _(actors: Gokarna, Dhundhukari, Bhakti, Jnana, Vairagya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/padma-purana.md) — (Padma Purana (Uttara Khanda, Bhagavata-Mahatmya))
- **Hiraṇmayena pātreṇa — the golden vessel over Truth's face** — A prayer to Pūṣan/the solar deity to unveil the golden disc hiding the face of Truth, and the identity 'that Person in the sun, He am I.' _(actors: Pūṣan / Sūrya / Yama; the dying seeker)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/isha-upanishad.md) — (Īśa Upaniṣad 15–16)
- **King Indradyumna founds the Jagannātha cult at Puri** — King Indradyumna recovers the divine dāru-brahman image, which Viśvakarmā carves into the Jagannātha–Balabhadra–Subhadrā triad at Puruṣottama-kṣetra (Puri) _(actors: Indradyumna, Viśvakarmā, Jagannātha, Balabhadra, Subhadrā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahma-purana.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa (Puruṣottama-māhātmya); Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Marriage of Śrīnivāsa and Padmāvatī** — Śrīnivāsa falls in love with and marries Padmāvatī (Alamēlu-maṅgā), lotus-born daughter of King Ākāśarāja and a form of Lakṣmī, enshrined at Tiruchanūr _(actors: Śrīnivāsa, Padmāvatī, King Ākāśarāja)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Medha-sūktas invoke intelligence and memory** — Short hymns beg Savitṛ, Sarasvatī, Agni, Indra and the Aśvins to grant medhā (intellect/memory), recited by students before Vedic study _(actors: Medhā; Savitṛ; Sarasvatī; Vedic students)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mahanarayana-upanishad.md) — (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad, Medha-sūktas)
- **Nabakalebara — Periodic Re-embodiment** — The perishable wooden images are periodically replaced and the secret Brahma-padārtha life-essence transferred; historical rites span 1969–2015 _(actors: Jagannātha triad, Dayitāpati priests)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (temple tradition / sthala-purāṇa; academic record)
- **Nanda Dynasty — Exterminator of Kshatriyas** — Mahapadma Nanda, born of a shudra woman, founds the first non-kshatriya empire, styled 'exterminator of all kshatriyas' _(actors: Mahapadma Nanda, Mahanandi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1.10-11)
- **Nādabindu and Haṃsa systematize inner sound (nāda/laya-yoga)** — Laya-yoga dissolves the mind in the ten unstruck inner sounds; the Haṃsa Upaniṣad sets the haṃsa-vidyā/ajapā-gāyatrī in a Sanatkumāra–Gautama dialogue _(actors: Sanatkumāra; Gautama)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/yoga-upanishads-overview.md) — (Nādabindu Up.; Haṃsa Up.)
- **Nārada questions Prajāpati on the paramahaṃsa** — Nārada asks Prajāpati to define the supreme renouncer, who casts off staff, tuft, and thread and wears only knowledge as his mark _(actors: Nārada; Prajāpati)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/sannyasa-upanishads-overview.md) — (Paramahaṃsa Upaniṣad)
- **Praśna 5 — meditation on Oṃ (one, two, three mātrās)** — Pippalāda teaches Śaibya that meditating on Oṃ's one/two/three mātrās wins the world of men, the moon, or Brahma-loka and the supreme Puruṣa _(actors: Pippalāda, Śaibya Satyakāma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/prashna-upanishad.md) — (Praśna Upaniṣad 5.1–5.7)
- **Prophesied Descent of Kalki** — Vishnu is prophesied to descend as Kalki at the end of Kali Yuga to end the age of strife and restore Satya Yuga _(actors: Vishnu; Kalki)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.2)
- **Puraścaraṇa — the preparatory regimen** — Before a mantra becomes siddha the sādhaka completes a cascade of japa, homa, tarpaṇa, abhiṣeka and brāhmaṇa-bhojana in a one-tenth decadal ratio _(actors: Tantric sādhakas)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mantra-shastra.md) — (Śāradā-tilaka Tantra; Mantra-mahodadhi; Meru-tantra)
- **Takṣaka Slays King Parīkṣit** — The serpent-chief Takṣaka, having been cursed-upon by Śṛṅgin's word against Parīkṣit, slays the king with his venom on the seventh day, triggering Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice _(actors: Takṣaka, Parīkṣit, Śṛṅgin)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Taming and regulating personified Kali** — Parīkṣit catches Kali beating the bull Dharma and cow Earth, spares the suppliant, and confines adharma by assigning Kali fixed abodes (gambling, drink, illicit sex, slaughter, gold) _(actors: Parīkṣit, personified Kali, Dharma (bull), Bhūmi (cow))_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.16–17)
- **The dead boy's soul revived to speak** — Nārada summons the departed jīva back into the corpse; the soul discourses on the deathless self and its countless past kin _(actors: Nārada, the revived jīva, Citraketu, Kṛtadyuti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/citraketu.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.15.10; 6.16.2–15)
- **The dog reveals himself as Dharma and Yudhiṣṭhira ascends in the body** — Indra offers to carry Yudhiṣṭhira to Svarga but forbids the dog; Yudhiṣṭhira refuses to abandon the faithful creature, whereupon the dog reveals himself as Dharma (his divine father) who praises his compassion, and Yudhiṣṭhira ascends to heaven in his living mortal body, an unprecedented feat _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Indra, the dog (Dharma))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.3)
- **The food-hymns and 'I am food' realization-chant** — The Bhṛgu-vallī closes with injunctions never to despise food and the liberated knower's exultant chant 'I am food, I am the eater of food.' _(actors: the liberated knower (Bhṛgu); the Taittirīya tradition)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/taittiriya-upanishad.md) — (Taittirīya Upaniṣad III.7–III.10)
- **The gopīs question the nature of the Deity** — The gopīs and sages ask who Kṛṣṇa truly is, how to worship Him, and what His mantra and abode are; the answers reaffirm Kṛṣṇa as the one Brahman behind all gods _(actors: gopīs, sages, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/gopala-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Uttara-tāpanī)
- **The Nimiṣa demons slain in a wink** — A host of Nimiṣa demons is destroyed at the site in an instant (nimiṣa), an alternative etymology for the name Naimiṣa _(actors: the ṛṣis, the Nimiṣa demons)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa; Mahābhārata)
- **The storming of Kailāsa** — Mīnākṣī marches on Śiva's Kailāsa, routs his gaṇas including Nandi and Vīrabhadra, drawing Śiva onto the field _(actors: Mīnākṣī, Śiva's gaṇas, Nandi, Vīrabhadra, Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **The Three Guṇas Mapped to the Trimūrti** — The Upaniṣad names sattva, rajas, tamas explicitly and maps them to Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Rudra as the One's threefold unfolding _(actors: sattva/rajas/tamas, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Rudra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/maitrayaniya-upanishad.md) — (Maitrī Upaniṣad 5.2)
- **The Yakṣa Appears** — Brahman manifests as an unrecognizable yakṣa (spirit) before the gods to humble them _(actors: Brahman (as yakṣa); the devas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 3.2–3)
- **Third Boon — The Secret of Death Requested** — Naciketas asks the great doubt of whether a man exists after death, the Upaniṣad's metaphysical innovation _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.20)
- **Two-birds image and turīya analysis** — The text re-quotes the two-birds (dvā suparṇā) verse and the witness of waking-dream-deep-sleep, weaving Māṇḍūkya-style turīya analysis into the Śaiva meditation _(actors: the jīva (eating bird); the Lord (witnessing bird))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaivalya-upanishad.md) — (Kaivalya Upaniṣad 12-17 (cf. Śvetāśvatara 4.6 / Muṇḍaka 3.1.1 / Ṛgveda 1.164.20))
- **Unity of Mantrarāja and Praṇava; Uttara phala-śruti** — The Uttara teaches that the man-lion Mantrarāja and the Oṃkāra are one, and that knowing this Oṃkāra-Narasiṃha grants liberation, crossing death into turīya _(actors: Narasiṃha-Brahman; the liberation-seeking knower)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/nrisimha-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Nṛsiṃha-uttara-tāpanīya Upaniṣad)
- **Vandi-koṇḍa līlā — carrying earth for piṭṭu and taking the cane-blow** — Śiva labours as a coolie for the piṭṭu-seller Vandi to dam the Vaikai; the king's cane-blow on the lazy labourer is felt by every living being _(actors: Śiva, old woman Vandi, King Varaguṇa Pāṇḍya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **Agni Fails to Burn the Straw** — Agni is sent first and cannot burn a single blade of grass set before him by the yakṣa _(actors: Agni; the yakṣa (Brahman))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 3.4–6)
- **Andal Composes the Tiruppavai at Srivilliputhur** — Andal (Goda) is born at Srivilliputhur, birthplace also of Periyalvar, where the Tiruppavai originates _(actors: Andal, Periyalvar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (Naalayira Divya Prabandham / Alvar hagiography)
- **Bindu-texts interiorize Oṃ (praṇava)** — Amṛtabindu, Dhyānabindu, Amṛtanāda and Brahmavidyā resolve Oṃ into bīja, bindu, nāda and kalā and into the soundless turīya, teaching that the mind alone binds and frees _(actors: —)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/yoga-upanishads-overview.md) — (Amṛtabindu (Brahmabindu) Up.; Dhyānabindu Up.; Amṛtanāda Up.; Brahmavidyā Up.)
- **Canonization as northernmost Jyotirliṅga** — Kedarnath is fixed as the northernmost of the twelve Jyotirliṅgas, 'Himālaye tu Kedāram,' in the Śiva Purāṇa and Śaṅkara's stotra _(actors: Śiva, Ādi Śaṅkara (attrib.))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kedarnath-kedara-kshetra.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Dvādaśa Jyotirliṅga Stotra)
- **Chanakya Uproots the Nandas** — A brahmana (Chanakya/Kautilya) overthrows the Nandas and enthrones Chandragupta, founding the Maurya dynasty _(actors: Chanakya/Kautilya, Chandragupta Maurya)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1.12)
- **Doctrine of māna-doṣa and canonical efficacy** — The texts hold that a correctly-measured image is prāsādika while a proportion-fault (māna-doṣa) brings harm, making the canon a ritual necessity rather than aesthetics _(actors: Varāhamihira; Mayamata and Śukranīti authorities)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/murti-lakshana-and-iconometry.md) — (Bṛhat Saṃhitā 58.30–31; Mayamata; Śukranīti 4)
- **Initiation and the Saṅkarṣaṇa mantra** — Freed of grief, Citraketu receives the Saṅkarṣaṇa mantra from Nārada and purifies himself by seven days of discipline _(actors: Nārada, Citraketu, Aṅgiras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/citraketu.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.16.18–53)
- **Janamejaya's Sarpa-Satra (Snake-Sacrifice)** — Janamejaya vows to exterminate the serpent race and undertakes the sarpa-satra, whose oblations draw nāgas of every size from across the worlds into the flames _(actors: Janamejaya, nāgas, Takṣaka)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata Āstīka Parva)
- **Kaṇṇappa's Eye-Offering at Srikalahasti** — The hunter-saint Kannappa, worshipping the linga his untaught way, gouges out his own eyes to stop the linga's bleeding eye; Shiva seizes his hand, restores his eyes and grants liberation, proving devotion outranks ritual _(actors: Kannappa (Tinnan), Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-bhuta-sthalams.md) — (Periya Purana (Kannappa Nayanar Puranam))
- **Kubera's wedding-loan to Śrīnivāsa** — To meet bridal expenses Śrīnivāsa borrows a vast sum from Kubera, vowing repayment with interest through all of Kali-yuga — the basis of the temple hundi donations _(actors: Śrīnivāsa, Kubera)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Lakulisha prophecy, last of the 28 Yogeshvaras** — The Purana prophesies Maheshvara descending in Kali Yuga as the ascetic Lakulisha, 28th Yogeshvara, with four disciples who found the Pashupata sect _(actors: Shiva (Lakulisha), Kushika, Garga, Mitra, Kaurushya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana (ch. 53))
- **Opening the rock / staying the flood for the Pāṇḍya** — Śiva cleaves a rock or stays the Vaikai flood for the Pāṇḍya, delivering the city _(actors: Śiva, Pāṇḍya king)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam)
- **Parikṣit insults sage Śamīka with a dead snake** — The lone Kuru heir Parikṣit, thirsty while hunting, loops a dead snake on the silent meditating sage Śamīka _(actors: Parikṣit, Śamīka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 36–40)
- **Phala-śruti and Śatarudriya benediction** — The closing fruit-of-recitation verses promise that whoever recites this knowledge, chanting it with the Śatarudriya, is purified of the great sins and attains kaivalya, oneness with Śiva _(actors: the reciter; Śiva (Rudra))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaivalya-upanishad.md) — (Kaivalya Upaniṣad closing verses 23-24 (cf. Yajurveda Śatarudriya/Rudram))
- **Praśna 6 — the Person of sixteen parts (ṣoḍaśa-kala puruṣa)** — Pippalāda answers Sukeśā that the sixteen kalās arise from the Person within the body and dissolve back into him as rivers lose name-and-form in the sea _(actors: Pippalāda, Sukeśā Bhāradvāja; prince Hiraṇyanābha Kausalya (referenced))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/prashna-upanishad.md) — (Praśna Upaniṣad 6.1–6.8)
- **Rudhirādhyāya blood-offering rite** — The Kālikā Purāṇa's blood-chapter prescribes the animal (and ideal human) sacrifice continued at Kāmākhyā _(actors: Kāmākhyā Devī, worshippers)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kamakhya-nilachala-kamarupa.md) — (Kālikā Purāṇa (Rudhirādhyāya))
- **Sañjaya escapes the fire and departs for the Himālaya** — Before the fire closes in, Dhṛtarāṣṭra orders his faithful charioteer Sañjaya to save himself; bereft of his master, Sañjaya retires to the Himālaya to perform penance and is never heard of again _(actors: Sañjaya, Dhṛtarāṣṭra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Naradagamana))
- **Satyam eva jayate — Truth alone triumphs** — The verse 'satyam eva jayate nānṛtaṃ' declares truth alone triumphs over falsehood; later adopted as the national motto of India under the Lion Capital of Aśoka _(actors: the sages (ṛṣis); Republic of India (adoption))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mundaka-upanishad.md) — (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 3.1.6; State Emblem of India)
- **Āṇḍāḷ's bridal procession and merging at Śrīraṅgam** — Viṣṇu commands that Gōdai be brought in bridal procession to Śrīraṅgam, where she enters the sanctum and merges into Raṅganātha _(actors: Āṇḍāḷ, Periyāḻvār, Raṅganātha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srivilliputhur-vatapatrasayi-andal-kshetra.md) — (Āṇḍāḷ hagiography; Guruparamparā)
- **The ṣaṭkarma — six applied prayogas** — The six acts (śānti, vaśīkaraṇa, stambhana, vidveṣaṇa, uccāṭana, māraṇa) deploy a perfected mantra, each with assigned deity, season, direction and seat _(actors: Tantric adepts; presiding deities (Rati, Kāmadeva, Kālī, Nirṛti, Bhairava, etc.))_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mantra-shastra.md) — (Mantra-mahodadhi; Śāradā-tilaka Tantra; Agni Purāṇa; Tantrarāja Tantra)
- **The Chakra-tīrtha discus-ford established** — The central tank at Nīmsār marks where the wheel's rim (or Viṣṇu's Sudarśana/Manomaya Cakra) struck the earth, opening a perennial spring said to well up from Pātāla _(actors: Brahmā / Viṣṇu (Hari), pilgrims)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa Naimiṣa-khaṇḍa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.1.4)
- **The chariot allegory of the Self** — Yama teaches the ratha-kalpanā: the Self as rider, body as chariot, intellect as charioteer, mind as reins, senses as horses, sense-objects as roads _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad I.3.3–9)
- **The cremation prayer — body to ashes, Agne naya supathā** — The dying invocation releasing breath to the immortal Wind and body to ashes, and the closing prayer to Agni to lead by the good path _(actors: Agni; the dying person / cremation officiant)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/isha-upanishad.md) — (Īśa Upaniṣad 17–18 (= Ṛgveda 1.189.1))
- **The Devas approach and learn Kṛṣṇa's supremacy** — The gods led by Brahmā and Indra approach the supreme Person and learn He is the inner Self and Lord of all the Devas, who themselves worship Him _(actors: Brahmā, Indra, the Devas, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/gopala-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Uttara-tāpanī)
- **The Gods Enter Their Seats in Man** — Each deity enters its station in the human body, becoming the corresponding sense-faculty _(actors: Ātman; Agni, Vāyu, Āditya, the Quarters, herbs/trees, Moon, Death, Waters)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad I.2.4-5)
- **The Ratha Yātrā Chariot Festival** — On Āṣāḍha dvitīyā the triad rides three giant chariots (Nandighoṣa, Tāḷadhvaja, Darpadalana) to the Guṇḍicā temple; the Gajapati king performs Chera Paṅharā _(actors: Jagannātha, Balabhadra, Subhadrā, Gajapati king)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa māhātmya layer; temple tradition)
- **The Sannyāsa corpus as charter of the Daśanāmī orders** — The group supplies the Śruti backing for the ekadaṇḍin Daśanāmī monastic system traditionally organised under Ādi Śaṅkara, who read his order back into these texts _(actors: Ādi Śaṅkara; Daśanāmī sannyāsins)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/sannyasa-upanishads-overview.md) — (Sannyāsa group; Daśanāmī tradition)
- **The Six-Limbed Ṣaḍaṅga-Yoga** — Śākāyanya sets out the sixfold yoga — prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhyāna, dhāraṇā, tarka, samādhi — prefiguring Patañjali _(actors: Sage Śākāyanya, the yogī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/maitrayaniya-upanishad.md) — (Maitrī Upaniṣad 6.18)
- **The third breast vanishes at the sight of Śiva** — Facing Śiva, her third breast disappears and her battle-fury turns to a bride's modesty, marking him as her destined lord _(actors: Mīnākṣī, Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **The thirsty hunt and dead-snake insult** — Exhausted and parched, and with Kali entered through his gold crown, Parīkṣit drapes a dead snake on the silently meditating sage Śamīka _(actors: Parīkṣit, sage Śamīka)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Āstīka Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.18)
- **Yama Tests Naciketas with Bribes** — Yama offers sons, cattle, gold, lands, long life and celestial maidens instead, but Naciketas rejects all fleeting pleasures and holds to the third boon _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.21-29)
- **Birth of Nammalvar at Azhwarthirunagari** — Nammalvar (Maran/Satakopan), foremost of the Alvars who sang the most Divya Desams, is born at Tirukkurugur/Azhwarthirunagari _(actors: Nammalvar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (Alvar hagiography)
- **Buddha absorbed as Vishnu's 9th avatara (Mayamoha rationale)** — Puranic tradition folds the Buddha into the Dashavatara as a deluder (Mayamoha) sent to lead the unworthy/asuras away from the Veda, both absorbing and discrediting Buddhism _(actors: Vishnu (as Buddha/Mayamoha), the asuras)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/nastika-darshanas-and-the-astika-nastika-frame.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.17-18; Bhagavata Purana 1.3.24)
