- **Ramanuja and Madhva — Vedanta Acharyas** — Ramanuja (~11th-12th c.) founds Vishishtadvaita; Madhva (1238-1317) founds Dvaita and the Udupi Krishna matha _(actors: Ramanuja, Madhva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Sri Bhashya; Dvaita texts)
- **Mahmud of Ghazni Sacks Somnath** — The Somnath temple is sacked by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1025–26 CE, beginning its history as the most-destroyed-and-rebuilt temple, last rebuilt in 1951 _(actors: Mahmud of Ghazni)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/12-jyotirlingas.md) — (recorded history)
- **Marine Excavations at Dvaraka (1983-1990)** — The NIO Marine Archaeology Unit under S. R. Rao excavates submerged structures, a jetty and stone anchors off Dvaraka and Bet Dvaraka, dating a port to c. 1500 BCE _(actors: S. R. Rao, NIO)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dwarka-bet-dwarka-saurashtra.md) — (S. R. Rao, The Lost City of Dvaraka (1999); NIO surveys)
- **North Indian Bhakti & Sant Movement** — 14th-17th c. vernacular devotion: Kabir, Mirabai, Chaitanya, Tulsidas (Ramcharitmanas), Surdas, Tukaram _(actors: Kabir, Mirabai, Chaitanya, Tulsidas)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Bhakti movement)
- **Shalivahana's victory inaugurates the Shaka era** — An alternate Gudi Padwa charter marks Shalivahana's victory and the start of the Shalivahana Shaka era _(actors: Shalivahana)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (folk)
- **Aurangzeb Demolishes and Ahilyabai Rebuilds Kashi Vishwanath** — Aurangzeb demolishes the Kashi Vishwanath temple in 1669 CE, and Ahilyabai Holkar rebuilds the present temple in 1780 _(actors: Aurangzeb, Ahilyabai Holkar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/12-jyotirlingas.md) — (recorded history)
- **Founding of the Khalsa** — On Vaisakhi in 1699 Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa, an event mapped onto the Mesha Sankranti harvest/new-year date _(actors: Guru Gobind Singh)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (Sikh tradition; Wikipedia, Vaisakhi)
- **Madhva Founds Dvaita Vedanta** — Madhva (1238-1317 CE) founds Dvaita Vedanta and the Udupi Krishna matha, holding an irreducible difference between jiva and Brahman _(actors: Madhva (Ananda Tirtha))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Dvaita Vedanta works)
- **Tulsidas composes the Hanuman Chalisa** — Goswami Tulsidas composes the 40-verse Awadhi Hanuman Chalisa and the Ramcharitmanas (1574), crystallizing North Indian Hanuman bhakti _(actors: Tulsidas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/hanuman.md) — (Tulsidas, Hanuman Chalisa, Ramcharitmanas)
- **Vijayanagara & Maratha Hindu Sovereignty** — Vijayanagara (1336-1646) last great southern Hindu empire; Shivaji (1630-1680) frames Hindavi Swarajya _(actors: Vijayanagara rulers, Shivaji)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Late-medieval history)
- **Brahmo Samaj Founded** — Raja Ram Mohan Roy founds the Brahmo Samaj on 20 Aug 1828, Calcutta — monotheist, anti-sati, anti-caste reform _(actors: Raja Ram Mohan Roy)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Brahmo Samaj history)
- **Kabir's Nirguna Bhakti** — Kabir (c. 1440-1518 CE), weaver-poet of the nirguna Sant tradition, composes dohas critiquing both Hindu ritualism and Islamic legalism, later claimed by Hindus, Muslims and Sikhs _(actors: Kabir)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Bijak; Bhakti movement (Wikipedia))
- **Sumitra Defeated by Mahapadma Nanda** — Sumitra, traditionally the last Ikshvaku king of Ayodhya, is defeated by Mahapadma Nanda of Magadha and flees to Rohtas, ending the dynasty _(actors: Sumitra, Mahapadma Nanda)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.22; Puranic king-lists)
- **Vasishtha's fire-pit and the Agnikula origin** — At Mt. Abu, Vasishtha's fire-pit (agni-kunda) gives rise to the Agnikula Rajput-origin legend _(actors: Vasishtha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/skanda-purana-khanda-map.md) — (Skanda Purana (Prabhasa-khanda, Arbuda-khanda))
- **Arya Samaj Founded** — Swami Dayananda Saraswati founds the Arya Samaj in 1875 with the slogan 'Back to the Vedas' _(actors: Swami Dayananda Saraswati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Satyarth Prakash (1875))
- **Birth of Santoshi Ma** — Santoshi Ma, a goddess of recent popular origin said to be a daughter of Ganesha, emerges through 1960s vrat literature and is propelled to fame by the 1975 film Jai Santoshi Maa _(actors: Santoshi Ma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-forms-and-navadurga.md) — (Jai Santoshi Maa (1975); vrata-katha tradition)
- **Guru Nanak Founds Sikhism** — Guru Nanak (1469-1539 CE) founds Sikhism within the Sant milieu, teaching nirguna devotion _(actors: Guru Nanak)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md)
- **Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and Gaudiya Vaishnavism** — Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (1486-1534 CE) leads ecstatic Krishna sankirtana in Bengal, founding the inspiration for Gaudiya Vaishnavism (Achintya Bheda Abheda) _(actors: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Bhakti movement (Wikipedia))
- **Manjunatha Linga Installed at Dharmasthala** — A Shiva linga from Kadri is later installed and named Manjunatha (attributed to Vadiraja Tirtha's 16th-c. influence), fusing folk daiva worship, Jain stewardship and Shaiva temple _(actors: Birmanna Pergade, Vadiraja Tirtha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Dharmasthala temple tradition)
- **Vivekananda & Ramakrishna Mission** — Vivekananda gives the 1893 Chicago Parliament address and founds the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897 _(actors: Swami Vivekananda, Ramakrishna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Ramakrishna Mission history)
- **Composition of the Adhyatma Ramayana** — The Advaita-Vedanta Adhyatma Ramayana, recasting Rama as supreme Brahman, is composed (c. 13th-15th c. CE) and embedded in the Brahmanda Purana _(actors: Vyasa (ascribed))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/README.md) — (Adhyatma Ramayana (Brahmanda Purana))
- **Dayananda founds the Arya Samaj condemning murti-puja** — Dayananda Sarasvati founds the Arya Samaj in 1875, condemning image-worship as un-Vedic and calling Hindus back to nirguna theism _(actors: Dayananda Sarasvati)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/mantra-japa-and-murti-puja.md) — (Arya Samaj)
- **Modern Global Hindu Movements** — 20th c. global gurus and movements: Yogananda, ISKCON (Prabhupada, 1966), TM, and yoga's worldwide export _(actors: Yogananda, Prabhupada, Maharishi Mahesh Yogi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Modern Hinduism)
- **Shankara founds Advaita and the Dashanami orders** — Adi Shankara (c. 8th c. CE) composes the Brahma Sutra Bhashya, organizes renunciate monks into the ten Dashanami orders, and founds four cardinal mathas _(actors: Adi Shankara)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/atman-brahman-and-the-six-darshanas.md) — (Brahma Sutra Bhashya; Advaita matha tradition)
- **Sri Yukteswar's Ascending-Yuga Variant** — Sri Yukteswar (The Holy Science, 1894) claims Kali ended ~1700 CE and we are now in ascending Dvapara Yuga _(actors: Sri Yukteswar)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (The Holy Science (1894))
- **Vijayanagara Empire** — The Vijayanagara Empire (1336-1646), the last great Hindu empire of the south, sustains temple Hinduism through the Mughal era _(actors: Vijayanagara rulers)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md)
- **Caitanya Mahāprabhu Rediscovers the Lost Tīrthas of Braj** — Visiting Braj c. 1515, Caitanya Mahāprabhu locates lost sites like Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Imlītalā by trance and deputes the Six Goswamis to recover the tīrthas and write the theology of bhakti _(actors: Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the Six Goswamis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (Gaudiya tradition; Six Goswamis (Wikipedia))
- **Lakulisha founds the Pashupata sampradaya** — The last of the 28 Yogeshvara avatars, Lakulisha, descends as the historical founder of the Pashupata sampradaya _(actors: Lakulisha (Shiva))_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Linga Purana; Kurma Purana)
- **Rūpa Goswami Recovers the Govinda-deva Deity** — Rūpa Goswami recovers the Rādhā-Govinda-deva deity at Gomā-ṭīlā c. 1525; the great red-sandstone temple is built in 1590 under Mān Singh of Amber with Akbar's patronage _(actors: Rūpa Goswami, Mān Singh, Akbar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (Six Goswamis (Wikipedia))
- **Shivaji and the Maratha Resurgence** — Shivaji (1630-1680) frames Hindu sovereignty as Hindavi Swarajya, leading the Maratha resurgence _(actors: Shivaji)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md)
- **Founding of the Brahmo Samaj** — Raja Ram Mohan Roy founds the Brahmo Samaj on 20 Aug 1828 in Calcutta, a monotheist, anti-idolatry, anti-sati, anti-caste reform movement _(actors: Raja Ram Mohan Roy; Dwarkanath Tagore)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Brahmo Samaj (Wikipedia/Britannica))
- **Rādhā-Ramaṇa Self-Manifests for Gopāla Bhaṭṭa** — The Rādhā-Ramaṇa deity self-manifests from a śālagrāma-śilā for Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Goswami in 1542 _(actors: Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Goswami)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (theharekrishnamovement.org)
- **Founding of the Arya Samaj** — Swami Dayananda Saraswati founds the Arya Samaj in 1875 in Bombay with the slogan 'Back to the Vedas,' rejecting Puranic ritual and idolatry, and publishes Satyarth Prakash _(actors: Swami Dayananda Saraswati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (Satyarth Prakash (1875))
- **Svāmī Haridāsa Manifests Banke Bihārī** — The singer-saint Svāmī Haridāsa manifests the combined Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa deity Banke Bihārī at Nidhivana and founds the Haridāsī Sampradāya of devotional music _(actors: Svāmī Haridāsa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (Banke Bihari Temple (Wikipedia))
- **Adi Shankara Consecrates Mukambika at Kollur** — Adi Shankara is said to have consecrated the Goddess Mukambika at Kollur, strongly associating the svayambhu shrine with him _(actors: Adi Shankara)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Kollur tradition)
- **Vallabhācārya Rediscovers Śrī Nāthajī on Govardhana** — Vallabhācārya, founder of the Puṣṭimārga, rediscovers the self-manifest Śrī Nāthajī (the Govardhana-dhāraṇa form) on Govardhana hill, later moved to Nathdwara _(actors: Vallabhācārya)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (Pustimarga tradition)
- **Vivekananda's Chicago Address and Ramakrishna Mission** — Swami Vivekananda delivers his 1893 Parliament of the World's Religions address in Chicago and founds the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897, carrying Vedanta to the West _(actors: Swami Vivekananda; Ramakrishna Paramahamsa)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md)
- **Sri Yukteswar's Ascending-Yuga Reframing** — Sri Yukteswar in The Holy Science (1894) holds Kali Yuga ended ~1700 CE and we are now in an ascending Dvapara Yuga on a 24,000-year precessional cycle, reframing the entire 'we are in Kali' premise _(actors: Sri Yukteswar)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md) — (The Holy Science (1894))
- **Founding of ISKCON** — A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada founds ISKCON in 1966, spreading Gaudiya Vaishnavism worldwide _(actors: A. C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md)
- **Rise of Hindu Nationalism** — Hindu nationalism crystallizes through Savarkar's Hindutva (1923), the RSS (1925) and the VHP (1964), shaping diaspora temple-building and live heritage debates _(actors: Savarkar; RSS; VHP)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/recorded-history.md)
- **Composition of Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas** — Tulsidas begins the Awadhi Ramcharitmanas on Ramanavami 1574 CE in Ayodhya, the dominant North-Indian bhakti retelling and basis of Ramlila _(actors: Tulsidas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/ramcharitmanas-tulsidas.md) — (Ramcharitmanas (Tulsidas))
- **Ramanuja composes the Sri Bhashya** — Ramanuja (1017-1137 CE) establishes Vishishtadvaita, reading souls and matter as the real body of Brahman _(actors: Ramanuja)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/atman-brahman-and-the-six-darshanas.md) — (Sri Bhashya)
- **Ramanuja's Saptavidha-anupapatti against Advaita maya** — Ramanuja launches the seven great untenables against the Advaita avidya/maya in his Sri Bhashya, the most famous demolition of the doctrine _(actors: Ramanuja)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/maya-and-avidya.md) — (Sri Bhashya)
- **Shankara founds the four cardinal mathas** — Adi Shankara organizes renunciates into the Dashanami orders and founds four mathas at Shringeri, Puri, Dvaraka, and Jyotir/Badri, each headed by a Shankaracharya _(actors: Adi Shankara)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/guru-shishya-parampara.md) — (Advaita matha tradition)
- **Woodroffe publishes The Serpent Power** — Sir John Woodroffe (Arthur Avalon) translates the Shat-chakra-nirupana in 1919, fixing the now-dominant seven-chakra image _(actors: John Woodroffe)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/chakras-and-kundalini.md) — (The Serpent Power (1919))
- **Ramcharitmanas Inscribed on UNESCO Memory of the World** — The Ramcharitmanas is inscribed on UNESCO's MOWCAP Regional Register on 7-8 May 2024 in Ulaanbaatar, alongside the Panchatantra and Sahridayaloka-Locana _(actors: UNESCO)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/ramcharitmanas-tulsidas.md) — (UNESCO MOWCAP 2024)
- **Basava founds the Virashaiva/Lingayat tradition** — Basava (12th c.) founds the Virashaiva/Lingayat movement rejecting temple icons in favor of the personal ishta-linga _(actors: Basava)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/guru-shishya-parampara.md) — (Virashaiva tradition)
- **Composition of Kamban's Iramavataram** — Kamban composes the Tamil Iramavataram (Kambaramayanam) under Chola patronage c. 12th c. CE, recasting Rama as full incarnate Vishnu and ending at his coronation _(actors: Kamban, Sadaiyappa Vallal)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/kamban-iramavataram.md) — (Kamban, Iramavataram)
- **Madhva founds Dvaita Tattvavada** — Madhva (1238-1317 CE) systematizes Dvaita with the five eternal differences, teaching eternal soul-God distinction _(actors: Madhva)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/atman-brahman-and-the-six-darshanas.md) — (Brahma Sutra Bhashya (Madhva))
- **Self-sacrifice of the Elder Brothers (Annanmar Katai)** — The twin Tamil warrior-brothers Ponnar and Cankar of Ponnivala, serving Shiva/Vishnu, willingly sacrifice themselves to the gods, their sister Tankal performing their funeral rites; they become guardian deities _(actors: Ponnar, Cankar, Tankal)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/regional-and-oral-epics.md) — (Annanmar Katai (Tamil oral epic))
- **Martyrdom and deification of Madurai Veeran** — The low-caste warrior-hero Madurai Veeran is executed and dismembered over a forbidden love, then deified as a Tamil guardian deity worshipped with his consorts _(actors: Madurai Veeran, Vellaiyammal, Bommakkal)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/regional-and-oral-epics.md) — (Maturai Viran (Tamil folk tradition))
- **Death and deification of Pabuji** — The Rajput hero-chieftain Pabuji Rathod, a camel-rescuer regarded as an incarnation of Lakshmana, dies in battle and is deified as a grama-devata and camel-protector god _(actors: Pabuji Rathod)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/regional-and-oral-epics.md) — (Pabuji ki Phad (Rajasthani oral epic))
- **Saga of Devnarayan** — Devnarayan, deified hero-king of the Gujar community held to be an incarnation of Vishnu, avenges the Bagaravat brothers and is worshipped via the giant phad scroll _(actors: Devnarayan, Savai Bhoj)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/regional-and-oral-epics.md) — (Devnarayan ki Phad (Rajasthani oral epic))
- **Romance of Dhola and Maru** — Dhola (prince Sal Kunvar) and Marvani, betrothed as children and separated, are reunited across desert and rival queens in the Rajasthani romance-epic _(actors: Dhola, Marvani/Maru)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/regional-and-oral-epics.md) — (Dhola Maru ra Duha (Rajasthani ballad cycle))
- **The 52 battles of Alha and Udal** — The brother-heroes Alha and Udal, Banaphar commanders of King Paramardideva of Mahoba, fight their 52 battles culminating in resistance to Prithviraj Chauhan (assoc. 1182 CE); Alha is held never to have died _(actors: Alha, Udal, Paramardideva, Prithviraj Chauhan)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/regional-and-oral-epics.md) — (Alha-Khand (attrib. Jagnik of Mahoba))
- **Lakulisa founds the Pasupata order** — Lakulisa (c. 2nd c. CE) founds the ash-smeared Lakulisa-Pasupata ascetic order, among the earliest organised Saiva sects _(actors: Lakulisa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/agamas-tantras-dharmashastras.md) — (Pasupata-sutras)
- **The Battle of Palnadu** — The fratricidal Battle of Palnadu (c. 1178-1182 CE) pits two factions of Palnadu chiefs; statesman-warrior Brahma Nayudu preaches an anti-caste order and the boy-hero Balachandrudu dies heroically, the fallen worshipped as the Palnati Virulu _(actors: Brahma Nayudu, Balachandrudu, Nagamma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/regional-and-oral-epics.md) — (Palnati Virula Katha; Srinatha's Palnati Vira Caritra)
- **Miracles of Male Madeshvara** — The miracle-working Virashaiva siddha Madeshvara of the Male Madeshvara hills, worshipped as a form of Shiva, is celebrated in the Kannada oral epic _(actors: Madeshvara)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/regional-and-oral-epics.md) — (Male Madeshvara (Kannada oral epic))
- **Behula recovers Lakhindar's life (Manasa-mangal)** — The merchant Chand Sadagar refuses serpent-goddess Manasa's worship, so she kills his son Lakhindar by snakebite on his wedding night, until the widowed bride Behula floats the corpse to the gods, wins his life back, and forces Chand to worship Manasa _(actors: Manasa, Chand Sadagar, Lakhindar, Behula)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/regional-and-oral-epics.md) — (Manasa-mangal (Bengali Mangal-kavya))
- **Vasugupta receives the Siva-Sutras** — Vasugupta (9th c.) receives and composes the Siva-Sutras and Spanda-Karika, founding the textual basis of non-dual Kashmir Saivism _(actors: Vasugupta)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/agamas-tantras-dharmashastras.md) — (Siva-Sutras, Spanda-Karika)
- **Chandi establishes her worship (Chandi-mangal)** — The fierce Durga-form Chandi establishes her worship among hunters and merchants through the Kalaketu hunter and Dhanapati/Srimanta merchant cycles _(actors: Chandi, Kalaketu, Dhanapati, Srimanta)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/regional-and-oral-epics.md) — (Chandi-mangal (Mukundarama, 16th c.))
- **Composition of the Krittivasi Ramayan** — Krittibas Ojha composes the Bengali Srirama Panchali (15th c. CE), the most beloved Bengali retelling and charter-text of Bengali Durga Puja _(actors: Krittibas Ojha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/krittivasi-ramayan.md) — (Krittivasi Ramayan)
- **Maṇḍana Misra converted to Advaita by Sankara** — The Mimamsaka Maṇḍana Misra is, by tradition, converted to Advaita Vedanta by Sankara, a hinge moment between Mimamsa and Vedanta _(actors: Maṇḍana Misra, Sankara)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/darshanas/mimamsa-sutras.md) — (Mimamsa tradition)
- **Vallabha founds Shuddhadvaita and Pushti-marga** — Vallabha (1479-1531 CE) teaches pure non-dualism with the world as real emanation of Krishna and the path of grace _(actors: Vallabha)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/atman-brahman-and-the-six-darshanas.md) — (Shuddhadvaita tradition)
- **Bonbibi protects the Sundarbans against Dakshin Ray** — The forest-goddess Bonbibi protects honey-gatherers and woodcutters of the Sundarbans against the tiger-demon Dakshin Ray, her cult shared by Hindus and Muslims _(actors: Bonbibi, Dakshin Ray, Shah Jongoli)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/regional-and-oral-epics.md) — (Bonbibi Jahuranama)
- **Sankara composes the Brahma-sutra-bhasya** — Adi Sankara (c. 8th c.) composes his Brahma-sutra-bhasya, the oldest surviving complete commentary, founding the Advaita reading of Vedanta _(actors: Adi Sankara)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/darshanas/brahma-sutras.md) — (Brahma-sutra-bhasya)
- **Ramanuja writes the Sri Bhasya** — Ramanuja (11th-12th c.) composes the Sri Bhasya on the Brahma Sutras, founding Visistadvaita and defending Pancaratra as Veda-concordant _(actors: Ramanuja)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/darshanas/brahma-sutras.md) — (Sri Bhasya)
- **Madhva writes the Dvaita commentary** — Madhva (13th c.) composes his Brahma-sutra-bhasya and Aṇu-bhasya, founding the Dvaita dualist school of Vedanta _(actors: Madhva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/darshanas/brahma-sutras.md) — (Brahma-sutra-bhasya, Aṇu-bhasya)
- **Gaṅgesa founds Navya-Nyaya** — Gaṅgesa Upadhyaya (c. 1325, Mithila) composes the Tattva-cintamaṇi, founding the Navya-Nyaya 'New Logic' school _(actors: Gaṅgesa Upadhyaya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/darshanas/nyaya-sutras.md) — (Tattva-cintamaṇi)
- **Praśastapada re-founds Vaiseṣika** — Praśastapada (c. 4th-6th c. CE) composes the Padartha-dharma-saṃgraha, re-founding classical Vaiseṣika and introducing a creator-Isvara into the atomist system _(actors: Praśastapada)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/darshanas/vaisheshika-sutras.md) — (Padartha-dharma-saṃgraha)
- **Chaitanya founds Achintya-bhedabheda** — Chaitanya (1486-1534 CE), systematized by the Gosvamis of Vrindavana, teaches inconceivable difference-and-non-difference, the basis of Gaudiya Vaishnavism _(actors: Chaitanya, Gosvamis)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/atman-brahman-and-the-six-darshanas.md) — (Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition)
- **Vivekananda founds the Ramakrishna Math** — Vivekananda, disciple of Ramakrishna, founds the Ramakrishna Math, a modern global lineage _(actors: Ramakrishna, Vivekananda)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/guru-shishya-parampara.md) — (Ramakrishna Math tradition)
- **Composition of Vimalasuri's Paumacariya** — Vimalasuri composes the Paumacariya (c. 3rd-5th c. CE), the earliest extant Jain Ramayana, rationalizing the epic and reframing Rama within Jain shalakapurusha cosmology _(actors: Vimalasuri)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/jain-and-buddhist-ramayanas.md) — (Paumacariya (Vimalasuri))
- **Gaudapada composes the Mandukya Karika** — Gaudapada (Shankara's parama-guru) develops ajata-vada in the earliest systematic Advaita text, holding nothing is ever truly born _(actors: Gaudapada)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/atman-brahman-and-the-six-darshanas.md) — (Mandukya Karika)
- **Vikramaditya's victory founds the Vikrama era** — The legendary Vikramaditya of Ujjain, after victory over the Shakas, founds the Vikrama Samvat era (epoch 57/58 BCE) _(actors: Vikramaditya)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/hindu-calendar-and-panchanga.md) — (Samvatsara tradition)
- **Discovery of the Paippalada Manuscripts in Odisha (1957)** — Durgamohan Bhattacharyya discovers a well-preserved set of Paippalada palm-leaf manuscripts in Odisha in 1957, becoming the basis of the modern critical edition of the lost recension _(actors: Durgamohan Bhattacharyya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/atharvaveda.md) — (Paippalada Samhita scholarship)
- **Mahavira takes his first disciple Indrabhuti Gautama** — Jains honor the Ashadha full moon as the day Mahavira took his first disciple, Indrabhuti Gautama _(actors: Mahavira, Indrabhuti Gautama)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/guru-shishya-parampara.md) — (Jain tradition)
- **Sayana Composes the Rigveda Bhashya at Vijayanagara** — Sayanacharya, minister-scholar at the Vijayanagara court under Bukka I and Harihara II, composes the authoritative classical commentary on the entire Rigveda with his brother Madhava _(actors: Sayanacharya, Madhava (Vidyaranya))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/rigveda.md) — (Sayana's Rigveda Bhashya)
- **Adi Shankara Founds Advaita Vedanta** — Adi Shankara (c. 8th c. CE) systematizes non-dualist Advaita Vedanta in his bhashyas on the prasthana-trayi, teaching that Brahman alone is real and Atman=Brahman _(actors: Adi Shankara)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upavedas-vedangas-darshanas.md) — (Shankara's bhashyas; Vivekachudamani)
- **Ramanuja Founds Vishishtadvaita** — Ramanuja (c. 11th-12th c. CE) establishes qualified non-dualism, teaching Brahman (Vishnu/Narayana) qualified by real souls and matter, with bhakti and prapatti central, in his Sri Bhashya _(actors: Ramanuja)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upavedas-vedangas-darshanas.md) — (Sri Bhashya)
- **Madhvacharya Founds Dvaita Vedanta** — Madhvacharya (c. 13th c. CE) establishes dualist Tattvavada with five eternal distinctions, holding God, souls, and matter as distinct realities and liberation by grace and bhakti _(actors: Madhvacharya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upavedas-vedangas-darshanas.md) — (Dvaita Vedanta works)
- **Chaitanya Mahaprabhu Founds Achintya Bheda Abheda** — Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (c. 15th-16th c. CE) founds the Gaudiya Vaishnava school of inconceivable simultaneous oneness and difference of soul and God _(actors: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upavedas-vedangas-darshanas.md) — (Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition)
- **Founding of Shree Siddhivinayaka, Prabhadevi** — Contractor Lakṣmaṇ Viṭhu Pāṭīl builds the Siddhivināyaka (Gaṇeśa) temple at Prabhādevī, Mumbai, funded by the devout childless Deubāī Pāṭīl who wished other barren women might obtain children by the deity; later grown into one of India's most-visited and wealthiest temples _(actors: Lakṣmaṇ Viṭhu Pāṭīl; Deubāī Pāṭīl; Gaṇeśa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Wikipedia, Siddhivinayak Temple, Mumbai)
- **Samādhi of Shirdi Sāī Bābā and rise of the Shirdi kṣetra** — On 15 October 1918 the composite supra-sectarian saint Sāī Bābā of Shirdi attains samādhi; his body is interred in the Buṭī Wāḍā (built as a Kṛṣṇa temple), which becomes the Samādhi Mandir, while his Dwārakāmāī mosque, ever-burning dhuni and ūdī anchor a modern all-India Sāī pilgrimage network _(actors: Sāī Bābā of Shirdi; Gopālrāo Buṭī; Govind Dabholkar ('Hemādpant'))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Śrī Sāī Satcharita; Wikipedia, Sai Baba of Shirdi)
- **Tilak popularizes public Ganesh Chaturthi** — Lokmanya Tilak popularizes the modern mass sarvajanik Ganesh Chaturthi in Maharashtra in 1893, a datable historical layer atop the Puranic myth _(actors: Lokmanya Tilak)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (recorded history)
- **Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath** — The same Ashadha full moon marks the Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath, observed as Guru Purnima across Indic traditions _(actors: Buddha)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Buddhist tradition)

## The Future Manvantaras (8–14) & the End  ·  55 events

*What the texts foretell after our age, up to the Night of Brahmā.*

- **Birth-story of Bhautya Manu** — When the sacrificial fire in sage Bhuti's ashram goes out, his disciple Shanti propitiates Agni, who rekindles the fire and grants the boon that the childless Bhuti will have a son — the future 14th Manu, Indra-Savarni/Bhautya _(actors: Bhuti, Shanti, Agni, Angiras)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-14-indra-savarni.md) — (Markandeya/Bhagavata Purana Manu-cycle; popular retellings)
- **Descent of Vishnu as Dharmasetu (11th Manvantara)** — In the 11th (Dharma-Savarni) manvantara Vishnu incarnates as Dharmasetu, born of Vaidhrita and Aryaka, to sustain cosmic order, the Manu himself being a prior manifestation of this avatar _(actors: Vishnu; Dharmasetu; Vaidhrita; Aryaka)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-11-dharma-savarni.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.13)
- **Descent of Vishnu as Rishabha (9th Manvantara)** — In the 9th (Daksha-Savarni) manvantara Vishnu incarnates as Rishabha, born of Ayushman and Ambudhara, to uphold dharma and support Indra Adbhuta and Manu Daksha-Savarni _(actors: Vishnu; Rishabha; Ayushman; Ambudhara)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-09-daksha-savarni.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.13)
- **Descent of Vishnu as Svadhaman (12th Manvantara)** — In the 12th (Rudra-Savarni) manvantara the Vishnu amsha Svadhaman/Sudhaman is born of Sunrita, wife of Satyasaha, to uphold dharma and Manu Rudra-Savarni's rule _(actors: Vishnu; Svadhaman; Satyasaha; Sunrita)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-12-rudra-savarni.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.13.29)
- **Descent of Vishnu as Vishvaksena (10th Manvantara)** — In the 10th (Brahma-Savarni) manvantara Vishnu manifests as Vishvaksena, born from the womb of Vishuchi in the house of the brahmana Vishvasrishta, to assist Manu Brahma-Savarni and his friend Indra Shambhu in upholding dharma _(actors: Vishnu; Vishvaksena; Vishuchi; Vishvasrishta; Shambhu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-10-brahma-savarni.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.13.21-23)
- **Kali Yuga reaches its nadir** — Dharma stands on one leg as mleccha and thieving kings dominate, prompting Vishnu's final descent _(actors: mleccha kings, the demon Kali, Vishnu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalki.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.24; Bhagavata Purana 12.2)
- **Ruci Refuses Marriage and Is Rebuked by the Pitris** — The ascetic Ruci refuses to wed, holding household life breeds only suffering, until his ancestral Pitris appear, teach the value of the five great sacrifices and householder duty, and Ruci composes the Pitri-stotra _(actors: Ruci; the Pitris)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-13-deva-savarni.md) — (Markandeya Purana 92-95)
- **Suratha's worship of the Goddess and rebirth as Savarni** — King Suratha, having lost his kingdom, worships Mahamaya/Durga and by her boon is destined to be reborn as Savarni, the eighth Manu _(actors: King Suratha, the merchant Samadhi, Durga (Mahamaya))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-08-savarni.md) — (Markandeya Purana 81-93 (Devi Mahatmya); Devi Bhagavata)
- **Bali ascends to the throne of Indra** — As recompense for his truthfulness, the daitya king Bali becomes Indra in the Savarni manvantara, fulfilling Vishnu's Vamana-boon _(actors: Bali, Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-08-savarni.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.2; Bhagavata Purana 8.13.15)
- **Birth of Kalki in Shambhala** — Vishnu is born as Kalki, son of the brahmin Vishnuyasha and Sumati, in the village of Shambhala _(actors: Kalki, Vishnuyasha, Sumati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalki.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.3.25, 12.2.18; Kalki Purana 1)
- **Brahma Commands Ruci to Marry** — After Ruci performs tapas for a hundred divine years, Brahma appears and commands him to marry and beget a son destined to be a Manu _(actors: Brahma; Ruci)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-13-deva-savarni.md) — (Markandeya Purana 92-95)
- **Close of the 14th Manvantara and end of the Kalpa** — When Bhautya's 71 mahayugas complete, the last Manu-period and the entire Day of Brahma end, dissolving into the Night of Brahma _(actors: Bhautya Manu, Brahma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-14-indra-savarni.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Reign of Bhautya Manu (14th Manvantara)** — Indra-Savarni (Bhautya) presides as the fourteenth and final Manu of the current Kalpa, with Suci as Indra, seven named sages, and the avatar Brhadbhanu sustaining the age _(actors: Indra-Savarni/Bhautya, Suci (Indra), Brhadbhanu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-14-indra-savarni.md) — (Vishnu Purana III.2; Bhagavata Purana 8.13.33-35; Matsya Purana 9)
- **Avatar Sarvabhauma enthrones Bali** — Vishnu incarnates as Sarvabhauma, son of Devaguhya and Sarasvati, wrests Svarga from the reigning Indra and bestows it on Bali _(actors: Sarvabhauma (Vishnu), Bali, Indra Purandara)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-08-savarni.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.13.15-16)
- **Descent of Brhadbhanu (avatar of the Bhautya age)** — Vishnu's sustaining avatar Brhadbhanu is born of Satrayana and Vitana as Hari's manifestation for the final Manvantara, though no deeds are narrated _(actors: Brhadbhanu, Satrayana, Vitana)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-14-indra-savarni.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.13.35; Vishnu Purana III.2)
- **Malini Given to Ruci in Marriage** — The apsaras Pramlocha presents her daughter Malini as Ruci's bride, fulfilling Brahma's command _(actors: Pramlocha; Malini; Ruci)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-13-deva-savarni.md) — (Markandeya Purana 92-95)
- **Tutelage under Parashurama and Shiva's gifts** — The chiranjivi Parashurama teaches and arms Kalki, who receives the white horse Devadatta, the sage-parrot Shuka, and a blazing sword from Shiva _(actors: Kalki, Parashurama, Shiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalki.md) — (Kalki Purana; Bhagavata Purana 12.2.19-20)
- **Bali Ascends as Indra of the Savarni Age** — In the 8th (Savarni) manvantara the chiranjivi Bali ascends to the throne of Indra, king of the devas, fulfilling Vishnu's earlier boon _(actors: Bali)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-08-savarni.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.2; Bhagavata Purana 8.13.15)
- **Birth of Manu Raucya** — From Malini's womb is born a son of great heroism and intellect who becomes the Manu Raucya (Deva-Savarni), presiding over the 13th manvantara _(actors: Malini; Ruci; Raucya)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-13-deva-savarni.md) — (Markandeya Purana 92-95)
- **Campaign against the adharmic and mleccha kings** — Mounted on Devadatta with his sword, Kalki sweeps the earth slaying thieves and barbarian warlords who abandoned dharma _(actors: Kalki, Devadatta, mleccha kings)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalki.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.2.19-20; Agni Purana)
- **Close of the 14th Manvantara / end of the Kalpa** — When Bhautya's 71 Mahayugas complete, the last Manu-period and the entire Day of Brahma end, closing the present Kalpa _(actors: Bhautya Manu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-14-indra-savarni.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Advent of Kalki** — When adharma reaches its limit, Vishnu incarnates as Kalki in the village of Shambhala, son of the brahmana Vishnuyasha, mounting the white horse Devadatta and bearing a blazing sword from Shiva _(actors: Kalki/Vishnu, Vishnuyasha, Sumati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Kalki Purana; Bhagavata Purana 12.2.18-19; Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **Descent of Vishnu as Sarvabhauma** — In the 8th manvantara Vishnu incarnates as Sarvabhauma, son of Devaguhya and Sarasvati, who wrests Svarga and the office of Indra from the reigning Indra Purandara and bestows it on Bali _(actors: Vishnu; Sarvabhauma; Bali; Purandara)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-08-savarni.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.13.15-16)
- **Descent of Vishnu as Yogeshvara (13th Manvantara)** — In the 13th (Deva-Savarni/Raucya) manvantara Vishnu incarnates as Yogeshvara, born of Devahotra and Brihati, who by his mystic yoga power frees the worlds from misery _(actors: Vishnu; Yogeshvara; Devahotra; Brihati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-13-deva-savarni.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.13.32)
- **Night of Brahma (naimittika pralaya)** — After the Kalpa ends the three worlds (Bhur, Bhuvar, Svar) are burned and flooded, and creation rests for one Night of Brahma before the next Kalpa dawns → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-14-indra-savarni.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Slaying of the demon Kali** — Kalki and his allies wage cosmic war against Kali personified and his progeny, finally vanquishing the age-demon _(actors: Kalki, demon Kali, Krodha, Himsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalki.md) — (Kalki Purana)
- **Kalki's cleansing of the wicked** — Kalki slaughters the mleccha and dasyu kings and robbers by the millions, exterminating the wicked who have lost all spiritual sense _(actors: Kalki)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.2.19-20; Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **Pramiti / Kalki prophecy in the Mahabharata** — Markandeya foretells the brahmin destroyer Pramiti (Kalki Vishnuyasha) who slaughters the mleccha kings and re-establishes the Krita age _(actors: Pramiti/Kalki, Markandeya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalki.md) — (Mahabharata 3.188-189 (Vana Parva))
- **Future Collapse of the Badrinath Route and Shift to Bhavishya Badri** — When adharma overwhelms the world, the Nara and Narayana mountains will collapse and seal the route to Badrinath, whereupon Badrinath will manifest at Bhavishya Badri, marked by the withering arm of the Joshimath Narasimha idol _(actors: Vishnu (Narasimha))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-kedar-pancha-badri.md) — (Skanda Purana (Badari-mahatmya) tradition)
- **Marriage to Padma/Padmavati and Rama** — Kalki weds Padma (Padmavati) of Simhala, an incarnation of Lakshmi, and the princess Rama of the Brihadratha line, fathering the first kings of the new age _(actors: Kalki, Padmavati, Rama, Lakshmi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalki.md) — (Kalki Purana)
- **Return of Satya Yuga and the cosmic reset** — With the destroyers gone the survivors' minds become spontaneously pure, becoming the seed-population of the next Satya Yuga, which dawns when Moon, Sun, and Jupiter together enter the asterism Pushya _(actors: Kalki, the survivors)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.2.23-24; Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **The future Manus (Sāvarṇi and after)** — The Madhya-bhāga details the future manvantaras — the Sāvarṇi group of Manus with their Indras, ṛṣis and devas in the second half of the present kalpa _(actors: Sāvarṇi Manus)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmanda-purana.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Madhya-bhāga))
- **Re-emergence of Devapi and Maru** — Two immortals, Devapi of the lunar line and Maru of the solar line, who survived all four yugas in meditation at Kalapa, re-emerge to re-found the kshatriya dynasties and teach proper dharma _(actors: Devapi, Maru)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.2.37-38; Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **Turning of Kali Yuga into the next Satya Yuga** — With the wicked destroyed and Kali subdued, the righteous are purified, dharma is restored on all four legs, and a new Satya Yuga dawns marked by the Sun, Moon and Jupiter conjoining in Pushya _(actors: Kalki, the purified righteous)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalki.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.24; Bhagavata Purana 12.2.23-24; Kalki Purana)
- **Future collapse of route and shift to Bhaviṣya Badrī** — At the close of the age the Nara and Nārāyaṇa peaks collapse and seal the route, after which Badrinath manifests permanently at Bhaviṣya Badrī, signalled by the withering arm of the Joshimath Narsingh idol _(actors: Nara/Nārāyaṇa peaks, Viṣṇu as Narasiṃha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/badrinath-badarikashrama-kshetra.md) — (Wikipedia (Sapta Badri) [folk eschatology])
- **Future manvantaras and the Sāvarṇi Manus** — Account of the fourteen Manus including the future Sāvarṇi group with their Indras, ṛṣis and devas, manvantaras 8–14 of the present kalpa _(actors: Sāvarṇi and the future Manus)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vayu-purana.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa; Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa)
- **Kalki's return and continuation of the wheel** — His mission complete, Kalki ascends to his abode while the new royal line he founded carries the cycle into the next Mahayuga _(actors: Kalki, the new kings)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalki.md) — (Kalki Purana; Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **Bali becomes Indra of the Savarni Manvantara** — Bali, demoted by Vamana in the present age, is foretold to become the Indra of the future 8th (Savarni) manvantara, the classic demotion-to-promotion arc _(actors: Bali)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.13, 8.22-23)
- **Parashurama to be Kalki's preceptor** — Parashurama is prophesied to reappear at Kali's end as the preceptor of the Kalki avatara, closing the cosmic loop into the next Satya Yuga _(actors: Parashurama, Kalki)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-chiranjivis.md) — (Kalki Purana)
- **The pralaya and final dissolution** — The Vishnu Purana describes the naimittika, prakritika, and atyantika dissolutions, with yoga as the road to moksha at the kalpa- and Brahma-life boundaries _(actors: Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 6))
- **Kalki closes the Kali age** — The Kalki avatara destroys the mleccha kings and restores the Krita-yuga, ending the age _(actors: Kalki)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 4))
- **Kalki prophecy** — The Bhāgavata Purāṇa and Kalki Purāṇa prophesy the future Kalki avatāra of Viṣṇu who will end Kali Yuga _(actors: Kalki (Viṣṇu))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa, Book 12; Kalki Purāṇa)
- **Preceptor of Kalki** — As a cirañjīvi surviving into Kali Yuga, Paraśurāma initiates and arms Kalki, the tenth avatāra, closing the Daśāvatāra loop _(actors: Paraśurāma, Kalki)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/parashurama.md) — (Kalki Purāṇa (late text))
- **Prakritika Pralaya — the Great Dissolution** — At the end of Brahma's 100-year life the cosmos collapses in reverse order of emanation, each element reabsorbed into its subtler source until only Prakriti and Brahman remain _(actors: Brahma, Prakriti, Brahman/Mahavishnu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahma-lifetime.md) — (Vishnu Purana 6.4, Bhagavata Purana 12.4.15-26)
- **Death of Brahma and birth of a new Brahma** — After 311.04 trillion years Brahma is reabsorbed; the cosmos rests in Maha-Vishnu, and after an equal span a new Brahma is born to begin the next Mahakalpa _(actors: Brahma, Maha-Vishnu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahma-lifetime.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.11.40-42, Vishnu Purana 6.4)
- **Bali becomes Indra in the future Savarni manvantara** — The demon-king Bali, demoted by Vamana in the present age, is foretold to become Indra in the 8th (Savarni) manvantara — the demotion-to-promotion arc _(actors: Bali)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.13, 8.22-23)
- **Kalki ends Kali Yuga and restores Satya** — At Kali's close the Kalki avatara destroys adharma and ushers in a new Satya Yuga, restarting the Mahayuga cycle _(actors: Kalki)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/yugas-and-mahayuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.2, Kalki Purana, Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **Kalki avatara descends** — At Kali's end the Lord descends as Kalki, son of Viṣṇuyasas in Sambhala, to destroy the wicked and inaugurate a new Satya Yuga _(actors: Kalki/Viṣṇu, Viṣṇuyasas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12)
- **Eleven Rudras emerge from Saṅkarṣaṇa's brows at pralaya** — At cosmic dissolution, eleven three-eyed trident-bearing Rudras emerge from between Ananta-Saṅkarṣaṇa's wrath-knit eyebrows to annihilate the entire creation _(actors: Saṅkarṣaṇa-Ananta, Rudra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/shesha-ananta.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.25.3)
- **Kalki ends Kali Yuga** — At the close of Kali Yuga, Vishnu will be born as Kalki, son of Vishnuyashas in Shambhala, riding the white horse Devadatta, destroying the wicked, defeating the demon Kali, and inaugurating the next Satya Yuga _(actors: Kalki (Vishnu), Vishnuyashas, the demon Kali, Padmavati)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.3.25, 12.2; Kalki Purana; Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **Naimittika Pralaya — the Night of Brahma** — At each kalpa's end seven suns and the Samvartaka fire scorch the three worlds, floods drown them into one ocean, and the universe is withdrawn into Narayana sleeping on Shesha until the next dawn _(actors: Narayana, Shesha)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/kalpa-and-pralaya.md) — (Vishnu Purana VI.3; Bhagavata Purana 12.4.6-13)
- **Maha-pralaya at the end of Brahma's life** — When Brahma's 100 years complete, twelve suns and the Samvartaka fire scorch the worlds, a deluge floods the cosmos, and all tattvas including Brahma reabsorb in reverse order into unmanifest Prakriti _(actors: Brahma, Prakriti, Brahman/Maha-Vishnu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahma-lifetime.md) — (Vishnu Purana 6.4; Bhagavata Purana 12.4.15-26)
- **Prakritika Pralaya — reverse-order elemental collapse** — At the end of Brahma's life each element loses its quality and merges into its cause back to Prakriti, dissolving everything manifest including Brahma into Purusha/Brahman _(actors: Brahma, the elements, Prakriti, Purusha)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/kalpa-and-pralaya.md) — (Vishnu Purana VI.4; Bhagavata Purana 12.4.15-22)
- **Birth of a new Brahma after Maha-pralaya** — After a span equal to Brahma's life, a new Brahma is generated from Maha-Vishnu's navel-lotus and the entire Mahakalpa cycle begins anew, time being beginningless and endless _(actors: Maha-Vishnu, new Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahma-lifetime.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.11.40-42; Vishnu Purana 6.4)
- **Kalpa-ending night of Brahma after the 14th manvantara** — At the close of the 14th (Indra-savarni/Bhautya) manvantara comes the Kalpa-ending night of Brahma (naimittika pralaya) _(actors: Brahma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.13; Vishnu Purana 3.2)

## Cross-Yuga & Recurring Myths  ·  1627 events

*Episodes the texts do not pin to one fixed age (recurring deva–asura wars, Śaiva/Śākta cycles).*

- **"As in dance, so in painting"** — the Citrasūtra's governing dictum yathā nṛtte tathā citre makes the painted body a frozen moment of dance, fixing gesture, proportion, and rasa as the shared grammar of the visual and performing arts _(actors: Mārkaṇḍeya, Vajra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnudharmottara-purana.md) — (Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa III.35–43)
- **"Hence I depart not" — the refusal of heaven** — when Dharma and Indra arrive with the celestial car, Vipaścit declines to ascend while thousands cry to him for relief, holding compassion for the distressed above the joys of Svarga _(actors: Vipaścit, Dharma, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vipashchit-in-hell.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa XV)
- **"I am lord only of the rest"** — Yama confesses he governs all mankind by Brahmā's appointment save the Vaiṣṇavas, over whom Hari alone rules — prabhur aham anya-nṛṇāṃ na vaiṣṇavānām _(actors: Yama, Viṣṇu, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yama-gita.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa III.7)
- **"If you are cut, do you not bleed?"** — the thoṭṭam's charter verse: Brahmin and Pulaya bleed the same red blood, so caste has no ground in the body _(actors: the Pulaya-Śiva, the Brahmin)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/pottan-theyyam.md) — (Poṭṭan thoṭṭam-pāṭṭu, Pulappoṭṭan samvāda)
- **"The air that clings to thy body"** — the tortured souls beg the king to stay, revealing that the cool wind was his own presence, whose radiated merit dispels their burning and pain _(actors: Vipaścit, the damned)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vipashchit-in-hell.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa XV)
- **"The whole earth is one family"** — the Hitopadeśa's friendship-book preserves the famed verse vasudhaiva kuṭumbakam, holding that to the noble-hearted no one is stranger _(actors: Nārāyaṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/hitopadesha.md) — (Hitopadeśa I, subhāṣita)
- **"We drink the same water"** — the argument extends to shared sun, water and toddy, dissolving the fictions of tīṇḍal and high/low caste _(actors: the Pulaya-Śiva, Śaṅkarācārya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/pottan-theyyam.md) — (Poṭṭan thoṭṭam)
- **A brahmin refuses Indra's throne** — Indra descends to Kālikā-grāma to check a mortal whose recitation of Gītā chapter 18 rivals his merit, and the reciter spurns Indra's seat to choose Viṣṇu-sāyujya _(actors: Indra, a brahmin reciter)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavad-gita/gita-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Gītā-Māhātmya 18)
- **A charter for shared karmic fruit** — Somaka's insistence on shouldering a sin committed for his sake stages the epic's loophole of loyalty, prefiguring Yudhiṣṭhira's own refusal to enter heaven alone _(actors: Somaka, the purohita, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jantu-somaka.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva CXXVIII; Svargārohaṇa Parva)
- **A lifetime of sons and grandsons** — over many years Suśīlā bears the king many sons who grow, marry, and give her grandsons — an entire ripening life of saṃsāric love lived inside the illusion _(actors: Suśīlā, Tāladhvaja)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada-maya-taladhvaja.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa VI.30)
- **Abhijit slips from the sky** — the 28th nakṣatra Abhijit falls from heaven while contesting seniority with Rohiṇī, the mythic charter behind the star and its victorious midday muhūrta _(actors: Abhijit, Rohiṇī, Skanda, Indra)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/muhurta-and-auspicious-timing.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana/Āraṇyaka Parva)
- **Agastya brings Tamil and founds the Siddhar lineage** — The sage Agastya, crossing south of the Vindhyas, is held in Tamil tradition to be the ādi-guru of the Siddhars and patron of Siddha medicine _(actors: Agastya (Agathiyar))_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/tamil-siddhars.md) — (Akattiyam; Siddha-vaidya corpus; Wikipedia (Agastya, Siddhar))
- **Agni reveals the Agni Purāṇa to Vasiṣṭha** — The fire-god Agni reveals the encyclopedic Agni Purāṇa, the essence of all sciences, to the sage Vasiṣṭha, who transmits it down the chain to Vyāsa and the Sūta _(actors: Agni, Vasiṣṭha, Vyāsa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/agni-purana.md) — (Agni Purāṇa 1)
- **Ajamila's Fall through the Dasi** — The virtuous brahmana Ajamila of Kanyakubja is overpowered by lust at the sight of a drunken dasi, casts off his wedded wife, and descends into a life of theft and deceit _(actors: Ajamila, the dasi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ajamila.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 6.1.20-27)
- **Akūpāra the tortoise remembers** — the oldest being on earth weeps and knows Indradyumna, for the lake he dwells in was scooped out by the hooves of the countless cattle the king gave away in charity _(actors: Akūpāra, Indradyumna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/indradyumna-akupara-oldest-beings.md) — (Mahābhārata 3.191 / Ganguli Vana CXCIX)
- **Alakṣmī expelled by the Kārtika lamps** — Jyeṣṭhā-Alakṣmī, risen from the churning before Lakṣmī and assigned to dwell in filth and strife, is driven out by the swept house and rows of lamps of the Kārtika/Dīpāvalī vow that invite Śrī in _(actors: Alakṣmī/Jyeṣṭhā, Lakṣmī, Duḥsaha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kartika-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Padma P.; Ṛgveda Khila, Śrī-Sūkta)
- **Alarka's 66,000-year youthful reign** — Alarka, son of Pratardana and (in the Mārkaṇḍeya splice) of Madālasā, rules the earth 66,000 years while remaining young, then renounces after Dattātreya's instruction _(actors: Alarka, Madālasā, Dattātreya)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kashi-line-divodasa.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.17.7–8; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa ~chs. 16–44)
- **Anaraṇya renounces his throne for Śivaloka** — grieving the loss of his favourite daughter, King Anaraṇya of the Indra-Sāvarṇi line abandons the kingdom for forest penance and attains Śivaloka, leaving his son Kīrtimān to rule _(actors: Anaraṇya, Kīrtimān)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/padma-pippalada.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Pārvatī-khaṇḍa 34)
- **Annam Brahma — food revealed as Brahman** — Varuṇa sends his son Bhṛgu into austerity, who first realizes that food (anna) itself is Brahman before ascending through breath, mind and bliss _(actors: Bhṛgu, Varuṇa)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/anna-naivedya-and-prasada.md) — (Taittirīya Upaniṣad 3.1–3.6)
- **Annapūrṇā feeds Śiva at Kāśī** — in the poem's Deva-frame the Great Goddess as Annadā fills the begging Śiva's bowl, the anna-theology that the giver of food sustains even the Absolute _(actors: Annapūrṇā/Annadā, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/annadamangal-bharatchandra.md) — (Annadāmaṅgal, Annadā-maṅgal khaṇḍa)
- **Annapūrṇā feeds Śiva in Kāśī** — Pārvatī as the goddess who is full of food gives alms to Śiva himself, who begs at her ladle; no one in her city goes hungry, and Śaṅkara enshrines her in the Annapūrṇā-stotra _(actors: Annapūrṇā, Śiva)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/anna-naivedya-and-prasada.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa, Kāśī Khaṇḍa; Devī-Bhāgavata)
- **Āpaduddhāraka — the rescuer from calamity** — invoked through the Vaṭuka-Bhairava Stotra and kavaca, the boy-Bhairava lifts devotees out of disease, enemies, debt, fear, and untimely death _(actors: Vaṭuka Bhairava, devotees)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vatuka-bhairava-origin.md) — (Tantric stotra tradition)
- **Apotheosis of the impaled god** — his wrongful, violent death on the stake generates godhood, making Kāttavarāyaṉ a kāval teyvam whose stake becomes his throne and emblem — the South Indian death-and-deification engine _(actors: Kāttavarāyaṉ)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kattavarayan-katai.md) — (Masilamani-Meyer, The Tale of Kāttavarāyaṉ) [scholarly] [folk]
- **Aśokasundarī born of the Kalpavṛkṣa** — lonely Pārvatī voices her wish before the wish-fulfilling tree, which produces a maiden of surpassing beauty named for ending the goddess's grief (śoka), reckoned a Śaiva daughter beside Gaṇeśa and Skanda _(actors: Pārvatī, Śiva, Aśokasundarī, Kalpavṛkṣa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ashokasundari-nahusha-hunda.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Bhūmi-khaṇḍa 103)
- **Atri rescued from the burning pit** — cast into a fiery chasm (ṛbīsa) by his enemies, Atri Saptavadhri is cooled and freed unharmed by the Aśvins with a coolness-giving draught _(actors: Aśvins, Atri Saptavadhri)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ashvins.md) — (Ṛgveda 1.116.8; 5.78.4–6)
- **Atri restores the darkened Sun** — the Āsura Svarbhānu strikes Sūrya with darkness and the ṛṣi Atri alone finds and re-fixes the sun in the sky by the fourth brahman-formula — the Vedic prototype of the Rāhu eclipse-myth _(actors: Atri, Svarbhānu, Sūrya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/brahmana-legends-catalog.md) — (Ṛgveda 5.40.5–9; Pañcaviṃśa Brāhmaṇa 4.5.2)
- **Aṭṭa-vīraṭṭāṉam — the eight feat-shrines** — a closed Tamil set of eight Śiva temples, each fixing one of his fierce cosmos-ordering deeds to a named delta town, the presiding liṅga called Vīraṭṭāṉeśvarar _(actors: Śiva, Nāyanār saints)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ashta-virattanam-eight-feat-shrines.md) — (Tēvāram; sthala-purāṇas)
- **Bala consents to be the gods' sacrificial victim** — The devas ask the truth-bound asura to serve as the pashu of their yajna, and Bala freely offers his own body to his enemies' rite _(actors: Bala/Vala, the devas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/bala-asura-navaratna-origin.md) — (Garuda Purana, Purva-khanda gem chapters; Buddhabhatta, Ratnapariksha)
- **Bala's ascendancy over the gods** — In the primordial deva–asura war the asura Bala (Vala) grows invincible and the devas, unable to slay him in battle, resort to stratagem _(actors: Bala/Vala, Indra, the devas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/bala-asura-navaratna-origin.md) — (Garuda Purana, Purva-khanda ch. ~68)
- **Bala's blood and eyes fall on Lanka** — The asura's blood falls into the Ravanaganga river of Simhala and his eyes on the same island, chartering Ceylon's ruby-gravels and blue-sapphire beds _(actors: Bala/Vala, the devas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/bala-asura-navaratna-origin.md) — (Buddhabhatta, Ratnapariksha, ruby and sapphire sections)
- **Bala's dismembered body becomes the gem-seeds** — Slain as a sanctified victim, Bala's members turn into the seeds of the gems: blood→ruby, teeth→pearl, bile→emerald, eyes→sapphire, bones→diamond _(actors: Bala/Vala, the devas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/bala-asura-navaratna-origin.md) — (Garuda Purana, Purva-khanda chs. ~68–70; Agni Purana 246)
- **Bāṇāī the Dhangar shepherdess** — Khaṇḍobā wins his second wife, the Dhangar shepherdess Bāṇāī, in pastoral guise, writing the pastoral layer into the high god's own biography _(actors: Khaṇḍobā, Bāṇāī, Mhāḷsā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/dhangar-oral-epics-biroba-mhaskoba-dhuloba.md) — (Bāṇāī ovī; Sontheimer)
- **Between ghost and god** — a fierce spirit or fallen pastoral hero, bound to a devotee and propitiated by possession and blood-sacrifice, is progressively deified into a temple-god and equated with Bhairava _(actors: the bhūt/vīragaḷ, the devotee-medium, Bhairava)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/dhangar-oral-epics-biroba-mhaskoba-dhuloba.md) — (Sontheimer, Between Ghost and God)
- **Bhadrā bound into the karaṇa cycle** — the fierce daughter of Sūrya and Chāyā, sister of Śani, is assigned by Brahmā a fixed seat as the Viṣṭi karaṇa so her destructive hours can be known and avoided _(actors: Bhadrā, Sūrya, Chāyā, Brahmā, Śani)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/muhurta-and-auspicious-timing.md) — (astrological/purāṇic lore [late text] [folk])
- **Bhadrāyu revived with holy ash** — the poisoned, forest-abandoned infant of queen Sumati dies and is resuscitated by the yogin Ṛṣabha with Śiva's bhasma, named Bhadrāyu, and taught the Śiva-kavaca _(actors: Bhadrāyu, Sumati, Ṛṣabha, Vajrabāhu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/brahmottara-khanda-vrata-tales.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa, Brāhmottara-khaṇḍa 10–11)
- **Bhakti above the sacrificial fire** — the Bhāgavata makes the yajña-patnī episode its charter that loving surrender outranks Vedic ritualism, with disqualified women reaching the Lord where learned twice-born ritualists fail _(actors: yajña-patnīs, the brāhmaṇa sacrificers, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yajna-patni-mokshana.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.23)
- **Bhṛgu curses Viṣṇu to mortal births** — After Viṣṇu beheads Śukra's mother sheltering the war-broken asuras, Bhṛgu curses him to be born again and again among mortals — the Matsya's charter for the human avatāras _(actors: Bhṛgu, Viṣṇu, Śukra's mother, Indra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/twelve-devasura-battles.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa, 47)
- **Bhṛgu revives Kāvyamātā** — Bhṛgu sprinkles water from his kamaṇḍalu and restores his beheaded wife to life, though the curse on Viṣṇu still stands _(actors: Bhṛgu, Kāvyamātā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhrigus-curse-on-vishnu.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata IV.14)
- **Bhṛgu's curse dooms Viṣṇu to mortal births** — finding his wife slain, Bhṛgu curses Viṣṇu to be born again and again among men and to live long separated from his consort — the charter of the avatāras _(actors: Bhṛgu, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhrigus-curse-on-vishnu.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara 51.14–17; Devī-Bhāgavata IV.14)
- **Bhṛgu's word makes Vītahavya a Brāhmaṇa** — the defeated king takes refuge with Bhṛgu, who tells the pursuing Pratardana "there are only Brāhmaṇas here" — and the true word of the ṛṣi transmutes the Kṣatriya into a Brāhmaṇa on the instant _(actors: Vītahavya, Bhṛgu, Pratardana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/matanga-vitahavya-varna-upakhyanas.md) — (Anuśāsana Parva ~31)
- **Bhṛṅgī cursed to be fleshless** — the Śiva-only gaṇa defends his lord as cheated, and the furious Goddess curses him to skin and bone, the etiology of his skeletal three-legged form _(actors: Bhṛṅgī, Pārvatī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shiva-parvati-dice-game.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa, Kedāra-khaṇḍa 34.115–116)
- **Bhujyu saved from the shipwreck** — the Aśvins pluck Bhujyu, son of Tugra, from the midst of the ocean and bear him home over three days in self-propelling winged ships _(actors: Aśvins, Bhujyu, Tugra)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ashvins.md) — (Ṛgveda 1.116.3–5; 1.117.14–15)
- **Bhuśuṇḍa the immortal crow recounts the kalpas** — Vasiṣṭha visits the crow-sage nested on the kalpa-taru on Meru, who remembers repeated ocean-churnings and pralayas and survives cosmic dissolution by prāṇa-contemplation _(actors: Bhuśuṇḍa, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yoga-vasishtha-tales-catalog.md) — (Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha VI.1.14–28)
- **Bhuśuṇḍa the immortal crow survives the pralayas** — The ancient crow on Meru's kalpa-tree tells Vasiṣṭha how he has watched dissolutions and world-ages repeat, abiding in prāṇa-contemplation while creation burns _(actors: Bhuśuṇḍa, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/yoga-vasishtha.md) — (Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha, Nirvāṇa prakaraṇa Pūrvārdha)
- **Biroba born of Māyavā** — the Dhangar shepherd-god is miraculously born of, or given by, the goddess Māyavā (Māyakkā) and fostered in a shepherd household, emerging to herd sheep and found his cult _(actors: Biroba, Māyavā, the Dhangar foster-family)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/dhangar-oral-epics-biroba-mhaskoba-dhuloba.md) — (Biroba ovī; Sontheimer, Pastoral Deities)
- **Birth of Bhadrakālī from Śiva's third eye** — Alerted by Nārada to Dārika's outrages, Śiva opens his third eye and from its fire Bhadrakālī is born fully armed as his daughter, with the vetāla given as her mount _(actors: Śiva, Bhadrakālī, Nārada, the vetāla)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/bhadrakali-kerala-bhagavati.md) — (Kerala Bhadrakālī-māhātmya; kaḷampāṭṭu invocations)
- **Birth of Sārasvata** — Dadhīca's seed, spilled at the sight of the apsaras Alambuṣā, falls into the Sarasvatī, who preserves it and bears the sage Sārasvata _(actors: Dadhīca, Alambuṣā, river-goddess Sarasvatī, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sarasvata-upakhyana-vriddhakumari.md) — (Mbh Śalya Parva 9.51; Ganguli LI)
- **Birth of the water-child Lauhitya** — Amoghā bears Brahmā's seed, conveyed through Śāntanu, and gives birth to a son in the form of water — the Brahmaputra _(actors: Amoghā, Śāntanu, Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/lauhitya-brahmaputra-origin.md) — (Kālikā Purāṇa, 83; Padma Purāṇa, Sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa 55)
- **Bobbariya, the Muslim mariner made daiva** — a Byāri merchant-sailor who dies at sea is deified as a Tuḷu sea-spirit guarding trade and fishermen, his shrine marked by the mast-like bobbariyana kambo _(actors: Bobbariya)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/panjurli-guliga-tulu-daivas.md) — (Bobbariya paddana) [folk]
- **Both cousins liberated** — Khāṇḍikya entrusts his son with the throne and by steady meditation on Viṣṇu attains release, and Keśidhvaja is freed likewise, closing the Viṣṇu Purāṇa on its mokṣa coda _(actors: Khāṇḍikya, Keśidhvaja)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/khandikya-keshidhvaja.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa VI.7)
- **Brahmā enthrones Ripuñjaya as Divodāsa** — In an age of anarchy Brahmā persuades the ascetic Ripuñjaya to rule the earth from Kāśī on condition that all gods withdraw to heaven _(actors: Brahmā, Ripuñjaya/Divodāsa)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kashi-line-divodasa.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa, Kāśī-khaṇḍa, Pūrvārdha ch. 43)
- **Brahmā's desire for Amoghā** — Brahmā, smitten by Amoghā, wife of the sage Śāntanu, is rebuked and departs in shame, his seed fallen at the hermitage _(actors: Brahmā, Amoghā, Śāntanu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/lauhitya-brahmaputra-origin.md) — (Kālikā Purāṇa, 82)
- **Brahmā's ten aśvamedhas at Kāśī** — Testing Divodāsa, Brahmā demands ten simultaneous horse-sacrifices, which the king executes flawlessly — the etiology of Daśāśvamedha Ghāṭ; Sūrya likewise stays as the twelve Ādityas of Kāśī _(actors: Brahmā, Divodāsa, Sūrya)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kashi-line-divodasa.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa, Kāśī-khaṇḍa, Uttarārdha ~chs. 54–55)
- **Brahmā's yajña at Puṣkara and Sāvitrī's curse** — Brahmā sacrifices at Puṣkara with substitute bride Gāyatrī when Sāvitrī delays, and her curse limits his worship to this one tīrtha _(actors: Brahmā, Sāvitrī, Gāyatrī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/padma-purana-khanda-map.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Sṛṣṭi-khaṇḍa, Puṣkara-māhātmya)
- **Brahmā, Śatarūpā, and the fifth head** — the Purāṇic reflex: Brahmā grows extra heads to keep gazing at his own created daughter Śatarūpā/Sandhyā, and Kāla Bhairava shears off the fifth head, incurring the brahmahatyā skull-penance _(actors: Brahmā, Śatarūpā, Kāla Bhairava)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prajapati-ushas-rudra-piercing.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa 3–4; Śiva Purāṇa, Śatarudra-saṃhitā)
- **Bṛhaspati impersonates Śukra and deludes the asuras** — While Śukra endures his vow for Śiva's mantras and weds Jayantī, Bṛhaspati teaches in his form and turns the asuras from their true guru _(actors: Śukra, Bṛhaspati, Jayantī, the asuras)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/twelve-devasura-battles.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa, 47)
- **Bṛhaspati impersonates the asura-guru** — during Śukra's hidden decade the deva-guru takes Śukra's very form, preaches a heterodox dharma to disunite the Daityas, and gets the returning true Śukra rejected as the fraud _(actors: Bṛhaspati, Daityas, Śukra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhrigus-curse-on-vishnu.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa 47; Devī-Bhāgavata IV.13)
- **Brihaspati's curse blinds Dirghatamas in the womb** — The embryo in Mamata's womb blocks Brihaspati's intruding seed, and the enraged god-priest curses him to be born into 'long darkness', giving the blind seer his name _(actors: Brihaspati, Mamata, Utathya, Dirghatamas (in womb))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dirghatamas.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva ~104; Brihaddevata 4)
- **Caṇḍikeśvara, guardian of the nirmālya** — as Śiva's appointed officer (adhikārin), Caṇḍeśa becomes the standing Āgamic recipient of all offerings already given to Śiva (nirmālya), from whom alone devotees may receive them _(actors: Caṇḍikeśvara, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/chandesvara-chandikeshvara.md) — (Śaiva Siddhānta Āgamas)
- **Candrāṅgada drowned and rescued by nāgas** — Sīmantinī's husband Candrāṅgada of Niṣadha sinks in a Yamunā whirlpool, is carried to Pātāla by nāga-maidens, honoured by Takṣaka for his Śiva-devotion, and returns alive to reunite with her — the Somavāra-vrata's proof _(actors: Candrāṅgada, Sīmantinī, Takṣaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/brahmottara-khanda-vrata-tales.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa, Brāhmottara-khaṇḍa 9)
- **Candrāvatī desecrates the prasād** — royal women scorn the Svasthānī offerings, casting the sacred flowers into the river, and lose husbands, sons, and kingdom until they re-perform the vow and are wholly restored _(actors: Candrāvatī, Svasthānī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/swasthani-brata-katha.md) — (Svasthānī Vrata Kathā, Goma cycle)
- **Chastity restores Pippalāda's youth** — pleased by her proven fidelity, Dharma reveals himself and grants boons: the aged Pippalāda is made young and vigorous, Padmā eternally youthful, with ten virtuous sons and boundless wealth _(actors: Dharma, Pippalāda, Padmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/padma-pippalada.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Pārvatī-khaṇḍa 35)
- **Ciṟuttoṇḍar's extreme naivedya** — The Nāyanār cooks and offers his own son as food to a Bhairava-guest, the limit-case of food-devotion, before the child is restored _(actors: Ciṟuttoṇḍar/Siruthondar, Śiva as Bhairava)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/anna-naivedya-and-prasada.md) — (Periya Purāṇam)
- **Consecration of Sthāṇu-tīrtha** — the ground where Śiva stood by the sage as the immovable Sthāṇu becomes Sthāneśvara (Thanesar) at Kurukṣetra, a tīrtha granting Śiva-sāyujya _(actors: Śiva, Dadhīca)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kshupa-dadhicha-dispute.md) — (Liṅga Purāṇa, Pūrva-bhāga ~35–36)
- **Cūḍālā appears as the sage Kumbha** — Disguised as a young brahmin sage claiming to be Nārada's pot-born son, Cūḍālā becomes her husband's guru and exposes his false renunciation through the cintāmaṇi and Vindhya-elephant parables _(actors: Cūḍālā/Kumbha, Śikhidhvaja, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/chudala-shikhidhvaja.md) — (Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha VI.1, ~chs. 84–96)
- **Cūḍālā liberates King Śikhidhvaja as the sage Kumbha** — The realized queen Cūḍālā, disguised as the brahmin youth Kumbha, teaches and tests her renunciate husband until both rule as jīvanmuktas _(actors: Cūḍālā, Śikhidhvaja)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/yoga-vasishtha.md) — (Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha, Nirvāṇa prakaraṇa Pūrvārdha)
- **Cūḍālā's awakening in the palace** — Queen Cūḍālā of Mālava attains Self-knowledge through self-inquiry (ātma-vicāra) while living as a reigning queen, without external renunciation _(actors: Cūḍālā, Śikhidhvaja)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/chudala-shikhidhvaja.md) — (Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha VI.1, ~ch. 78)
- **Curds bought with a gold ring** — thirsty on the march, the two disguised Lords drink the milkmaid Māṇikā's curds and, having no coin, pay her with a gold ring, bidding her collect the debt from the king coming behind _(actors: Jagannātha, Balabhadra, Māṇikā the milkmaid)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kanchi-kaveri-jagannatha-legend.md) — (Kāñcī-Kāverī) [regional] [folk]
- **Cyavana initiates the gleaner** — Dharmāraṇya seeks out Cyavana of Bhṛgu's line for formal saṃskāra into the Uñcha vow, then takes up Yama and Niyama and withdraws into another forest to live it _(actors: Dharmāraṇya, Cyavana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/unchavritti-brahmin-naga-padmanabha.md) — (Śānti Parva CCCLXV)
- **Dadhīca's curse foretelling the Dakṣa-yajña** — victorious, Dadhīca curses the gods for siding with the king and prophesies that Rudra will scatter and burn them all, Viṣṇu included, at the future sacrifice of Dakṣa _(actors: Dadhīca, the Devas, Rudra, Dakṣa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kshupa-dadhicha-dispute.md) — (Liṅga Purāṇa, Pūrva-bhāga ~35–36)
- **Dakṣa's sacrifice and Satī's fire (Svasthānī telling)** — Satī, humiliated at her father Dakṣa's Śiva-excluding sacrifice, immolates herself, and Śiva's hosts wreck the rite _(actors: Satī, Dakṣa, Śiva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/swasthani-brata-katha.md) — (Svasthānī Vrata Kathā, Śaiva chapters)
- **Damanaka sunders lion and bull** — the jackal Damanaka poisons the friendship of lion-king Piṅgalaka and the bull Sañjīvaka with insinuation until the lion kills his friend, the exemplum of Suhṛdbheda _(actors: Damanaka, Karaṭaka, Piṅgalaka, Sañjīvaka)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/hitopadesha.md) — (Hitopadeśa II, Suhṛdbheda)
- **Dambhodbhava's daily boast** — the universal emperor Dambhodbhava asks each morning whether anyone on earth is his equal in battle, until brāhmaṇas name the ascetics Nara and Nārāyaṇa as his superiors _(actors: Dambhodbhava, the brāhmaṇas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dambhodbhava-nara-narayana.md) — (Mahābhārata CE 5.94, Udyoga Parva)
- **Dārika's boon from Brahmā** — The asura Dārika wins invincibility against every male being — god, asura, or human — leaving only a woman able to kill him, and tyrannizes the worlds _(actors: Dārika, Brahmā, Dānavēndra)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/bhadrakali-kerala-bhagavati.md) — (Kerala Bhadrakālī-māhātmya; mudiyettu tōṟṟam tradition)
- **Dārika-vadham — the beheading of Dārika** — After a long war in which the vetāla drinks the demon blood before it seeds new demons, Bhadrakālī severs Dārika's head and holds it aloft, the defining Kerala Bhagavati icon _(actors: Bhadrakālī, Dārika, Kūḷi, the vetāla)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/bhadrakali-kerala-bhagavati.md) — (Kerala Bhadrakālī-māhātmya; mudiyettu tradition)
- **Death teaches Naciketas the yogic Song** — the Agni Purāṇa's Yama-Gītā, framed on the Kaṭha archetype, has Yama expound jñāna, yoga, and the chariot-of-the-body path to release _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yama-gita.md) — (Agni Purāṇa 381)
- **Deva Śarmā's tapas at Devprayag** — the sage's austerities and divine vision at the confluence give Devprayag its name [regional] _(actors: Deva Śarmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/panch-prayag-alaknanda-confluences.md) — (Wikipedia, Devprayag; Kedāra-khaṇḍa tradition)
- **Devaśarman and the goatherd Mitravat** — a brahmin seeking supreme knowledge learns from a forest goatherd that steady duty ripens into wisdom, the lesson of Gītā chapter 2 _(actors: Devaśarman, Mitravat, Sukarman)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavad-gita/gita-mahatmya-tales.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Gītā-Māhātmya 2)
- **Devaśayanī and Prabodhinī — Viṣṇu's four-month cosmic sleep** — Viṣṇu lies down on Śeṣa at Āṣāḍha śukla Ekādaśī and wakes at Kārttika śukla Ekādaśī, the two tithis bounding Cāturmāsya and the Tulasī-vivāha _(actors: Viṣṇu, Śeṣa, Tulasī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ekadashi-mahatmyas-catalog.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Uttara-khaṇḍa; pan-purāṇic calendar lore)
- **Dhaneśvara saved by the company of Kārttika-vratins** — a lifelong cheat dying among Kārttika observers on the Narmadā is spared Yama's hells by their contagious merit _(actors: Dhaneśvara, Yama, Kārttika-vratins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/masa-mahatmyas-kartika-magha-vaishakha.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Kārttika-māhātmya)
- **Dharma disguised tests Padmā's chastity** — the god Dharma takes the guise of a lustful king and, meeting Padmā at the celestial river, urges her to cast off the ruthless old brahmin, but she refuses utterly _(actors: Dharma, Padmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/padma-pippalada.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Pārvatī-khaṇḍa 35)
- **Dharmāraṇya converted to the gleaner's life** — his doubt dispelled, the brāhmaṇa declares he has learnt the value of the Uñcha vow and resolves to abandon acquisition for the humblest, harm-minimal livelihood _(actors: Dharmāraṇya, Padmanābha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/unchavritti-brahmin-naga-padmanabha.md) — (Śānti Parva CCCLXV)
- **Dharmāraṇya seeks the Nāga Padmanābha** — a righteous but doubt-gnawed brāhmaṇa, unsure which dharma most surely wins liberation, journeys to the serpent-city in the Naimiṣa forest on the Gomatī to question the virtuous Nāga _(actors: Dharmāraṇya, Padmanābha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/unchavritti-brahmin-naga-padmanabha.md) — (Śānti Parva CCCLV, CCCLXI)
- **Dhuloba, the dust-lord of the flock** — the fierce Bhairava-type Dhangar god of the Vīr–Phalṭaṇ tract is born, marries and founds his cult in his own sung ovī _(actors: Dhuloba, his Dhangar devotees)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/dhangar-oral-epics-biroba-mhaskoba-dhuloba.md) — (Dhuloba ovī; Sontheimer)
- **Dīrghajihvī the soma-licker trapped** — Indra, unable to catch the demoness who licks up the gods' soma with her long tongue, fashions the youth Sumitra Kutsa to seduce and destroy her _(actors: Indra, Dīrghajihvī, Sumitra Kutsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/brahmana-legends-catalog.md) — (Jaiminīya Brāhmaṇa 1.161–163)
- **Dundubhinirhrāda hunts the brahmins of Kāśī** — the Daitya uncle of Prahlāda, avenging Hiraṇyākṣa, resolves to starve the gods by devouring their sacrificing brahmins and comes to Kāśī, ambushing them in the shapes of forest-dweller, water-beast, invisible form, and tiger, leaving not even a bone _(actors: Dundubhinirhrāda, the brahmins of Kāśī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yuddha-khanda-minor-vadhas.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa, Rudra-saṃhitā, Yuddha-khaṇḍa 58)
- **Durgama steals the Vedas** — the asura Durgama, son of Ruru of Hiraṇyākṣa's line, wins the four Vedas as a boon from Brahmā, extinguishing all yajña so that the rains fail and a hundred-year drought grips the earth _(actors: Durgama, Brahmā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shakambhari-shatakshi-durgamasura.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa VII.28)
- **Even Mārkaṇḍeya is not old enough** — the deathless sage who survives the deluge confesses he does not know Indradyumna and sends him to an elder still, the owl Prāvārakarṇa _(actors: Mārkaṇḍeya, Indradyumna, Prāvārakarṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/indradyumna-akupara-oldest-beings.md) — (Mahābhārata 3.191 / Ganguli Vana CXCIX)
- **Faith held before vindication** — Nandabhadra refutes the materialist on scripture and reason, defends the devas and Liṅga-worship, then walks to the Bahūdaka tīrtha at Mahīsāgara-Saṅgama to end his life _(actors: Nandabhadra, Satyavrata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nandabhadra-tested-faith.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa, Kaumārikā-khaṇḍa 45)
- **Gaṇeśa settles in Kāśī as Ḍhuṇḍhirāja** — Disguised as an aged brāhmaṇa astrologer, Gaṇeśa wins the city's trust, foretells the counselor to come on the eighteenth day, and remains as Ḍhuṇḍhi-Vināyaka, chief guardian Gaṇeśa of Kāśī _(actors: Gaṇeśa, Śiva, Divodāsa)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kashi-line-divodasa.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa, Kāśī-khaṇḍa, Uttarārdha ~chs. 56–57)
- **Garuḍa humbled and restored at Garuḍa-tīrtha** — Garuḍa imprisons the Śiva-protected serpent Maṇināga, is crushed under Viṣṇu's little finger, and rises stronger after bathing in the Gautamī _(actors: Garuḍa, Maṇināga, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Nandin)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gautami-mahatmya-tales-catalog.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa, Gautamī-māhātmya, vulgate adh. 90)
- **Garuḍa reconciled and the wedding of Sumukha and Guṇakeśī** — the humbled Garuḍa makes peace with Sumukha, who weds Guṇakeśī, laying to rest the bird-and-serpent enmity in this instance _(actors: Garuḍa, Sumukha, Guṇakeśī, Mātali)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/matali-sumukha-naga-bridegroom.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva 5.103)
- **Garuda seizes the bile of Bala, seeding the emeralds** — Bala's bile, taken by the serpent-king Vasuki, is snatched by Garuda and dropped in a remote mountain land, whence the emerald mines _(actors: Garuda, Vasuki, Bala/Vala)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/bala-asura-navaratna-origin.md) — (Buddhabhatta, Ratnapariksha, emerald section; Garuda Purana emerald chapter)
- **Garuḍa's one-month death-term revealed** — Nārada discloses that Garuḍa devoured Sumukha's father Cikura and has fixed a term one month hence to eat Sumukha too, dismaying the grandfather Āryaka _(actors: Nārada, Sumukha, Garuḍa, Āryaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/matali-sumukha-naga-bridegroom.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva 5.101)
- **Gaurī wins half of Śiva's body by the Kedāra vrata** — Pārvatī keeps the 21-day Kedāra Gaurī vow and is granted the left half of Śiva, the vrata-charter for Ardhanārīśvara _(actors: Pārvatī/Gaurī, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vrata-kathas-catalog.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa [attrib.], Kedāra-vrata-kathā) [late text] [regional]
- **Gautama's curse of Devī-aversion** — outraged at the framing, Gautama curses his benefactees to become averse to Gāyatrī and Mūla-Prakṛti Śrī Devī, to Veda, sandhyā and yajña, and to turn instead to Kāpālikas, Bauddha śāstras and pāṣaṇḍa heresy _(actors: Gautama, the brāhmaṇas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gautama-curse-on-the-brahmins.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata XII.9)
